117fn scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
118    scheduler_turn: u64,
119    virtual_nanoseconds: u64,
120    internal_io_poll: bool,
121    runtime_maps_read: bool,
122) -> String {
123    crate::detlog::record_suffix(crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommit {
124        scheduler_turn,

126        internal_io_poll,
127        runtime_maps_read,

151/// The response from the scheduler that wakes back up a guest thread after a request.
152#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
153pub enum SchedResponse {
154    /// Keep running.
155    Go(Option<SchedValue>),
156
157    /// The guest was interupted by a signal while waiting on the scheduler, and will now execute
158    /// the handler.
159    Signaled(Option<Vec<SigWrapper>>),
160    ObserveSignal(Box<parked::AlarmControl>),
161    /// The original qualified in-guest sleep must stage its consumed SIGALRM.
162    InGuestFatalAlarm,
163    // TODO: Time to exit, or an exit is already under way
164    // Exit,
165}

167#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialOrd, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
168/// A value that the scheduler returns to the guest when resuming.  This is weakly typed in that it
169/// is only relevant to certain scheduler requests, and its meaning is dependent on what was
170/// requested of the scheduler.
171///
172/// It can be used to have the scheduler EMULATE behaviors (syscalls) that would normally happen in
173/// the guest. The first application for this is futexes.
174pub enum SchedValue {
175    /// The action timed out while waiting on the scheduler.
176    TimeOut,
177    /// A signal ended a futex wait (`SchedResponse::Signaled`), as distinct from a
178    /// wakeup or from the `EINTR` value some non-signal early returns carry
179    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>). It carries the
180    /// signals the scheduler committed to the waiter at the wake, as a kernel
181    /// signal set, which the waiter's own check may then count although it
182    /// holds them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005>).
183    Signaled(u64),
184    // TODO(T137799529) make this more strongly typed, an enum for different scenarios:
185    Value(u64),
186    /// The answer to a futex requeue (`FutexAction::RequeueRequest`): how many
187    /// waiters it woke and how many it moved to the other futex.
188    Requeued {
189        /// Waiters woken.
190        woken: u64,
191        /// Waiters moved onto the target futex.
192        moved: u64,
193    },
194}

241/// A thread waiting on a futex, including the bitset accepted by wake operations.
242#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
243pub struct FutexWaiter {
244    dettid: DetTid,
245    response: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
246    bitset: u32,
247    /// Where to read the kernel's view of this waiter's signal state, on a backend
248    /// that reports it. `None` otherwise: a scheduler-sent signal then wakes the
249    /// waiter whatever its disposition, and a cross-task signal does not.
250    signal_watch: Option<FutexSignalWatch>,
251}
252
253/// What a precise-mode futex waiter's backend tells the scheduler about the
254/// waiter's signals when the wait begins
255/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
256///
257/// Only the mask is captured. It belongs to the waiting thread, and only that
258/// thread can change it, so it cannot change while the thread is parked. The
259/// dispositions belong to the whole process and a sibling can change them with
260/// `rt_sigaction` at any time, so they are NOT captured here: the scheduler reads
261/// them from the kernel at the moment it commits a wake
262/// (`Scheduler::parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
263#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
264pub struct FutexSignalWatch {
265    /// Kernel sigset of the signals the waiter's mask leaves unblocked, without
266    /// the backend's own preemption signal.
267    pub unblocked: u64,
268    /// Whether a default `SIGTSTP`, `SIGTTIN`, or `SIGTTOU` leaves the wait parked:
269    /// set for a timed futex wait, whose restart would not keep its deadline
270    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`). Fixed by the call, so it
271    /// cannot change while the waiter is parked.
272    pub defers_default_stops: bool,
273    /// The waiter's process, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
274    pub pid: i32,
275    /// The waiter's thread, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
276    pub tid: i32,
277}

279/// Which processes a host-timed signal source can signal once a guest arms it
280/// (`Scheduler::record_host_timed_signals`).
281#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
282pub enum HostTimedSignalScope {
283    /// Only the process of the thread that armed it.
284    Caller,
285    /// Any process of the container: the receiver can be another process, a
286    /// process group, or a process Hermit does not track.
287    Container,
288}

290/// The one-bit kernel sigset for a 1-based signal number, or 0 when out of range.
291pub(crate) fn kernel_signal_bit(raw_signal: i32) -> u64 {
292    if (1..=64).contains(&raw_signal) {
293        1_u64 << (raw_signal - 1)
294    } else {
295        0
296    }
297}
298
299/// Every signal Linux sends because of a terminal, as a kernel sigset. Once a
300/// guest process may have the terminal as its controlling terminal, or be in
301/// the terminal's foreground process group, each can arrive at a moment set
302/// by host timing:
303///
304/// - SIGHUP and SIGCONT when the terminal hangs up, as when its other end
305///   closes, or when the session leader exits (`tty_vhangup_session`,
306///   `disassociate_ctty`).
307/// - SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the interrupt, quit and suspend
308///   characters (`isig`), sent to the foreground process group when the
309///   kernel processes the terminal's input, which it does on a kernel worker
310///   rather than inside the call that supplied the input.
311/// - SIGWINCH when the window size changes (`tty_do_resize`, which
312///   `pty_resize` reaches for a pseudoterminal), sent to the foreground
313///   process group: a terminal emulator outside the container changes the
314///   size when its user resizes the window.
315/// - SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU when a process of a background process group reads
316///   the terminal, or writes it or changes its settings while TOSTOP is set
317///   (`__tty_check_change`, `job_control`), sent to that process's group,
318///   which can hold a process Hermit does not schedule. Linux sends them
319///   inside the caller's call, so for a guest's own read or write the record
320///   holds them longer than needed.
321///
322/// The scheduler records the whole set at launch when the guest may start
323/// with a terminal (`startup_host_timed_signals`), and so does a guest call
324/// that gives a session a controlling terminal or names the terminal's
325/// foreground process group (`syscalls/files.rs`). From then on no gated wait
326/// ends for any of them, whoever sends it: each is held until the call
327/// returns, as before blocked waits decided interruption from the kernel's
328/// signal state (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>, and the
329/// round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
330/// interruption" of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
331pub(crate) fn terminal_signals() -> u64 {
332    [
333        libc::SIGHUP,
334        libc::SIGCONT,
335        libc::SIGINT,
336        libc::SIGQUIT,
337        libc::SIGTSTP,
338        libc::SIGWINCH,
339        libc::SIGTTIN,
340        libc::SIGTTOU,
341    ]
342    .into_iter()
343    .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal))
344}
345
346/// The signals recorded as host-timed for every process of the container
347/// before the guest's first instruction (`host_timed_signals_everywhere`):
348/// every signal a terminal sends (`terminal_signals`) when the guest may start
349/// with a terminal and blocked waits decide interruption from the kernel's
350/// signal state (`Config::guest_may_inherit_a_terminal`), and nothing
351/// otherwise. The guest makes no traced call that arms them, so no guest turn
352/// could record them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
353fn startup_host_timed_signals(cfg: &Config) -> u64 {
354    if cfg.backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption && cfg.guest_may_inherit_a_terminal {
355        terminal_signals()
356    } else {
357        0
358    }
359}

361/// Render an already-sorted thread list for a diagnostic, or `none`.
362fn render_tid_list(tids: &[DetTid]) -> String {
363    if tids.is_empty() {
364        "none".to_owned()
365    } else {
366        tids.iter()
367            .map(|t| format!("dtid {}", t))
368            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
369            .join(", ")
370    }
371}

373/// Deterministically pick one element from `choices` using the supplied PRNG,
374/// returning `None` for an empty slice. This is the single random-selection
375/// primitive used by the targeted-chaos scheduling points, so their choices stay
376/// reproducible under a fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
377fn chaos_pick<T: Copy>(prng: &mut Pcg64Mcg, choices: &[T]) -> Option<T> {
378    choices.choose(prng).copied()
379}

381fn take_matching_futex_waiters(waiters: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>, wake_mask: u32) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
382    let (matching, remaining) = std::mem::take(waiters)
383        .into_iter()
384        .partition(|waiter| waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0);
385    *waiters = remaining;
386    matching
387}

389/// Actions that are blocked on another internal action of the guest, such as a pipe communication,
390/// or are blocked on external conditions such as a network request.  These cannot consume a logical
391/// turn until a matching unblocking action is ready.
392///
393/// This structure will NOT include blocking operations that are implemented via polling.
394/// See NOTE [Blocking Syscalls via Internal Polling] in this folder.
395#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
396pub struct BlockedPool {
397    /// BLOCKED futex transactions, waiting for wakers. Multiple threads may be blocked on
398    /// the same futex.
399    ///
400    /// INVARIANT: because Futexes aren't currently modeled with `ResourceID`, a thread
401    /// waiting on a futex will have a request filled in `next_turns` but for zero resources.
402    pub futex_waiters: HashMap<FutexID, Vec<FutexWaiter>>,
403
404    /// Futex waiters whose deadlines expired and must receive `ETIMEDOUT` when scheduled.
405    /// Timed-out waiters are removed from `futex_waiters` before entering the run queue.
406    pub timed_out_futex_waiters: HashSet<DetTid>,
407
408    /// Threads whose next event is waiting on a point in time to proceed.
409    ///
410    /// This is sorted by soonest time of occurrence.
411    /// NOTE: futex waiters will ALSO appear in here if they have timeouts.
412    pub timed_waiters: TimedEvents,
413
414    /// Threads parked until a matching child process exits logically.
415    pub child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetTid, (DetPid, ChildWaitSpec)>,
416
417    /// Threads parked between logical process exit and a backend's final
418    /// physical-exit report.
419    pub physical_child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetPid, BTreeSet<DetTid>>,
420
421    /// Waiters whose deterministic physical-exit handoff is ready to commit.
422    pub physical_child_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
423
424    /// Blockers on external IO that are in the middle of executing (or have finished) and
425    /// are waiting for permission from the scheduler to resume.
426    ///
427    /// The protocol here is that the `(request,response)` pair (in `next_turns`) for
428    /// threads in `external_io_blockers` will have the request filled in with an
429    /// `BlockedExternalContinue` request when the thread is past its blocking action and
430    /// waiting for permission to resume. A failed operation governed by `BlockingVfork` instead
431    /// reports `VforkFailed`, which follows the same re-admission path after cancelling its
432    /// barrier. The request will stay empty while the thread is doing the blocking action. This is
433    /// different than the normal relationship
434    pub external_io_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
435
436    /// Threads executing the real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the runnable set.
437    /// These retain the kernel's atomic temporary-mask semantics, but unlike
438    /// arbitrary external IO they cannot complete without a signal.
439    pub rt_sigsuspend_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
440
441    /// The signal mask each thread in `external_io_blockers` or
442    /// `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` sleeps under, recorded when the scheduler
443    /// committed its blocking request: the call's own temporary mask
444    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`), or else the thread's mask read
445    /// while it was still stopped at that request. `None` records a mask that
446    /// could not be read. Such a thread runs outside the schedule, so its live
447    /// mask is host-timed; `kernel_sigchld_target` uses this record instead.
448    /// An entry lives exactly as long as the thread's blocking-pool entry.
449    pub out_of_scheduler_masks: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<u64>>,
450
451    /// Parents parked awaiting deterministic delivery of a host-async `SIGCHLD`.
452    ///
453    /// When a guest child process exits, the kernel raises `SIGCHLD` on the
454    /// parent at a moment decided purely by host timing. If the resulting
455    /// `InboundSignal` turn is committed as soon as it arrives, its position
456    /// races whatever guest work was already runnable -- classically a `make -jN`
457    /// jobserver `pselect6` continuation -- and `--strict --verify` diverges.
458    ///
459    /// Instead the parent is parked here, out of the run queue, and re-admitted
460    /// by `step2e_process_signal_deferred` only once no ordinary (non-poller)
461    /// guest work remains: the same deterministic-work-first policy that governs
462    /// `external_io_blockers`. The physical signal has already been delivered by
463    /// the kernel, so the handler's `wait4`/`waitpid` still reaps a real host
464    /// zombie and no synthetic signal is ever generated.
465    pub sigchld_deferred: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
466
467    /// Deferred `SIGCHLD` parents that `step2e_process_signal_deferred` has
468    /// re-admitted to the run queue, and threads whose `SIGCHLD` delivery the
469    /// scheduler already placed: a child-exit timer's commit of a deferred
470    /// delivery, and a thread sleeping outside the schedule that the
471    /// scheduler's `SIGCHLD` woke (`arm_signaled_background`). Their
472    /// `InboundSignal` turn must be granted rather than deferred (again) on the
473    /// turn the scheduler selects them.
474    pub sigchld_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
475
476    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` that the
477    /// scheduler signaled at a committed point (`wake_signaled_guest`) while
478    /// they slept with no posted request. Their request was consumed when they
479    /// were backgrounded, so the scheduler cannot counterfeit one; it waits
480    /// for each one's own continuation (the InboundSignal its signal stop
481    /// posts) and requeues them all at the top of the next scheduler pass
482    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), so host delivery timing decides
483    /// only how long the scheduler spins, not where they enter the run queue.
484    pub signaled_background: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
485
486    /// Threads the scheduler signaled at a committed point while they were
487    /// still stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask
488    /// does not block the signal. The call's handler checked for a pending
489    /// signal before posting that request, so it could not see this one; the
490    /// thread's current mask may block it, so the kernel holds it pending until
491    /// the real `rt_sigsuspend` installs the temporary mask, and then delivers
492    /// it at once. Granting the request therefore arms the thread for the
493    /// release barrier (`arm_signaled_background`) as if the signal had been
494    /// sent one turn later, when it slept; otherwise the pool would hold a
495    /// sleeper the scheduler counts as unwakeable, and the next pass reports a
496    /// deadlock before the thread's signal stop is posted.
497    pub signaled_sigsuspend_requests: BTreeMap<DetTid, Signal>,
498
499    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` whose call `hermit replay` serves
500    /// from the recording (`Resources::replay_served_from_log`). Such a call
501    /// cannot block, so `step2c_process_io_blockers` commits no turn until all
502    /// of them have finished, then readmits them, in thread order, before any
503    /// other background call. An entry lives exactly
504    /// as long as the thread's `external_io_blockers` entry.
505    pub replay_log_served: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
506}
507
508impl BlockedPool {
509    /// Returns true if there are NO blocked threads waiting outside the run-queue.
510    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
511        self.no_futex_waiters()
512            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
513            && self.child_waiters.is_empty()
514            && self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
515            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
516            && self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
517            && self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
518            && self.sigchld_deferred.is_empty()
519    }
520
521    /// True if there are no runnable threads, and the only blocked ones are externally-blocked.
522    fn only_external_blocked(&self) -> bool {
523        let has_external_wait = !self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
524            || !self.child_waiters.is_empty()
525            || !self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
526        self.no_futex_waiters()
527            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
528            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
529            && (has_external_wait || !self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty())
530    }
531
532    /// Returns true if there are zero threads blocked on futexes.
533    fn no_futex_waiters(&self) -> bool {
534        self.futex_waiters.iter().all(|(_, v)| v.is_empty())
535    }
536}

538/// Validate a request made by a thread executing outside the runnable set.
539/// A signal may interrupt a real blocking syscall before its ordinary
540/// continuation request is posted, so an inbound-signal request is ready too.
541/// `vfork` is excluded because a signal does not satisfy its child barrier.
542fn blocking_request_is_ready(
543    req: &Resources,
544    expected: ExternalOpId,
545    signal_can_complete: bool,
546) -> bool {
547    assert_eq!(req.resources.len(), 1);
548    let rsrc = req.resources.iter().next().unwrap().0;
549    match rsrc {
550        ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(op_id) => {
551            assert_eq!(*op_id, expected);
552            true
553        }
554        ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) if signal_can_complete => true,
555        other => panic!("expected external continue request, got {other:?}"),
556    }
557}

559/// Runtime state for enforcing a [`HappensBeforeProgram`] inside the scheduler.
560///
561/// The scheduler holds each edge's AFTER anchor -- removing that thread from the
562/// run queue -- until the edge's BEFORE anchor has *fired*, so an authored
563/// partial order deterministically reproduces a known race instead of relying on
564/// a seed lottery. An anchor "fires" when its thread is granted passage past the
565/// corresponding checkpoint (see [`Scheduler::hb_checkpoint`]).
566///
567/// Two position kinds are enforced: [`Position::SyscallCount`] and the syscall
568/// occurrence anchors (`Anchor::is_syscall_occurrence`, "the thread's Nth
569/// `writev` to fd 9"), which the guest counts per thread and names in its
570/// checkpoint ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]). A syscall-occurrence
571/// anchor with the posthook phase checks in after its call's result is final
572/// instead of at its entry, and an interrupted call that reached one is
573/// refused (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`,
574/// [`Scheduler::hb_posthook_interrupted`];
575/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>). Other position kinds are retained
576/// for diagnostics but never fire; [`HbRuntime::new`] warns about them so a run
577/// never silently ignores an ordering constraint. An anchor that never fires
578/// is refused by name (`HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED`, exit 122): a BEFORE
579/// anchor whose held thread can never proceed, at the terminal deadlock
580/// ([`HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal`]), and any syscall-occurrence anchor still
581/// unfired when the scheduler finishes ([`HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report`]).
582/// A gate that would hold a vfork child before its exec is refused when it
583/// closes (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD`). A version-2 program also bounds
584/// every hold by its budget (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`,
585/// [`Scheduler::hb_check_hold_budget`]) and refuses a non-leader exec on an
586/// identity a relative anchor names
587/// (`HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT`).
588#[derive(Debug)]
589struct HbRuntime {
590    /// The validated, normalized program (anchors indexed by name, plus edges).
591    program: HappensBeforeProgram,
592    /// Names of anchors that have fired. Monotonic: an anchor fires at most once,
593    /// when its thread is first granted passage past it.
594    fired: BTreeSet<String>,
595    /// Threads currently parked at an AFTER anchor, out of the run queue, awaiting
596    /// their gating BEFORE anchor(s). A `BTreeSet` keeps re-admission order
597    /// deterministic.
598    parked: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
599    /// Threads observed at creation time, in deterministic spawn order, so an
600    /// anchor addressed by `spawn_ordinal` resolves to a concrete `DetTid`.
601    /// Index 0 is the root thread; index N (1-based) is the Nth spawned child,
602    /// matching [`ThreadRef::spawn_ordinal`] semantics.
603    spawn_order: Vec<DetTid>,
604    /// Set when a newly fired anchor may have opened a parked thread's gate, so
605    /// [`Scheduler::hb_flush_wakes`] re-admits parked threads at the next
606    /// `step3` boundary. Re-admission is *deferred* to that boundary because it
607    /// pushes to the run queue, which is illegal while a `tentative_pop`
608    /// selection is in progress (as it is inside `block_for_one_resource`,
609    /// where anchors fire).
610    wake_pending: bool,
611    /// For each parked thread, the anchors it is held at (those whose gate was
612    /// closed when it reached them), so a gate that can never open is refused
613    /// by naming the BEFORE anchors it waits on. Kept in step with `parked`.
614    held_at: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<String>>,
615    /// The logical holds a version-2 budget is charged against: for each
616    /// thread whose gate is closed, the committed virtual time (ns) at which
617    /// it was first parked there and the anchors it is held at. Unlike
618    /// `parked` and `held_at`, which `hb_flush_wakes` clears whenever any
619    /// anchor fires, a hold ends only when the thread is granted passage or
620    /// removed, so a wake that leaves its gate closed does not reset the
621    /// budget.
622    holds: BTreeMap<DetTid, HbHold>,
623}
624
625/// One logical hold ([`HbRuntime::holds`]).
626#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
627struct HbHold {
628    /// Committed virtual time, in ns, when the hold began.
629    since_ns: u64,
630    /// The anchors the thread is held at.
631    anchors: Vec<String>,
632}
633
634impl HbRuntime {
635    /// Build runtime state from a normalized program, warning about any anchor
636    /// whose position kind this milestone does not enforce.
637    fn new(program: HappensBeforeProgram) -> Self {
638        for anchor in program.unenforced_positions() {
639            tracing::warn!(
640                "[happens-before] anchor {} uses position '{}', which the scheduler does not yet \
641                 enforce (only syscall counts and syscall occurrences are enforced); this \
642                 ordering constraint will NOT be applied",
643                anchor.name,
644                anchor.position,
645            );
646        }
647        Self {
648            program,
649            fired: BTreeSet::new(),
650            parked: BTreeSet::new(),
651            spawn_order: Vec::new(),
652            wake_pending: false,
653            held_at: BTreeMap::new(),
654            holds: BTreeMap::new(),
655        }
656    }
657
658    /// Record a thread at creation time for `spawn_ordinal` resolution. Idempotent
659    /// and cheap; the root thread lands at index 0, the Nth child at index N.
660    fn note_spawn(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
661        if !self.spawn_order.contains(&dettid) {
662            self.spawn_order.push(dettid);
663        }
664    }
665
666    /// True when `tref` resolves to `dettid`, by explicit `DetTid` or by
667    /// `spawn_ordinal` against the observed spawn order.
668    fn thread_matches(&self, tref: &ThreadRef, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
669        if let Some(d) = tref.dettid {
670            return d == dettid;
671        }
672        if let Some(ord) = tref.spawn_ordinal {
673            return self.spawn_order.get(ord as usize).copied() == Some(dettid);
674        }
675        false
676    }
677
678    /// Names of anchors on `dettid` whose enforced position is exactly
679    /// `SyscallCount(count)`.
680    fn anchors_at_syscall(&self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) -> Vec<String> {
681        self.program
682            .anchors
683            .values()
684            .filter(|a| {
685                matches!(a.position, Position::SyscallCount(n) if n == count)
686                    && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
687            })
688            .map(|a| a.name.clone())
689            .collect()
690    }
691
692    /// Of the syscall-occurrence anchors a checkpoint names (the guest counted
693    /// them reached on its thread), the ones that are syscall-occurrence
694    /// anchors on `dettid`: its own dettid, or a spawn ordinal that resolves to
695    /// it. A name that is not such an anchor on this thread is ignored.
696    fn occurrence_anchors_on(&self, dettid: DetTid, names: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
697        names
698            .iter()
699            .filter(|name| {
700                self.program.anchors.get(*name).is_some_and(|a| {
701                    a.is_syscall_occurrence() && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
702                })
703            })
704            .cloned()
705            .collect()
706    }
707
708    /// The refusal for a terminal state in which threads are held at gates that
709    /// can never open, or `None` when no thread is held. Names, for each held
710    /// thread, the unfired BEFORE anchors of the hard edges into the anchors it
711    /// is held at: those are the points the guest never reached, the likeliest
712    /// cause being a wrong count, `fd` or `nth` in the spec. Byte-stable.
713    fn held_gate_refusal(&self) -> Option<String> {
714        if self.parked.is_empty() {
715            return None;
716        }
717        let mut lines = Vec::new();
718        for dettid in &self.parked {
719            let held_at = self.held_at.get(dettid).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
720            for after in &held_at {
721                for edge in self.program.edges.iter().filter(|e| {
722                    &e.after == after
723                        && e.strength == Strength::Hard
724                        && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
725                }) {
726                    let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
727                    lines.push(format!(
728                        "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired; it holds dtid {} at anchor \
729                         '{}' (edge {} -> {})",
730                        before.name,
731                        before.thread.label,
732                        before.position,
733                        dettid,
734                        after,
735                        edge.before,
736                        edge.after
737                    ));
738                }
739            }
740        }
741        Some(format!(
742            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: happens-before BEFORE anchor(s) never fired, and the \
743             thread(s) they hold cannot proceed because nothing else can run:\n{}",
744            lines.join("\n")
745        ))
746    }
747
748    /// The refusal for syscall-occurrence anchors that never fired, or `None`
749    /// when every one fired. Such an anchor names a point the guest never
750    /// reached (or reached fewer than `nth` times), so an edge it is part of
751    /// was never exercised; the run must say so rather than pass. Lists the
752    /// anchors in name order, each with its position and the edges that use
753    /// it, and carries no host-dependent text, so it is byte-identical across
754    /// runs. Count anchors are not covered: an unreached count anchor is
755    /// silently ignored, as before.
756    fn unfired_occurrence_report(&self) -> Option<String> {
757        let unfired: Vec<String> = self
758            .program
759            .anchors
760            .values()
761            .filter(|a| a.is_syscall_occurrence() && !self.fired.contains(&a.name))
762            .map(|a| {
763                let edges: Vec<String> = self
764                    .program
765                    .edges
766                    .iter()
767                    .filter(|e| e.before == a.name || e.after == a.name)
768                    .map(|e| format!("{} -> {}", e.before, e.after))
769                    .collect();
770                // A relative anchor whose base never fired could not even
771                // start counting: name the base too.
772                let base = match &a.from {
773                    Some(base) if !self.fired.contains(base) => {
774                        format!("counted from '{}', which never fired either; ", base)
775                    }
776                    Some(base) => format!("counted from '{}'; ", base),
777                    None => String::new(),
778                };
779                format!(
780                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired ({}edges: {})",
781                    a.name,
782                    a.thread.label,
783                    a.position,
784                    base,
785                    if edges.is_empty() {
786                        "none".to_owned()
787                    } else {
788                        edges.join(", ")
789                    }
790                )
791            })
792            .collect();
793        if unfired.is_empty() {
794            return None;
795        }
796        Some(format!(
797            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: {} happens-before syscall-occurrence anchor(s) never \
798             fired before the guest finished, so the ordering they name was not exercised:\n{}",
799            unfired.len(),
800            unfired.join("\n")
801        ))
802    }
803
804    /// The unfired BEFORE anchors that hold a thread at `after`, one line each,
805    /// in the form the refusals use. Byte-stable.
806    fn unfired_befores(&self, after: &str) -> Vec<String> {
807        self.program
808            .edges
809            .iter()
810            .filter(|e| e.after == after && e.strength == Strength::Hard)
811            .filter(|e| !self.fired.contains(&e.before))
812            .map(|edge| {
813                let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
814                format!(
815                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired (edge {} -> {})",
816                    before.name, before.thread.label, before.position, edge.before, edge.after
817                )
818            })
819            .collect()
820    }
821
822    /// The refusal for a hold that has outlasted the version-2 budget at
823    /// committed time `now_ns`, or `None`. Holds are checked in `DetTid`
824    /// order; the first over budget is named, with the BEFORE anchors it
825    /// waits on. The text carries no time other than the budget, so it is
826    /// byte-identical across runs.
827    fn hold_budget_refusal(&self, now_ns: u64) -> Option<String> {
828        let budget = self.program.max_hold_ns?;
829        let (dettid, hold) = self.holds.iter().find(|(_, hold)| {
830            now_ns.saturating_sub(hold.since_ns) > budget
831                && hold.anchors.iter().any(|a| self.anchor_blocked(a))
832        })?;
833        let lines: Vec<String> = hold
834            .anchors
835            .iter()
836            .flat_map(|after| self.unfired_befores(after))
837            .collect();
838        Some(format!(
839            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid {} has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
840             {:?} for more than max_hold_ns = {} virtual ns, waiting on:\n{}",
841            dettid,
842            hold.anchors,
843            budget,
844            lines.join("\n")
845        ))
846    }
847
848    /// The refusal for a non-leader exec in which `caller` takes over
849    /// `leader`'s identity while a relative anchor, or the base of one, is on
850    /// either thread, or `None`. Its activation state belongs to one task and
851    /// is not carried across the replacement in this version.
852    fn relative_identity_refusal(&self, caller: DetTid, leader: DetTid) -> Option<String> {
853        let names: Vec<String> = self
854            .program
855            .relative_anchors()
856            .filter(|(relative, _)| {
857                self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, caller)
858                    || self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, leader)
859            })
860            .map(|(relative, base)| format!("'{}' (from '{}')", relative.name, base.name))
861            .collect();
862        if names.is_empty() {
863            return None;
864        }
865        Some(format!(
866            "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {} execs and takes over the \
867             identity of dtid {}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) {} are on these \
868             threads; relative anchors are not carried across a non-leader exec.",
869            caller,
870            leader,
871            names.join(", ")
872        ))
873    }
874
875    /// True when anchor `name` is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
876    /// endpoint has not yet fired -- i.e. a thread reaching `name` must be held.
877    fn anchor_blocked(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
878        self.program.edges.iter().any(|e| {
879            e.after == name && e.strength == Strength::Hard && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
880        })
881    }
882}
883
884/// Which end of a thread's priority band a run-queue admission targets.
885#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
886pub(crate) enum AdmitSide {
887    /// Run before an equal-priority peer (`runqueue_push_front`).
888    Front,
889    /// Ordinary tail admission (`runqueue_push_back`).
890    Back,
891}
892
893/// How a run-queue admission's side is determined.
894///
895/// The side is *resolved* — not merely applied — at the deterministic drain
896/// ([`Scheduler::drain_pending_run_queue_admissions`]). Buffering the *intent*
897/// rather than an already-chosen `AdmitSide` is what keeps the admission a pure
898/// function of deterministic scheduler state: any PRNG draw that picks the side
899/// (`RunsPostFork::Random`) is consumed at the drain, in canonical `DetTid`
900/// order, instead of in host RPC / lock-acquisition order at the handler. See
901/// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`].
902#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
903pub(crate) enum AdmitIntent {
904    /// The side is fixed regardless of scheduler state; consumes no PRNG.
905    Fixed(AdmitSide),
906    /// The side follows the post-fork policy; `RunsPostFork::Random` draws from
907    /// the scheduler PRNG at resolution time.
908    PostFork(RunsPostFork),
909}
910
911/// Why a raw TID must be removed from the physical run queue at the next
912/// deterministic drain.
913#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
914enum RemovalDisposition {
915    /// The current thread incarnation is gone. Any admission recorded for the
916    /// same raw TID is stale and must be cancelled.
917    Retire,
918    /// Linux nonleader exec destroyed the old process leader and reassigned
919    /// its raw TID to the caller's replacement image. Remove the old physical
920    /// queue slot, but preserve the one causally paired replacement admission.
921    ReplaceThenAdmit,
922}
923
924#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
925enum WaitidSignalRequest {
926    /// An in-flight wait that a pending signal should wake: either the legacy
927    /// `waitid` kernel-polling loop or a scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle
928    /// resource.
929    ///
930    /// Deliberately does NOT distinguish the two. Queue residency is not a
931    /// property of the resource and must be decided at the drain, not inferred
932    /// here: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its
933    /// `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue` pushes a thread back before it
934    /// issues its next request, so either request can be held by a thread that
935    /// is already in the run queue.
936    Parked,
937    Pending(Vec<SigWrapper>),
938}
939
940/// The state for the deterministic scheduler.
941#[derive(Debug)]
942pub struct Scheduler {
943    /// Monotonically count upwards.
944    pub turn: u64,
945
946    /// The queue of logically UNBLOCKED guest threads waiting for a turn.  After a new
947    /// thread is created, it should always have an entry in here, but it goes to the end
948    /// of the line after its turn. Unblocked threads are dequed in priority order, then
949    /// round-robin within a priority level.
950    /// NB: Polling threads are considered unblocked, and their polling intervals are managed by the RunQueue
951    pub run_queue: RunQueue,
952
953    /// Stores the communication endpoints for rendevous with each guest on its next turn.
954    /// When the thread parks it provides its request for resources, and waits for a
955    /// response.  After a new thread is created, it should always have an entry in here.
956    ///
957    /// Parked threads are READY, waiting only for the scheduler.
958    ///
959    /// (N.B.  This is a BTreeMap because we iterate over it, printing the
960    /// contents, and BTreeMap gives us a predictable order, unlike HashMap.)
961    pub next_turns: BTreeMap<DetTid, ThreadNextTurn>,
962
963    /// Thread pidfds for backends whose scheduler identities do not name host
964    /// tasks directly. The address-space identity prevents stale exec cleanup
965    /// from removing a replacement image's descriptor.
966    physical_thread_pidfds: BTreeMap<DetTid, (MmId, i32, i32, OwnedFd)>,
967
968    /// The current set of actions in the background.
969    #[allow(dead_code)]
970    pub bg_action_pool: HashMap<ActionID, Action>,
971
972    /// The logical, global time consumed by actions that have been committed already.
973    pub committed_time: LogicalTime,
974
975    /// INVARIANT: Thread IDs in `blocked` are absent from `run_queue`.
976    pub blocked: BlockedPool,
977
978    /// Kernel-blocked vfork parents and their children, once registered.
979    vfork_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<DetTid>>,
980
981    /// Exact parent address space captured when BlockingVfork is granted.
982    /// A child self-registration can use this one-shot causal authority even
983    /// when Linux reused a TID retired by an earlier transferred exec.
984    vfork_registration_origins: BTreeMap<DetTid, MmId>,
985
986    /// Vfork parents that died, without an Exit grant, before their child
987    /// registered: the barrier is cancelled so no other turn is excluded, but
988    /// the child's still-outstanding `CreateVforkChildThread` must settle
989    /// against this record instead of the barrier. A new vfork by the same
990    /// TID clears a stale record ([`Scheduler::begin_vfork_barrier`]).
991    dead_vfork_parents: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
992    /// Vfork parents that died while their registered child was still known
993    /// to the scheduler. Their barrier is kept until the child's next release
994    /// edge, which happens at a deterministic point: its `Exit` grant, its
995    /// successful exec, or its logical kill
996    /// ([`Scheduler::release_vfork_child`]). Dropping it at the
997    /// parent's own retirement would let other threads be selected at a
998    /// moment the host chooses: on ptrace a SIGKILL from another process
999    /// retires its target only at the target's deregistration
1000    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984>).
1001    dead_parent_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1002    /// Vfork parents whose registered child reached a release edge (its
1003    /// `Exit` grant, its successful exec, or its logical kill) while the
1004    /// parent was alive. The barrier stays, and step2a waits without
1005    /// committing a turn until the parent's fate is known (its continuation
1006    /// or its retirement), then drops it. Recording the release whether or
1007    /// not the parent's death has been seen keeps the drop independent of the
1008    /// order in which those host-timed events arrive.
1009    released_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1010
1011    /// Processes a committed SIGKILL has doomed
1012    /// ([`Scheduler::record_committed_sigkill`]). They will die even if a
1013    /// thread of theirs is held at a happens-before gate, so a wait for one is
1014    /// never part of a deadlock. An entry is dropped when its process is
1015    /// reaped.
1016    sigkilled_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1017    /// Threads granted their `Exit` (an `exit` or `exit_group`), inside their
1018    /// own committed turn. A thread that leaves the scheduler without one died
1019    /// of a signal or with its process, so its process is going down
1020    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`]). Cleared when
1021    /// the tid is registered again.
1022    committed_exits: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1023    /// Set by a SIGKILL whose victim the scheduler cannot name (a pidfd with
1024    /// no recorded process): from then on no child wait counts as part of a
1025    /// deadlock ([`Scheduler::record_unresolved_sigkill`]).
1026    unresolved_sigkill: bool,
1027
1028    /// Threads whose run-queue admission was recorded by a global-request
1029    /// handler while a `tentative_pop` transaction was live, deferred to the
1030    /// next deterministic drain point (`step2`) so it cannot mutate the run
1031    /// queue underneath the daemon's tentative selection. Keyed by `DetTid`
1032    /// so the drain order among co-pending admissions is canonical rather than
1033    /// lock-acquisition dependent. The stored value is the *unresolved*
1034    /// [`AdmitIntent`], so any side-selecting PRNG draw is deferred to the
1035    /// `DetTid`-ordered drain rather than performed in host RPC order. See
1036    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] and
1037    /// [`Scheduler::drain_pending_run_queue_admissions`].
1038    pending_run_queue_admissions: BTreeMap<DetTid, AdmitIntent>,
1039
1040    /// Run-queue *removals* requested by a global-request handler
1041    /// (`reconnect_after_exec` -> `logically_kill_thread`), deferred to the same
1042    /// deterministic drain point (`step2`). `RunQueue::remove_tid` carries the same
1043    /// `tentative_selection.is_none()` guard as the push operations, so a
1044    /// multi-threaded exec that reconnects on an asynchronous backend (DBT)
1045    /// inside the daemon's tentative window would otherwise trip it, poison the
1046    /// scheduler mutex, and hang the run.
1047    ///
1048    /// A `Retire` target is already logically dead (its `next_turns` entry is
1049    /// gone and its request is `ThreadExited`). `ReplaceThenAdmit` is the one
1050    /// Linux exception: a nonleader exec has installed a fresh registration at
1051    /// the destroyed leader's raw TID, but the old incarnation's physical queue
1052    /// slot must still be removed. Both are filtered from
1053    /// [`Scheduler::are_all_quiesced`] until this drain establishes the intended
1054    /// physical queue state.
1055    ///
1056    /// The map is drained before admissions. Ordinary retirement cancels a
1057    /// buffered admission for the same raw TID; the explicitly classified exec
1058    /// replacement preserves exactly one causally paired admission.
1059    pending_run_queue_removals: BTreeMap<DetTid, RemovalDisposition>,
1060
1061    /// Cross-task signals physically queued while their sole target was parked
1062    /// in waitid or restartable internal IO polling. Applied at step2, where
1063    /// run-queue mutation is safe.
1064    pending_cross_task_signals: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<SigWrapper>>,
1065
1066    /// Whether the scheduler models which thread the kernel gives a signal it
1067    /// sends, from the signal masks it reads from the kernel: set exactly when
1068    /// threads are serialized and the backend decides blocked-wait interruption
1069    /// from the kernel's signal state
1070    /// (`backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`). Under it the
1071    /// scheduler records the mask of each thread it releases into a call
1072    /// outside the schedule (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`), wakes such
1073    /// a thread at a fixed point when its own signal reaches it
1074    /// (`arm_signaled_background`), and sends a child-exit `SIGCHLD` to the
1075    /// thread the kernel would give it (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
1076    models_signal_targets: bool,
1077
1078    /// Signals that a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to a process,
1079    /// keyed by that process: no gated wait of the process ends for them
1080    /// (`host_timed_signals`). An entry is added in the turn of the call that
1081    /// arms the source and is never removed
1082    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
1083    host_timed_signals: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1084
1085    /// Signals that a host-timed source can post to any process of the
1086    /// container: one a guest armed (`HostTimedSignalScope::Container`), and
1087    /// from the start, a terminal the guest may have inherited
1088    /// (`startup_host_timed_signals`). Never removed.
1089    host_timed_signals_everywhere: u64,
1090
1091    /// Kernel signal states that tests install for parked futex waiters, in
1092    /// place of reading `/proc`.
1093    #[cfg(test)]
1094    test_kernel_signal_states: BTreeMap<DetTid, KernelSignalState>,
1095
1096    /// Read failures that tests install for emulated sleepers, in place of
1097    /// reading `/proc` (`sleep_signal`).
1098    #[cfg(test)]
1099    test_sleeper_read_failures: BTreeMap<DetTid, sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable>,
1100
1101    /// How many times `read_thread_blocked_mask` was asked for a thread's mask,
1102    /// so a test can show that a path which must not read `/proc` does not.
1103    #[cfg(test)]
1104    test_kernel_mask_reads: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize,
1105
1106    /// Child-TID futexes whose kernel clear may still be racing a guest join.
1107    cleared_child_tids: HashMap<FutexID, DetTid>,
1108
1109    /// The rendered report for a terminal deadlock, once one has been detected.
1110    ///
1111    /// Set instead of panicking, and consumed by `sched_loop_inner`, which
1112    /// prints it and exits the container. Panicking here does not end the run:
1113    /// the scheduler is a `tokio::spawn`ed task, so its panic is captured by the
1114    /// task harness while every guest stays parked on an
1115    /// `Ivar<SchedResponse>` that only the (now dead) scheduler could fill --
1116    /// the run then hangs until an external timeout. Unwinding would also
1117    /// poison the scheduler mutex on the way out.
1118    terminal_deadlock: Option<String>,
1119
1120    /// A scheduler turn refused because its configured charge would pass the
1121    /// end of representable virtual time (`--scheduler-turn-cost`). Like
1122    /// [`Scheduler::terminal_deadlock`], `bump_global_time` records it and
1123    /// `sched_loop_inner` prints it and exits, because a panic in the
1124    /// scheduler task would leave every guest parked. Both turn functions
1125    /// return as soon as it is set, before any maintenance, selection, grant
1126    /// or signal observation, so nothing new waits on a guest.
1127    terminal_clock_exhaustion: Option<String>,
1128
1129    /// Set when `terminal_deadlock` is a policy refusal of the happens-before
1130    /// spec (a gate that can never open, or a hold inside a vfork child) rather
1131    /// than a scheduler failure: the run then exits with
1132    /// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT` instead of the fatal status.
1133    terminal_is_refusal: bool,
1134
1135    /// The scheduler turn at which `step2d_handle_empty_queue` last logged
1136    /// "zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.", while that empty state lasts.
1137    ///
1138    /// The line reports a logical transition: every thread is dead or gone and
1139    /// nothing waits. Once logged, the daemon may pass through the empty-queue
1140    /// step again before it can exit, and how many extra passes it makes is
1141    /// host timing. It waits for a SaBRe supervisor to report a final wait
1142    /// status (`pending_physical_process_exits`), and it drains a removal that
1143    /// a dead thread's second, reactive exit hook queued
1144    /// (`pending_run_queue_removals`). Neither is a thread. This records that
1145    /// the current empty state was already reported, so those passes add no
1146    /// line. It is cleared as soon as the step sees a thread or a waiter again,
1147    /// and a committed turn makes the recorded turn stale.
1148    ///
1149    /// See <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360> and
1150    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223>.
1151    empty_queue_kick_turn: Option<u64>,
1152

1155    // callback and daemon wait clones its own subscriber, unlike an Ivar.

1373// type ThreadTree = HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>;
1374#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
1375pub struct ThreadTree {
1376    /// Invariant: this is None only if `tree` is also empty.
1377    /// That is any ThreadTree of size zero or more has a root.
1378    root: Option<DetTid>,
1379    /// Invariant: every `DetTid` in the tree has an entry here, though if it is a leaf,
1380    /// it will have an empty children-vector.
1381    tree: HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1382
1383    /// The subset of threads that are also thread group leaders.  This tracks both the
1384    /// Tid, but it is (numerically) the same as Pid for group leaders in Linux.
1385    thread_group_leaders: HashSet<DetTid>,
1386
1387    /// Go from a Tid to the Pid/Tid of the containing process (i.e. a reverse view of a
1388    /// transitive closure of `thread_tree`).  Every thread should have an entry in
1389    /// here. If, however, a thread is a group leader, this will map back to itself.
1390    thread_to_leader: HashMap<DetTid, DetPid>,
1391
1392    /// Reverse map from a process (group-leader `DetPid`) to its effective Linux
1393    /// wait parent, including `CLONE_PARENT`. Populated when a new group leader
1394    /// is registered; the root process has no entry. Entries survive logical
1395    /// exit until the terminal status is consumed.
1396    process_parent: HashMap<DetPid, DetPid>,
1397
1398    /// Linux child-wait identity for each process leader. Unlike the thread
1399    /// tree edge, this records the effective wait parent after CLONE_PARENT,
1400    /// the exact creating task for __WNOTHREAD, clone exit-signal class, and
1401    /// mutable process-group/session membership.
1402    process_wait: HashMap<DetPid, ProcessWaitMetadata>,
1403
1404    /// How many times each process has exec'd successfully (Linux's
1405    /// `self_exec_id`), for the exit-signal rule a parent's exec applies
1406    /// (`ProcessWaitMetadata::parent_exec_generation`).
1407    exec_generations: HashMap<DetPid, u64>,
1408
1409    /// Processes that made themselves child subreapers with
1410    /// `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)` (Linux's
1411    /// `signal_struct::is_child_subreaper`). The flag survives exec, because
1412    /// the process keeps its pid, and a forked child does not inherit it.
1413    child_subreapers: HashSet<DetPid>,
1414
1415    /// Processes whose parent exited with no live child subreaper above it,
1416    /// so Linux gave them to the container's init (`reparent_orphans`). Their
1417    /// `process_parent` and wait metadata still name the dead parent, as
1418    /// before subreapers were modeled (exit classification reads that link),
1419    /// but a subreaper search must not climb past them: their real parent is
1420    /// init.
1421    init_orphans: HashSet<DetPid>,
1422
1423    /// Processes whose exit the scheduler granted (`ResourceID::Exit` for the
1424    /// whole group, or for its last live thread), so that their logical exit
1425    /// is fixed between committed turns. A process that dies without one is
1426    /// recorded only at its host-timed deregistration (`reparent_orphans`).
1427    granted_exits: HashSet<DetPid>,
1428
1429    /// How many PID namespaces below the container's each process lives in;
1430    /// absent means zero. A child inherits its creator's depth and adds one
1431    /// for `CLONE_NEWPID` (`enter_new_pid_namespace`); `unshare` and `setns`
1432    /// are refused, so `clone` is the only way in. Linux's `find_new_reaper`
1433    /// looks for a subreaper only among ancestors at the exited process's
1434    /// own depth (`find_child_reaper`).
1435    pid_ns_depth: HashMap<DetPid, u32>,
1436}
1437
1438#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
1439struct ProcessWaitMetadata {
1440    wait_parent: Option<DetPid>,
1441    wait_owner: DetTid,
1442    /// The child's exit signal as Linux keeps it (`task_struct::exit_signal`):
1443    /// the clone signal, its creator's for CLONE_PARENT, and SIGCHLD after the
1444    /// child's own successful exec. It decides the wait class (a child whose
1445    /// signal is not SIGCHLD is reaped only with __WCLONE or __WALL); the
1446    /// notification can differ (`ThreadTree::notification_signal`).
1447    exit_signal: libc::c_int,
1448    /// The wait parent's exec count when this child was created (Linux's
1449    /// `parent_exec_id`), or its creator's for CLONE_PARENT.
1450    parent_exec_generation: u64,
1451    process_group: DetPid,
1452    session: DetPid,
1453}
1454
1455use pretty::Doc;
1456use pretty::RcDoc;
1457
1458use self::replayer::DesyncStats;
1459use self::replayer::Replayer;
1460
1461impl ThreadTree {
1462    /// Internal helper. Add a [child] process to the tree, with the parent being `None`
1463    /// if it's the root of the tree.
1464    fn add_edge(&mut self, parent: Option<DetTid>, child: DetTid) {
1465        match parent {
1466            None => {
1467                self.root = Some(child);
1468                // Ensure an entry, even if the children vector is empty:
1469                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
1470            }
1471            Some(p) => {
1472                let vec = self.tree.entry(p).or_default();
1473                vec.push(child);
1474                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
1475            }
1476        }
1477    }
1478
1479    /// Read the children of a thread, which is assumed to have an entry in the tree.
1480    pub fn get_children(&self, parent: &DetTid) -> &Vec<DetTid> {
1481        self.tree
1482            .get(parent)
1483            .expect("Internal failure: tid was not found in ThreadTree")
1484    }
1485
1486    /// Convert to pretty-printed document.
1487    ///
1488    /// For example, a binary tree of depth two may print as `(1 (2 3 4) (5 6 7))`,
1489    /// showing each thread ID grouped with its children.
1490    ///
1491    /// The thread_group_leaders argument is used for additional context into account when
1492    /// pretty-printing a `ThreadTree`.  This will indicate which children are within new
1493    /// thread groups using square brackets:
1494    ///
1495    ///   `[1 [2 [3] 4] (5 6 7)]`
1496    // TODO: it would also be nice to store a fixed prefix of the binary name and listing
1497    // that along with the thread ID.
1498    pub fn pretty_print(&self) -> String {
1499        fn walk<'a>(
1500            tt: &'a HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1501            tgl: &HashSet<DetTid>,
1502            current: &DetTid,
1503        ) -> RcDoc<'a, ()> {
1504            if let Some(children) = tt.get(current) {
1505                if tgl.contains(current) {
1506                    RcDoc::text("[")
1507                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1508                        .append(if children.is_empty() {
1509                            RcDoc::text("")
1510                        } else {
1511                            RcDoc::text(" ").append(
1512                                RcDoc::intersperse(
1513                                    children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
1514                                    Doc::line(),
1515                                )
1516                                .nest(1)
1517                                .group(),
1518                            )
1519                        })
1520                        .append(RcDoc::text("]"))
1521                } else if children.is_empty() {
1522                    RcDoc::as_string(current)
1523                } else {
1524                    RcDoc::text("(")
1525                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1526                        .append(RcDoc::text(" "))
1527                        .append(
1528                            RcDoc::intersperse(
1529                                children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
1530                                Doc::line(),
1531                            )
1532                            .nest(1)
1533                            .group(),
1534                        )
1535                        .append(RcDoc::text(")"))
1536                }
1537            } else {
1538                // This should be unreachable if the invariants are maintained:
1539                RcDoc::text("<ThreadTree corrupt, missing tid: ")
1540                    .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1541                    .append(RcDoc::text(">"))
1542            }
1543        }
1544
1545        let root = match self.root {
1546            None => return "[]".into(),
1547            Some(root) => root,
1548        };
1549
1550        let doc = walk(&self.tree, &self.thread_group_leaders, &root);
1551        let width = 100;
1552        let mut vec = Vec::new();
1553        doc.render(width, &mut vec).unwrap();
1554        String::from_utf8(vec).unwrap()
1555    }
1556
1557    #[allow(dead_code)]
1558    /// Number of threads with entries in the tree.
1559    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
1560        self.tree.len()
1561    }
1562
1563    /// Simultaneously update the thread tree and leader tracking to reflect the creation
1564    /// of a new child thread.
1565    #[cfg(test)]
1566    pub fn add_child(
1567        &mut self,
1568        parent_dettid: DetTid,
1569        child_dettid: DetTid,
1570        is_group_leader: bool,
1571    ) {
1572        self.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
1573            parent_dettid,
1574            child_dettid,
1575            is_group_leader,
1576            false,
1577            libc::SIGCHLD,
1578        );
1579    }
1580
1581    /// Add a child while preserving the Linux identities used by wait-family
1582    /// selection. `clone_parent` changes the child's effective wait parent and
1583    /// owner to the caller's own parent task; threads never enter this process
1584    /// metadata table.
1585    pub fn add_child_with_wait_metadata(
1586        &mut self,
1587        parent_dettid: DetTid,
1588        child_dettid: DetTid,
1589        is_group_leader: bool,
1590        clone_parent: bool,
1591        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
1592    ) {
1593        // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
1594        if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
1595            self.add_edge(None, child_dettid);
1596        } else {
1597            self.add_edge(Some(parent_dettid), child_dettid);
1598        }
1599        if is_group_leader {
1600            self.thread_group_leaders.insert(child_dettid);
1601            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, child_dettid);
1602            // A reused pid starts with neither Linux attribute: the flag is
1603            // not inherited, and the new process has its own live parent.
1604            self.child_subreapers.remove(&child_dettid);
1605            self.init_orphans.remove(&child_dettid);
1606            self.granted_exits.remove(&child_dettid);
1607            // The child lives in its creator's PID namespace until
1608            // `enter_new_pid_namespace` says otherwise.
1609            let creator_depth = self
1610                .thread_to_leader
1611                .get(&parent_dettid)
1612                .filter(|_| parent_dettid != child_dettid)
1613                .map_or(0, |creator| self.pid_ns_depth(*creator));
1614            if creator_depth == 0 {
1615                self.pid_ns_depth.remove(&child_dettid);
1616            } else {
1617                self.pid_ns_depth.insert(child_dettid, creator_depth);
1618            }
1619            if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
1620                self.process_wait.insert(
1621                    child_dettid,
1622                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
1623                        wait_parent: None,
1624                        wait_owner: child_dettid,
1625                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
1626                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
1627                        process_group: child_dettid,
1628                        session: child_dettid,
1629                    },
1630                );
1631            } else {
1632                let parent_process = self
1633                    .thread_to_leader
1634                    .get(&parent_dettid)
1635                    .copied()
1636                    .expect("process child parent must have a thread-group leader");
1637                let parent_metadata = self.process_wait.get(&parent_process).copied().unwrap_or(
1638                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
1639                        wait_parent: None,
1640                        wait_owner: parent_dettid,
1641                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
1642                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
1643                        process_group: parent_process,
1644                        session: parent_process,
1645                    },
1646                );
1647                // CLONE_PARENT makes the child a sibling of its creator: Linux
1648                // gives it the creator's parent, the creator's `parent_exec_id`
1649                // and the exit signal of the creator's process, whatever
1650                // signal the clone asked for (`copy_process`).
1651                let (wait_parent, wait_owner, exit_signal, parent_exec_generation) = if clone_parent
1652                {
1653                    (
1654                        parent_metadata.wait_parent,
1655                        parent_metadata.wait_owner,
1656                        parent_metadata.exit_signal,
1657                        parent_metadata.parent_exec_generation,
1658                    )
1659                } else {
1660                    (
1661                        Some(parent_process),
1662                        parent_dettid,
1663                        exit_signal,
1664                        self.exec_generation(parent_process),
1665                    )
1666                };
1667                if let Some(wait_parent) = wait_parent {
1668                    self.process_parent.insert(child_dettid, wait_parent);
1669                }
1670                self.process_wait.insert(
1671                    child_dettid,
1672                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
1673                        wait_parent,
1674                        wait_owner,
1675                        exit_signal,
1676                        parent_exec_generation,
1677                        process_group: parent_metadata.process_group,
1678                        session: parent_metadata.session,
1679                    },
1680                );
1681            }
1682        } else {
1683            let parent_leader: DetPid =
1684                    *self
1685                        .thread_to_leader
1686                        .get(&parent_dettid)
1687                        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
1688                            panic!("recv_create_child_thread: parent {} of child dtid {} does not exist in thread_to_leader map!",
1689                                   parent_dettid, child_dettid);
1690                        });
1691            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, parent_leader);
1692        }
1693    }
1694
1695    /// The process that created `pid` (its parent process), if `pid` is not the
1696    /// root process. Returns a possibly-stale parent if that process has since
1697    /// exited; callers deliver through `select_signal_target`, which drops a
1698    /// signal to a `Gone` target.
1699    pub fn parent_process(&self, pid: &DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
1700        self.process_parent.get(pid).copied()
1701    }
1702
1703    /// Preserve a surviving exec task's children when Linux replaces its TID
1704    /// with the process leader's. The creation tree remains historical; only
1705    /// the current task identity used by `__WNOTHREAD` changes. Scope the move
1706    /// to this effective parent so retained records from an older use of the
1707    /// same raw TID and `CLONE_PARENT` children keep their own wait identities.
1708    fn transfer_exec_wait_owner(&mut self, process: DetPid, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
1709        for metadata in self.process_wait.values_mut() {
1710            if metadata.wait_parent == Some(process) && metadata.wait_owner == former {
1711                metadata.wait_owner = leader;
1712            }
1713        }
1714    }
1715
1716    /// `process`'s successful exec count (`exec_generations`).
1717    fn exec_generation(&self, process: DetPid) -> u64 {
1718        self.exec_generations.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
1719    }
1720
1721    /// Apply Linux's exit-signal rules for a successful exec by `process`: its
1722    /// own exit signal becomes SIGCHLD (so it leaves the clone wait class),
1723    /// and its exec count advances, which turns the notification of each child
1724    /// it created before this exec into SIGCHLD (`notification_signal`).
1725    pub fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
1726        *self.exec_generations.entry(process).or_insert(0) += 1;
1727        if let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&process) {
1728            metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
1729        }
1730    }
1731
1732    /// The signal Linux notifies `child`'s wait parent with when `child`
1733    /// exits (`do_notify_parent`): its exit signal, except that a signal other
1734    /// than SIGCHLD becomes SIGCHLD once the parent has exec'd since creating
1735    /// the child (its `parent_exec_id` no longer matches). 0 means none.
1736    /// `None` for a process without wait metadata.
1737    pub fn notification_signal(&self, child: DetPid) -> Option<libc::c_int> {
1738        let metadata = self.process_wait.get(&child)?;
1739        let parent_execed = metadata
1740            .wait_parent
1741            .is_some_and(|parent| self.exec_generation(parent) != metadata.parent_exec_generation);
1742        Some(if metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD && parent_execed {
1743            libc::SIGCHLD
1744        } else {
1745            metadata.exit_signal
1746        })
1747    }
1748
1749    pub fn process_group(&self, pid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
1750        self.process_wait
1751            .get(&pid)
1752            .map(|metadata| metadata.process_group)
1753    }
1754
1755    pub fn set_process_group(&mut self, pid: DetPid, process_group: DetPid) -> bool {
1756        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
1757            return false;
1758        };
1759        metadata.process_group = process_group;
1760        true
1761    }
1762
1763    /// Mirror a successful `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, on)` by `pid`.
1764    pub fn set_child_subreaper(&mut self, pid: DetPid, on: bool) {
1765        if on {
1766            self.child_subreapers.insert(pid);
1767        } else {
1768            self.child_subreapers.remove(&pid);
1769        }
1770    }
1771
1772    /// Whether `pid` is a child subreaper (`set_child_subreaper`).
1773    pub fn is_child_subreaper(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
1774        self.child_subreapers.contains(&pid)
1775    }
1776
1777    /// Give `child` a new wait parent after its parent's process exited, as
1778    /// Linux's `reparent_leader` does: `reaper` and its thread `owner`. The
1779    /// exit signal becomes SIGCHLD, and the reaper's exec count is taken so
1780    /// that the notification is SIGCHLD too.
1781    fn reparent_child(&mut self, child: DetPid, reaper: DetPid, owner: DetTid) {
1782        let reaper_exec_generation = self.exec_generation(reaper);
1783        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&child) else {
1784            return;
1785        };
1786        metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
1787        metadata.wait_parent = Some(reaper);
1788        metadata.wait_owner = owner;
1789        metadata.parent_exec_generation = reaper_exec_generation;
1790        self.process_parent.insert(child, reaper);
1791    }
1792
1793    /// The children of `exited` whose new parent is still undecided: those
1794    /// whose wait parent is `exited` and that did not already go to init. In
1795    /// ascending pid order, because `process_wait` is a hash map and the
1796    /// order decides the order of the re-parenting records and wakes.
1797    fn undecided_orphans_of(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Vec<DetPid> {
1798        let mut orphans: Vec<DetPid> = self
1799            .process_wait
1800            .iter()
1801            .filter(|(child, metadata)| {
1802                metadata.wait_parent == Some(exited) && !self.is_init_orphan(**child)
1803            })
1804            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
1805            .collect();
1806        orphans.sort();
1807        orphans
1808    }
1809
1810    /// The process `tid` belongs to in the thread tree: its thread group's
1811    /// leader, or `None` for an unregistered thread.
1812    pub fn process_of(&self, tid: DetTid) -> Option<DetPid> {
1813        self.thread_to_leader.get(&tid).copied()
1814    }
1815
1816    /// `pid` was created with `CLONE_NEWPID`: it is the init of a PID
1817    /// namespace one level below its creator's (`pid_ns_depth`).
1818    pub fn enter_new_pid_namespace(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
1819        let depth = self.pid_ns_depth(pid) + 1;
1820        self.pid_ns_depth.insert(pid, depth);
1821    }
1822
1823    /// `pid_ns_depth` of `pid`.
1824    pub fn pid_ns_depth(&self, pid: DetPid) -> u32 {
1825        self.pid_ns_depth.get(&pid).copied().unwrap_or(0)
1826    }
1827
1828    /// Record that `child` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
1829    fn orphan_to_init(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
1830        self.init_orphans.insert(child);
1831    }
1832
1833    /// Whether `pid` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
1834    fn is_init_orphan(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
1835        self.init_orphans.contains(&pid)
1836    }
1837
1838    pub fn create_session(&mut self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
1839        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
1840            return false;
1841        };
1842        metadata.session = pid;
1843        metadata.process_group = pid;
1844        true
1845    }
1846
1847    /// Return the set of thread IDs in the "same process" as me (same TGID), including
1848    /// myself.
1849    ///
1850    /// Whether `tid` has been registered in the tree. A process the backend
1851    /// reports gone before it registers is not (asynchronous exit completion).
1852    pub fn contains(&self, tid: &DetTid) -> bool {
1853        self.thread_group_leaders.contains(tid) || self.thread_to_leader.contains_key(tid)
1854    }
1855
1856    /// Locks: takes scheduler lock.
1857    pub fn my_thread_group(&self, me: &DetTid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
1858        let root_tid: DetTid = if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(me) {
1859            *me
1860        } else {
1861            *self
1862                .thread_to_leader
1863                .get(me)
1864                .expect("thread must be in to_leader table")
1865        };
1866        let mut stack: Vec<DetTid> = vec![root_tid];
1867        let mut acc: Vec<DetTid> = vec![];
1868
1869        while let Some(first) = stack.pop() {
1870            if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(&first) && first != root_tid {
1871                continue; // Stop traversal when we walk into child processes.
1872            } else {
1873                acc.push(first);
1874            }
1875            let children = self.get_children(&first);
1876            stack.extend_from_slice(children);
1877        }
1878        assert!(acc.contains(me));
1879        acc
1880    }
1881}
1882
1883impl std::fmt::Display for ThreadTree {
1884    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
1885        // Print with empty thread_group_leaders since we don't have that information in
1886        // this context:
1887        write!(f, "{}", self.pretty_print())
1888    }
1889}
