1891// TODO (T137183027, T137184765)
1892/// A simple backoff strategy while we have any realtime/polling elements in the system.
1893/// When all external polling is removed, we can remove this.
1894struct Backoff {
1895    count: u64,
1896}
1897
1898impl Backoff {
1899    fn new() -> Self {
1900        Backoff { count: 0 }
1901    }
1902
1903    async fn further(&mut self, blocking: bool) {
1904        self.count += 1;
1905        const YIELDS_FIRST: u64 = 10;
1906        if blocking {
1907            if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
1908                std::thread::yield_now();
1909            } else {
1910                let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
1911                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros));
1912            }
1913        } else if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
1914            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
1915        } else {
1916            let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
1917            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros)).await;
1918        }
1919    }
1920
1921    fn reset(&mut self) {
1922        self.count = 0;
1923    }
1924}
1925
1926/// Sleep length for backoff round `round` (1-based): 2^round microseconds, capped at
1927/// 10 ms once 2^round would pass 8192 us.
1928fn backoff_sleep_micros(round: u64) -> u64 {
1929    if round > 13 { 10_000 } else { 1 << round }
1930}
1931
1932impl Default for Backoff {
1933    fn default() -> Self {
1934        Self::new()
1935    }
1936}
1937
1938pub(crate) type SchedulerObserver = Arc<dyn Fn(&'static str) + Send + Sync>;
1939
1940pub(crate) async fn sched_loop(sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>, timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) {
1941    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, false, None).await;
1942}
1943
1944pub(crate) async fn sched_loop_external(
1945    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
1946    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
1947    observer: SchedulerObserver,
1948) {
1949    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, true, Some(observer)).await;
1950}
1951
1952async fn sched_loop_inner(
1953    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
1954    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
1955    blocking_backoff: bool,
1956    observer: Option<SchedulerObserver>,
1957) {
1958    // The "daemon task starting up" INFO line is deliberately NOT emitted here.
1959    //
1960    // This body runs inside a `tokio::spawn`ed task (see
1961    // `GlobalState::initialize`), so the moment it is first polled is
1962    // unsynchronized with the spawning thread's continued bootstrap. That made
1963    // the line race the root thread's `USER RAND` / `CHAOSRAND` seeding lines
1964    // from `ThreadState::new`, and the L2 comparator reads the INFO stream as
1965    // ordered evidence: the two runs were identical as multisets and differed
1966    // only in this one line's position, which is a real `bitwise_parity: false`.
1967    //
1968    // The announcement is now emitted by whoever starts the daemon, in that
1969    // thread's program order, so it is deterministically sequenced after
1970    // `Scheduler::new`'s `SCHEDRAND` line and before the root `ThreadState`.
1971    // That is the order the ptrace backend already produced reliably.
1972    //
1973    // The observer callback stays here, at the point the task genuinely begins
1974    // executing, because it is a barrier signal for external backends and is
1975    // not part of the compared log stream. Moving the log does not cost us the
1976    // "it actually started" observation for the consumer that needs it.
1977    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
1978        observer("daemon task starting; waiting for guest thread");
1979    }
1980    let (iv, stop_after_iter) = {
1981        // Block until queue is populated.
1982        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
1983        (sched.started_up.clone(), sched.stop_after_iter)
1984    };
1985    if until_backend_failure(&sched, iv.get()).await.is_err() {
1986        return;
1987    }
1988    info!("[scheduler] guest in queue, scheduler proceeding..",);
1989    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
1990        observer("guest registered; deterministic scheduler proceeding");
1991    }
1992    let mut iter: u64 = 0;
1993    // We keep track of whether the last turn was a SKIP:
1994    let mut last_res = Err(SkipTurn);
1995    let mut backoff = Backoff::new();
1996    let mut observed_turn = false;
1997
1998    loop {
1999        if sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failed() {
2000            return;
2001        }
2002        // TODO (T137183027, T137184765): as part of the current strategy for blocking IO ops (see
2003        // SPINNING below), we need to make sure that other threads can progress so we don't
2004        // busy-wait too tightly.
2005        if last_res.is_err() {
2006            backoff.further(blocking_backoff).await;
2007        } else {
2008            backoff.reset();
2009        }
2010
2011        trace!("[scheduler] loop iteration {}", iter);
2012        if stop_after_iter.is_some() && iter > stop_after_iter.unwrap() {
2013            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2014            tracing::warn!(
2015                "[scheduler] Early exit during sched loop iteration {} due to --stop-after-iter.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2016                iter,
2017                sched.full_summary()
2018            );
2019            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2020        }
2021        iter += 1;
2022
2023        // If there are NO threads left in the system, then we're truly done:
2024        {
2025            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2026            sched.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop);
2027            if sched.backend_failed() {
2028                return;
2029            }
2030            // A thread held at a happens-before gate is in neither the run queue
2031            // nor `blocked`, but it is still a live thread: without this the loop
2032            // exited while it waited and the guest hung with no scheduler and no
2033            // deadlock report (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
2034            if sched.run_queue.is_empty()
2035                && sched.blocked.is_empty()
2036                && sched
2037                    .happens_before
2038                    .as_ref()
2039                    .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty())
2040                && sched.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
2041                && sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty()
2042                && sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty()
2043                && !sched.control_barrier()
2044            {
2045                // A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired names an ordering
2046                // the run never exercised: refuse by name instead of passing.
2047                // Printed like the deadlock report (no timestamp), so it is
2048                // byte-identical across runs.
2049                if let Some(report) = sched
2050                    .happens_before
2051                    .as_ref()
2052                    .and_then(HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report)
2053                {
2054                    eprintln!("{}", report);
2055                    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2056                }
2057                info!("[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.");
2058                if let Some(refusal) = sched.unreplayed_rejoins() {
2059                    drop(sched);
2060                    exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2061                }
2062                if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2063                    observer("run queue empty; scheduler completed");
2064                }
2065                return;
2066            } else if let Some(stop) = sched.stop_after_turn
2067                && sched.turn > stop
2068            {
2069                tracing::warn!(
2070                    "[scheduler] Early exit during turn {} due to --stop-after-turn.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2071                    sched.turn,
2072                    sched.full_summary()
2073                );
2074                immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2075            }
2076        }
2077
2078        // Otherwise we trust the turn function to either choose a runnable thread or wait
2079        // until something blocked is ready to run again.
2080        last_res = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), timer.clone(), &last_res).await;
2081
2082        // A vfork barrier whose backend event never arrived. Taken here, after
2083        // either turn function, because both run step2a: the ordinary one
2084        // through `step2_process_blocked` and the signal-control one through
2085        // `step2_drain_prefix`.
2086        let vfork_refusal = sched.lock().unwrap().vfork_barrier_refusal.take();
2087        if let Some(refusal) = vfork_refusal {
2088            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2089        }
2090
2091        // A terminal deadlock ends the run here, alongside the two
2092        // `--stop-after-*` exits above, rather than by panicking out of the
2093        // scheduler task (see `report_terminal_deadlock`).
2094        //
2095        // Printed with `eprintln!` rather than `tracing::error!` on purpose: the
2096        // tracing writer prefixes a real wall-clock timestamp, and this report
2097        // is required to be byte-identical across runs of the same program.
2098        let terminal = {
2099            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2100            let is_refusal = sched.terminal_is_refusal;
2101            sched
2102                .take_terminal_deadlock()
2103                .map(|report| (report, is_refusal))
2104        };
2105        if let Some((report, is_refusal)) = terminal {
2106            eprintln!("{}", report);
2107            if is_refusal {
2108                // A happens-before spec the guest cannot satisfy: a policy
2109                // refusal, distinct from the guest's status and from a failure.
2110                std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2111            }
2112            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2113        }
2114        // Virtual time ran out under a configured --scheduler-turn-cost: end
2115        // the run the same way, rather than saturate the clock.
2116        if let Some(report) = sched.lock().unwrap().terminal_clock_exhaustion.take() {
2117            eprintln!("{}", report);
2118            immediate_fatal_exit();
2119        }
2120
2121        if last_res.is_ok() && !observed_turn {
2122            if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2123                observer("completed a deterministic scheduling turn");
2124            }
2125            observed_turn = true;
2126        }
2127    }
2128}
2129
2130/// A place in the daemon loop, inside one of its scheduler-lock holds, where a
2131/// test can land a host-timed backend report. Production builds compile
2132/// [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] to nothing.
2133///
2134/// Two reports reach the scheduler from backend threads at host-chosen times
2135/// near the end of a run: the SaBRe ptrace supervisor's
2136/// `complete_physical_process_exit` when the kernel delivers a process's final
2137/// wait status, and a dead thread's second, reactive `logically_kill_thread`
2138/// from its exit hook. Each can take the scheduler lock between any two of the
2139/// daemon's lock holds. These points sit before the top-of-loop exit check and
2140/// on both sides of the empty-queue step's decision, the two decisions that
2141/// read that state, so a test can land a report at each point in turn, with no
2142/// sleeps.
2143#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2144enum SchedLoopPoint {
2145    /// In the top-of-loop exit check's lock hold, before it reads any state.
2146    LoopTop,
2147    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, before it reads any state.
2148    BeforeEmptyQueue,
2149    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, after it has decided.
2150    AfterEmptyQueue,
2151}
2152
2153/// What the scheduler does with a child process's exit notification to its
2154/// parent, decided at the child's exit grant
2155/// (`Scheduler::classify_child_exit_notification`).
2156#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2157pub(crate) enum ChildExitNotification {
2158    /// Linux sends nothing: the parent explicitly ignores SIGCHLD, whether or
2159    /// not it blocks it.
2160    None,
2161    /// Linux discards the signal at generation: SIGCHLD is default-ignored and
2162    /// the receiving task does not block it.
2163    Discard,
2164    /// Linux delivers the signal: the parent catches it, or the receiving task
2165    /// blocks it (a blocked signal stays pending).
2166    Deliver,
2167    /// Hermit cannot classify the notification; the synthetic SIGCHLD path
2168    /// applies as before.
2169    Undecided,
2170}
2171
2172/// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order for an effective SIGCHLD: explicit SIG_IGN
2173/// suppresses it regardless of blocking; a blocked signal stays pending; a
2174/// caught one is delivered; a default-ignored, unblocked one is discarded.
2175pub(crate) fn classify_sigchld_notification(
2176    ignored: bool,
2177    caught: bool,
2178    blocked: bool,
2179) -> ChildExitNotification {
2180    if ignored {
2181        ChildExitNotification::None
2182    } else if blocked || caught {
2183        ChildExitNotification::Deliver
2184    } else {
2185        ChildExitNotification::Discard
2186    }
2187}
2188
2189/// A hex signal mask field (`SigIgn`, `SigCgt`, `SigBlk`) of
2190/// `/proc/<pid>/status`, or of `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/status` for a thread.
2191#[cfg_attr(test, allow(dead_code))]
2192fn proc_status_signal_mask(pid: DetPid, tid: Option<DetTid>, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
2193    let path = match tid {
2194        Some(tid) => format!("/proc/{}/task/{}/status", pid.as_raw(), tid.as_raw()),
2195        None => format!("/proc/{}/status", pid.as_raw()),
2196    };
2197    parse_proc_status_signal_mask(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?, field)
2198}
2199
2200fn parse_proc_status_signal_mask(status: &str, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
2201    status.lines().find_map(|line| {
2202        let value = line.strip_prefix(field)?.strip_prefix(':')?;
2203        u64::from_str_radix(value.trim(), 16).ok()
2204    })
2205}

2211/// The release barrier's watchdog expired (`step2_release_signaled_background`):
2212/// committed signals armed these background threads, and they had still not
2213/// posted their continuations when it fired. Their admission point can no
2214/// longer be fixed by the scheduler, so the run is refused instead of being
2215/// continued with an order that host delivery time decides
2216/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
2217#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2218pub struct SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
2219    /// The armed threads that posted no continuation, in `DetTid` order.
2220    pub unposted: Vec<DetTid>,
2221    /// How long, in host time, the barrier had waited when it refused.
2222    pub waited: Duration,
2223}
2224
2225impl std::fmt::Display for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
2226    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2227        write!(
2228            f,
2229            "hermit refused to continue the run: the signaled background threads {:?} \
2230             posted no continuation within {:?} of the release barrier, so their \
2231             admission order would depend on host signal delivery time",
2232            self.unposted.iter().map(|t| t.as_raw()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
2233            self.waited
2234        )
2235    }
2236}

2238impl std::error::Error for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {}

2240/// Which of its two waits a vfork barrier was in when step2a's valve expired
2241/// (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`).
2242#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2243pub enum VforkBarrierState {
2244    /// The parent's vfork was granted and its child has not registered.
2245    Pending,
2246    /// The registered child reached a release edge (its `Exit` grant, its
2247    /// successful exec, or its logical kill) while its parent was alive.
2248    Released,
2249}

2251/// One vfork barrier that was still waiting for a backend event when step2a's
2252/// valve expired.
2253#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2254pub struct VforkBarrierWait {
2255    /// The vfork parent.
2256    pub parent: DetTid,
2257    /// Its registered child, or `None` while the barrier is `Pending`.
2258    pub child: Option<DetTid>,
2259    /// Which wait the barrier was in.
2260    pub state: VforkBarrierState,
2261}
2262
2263impl VforkBarrierWait {
2264    /// The backend event the barrier was waiting for.
2265    pub fn awaited(&self) -> &'static str {
2266        match self.state {
2267            VforkBarrierState::Pending => "the child's registration",
2268            VforkBarrierState::Released => "the parent's continuation or retirement",
2269        }
2270    }
2271}

2273/// Step2a's valve expired (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`): a vfork
2274/// barrier waited, committing nothing, for a backend event that had not
2275/// arrived when it fired. Selecting other threads instead would let host
2276/// timing decide the schedule, so the run is refused
2277/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>).
2278#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2279pub struct VforkBarrierRefusal {
2280    /// The barriers still waiting, in parent `DetTid` order.
2281    pub waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait>,
2282    /// How long, in host time, step2a had waited when it refused.
2283    pub waited: Duration,
2284}
2285
2286impl std::fmt::Display for VforkBarrierRefusal {
2287    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2288        write!(
2289            f,
2290            "hermit refused to continue the run: vfork barriers waited {:?} for backend \
2291             events that never arrived:",
2292            self.waited
2293        )?;
2294        for wait in &self.waits {
2295            write!(f, " parent {}", wait.parent.as_raw())?;
2296            match wait.child {
2297                Some(child) => write!(f, " (child {})", child.as_raw())?,
2298                None => write!(f, " (no child registered)")?,
2299            }
2300            write!(f, " {:?}, awaiting {};", wait.state, wait.awaited())?;
2301        }
2302        Ok(())
2303    }
2304}

2306impl std::error::Error for VforkBarrierRefusal {}

2308/// End the run on a scheduler refusal: write it to stderr and exit with
2309/// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`, the status for "hermit examined the run and
2310/// refused it", as the network replay refusal does. Only the ptrace backend
2311/// arms the release barrier or runs record/replay, and a ptrace guest does not
2312/// outlive this process (Reverie sets `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`). A vfork barrier
2313/// refusal can come from any backend; it ends the run the way a terminal
2314/// deadlock refusal does. In Hermit's default container no guest outlives it:
2315/// the scheduler then runs in the init of the private PID namespace that
2316/// `Container::run` forks the guest into, and when a namespace init exits the
2317/// kernel `SIGKILL`s every remaining member (hermit-cli's container.rs,
2318/// `on_container_init_stop_signal`). That does not hold everywhere. With
2319/// `--no-namespace` the run gets no PID namespace, and hermit-cli's run.rs
2320/// (`log_cap_refusal`) names, for every backend, a way its guest can outlive an
2321/// exit like this one, ptrace's being the window before `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`
2322/// binds the guest. On DBT the scheduler runs in the DBT runtime
2323/// (`GlobalState::init_for_external_scheduler`), and the DynamoRIO guest is a
2324/// plain child of hermit that no PID namespace binds.
2325pub(crate) fn exit_on_scheduler_refusal(refusal: &dyn std::fmt::Display) -> ! {
2326    {
2327        use std::io::Write;
2328        let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
2329    }
2330    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2331}

2334/// selected task. The public backend callback still supplies its actual task.
2335#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2336struct BackendFailureLocation {
2337    pid: reverie::Pid,
2338    tid: Option<reverie::Tid>,
2339    phase: &'static str,
2340}

2342/// Wait without manufacturing a normal scheduler request or response. The
2343/// caller must check the terminal state again under the mutex before mutation.
2344async fn until_backend_failure<T>(
2345    sched: &Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2346    wait: impl std::future::Future<Output = T>,
2347) -> Result<T, SkipTurn> {
2348    let failure = {
2349        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2350        if sched.backend_failed() {
2351            return Err(SkipTurn);
2352        }
2353        sched.backend_failure_waiter()
2354    };
2355    futures::pin_mut!(wait, failure);
2356    match futures::future::select(failure, wait).await {
2357        futures::future::Either::Left((notice, _)) => {
2358            notice.expect("scheduler owns the failure sender until publication");
2359            Err(SkipTurn)
2360        }
2361        futures::future::Either::Right((value, _)) => Ok(value),
2362    }
2363}
2364
2365/// Advance turn by 1 turn, blocking when necessary to make it happen.
2366/// Return the outcome of the turn as well as which resources were used, if any.
2367///
2368/// WARNING: this is duplicated with the non-blocking `step` function below.
2369/// TODO: this duplication is temporary and they should be either combined or one removed soon.
2370async fn do_ordinary_turn_blocking(
2371    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2372    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2373    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
2374) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
2375    // Loop until all threads are parked, then proceed:
2376    //
2377    // TODO: First, this check can move after step2, before we commit the action. Second,
2378    // it can later grow more sophisticated to only check the completion of dependent
2379    // actions, not all outsanding guest actions.
2380    loop {
2381        // We must read the queue carefully, because it can grow in the background
2382        // everytime we await.  However, while it can *grow*, it cannot change order, as
2383        // only the scheduler thread (us) actually rotates entries from the front to the back.
2384        let req_ivar = {
2385            let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
2386            if mg.backend_failed() {
2387                return Err(SkipTurn);
2388            }
2389            let arc = global_time.clone();
2390
2391            let next_outstanding = mg.step1_check_quiescence(&arc, last_turn);
2392            // A refused charge ends the turn here, before any maintenance,
2393            // selection or grant; `sched_loop_inner` then reports it and exits.
2394            if mg.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
2395                return Err(SkipTurn);
2396            }
2397            match next_outstanding {
2398                None => {
2399                    trace!("Scheduler observed full quiescense, proceeding...");
2400                    break;
2401                }
2402                Some(iv) => iv.clone(),
2403            }
2404        };
2405        trace!("Scheduler wait for full quiescense, on {}...", req_ivar);
2406        let _ = until_backend_failure(&sched, req_ivar).await?;
2407    }
2408
2409    // Here we copy some information while holding the sched lock, and then release it so
2410    // we can `.await` below:
2411    let (next_dtid, req, resp) = {
2412        let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2413        if sched.backend_failed() {
2414            return Err(SkipTurn);
2415        }
2416        let blocked = sched.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
2417        if let Some(refusal) = sched.signaled_background_refusal.take() {
2418            drop(sched);
2419            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2420        }
2421        if let Some(refusal) = sched.rejoin_refusal.take() {
2422            drop(sched);
2423            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2424        }
2425        blocked?;
2426        sched.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?
2427    };
2428
2429    finish_selected_turn(sched, global_time, next_dtid, req, resp).await
2430}
2431
2432pub async fn do_a_turn_blocking(
2433    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2434    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2435    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
2436) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
2437    // Installed before the first guest thread registers, so every turn of a
2438    // run takes the same branch.
2439    let controlled = sched.lock().unwrap().signal_control_installed();
2440    if !controlled {
2441        return do_ordinary_turn_blocking(sched, global_time, last_turn).await;
2442    }
2443    #[cfg(test)]
2444    {
2445        sched.lock().unwrap().controlled_turn_entries += 1;
2446    }
2447    let result = async {
2448        // A control pause retains both its maintenance position and the unpaid
2449        // obligation of the preceding real turn. Transport messages never pay it.
2450        enum Action {
2451            Wait {
2452                request: Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>>,
2453                control: Ivar<()>,
2454                barrier: bool,
2455            },
2456            Select(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>),
2457        }
2458        let mut charged = false;
2459        let mut refresh = false;
2460        let mut maintenance = 0;
2461        // The reference admits one due event before a selection. Control
2462        // callbacks may refresh observed time, but must not spend that event
2463        // budget again and reverse ordinary sleepers' queue-front order.
2464        let mut timed_event_processed = false;
2465        let mut empty_queue_skip = false;
2466        loop {
2467            signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
2468            let action = {
2469                let mut state = sched.lock().unwrap();
2470                state.drain_control_intents();
2471                if state.backend_failed() {
2472                    return Err(SkipTurn);
2473                }
2474                let barrier = state.control_barrier();
2475                if empty_queue_skip && !barrier {
2476                    return Err(SkipTurn);
2477                }
2478                let request = state.are_all_quiesced();
2479                if !barrier && request.is_none() {
2480                    if !charged {
2481                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, last_turn);
2482                        charged = true;
2483                        // A refused charge ends the turn before maintenance,
2484                        // alarm selection, signal observations or grants can
2485                        // start; `sched_loop_inner` reports it and exits.
2486                        if state.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
2487                            return Err(SkipTurn);
2488                        }
2489                    } else if refresh {
2490                        // A hook can advance real observed logical time. Refresh
2491                        // eligibility without charging again. An earlier empty
2492                        // due check leaves the one-event budget available; an
2493                        // actual pop consumes it until this turn returns.
2494                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
2495                        if !timed_event_processed {
2496                            timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
2497                        }
2498                        // Idempotent and spends no event budget, so it runs on
2499                        // every refresh.
2500                        state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
2501                        if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
2502                            state.fail_parked_selection(error);
2503                            continue;
2504                        }
2505                    }
2506                    refresh = false;
2507                    if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
2508                        continue;
2509                    }
2510                    match maintenance {
2511                        0 => {
2512                            state.step2_drain_prefix()?;
2513                            maintenance = 1;
2514                            continue;
2515                        }
2516                        1 => {
2517                            if !timed_event_processed {
2518                                timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
2519                            }
2520                            state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
2521                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
2522                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
2523                            }
2524                            maintenance = 2;
2525                            continue;
2526                        }
2527                        2 => {
2528                            state.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
2529                            maintenance = 3;
2530                            continue;
2531                        }
2532                        3 => {
2533                            state.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
2534                            maintenance = 4;
2535                            continue;
2536                        }
2537                        4 => {
2538                            empty_queue_skip =
2539                                state.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err();
2540                            // Select at the time to which the empty queue just
2541                            // advanced, before a later pass can advance again.
2542                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
2543                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
2544                            }
2545                            maintenance = 5;
2546                            continue;
2547                        }
2548                        _ => {
2549                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
2550                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
2551                                continue;
2552                            }
2553                            // Installing an observation creates an empty callback
2554                            // gate. Await its hook/finish before any tentative pop.
2555                            if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
2556                                continue;
2557                            }
2558                            let (tid, req, resp) = state.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?;
2559                            Action::Select(tid, req, resp)
2560                        }
2561                    }
2562                } else {
2563                    Action::Wait {
2564                        request,
2565                        control: state.control_waiter(),
2566                        barrier,
2567                    }
2568                }
2569            };
2570            match action {
2571                Action::Select(tid, req, resp) => {
2572                    return finish_selected_turn(
2573                        sched.clone(),
2574                        global_time.clone(),
2575                        tid,
2576                        req,
2577                        resp,
2578                    )
2579                    .await;
2580                }
2581                Action::Wait {
2582                    request,
2583                    control,
2584                    barrier,
2585                } => {
2586                    if barrier {
2587                        until_backend_failure(&sched, control).await?;
2588                    } else if let Some(request) = request {
2589                        let wait = async {
2590                            futures::pin_mut!(request, control);
2591                            let _ = futures::future::select(request, control).await;
2592                        };
2593                        until_backend_failure(&sched, wait).await?;
2594                    }
2595                    refresh = true;
2596                }
2597            }
2598        }
2599    }
2600    .await;
2601    signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
2602    result
2603}
2604
2605/// Complete the selected transaction. Keeping the await and post-await checks
2606/// together also lets native controls hold the real request wait open while
2607/// consuming cleanup races with the daemon.
2608pub(crate) async fn finish_selected_turn(
2609    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2610    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2611    next_dtid: DetTid,
2612    req: Ivar<SchedRequest>,
2613    resp: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
2614) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
2615    // Step 1B: wait for the selected thread to make its request.
2616    trace!(
2617        "[sched-daemon] waiting for next thread (dtid {}) to park...",
2618        next_dtid
2619    );
2620    let rsrcs: Resources = match until_backend_failure(&sched, req.get()).await? {
2621        Err(ThreadExited) => {
2622            debug!(
2623                "[sched-daemon] woke up on request {}, but fizzling because next thread, {}, exited.",
2624                &req, &next_dtid
2625            );
2626            // The selected thread died while we awaited its request, so this turn
2627            // is skipped without reaching step4-6. `step3_peek` opened a
2628            // tentative_pop for `next_dtid`; close it here (undo, since the turn
2629            // did not commit) before returning. Otherwise the tentative selection
2630            // outlives the turn, and the next pass's step2 removal drain calls
2631            // `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is still `Some`, tripping
2632            // the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect panic moved one
2633            // pass" defect. The dead thread's buffered removal drains
2634            // deterministically on the next pass, once this undo has closed the
2635            // window.
2636            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2637            if !sched.backend_failed() {
2638                sched.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
2639            }
2640            return Err(SkipTurn);
2641        }
2642        Ok(r) => r,
2643    };
2644    trace!("[sched-daemon] daemon woke up on {}...", &req);
2645
2646    // Since the scheduler is asynchronous, we need to check our assumptions.  Polling is
2647    // sufficient here because the thread cannot be racing with us to exit since we know
2648    // it is *already* parked.
2649    let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
2650    if mg.backend_failed() {
2651        return Err(SkipTurn);
2652    }
2653    mg.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(next_dtid)?;
2654    // A terminal verdict recorded while the lock was released (for example
2655    // by the exec reconnect handler) ends the run after this turn: do not
2656    // commit or grant it, so no guest runs concurrently with the exit.
2657    if mg.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
2658        mg.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
2659        return Err(SkipTurn);
2660    }
2661
2662    // The logical COMMIT point for the turn is during step4:
2663    mg.step4_resource_block(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
2664    mg.step5_guest_unblock(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
2665    let sched_yield = rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::SchedYield);
2666    mg.step6_reenquue(next_dtid, sched_yield);
2667    if let Some(call) = rsrcs.as_exit_syscall() {
2668        mg.step7_simulate_exit_posthook(next_dtid, call, &global_time);
2669    }
2670    Ok(rsrcs)
2671}
2672
2673// A futex request contains only one resource request, for FutexWait.
2674fn assert_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) {
2675    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
2676        Some(Ok(req)) => {
2677            if !(req.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::FutexWait) && req.resources.len() == 1) {
2678                panic!(
2679                    "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected empty resource request, found: {:?}",
2680                    nextturn.dettid, req
2681                )
2682            }
2683        }
2684        _ => panic!(
2685            "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected request for zero resources, instead found no request.",
2686            nextturn.dettid
2687        ),
2688    }
2689}
2690
2691// Test if the request was from a futex_wait call.
2692fn is_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) -> bool {
2693    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
2694        Some(Ok(req)) => Scheduler::is_x_turn(&req, &ResourceID::FutexWait),
2695        _ => false,
2696    }
2697}

2705/// The result of consuming a SchedEvent during --replay-preemptions-from.  This represents some
2706/// decisions about what to do next, but are actions which we cannot implement inside

2709    /// Should we keep runnning this thread, if false we background the current thread after this schedevent to let the next thread run.
2710    pub keep_running: bool,
2711    /// A remaining (delta) timeslice this thread is required to run according to the replay schedule
2712    pub timeslice_remaining: Option<LogicalTime>,
2713    /// Should we print the stacktrace in the guest, as per --stacktrace-event
2714    pub print_stack: MaybePrintStack,
2715    /// The number of this event in the global total order of events.
2716    #[allow(dead_code)]
2717    pub event_ix: u64,
2718}

2721/// a response that further includes a path means print to a file at that location.
2722pub type MaybePrintStack = Option<Option<PathBuf>>;

2724enum ThreadStatus {

2726    Gone,
2727    Running,

2732impl Scheduler {
2733    /// Create a new scheduler based on the configuration.
2734    pub fn new(cfg: &Config) -> Self {
2735        let (replayer, m_vec) = match &cfg.replay_schedule_from {
2736            Some(path) => {
2737                trace!("Scheduler loading trace from path {}", path.display());
2738                let vec = read_trace(path);
2739                trace!("Trace loaded, length {}", vec.len());
2740
2741                let toprint = cfg
2742                    .stacktrace_event
2743                    .iter()
2744                    .map(|(ix, path)| (*ix, Some(vec[*ix as usize].clone()), path.clone()))
2745                    .collect();
2746                let mut replayer = Replayer::new(vec);
2747                replayer.replay_exhausted_panic = cfg.replay_exhausted_panic;
2748                replayer.die_on_desync = cfg.die_on_desync;
2749                (Some(replayer), Some(toprint))
2750            }
2751            None => (
2752                None,
2753                if cfg.stacktrace_event.is_empty() {
2754                    None
2755                } else {
2756                    let vec: Vec<_> = cfg
2757                        .stacktrace_event
2758                        .iter()
2759                        .map(|(ix, path)| (*ix, None, path.clone()))
2760                        .collect();
2761                    Some(vec)
2762                },
2763            ),
2764        };
2765
2766        let stacktrace_events: Option<StacktraceEventsIter> = m_vec.map(|mut v| {
2767            v.sort_by_key(|(ix, _, _)| *ix);
2768            v.into_iter().peekable()
2769        });
2770
2771        let (backend_failure_sender, backend_failure_wake) = oneshot::channel();
2772        Self {
2773            preemption_writer: if cfg.record_preemptions {
2774                Some(PreemptionWriter::new(cfg.record_preemptions_to.clone()).with_epoch(cfg.epoch))
2775            } else {
2776                None
2777            },
2778            replayer,

2891    /// Record a newly created thread for happens-before `spawn_ordinal`
2892    /// resolution. A no-op unless a happens-before program is active.
2893    pub fn hb_note_spawn(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {

2895            hb.note_spawn(dettid);

2899    pub(crate) fn register_physical_thread(
2900        &mut self,
2901        dettid: DetTid,
2902        mm: MmId,
2903        physical_pid: i32,
2904        physical_tid: i32,
2905    ) -> std::io::Result<()> {
2906        if physical_pid <= 0 || physical_tid <= 0 {
2907            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
2908                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
2909                "host process and thread IDs must be positive",
2910            ));
2911        }
2912        if let Some((known_mm, known_pid, known_tid, _)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid)
2913        {
2914            if *known_mm == mm && *known_pid == physical_pid && *known_tid == physical_tid {
2915                return Ok(());
2916            }
2917            if *known_mm == mm {
2918                return Err(std::io::Error::new(
2919                    std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
2920                    format!(
2921                        "scheduler identity {dettid} already names host process {known_pid} thread {known_tid}"
2922                    ),
2923                ));
2924            }
2925        }
2926        let raw_fd = unsafe {
2927            libc::syscall(
2928                libc::SYS_pidfd_open,
2929                physical_tid,
2930                libc::O_EXCL as libc::c_uint,
2931            )
2932        };
2933        if raw_fd < 0 {
2934            return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
2935        }
2936        // SAFETY: pidfd_open returned a new descriptor owned by this process.
2937        let pidfd = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(raw_fd as libc::c_int) };
2938        self.physical_thread_pidfds
2939            .insert(dettid, (mm, physical_pid, physical_tid, pidfd));
2940        Ok(())
2941    }
2942
2943    fn remove_physical_thread(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid, mm: MmId) {
2944        if self
2945            .physical_thread_pidfds
2946            .get(dettid)
2947            .is_some_and(|(registered_mm, ..)| *registered_mm == mm)
2948        {
2949            self.physical_thread_pidfds.remove(dettid);
2950        }
2951    }

2954    pub(crate) fn physical_thread_identity(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<(MmId, i32, i32)> {
2955        self.physical_thread_pidfds
2956            .get(&dettid)
2957            .map(|(mm, pid, tid, _)| (*mm, *pid, *tid))

2960    /// Record, in the sender's committed turn, that a SIGKILL to `dettid` (or
2961    /// to process `target_process`) succeeded. The process will die even
2962    /// while one of its threads is held at a happens-before gate, so
2963    /// [`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`] never counts a
2964    /// wait for it as part of a deadlock. On ptrace its retirement comes later,
2965    /// at its host-timed deregistration
2966    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994); this record is
2967    /// decided by the sender's syscall, so it is deterministic.
2968    pub(crate) fn record_committed_sigkill(
2969        &mut self,
2970        dettid: DetTid,
2971        target_process: Option<DetPid>,
2972    ) {
2973        let process = target_process.or_else(|| {
2974            self.thread_tree
2975                .thread_to_leader
2976                .get(&dettid)
2977                .map(|leader| DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw()))
2978        });
2979        match process {
2980            Some(process) => {
2981                self.sigkilled_processes.insert(process);
2982            }
2983            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
2984        }
2985    }
2986
2987    /// Record a successful SIGKILL the scheduler is not told about one victim
2988    /// at a time: every process now in process group `group`, or, for `None`
2989    /// (a pidfd whose process Detcore did not record), an unknown process.
2990    /// An unknown victim makes every child wait count as input that may still
2991    /// arrive for the rest of the run.
2992    pub(crate) fn record_unresolved_sigkill(&mut self, group: Option<DetPid>) {
2993        match group {
2994            Some(group) => {
2995                let members: Vec<DetPid> = self
2996                    .thread_tree
2997                    .process_wait
2998                    .iter()
2999                    .filter(|(_, metadata)| metadata.process_group == group)
3000                    .map(|(process, _)| *process)
3001                    .collect();
3002                self.sigkilled_processes.extend(members);
3003            }
3004            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
3005        }
3006    }
3007
3008    /// Whether a committed SIGKILL doomed `process`, and whether one with an
3009    /// unnamed victim was seen (test observation of the record above).
3010    #[cfg(test)]
3011    pub(crate) fn sigkill_recorded(&self, process: DetPid) -> (bool, bool) {
3012        (
3013            self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&process),
3014            self.unresolved_sigkill,
3015        )
3016    }

3018    /// A thread is being registered on `dettid`: any committed exit recorded
3019    /// for an earlier thread with that tid no longer applies.
3020    pub(crate) fn forget_committed_exit(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
3021        self.committed_exits.remove(&dettid);
3022    }

3024    pub(crate) fn note_process_sigkill(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, detpid: DetPid) {
3025        if !self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
3026            return;
3027        }
3028        let Some((mm, _, _, _)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid) else {
3029            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
3030                format!(
3031                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot complete SIGKILL for dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
3032                    dettid,
3033                )
3034            });
3035            return;
3036        };
3037        let mm = *mm;
3038        self.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, mm);
3039    }

3042        !self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&parent)

3045    /// Refuse the run (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`, exit 122) for a
3046    /// syscall entry of `dettid` that reached posthook `anchors` and returned
3047    /// the internal restart `code`: whether that entry returns `EINTR` or is
3048    /// restarted and never returns is decided by the kernel after this point
3049    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>).
3050    ///
3051    /// The guest names every spawn-ordinal anchor at its nth matching call on
3052    /// any thread, as for a completed call, so only the anchors that resolve
3053    /// to `dettid` count ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]); with none,
3054    /// the turn proceeds. Otherwise nothing fires, the verdict is recorded (an
3055    /// earlier pending verdict and its classification are kept), and the turn
3056    /// grants nothing, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit.
3057    fn hb_posthook_interrupted(
3058        &mut self,
3059        dettid: DetTid,
3060        count: u64,
3061        anchors: &[String],
3062        code: &str,
3063    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3064        let anchors = self
3065            .happens_before
3066            .as_ref()
3067            .expect("posthook refusal issued without a happens-before program")
3068            .occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, anchors);
3069        if anchors.is_empty() {
3070            return Ok(());
3071        }
3072        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3073            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
3074                "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid {} reached posthook happens-before \
3075                 anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}, and the call was interrupted ({}); whether \
3076                 it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
3077                 checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook \
3078                 or on a call that is not interrupted.",
3079                dettid, anchors, count, code
3080            ));
3081            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3082        }
3083        self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
3084    }
3085
3086    /// Handle a happens-before checkpoint issued by `dettid` after its `count`th
3087    /// intercepted syscall (see `Detcore::handle_syscall_event`).
3088    ///
3089    /// Grants passage (firing every anchor at `SyscallCount(count)` on this
3090    /// thread and re-admitting any parked threads whose gate may now be open)
3091    /// unless a reached anchor is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
3092    /// anchor has not fired, in which case the thread is parked out of the run
3093    /// queue until a later firing wakes it. Mirrors the `SleepUntil` park/skip
3094    /// protocol: the request/response ivars are left intact so the re-admitted
3095    /// thread re-evaluates this same checkpoint on its next turn.
3096    fn hb_checkpoint(
3097        &mut self,
3098        dettid: DetTid,
3099        count: u64,
3100        occurrence_anchors: &[String],
3101    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3102        let (reached, blocked) = {
3103            let hb = self
3104                .happens_before
3105                .as_ref()
3106                .expect("hb checkpoint issued without a happens-before program");
3107            let mut reached = hb.anchors_at_syscall(dettid, count);
3108            reached.extend(hb.occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, occurrence_anchors));
3109            let blocked = reached.iter().any(|name| hb.anchor_blocked(name));
3110            (reached, blocked)
3111        };
3112
3113        if reached.is_empty() {
3114            // No anchor addresses this (thread, count); nothing to gate or fire.
3115            return Ok(());
3116        }
3117
3118        if blocked {
3119            info!(
3120                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} held at happens-before \
3121                 anchor(s) {:?} (syscall count {}) awaiting a BEFORE anchor",
3122                self.turn, dettid, reached, count
3123            );
3124            if self
3125                .vfork_barriers
3126                .values()
3127                .any(|child| *child == Some(dettid))
3128            {
3129                // While a vfork child runs, no other thread can be selected
3130                // (`step3_peek`), so a BEFORE anchor could never fire and the run
3131                // would spin with no report
3132                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3930). Refuse instead.
3133                // Keep an earlier verdict, and its classification, if one is
3134                // already pending.
3135                if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3136                    self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
3137                        "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD: happens-before anchor(s) {:?} would hold \
3138                         dtid {}, a vfork child that has not exec'd yet; while it runs no other \
3139                         thread can, so its gate could never open. Anchor the edge on a point \
3140                         before the vfork or after the child's exec.",
3141                        reached, dettid
3142                    ));
3143                    self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3144                }
3145            }
3146            let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
3147            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3148            hb.parked.insert(dettid);
3149            hb.held_at.insert(dettid, reached.clone());
3150            hb.holds.entry(dettid).or_insert_with(|| HbHold {
3151                since_ns: now_ns,
3152                anchors: reached.clone(),
3153            });
3154            return self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
3155        }
3156
3157        // Grant passage: fire the reached anchors. Only wake parked threads when a
3158        // new anchor actually fired, so an idempotent re-grant causes no churn.
3159        let mut newly_fired = false;
3160        {
3161            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3162            // Passage granted: any hold of this thread is over.
3163            hb.holds.remove(&dettid);
3164            for name in &reached {
3165                if hb.fired.insert(name.clone()) {
3166                    newly_fired = true;
3167                }
3168            }
3169        }
3170        if newly_fired {
3171            debug!(
3172                "[happens-before] dettid {} fired anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}",
3173                dettid, reached, count
3174            );
3175            // Defer the actual re-admission: we are inside `block_for_one_resource`
3176            // with a `tentative_pop` selection live, and pushing to the run queue
3177            // now would trip the queue's transaction assertion. The next
3178            // `step2_drain_prefix` flushes (`step3_peek` as a backstop).
3179            self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().wake_pending = true;
3180        }
3181        Ok(())
3182    }
3183
3184    /// If a happens-before anchor fired since the last check, re-admit every
3185    /// parked thread to the run queue so it re-evaluates its gate on its next
3186    /// turn. Threads still blocked re-park; the request/response ivars are
3187    /// untouched, so no request needs re-filling. Deterministic: parked threads
3188    /// are iterated in `DetTid` order.
3189    ///
3190    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, with the other deferred run-queue
3191    /// admissions and before step2c and step2d look at the queue, and from
3192    /// `step3_peek` *before* the turn's `tentative_pop`. Both are points with no
3193    /// live selection transaction: anchors fire deep inside
3194    /// `block_for_one_resource` while a selection is live, so the actual
3195    /// re-admission must be deferred to one of them.
3196    fn hb_flush_wakes(&mut self) {
3197        match self.happens_before.as_mut() {
3198            Some(hb) if hb.wake_pending => hb.wake_pending = false,
3199            _ => return,
3200        }
3201        let parked: Vec<DetTid> = self
3202            .happens_before
3203            .as_ref()
3204            .map(|hb| hb.parked.iter().copied().collect())
3205            .unwrap_or_default();
3206        for dettid in parked {
3207            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3208            hb.parked.remove(&dettid);
3209            hb.held_at.remove(&dettid);
3210            if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
3211                let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
3212                trace!(
3213                    "[happens-before] re-admitting parked dettid {} at queue position {}",
3214                    dettid, pos
3215                );
3216            }
3217        }
3218    }
3219
3220    /// Refuse the run when a held thread has outlasted a version-2 program's
3221    /// hold budget (`max_hold_ns`), charged in committed virtual time.
3222    ///
3223    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, so at every step2 pass of both turn
3224    /// loops, before selection. It reads only `committed_time` and the
3225    /// scheduler's own hold records, and it ends the run rather than releasing
3226    /// the thread, so it never decides which thread runs. A run with no
3227    /// version-2 program, or no hold, returns at once.
3228    fn hb_check_hold_budget(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3229        let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
3230        let Some(refusal) = self
3231            .happens_before
3232            .as_ref()
3233            .and_then(|hb| hb.hold_budget_refusal(now_ns))
3234        else {
3235            return Ok(());
3236        };
3237        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3238            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
3239            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3240        }
3241        Err(SkipTurn)
3242    }
3243
3244    /// Fill in a resource request, which is exactly what might make the next logical
3245    /// step become unblocked.
3246    pub fn request_put(
3247        &mut self,
3248        req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>,
3249        rs: Resources,
3250        _global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3251    ) {
3252        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3253        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1041): A guest resource-request RPC can race an
3254        // asynchronous signal delivery. `force_unblock_thread` replaces
3255        // `next_turns[tid].req` with an already-full Ivar carrying an
3256        // `InboundSignal` request (see the `Ivar::full` at the bottom of this
3257        // file). If the guest's own resource-request then lands on that same
3258        // turn, the previous unconditional `req.put()` panicked with "Ivar
3259        // multiple put" (observed intermittently on `timeout 5 echo hi` under
3260        // `--strict --verify`, where a 5s SIGALRM races the child's `wait4`).
3261        // Tolerate exactly that case: drop the late guest request and let the
3262        // signal turn win — the interrupted syscall (e.g. `rt_sigsuspend`)
3263        // restarts and re-issues a fresh request on the next turn. Any other
3264        // double-put still panics, preserving the write-once Ivar invariant.
3265        // Mirrors the `try_put` guard in `logically_kill_thread` (PR-845).
3266        if let Some(dropped) = req.try_put(Ok(rs)) {
3267            let tolerated = matches!(
3268                req.try_read(),
3269                Some(Ok(existing))
3270                    if existing
3271                        .resources
3272                        .keys()
3273                        .any(|r| {
3274                            matches!(
3275                                r,
3276                                ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) | ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_)
3277                            )
3278                        })
3279            );
3280            if tolerated {
3281                trace!(
3282                    "[request_put] dropping late guest request {:?}; an async inbound signal already filled the request for this turn (req {})",
3283                    dropped, req
3284                );
3285            } else {
3286                panic!(
3287                    "Ivar multiple put exception in request_put! Attempted to write {:?} to {}; existing content is not an inbound-signal request.",
3288                    dropped, req
3289                );
3290            }
3291        }
3292    }

3294    /// Poll the resource request and *if* it is not currently observed to be full, return
3295    /// the IVar that *will* contain it in the future.
3296    fn check_request(&self, det_tid: &DetTid) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
3297        let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(det_tid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
3298            panic!(
3299                "[check_request] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
3300                det_tid
3301            )
3302        });
3303        if nextturn.req.try_read().is_none() {
3304            Some(nextturn.req.clone())
3305        } else {
3306            None
3307        }
3308    }
3309
3310    /// Returns None if all are parked, otherwise the unfilled request of the next we're waiting on.
3311    fn are_all_quiesced(&self) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
3312        // Skip raw TIDs whose old run-queue incarnation is pending removal.
3313        // `Retire` targets have no `next_turns` entry, while
3314        // `ReplaceThenAdmit` targets have a fresh registration that must not be
3315        // waited on until the drain removes the old physical slot and admits
3316        // that replacement.
3317        self.run_queue
3318            .tids()
3319            .filter(|dt| !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(dt))
3320            .find_map(|dt| self.check_request(dt))
3321    }

3323    /// Try to pop the next event from the sorted list of stacktrace_events, if it matches the given
3324    /// index.  This is idempotent, because subsequent attempts will just fizzle.
3325    fn try_pop_stacktrace_event(
3326        &mut self,
3327        current_ix: u64,
3328        observed: &SchedEvent,
3329    ) -> MaybePrintStack {
3330        let mut result = None;
3331        if let Some(iter) = &mut self.stacktrace_events
3332            && let Some((next_ix, event, m_path)) = iter.peek()
3333        {
3334            let go = if let Some(ev) = event {
3335                (*next_ix == current_ix && events_consistent(observed, ev))
3336                    || events_match(observed, ev)
3337            } else {
3338                *next_ix == current_ix
3339            };
3340            if go {
3341                info!(
3342                    "Now output stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
3343                    current_ix, observed,
3344                );
3345                if m_path.is_none() {
3346                    crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
3347                        "\nPrinting stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
3348                        current_ix,
3349                        observed,
3350                    );
3351                }
3352                result = Some(m_path.clone());
3353                let _ = iter.next();
3354            }
3355        }
3356        result
3357    }
3358
3359    /// Verify that the event we're replaying matches what just happened.  Set up the next
3360    /// (replayed) event to run.  Return true if the current thread will keep running and false if
3361    /// it needs to be descheduled.
3362    ///
3363    /// PreReq: we're running under --replay-schedule-from
3364    pub fn consume_schedevent(&mut self, observed: &SchedEvent) -> ConsumeResult {
3365        debug_assert!(self.replayer.is_some());
3366        let mytid = observed.dettid;
3367
3368        if let Some((ix, action)) = self.replayer.as_mut().map(|r| {
3369            let current_ix = r.traced_event_count;
3370            (current_ix, r.observe_event(observed))
3371        }) {
3372            let print_stack = self.try_pop_stacktrace_event(ix, observed);
3373            debug!("Next ReplayAction = {:?}", action);
3374
3375            match action {
3376                replayer::ReplayAction::Continue(timeslice_remaining) => {
3377                    return ConsumeResult {
3378                        keep_running: true,
3379                        print_stack,
3380                        event_ix: ix,
3381                        timeslice_remaining,
3382                    };
3383                }
3384                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::FatalDesync) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
3385                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::ReplayExausted) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
3386                replayer::ReplayAction::ContextSwitch(is_now, new_tid, timeslice_remaining) => {
3387                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(mytid, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
3388                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(new_tid, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
3389                    if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(new_tid) {
3390                        // If it is not yet in next_turns, that is because it was JUST spawned and
3391                        // hasn't showed up yet, but it will by the next scheduler turn.
3392                        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&new_tid) {
3393                            tracing::warn!(
3394                                "Attempted to context switch to tid {}, but it is not runnable atm. This could be legitimate if it is awoken by another thread exiting (futex wake).",
3395                                new_tid
3396                            );
3397                            // TODO(T138906107): make this a fatal error when RESYNC capability is robust enough.
3398                            // immediate_fatal_exit();
3399                        }
3400                    }
3401                    self.timeslices.insert(new_tid, timeslice_remaining);
3402                    return ConsumeResult {
3403                        keep_running: !is_now,
3404                        print_stack,
3405                        event_ix: ix,
3406                        timeslice_remaining,
3407                    };
3408                }
3409            };
3410        }
3411
3412        ConsumeResult {
3413            keep_running: true,
3414            print_stack: None,
3415            event_ix: 0,
3416            timeslice_remaining: None,
3417        }
3418    }

3420    /// Updates the address Linux clears and wakes when this thread exits.
3421    ///
3422    /// `set_tid_address(2)` replaces the value supplied by clone. A zero
3423    /// address disables the exit-time store and wake.
3424    pub fn set_child_tid_address(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, address: usize) -> bool {
3425        let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
3426            return false;
3427        };
3428        next_turn.child_tid_addr = address;
3429        true
3430    }

3432    /// Freeze the live sibling set at the caller's deterministic exec boundary.
3433    /// A failed exec must not kill these threads; only successful exec, or an
3434    /// actual exit receipt for a sibling, authorizes its eventual retirement.
3435    pub(crate) fn prepare_exec_teardown(
3436        &mut self,
3437        caller: DetTid,
3438        process: DetPid,
3439        mm: MmId,
3440    ) -> bool {
3441        if self.registered_process(caller) != Some(process)
3442            || !self.next_turns.contains_key(&caller)
3443            || !self.rpc_incarnation_matches(caller, mm)
3444            || self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&process)
3445        {
3446            return false;
3447        }
3448        let siblings = self
3449            .thread_tree
3450            .my_thread_group(&process)
3451            .into_iter()
3452            .filter(|tid| *tid != caller && self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
3453            .collect();
3454        self.exec_teardowns.insert(
3455            process,
3456            ExecTeardown {
3457                caller,
3458                mm,
3459                siblings,
3460                observed: BTreeSet::new(),
3461            },
3462        );
3463        true
3464    }
3465
3466    /// Account a physical exit without letting host callback order mutate the
3467    /// scheduler. The hook must return promptly: ptrace awaits the displaced
3468    /// leader's hook before invoking the survivor's successful exec callback.
3469    pub(crate) fn defer_exec_sibling_retirement(
3470        &mut self,
3471        tid: DetTid,
3472        process: DetPid,
3473        mm: MmId,
3474    ) -> bool {
3475        let Some(teardown) = self.exec_teardowns.get_mut(&process) else {
3476            return false;
3477        };
3478        if teardown.mm != mm || !teardown.siblings.contains(&tid) {
3479            return false;
3480        }
3481        teardown.observed.insert(tid);
3482        true
3483    }
3484
3485    /// The exact old-image receipt replaces absence of a scheduler registration
3486    /// as proof that a transferred exec's displaced leader was consumed.
3487    pub(crate) fn exec_sibling_retirement_observed(
3488        &self,
3489        tid: DetTid,
3490        process: DetPid,
3491        mm: MmId,
3492    ) -> bool {
3493        self.exec_teardowns
3494            .get(&process)
3495            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.mm == mm && teardown.observed.contains(&tid))
3496    }
3497
3498    /// Apply retirement in sorted order at the successful exec edge, or retire
3499    /// just physically consumed owners when an exec attempt fails. The caller
3500    /// remains registered with its empty request, so no turn can overtake the
3501    /// complete replacement registration. The ordinary removal path retains
3502    /// its INFO event, futex wakes and tentative-safe run-queue buffering.
3503    pub(crate) fn finish_exec_teardown(
3504        &mut self,
3505        caller: DetTid,
3506        process: DetPid,
3507        mm: MmId,
3508        succeeded: bool,
3509    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
3510        if !self
3511            .exec_teardowns
3512            .get(&process)
3513            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.caller == caller && teardown.mm == mm)
3514        {
3515            return Vec::new();
3516        }
3517        let teardown = self.exec_teardowns.remove(&process).unwrap();
3518        let retired: Vec<_> = if succeeded {
3519            teardown.siblings
3520        } else {
3521            teardown.observed
3522        }
3523        .into_iter()
3524        .collect();
3525        for tid in &retired {
3526            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &process, mm);
3527            self.timeslices.remove(tid);
3528        }
3529        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
3530        retired
3531    }
3532
3533    /// Remove a thread from the deterministic scheduler.  In order to call this, the precondition
3534    /// is that this thread will execute no further (visible) instructions.
3535    ///
3536    /// This is called while the guest is running, not in the middle of a scheduler turn.
3537    ///
3538    /// This is IDEMPOTENT, and it may indeed be called twice, both to proactively remove a thread,
3539    /// and then reactively in response to an exit hook.
3540    pub fn logically_kill_thread(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid, detpid: &DetPid, mm: MmId) {
3541        if self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation {
3542            self.logically_killed_threads.insert(*dtid);
3543        }
3544        // Remove from the runnable queue at the next deterministic drain. This
3545        // is safe even if an asynchronous exec reconnect races a live
3546        // tentative_pop: the handler never reaches the run queue's mutation
3547        // guard and cannot poison the scheduler mutex.
3548        self.deschedule_or_defer(*dtid);
3549        // Remove from all non-runnable pools:
3550        self.remove_blocking_entries(dtid);
3551        self.retire_sigalrm_thread(*dtid, *detpid);
3552        self.remove_physical_thread(dtid, mm);
3553        // A killed vfork parent must not leave its barrier behind: step2a
3554        // drops a barrier only when it can read the parent's pending request,
3555        // which `next_turns.remove` below discards, and while any barrier
3556        // exists `step3_peek` selects only a barrier's child, so a barrier
3557        // left behind stops the schedule once that child is gone
3558        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
3559        self.retire_vfork_parent(*dtid);
3560        // A killed vfork child is its own barrier's release edge.
3561        self.release_vfork_child(*dtid);
3562        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(dtid);
3563        self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(dtid);
3564        if dtid.as_raw() == detpid.as_raw() {
3565            self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(detpid);
3566        }
3567        self.real_timers.retire_task(*detpid, *dtid);
3568        self.retire_parked_requests(*dtid);
3569
3570        let _ = self.priorities.remove(dtid);
3571        match self.next_turns.remove(dtid) {
3572            None => {
3573                trace!(
3574                    "logically_kill_thread: thread already removed from scheduler: {}",
3575                    &dtid
3576                );
3577            }
3578            Some(nextturn) => {
3579                info!(
3580                    "logically_kill: Scheduler removing all knowledge of [det]tid {} in pid {}..",
3581                    dtid, detpid
3582                );
3583                // Put in a dummy request to unblock the scheduler that might be
3584                // waiting for the thread to park.
3585                //
3586                // WARNING: this try_put should potentially turn back into a put(), if we can narrow
3587                // down the exit scenarios and ensure that they happen when the guest is running and
3588                // has NOT filled its request to the scheduler yet.
3589                let request_was_pending = nextturn.req.try_put(Err(ThreadExited)).is_some();
3590                if request_was_pending
3591                    && self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
3592                    && !self.backend_failed()
3593                {
3594                    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3595                    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review killed-thread RPC cancellation.
3596                    nextturn.resp.try_put(SchedResponse::Signaled(None));
3597                }
3598                if nextturn.child_tid_addr != 0 {
3599                    self.wake_futex_child_cleartid(
3600                        FutexID::private(mm, nextturn.child_tid_addr),
3601                        *dtid,
3602                    );
3603                }
3604            }
3605        }
3606
3607        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3608        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
3609        let live_process_thread = self
3610            .thread_tree
3611            .my_thread_group(detpid)
3612            .into_iter()
3613            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
3614        // A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process
3615        // in the thread tree, although the backend reports its creator's pid
3616        // (`ResourceID::Exit` below makes the same distinction). Its exit
3617        // still decides its orphans, when its last thread leaves.
3618        if let Some(registered) = self.registered_process(*dtid)
3619            && registered != *detpid
3620            && !self
3621                .thread_tree
3622                .my_thread_group(&registered)
3623                .into_iter()
3624                .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid))
3625        {
3626            self.reparent_orphans(registered);
3627        }
3628        if !live_process_thread {
3629            let _ = self.begin_physical_process_exit(*detpid);
3630            self.reparent_orphans(*detpid);
3631            self.logically_exited_processes.insert(*detpid);
3632            if let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(detpid) {
3633                self.wake_child_waiters(parent, *detpid);
3634            }
3635            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_process_timers(*detpid);
3636            self.real_timers.retire_process(*detpid);
3637        }
3638    }
