3640    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-4000): orphan re-parenting to a child subreaper.
3641    /// Re-parent the children of `exited`, whose last thread just left the run
3642    /// set, as Linux's `forget_original_parent` does in `exit_notify`.
3643    ///
3644    /// The new parent is the nearest process on `exited`'s parent chain that
3645    /// is a child subreaper and still has a live thread (`find_new_reaper`).
3646    /// A child that has already exited becomes waitable by its new parent
3647    /// here. Without such a subreaper the child goes to the container's init,
3648    /// which no guest can wait for; its record is left as it was before
3649    /// subreapers were modeled, naming the dead parent, so a program that
3650    /// never sets the flag sees no change.
3651    ///
3652    /// This runs in the same scheduler critical section that makes `exited`
3653    /// itself waitable, so it is exactly as deterministic as that moment and
3654    /// never opens a window of its own. For an `exit` or `exit_group` with
3655    /// sequentialized threads (strict mode), that moment follows the
3656    /// scheduler-ordered `ResourceID::Exit` grant and precedes the next
3657    /// committed turn: the exiting thread goes back into the run queue with an
3658    /// empty request, and the quiesce wait (`are_all_quiesced`) selects no
3659    /// turn until its deregistration fills it. For a process killed by a
3660    /// signal it is the host-timed
3661    /// deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994), and the
3662    /// re-parent moves with it. On ptrace the kernel has already re-parented by
3663    /// then: the deregistration carries the final exit status, which the tracer
3664    /// sees only after `exit_notify`.
3665    ///
3666    /// The decision is made once per exit. `logically_kill_thread` can run
3667    /// again for the same dead process, from a thread's late exit hook at a
3668    /// moment the host chooses; by then every child has either moved to its
3669    /// subreaper or is an init orphan, and neither is collected again. A
3670    /// process that died without an Exit grant records a determinism loss
3671    /// when a subreaper adopts its orphans.
3672    ///
3673    /// Children are visited in pid order, so the waiters they wake join the
3674    /// run queue in an order that does not depend on hashing.
3675    fn reparent_orphans(&mut self, exited: DetPid) {
3676        let orphans = self.thread_tree.undecided_orphans_of(exited);
3677        if orphans.is_empty() {
3678            return;
3679        }
3680        let reaper = self.find_child_reaper(exited);
3681        if let Some((reaper, _)) = reaper
3682            && !self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&exited)
3683        {
3684            // Without an Exit grant (SIGKILL, another fatal signal, a fault)
3685            // the parent's exit is recorded at its host-timed deregistration,
3686            // and so is this adoption
3687            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). Say so rather
3688            // than let verification compare a schedule that host timing chose.
3689            self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
3690                "subreaper {reaper} adopted the orphans of process {exited}, which died without an Exit grant, at its host-timed deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994)"
3691            ));
3692        }
3693        for child in orphans {
3694            let Some((reaper, owner)) = reaper else {
3695                debug!(
3696                    "[scheduler] orphan {} of exited process {} goes to the container init",
3697                    child, exited
3698                );
3699                self.thread_tree.orphan_to_init(child);
3700                continue;
3701            };
3702            self.thread_tree.reparent_child(child, reaper, owner);
3703            info!(
3704                "[scheduler] re-parenting orphan {} of exited process {} to subreaper {}",
3705                child, exited, reaper
3706            );
3707            if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
3708                self.wake_child_waiters(reaper, child);
3709            }
3710        }
3711    }
3712
3713    /// Record a determinism loss for the run (`detlog::write_loss_notice`).
3714    /// Tests read the reasons this scheduler recorded, rather than the
3715    /// process-wide latch, which keeps whichever reason any test wrote first.
3716    fn note_determinism_loss(&mut self, reason: String) {
3717        #[cfg(test)]
3718        self.determinism_losses.push(reason.clone());
3719        crate::detlog::write_loss_notice(&reason);
3720    }
3721
3722    /// The process and thread that inherit `exited`'s orphans
3723    /// (`reparent_orphans`): the nearest live child subreaper among its
3724    /// ancestors, and that process's first live thread, its leader if the
3725    /// leader is live (Linux's `find_alive_thread`). The search stops at a
3726    /// process that already went to the container's init: Linux's parent
3727    /// chain from there leads to init, whatever the stale record names. It
3728    /// also stops at a PID namespace boundary, as Linux's `find_new_reaper`
3729    /// does: an ancestor in an outer namespace never adopts. (Linux then gives
3730    /// the orphan to its own namespace's init; that adoption is not modeled,
3731    /// so such an orphan is left as before subreapers were.)
3732    fn find_child_reaper(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Option<(DetPid, DetTid)> {
3733        if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(exited) {
3734            return None;
3735        }
3736        let depth = self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(exited);
3737        let mut ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&exited);
3738        while let Some(candidate) = ancestor {
3739            if self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(candidate) != depth {
3740                return None;
3741            }
3742            if self.thread_tree.is_child_subreaper(candidate) {
3743                let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
3744                    .thread_tree
3745                    .my_thread_group(&candidate)
3746                    .into_iter()
3747                    .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
3748                    .collect();
3749                live.sort_by_key(|tid| (*tid != candidate, *tid));
3750                if let Some(owner) = live.first() {
3751                    return Some((candidate, *owner));
3752                }
3753            }
3754            if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(candidate) {
3755                return None;
3756            }
3757            ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&candidate);
3758        }
3759        None
3760    }

3762    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3763    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1173): Review SaBRe exec incarnation reconciliation.
3764    /// Apply Linux's successful-exec rule when a backend reloads its tool.
3765    ///
3766    /// Every sibling disappears. If a non-leader called exec, Linux also changes
3767    /// that surviving task's TID to the process leader's TID. In that case the old
3768    /// caller registration is retired and a fresh leader registration is installed
3769    /// before it is removed, so process-exit barriers cannot observe a transiently
3770    /// empty thread group.
3771    pub fn reconnect_after_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
3772        self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, None)
3773    }
3774
3775    /// Reconnect a non-leader exec whose backend preserved the caller's Tool
3776    /// state and PMU. The replay cursor, rather than the destroyed leader's
3777    /// pending duration, determines the replacement's next grant. The grant
3778    /// returns a relative duration; reconnect itself advances neither time nor
3779    /// the replay cursor and does not issue a scheduler turn.
3780    pub(crate) fn reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
3781        assert_ne!(reconnect.caller, reconnect.new_leader);
3782        let replay_resume = self.replayer.as_ref().and_then(Replayer::next_resume);
3783        let former = reconnect.caller;
3784        let leader = reconnect.new_leader;
3785        let consumed_syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.get(&leader).copied().unwrap_or(0);
3786        let retired = self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, replay_resume);
3787        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.insert(former);
3788        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
3789            .insert(leader, consumed_syscalls);
3790        retired
3791    }
3792
3793    fn reconnect_exec(
3794        &mut self,
3795        reconnect: ExecReconnect,
3796        replay_resume: Option<(DetTid, Option<LogicalTime>)>,
3797    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
3798        let ExecReconnect {
3799            caller,
3800            new_leader,
3801            detpid,
3802            pre_exec_mm,
3803            post_exec_mm,
3804            child_tid_addr,
3805            reconnect_priority,
3806        } = reconnect;
3807        let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
3808        assert!(group.contains(&caller));
3809        assert!(group.contains(&new_leader));
3810        self.exec_incarnations.insert(new_leader, post_exec_mm);
3811        // Reloading backends enter thread-start before handle_post_exec. Cancel
3812        // old POSIX deadlines before admitting the replacement's first turn.
3813        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_posix_timers(detpid);
3814
3815        let siblings = if self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&detpid) {
3816            let teardown = &self.exec_teardowns[&detpid];
3817            assert_eq!((teardown.caller, teardown.mm), (caller, pre_exec_mm));
3818            self.finish_exec_teardown(caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm, true)
3819        } else {
3820            // Reloading backends and older callers may already have retired
3821            // their siblings; retain their existing idempotent reconciliation.
3822            let mut siblings: Vec<_> = group.into_iter().filter(|tid| *tid != caller).collect();
3823            siblings.sort();
3824            for sibling in &siblings {
3825                self.logically_kill_thread(sibling, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
3826                self.timeslices.remove(sibling);
3827            }
3828            siblings
3829        };
3830
3831        if caller == new_leader {
3832            self.next_turns
3833                .get_mut(&caller)
3834                .expect("exec caller must retain a scheduler registration")
3835                .child_tid_addr = child_tid_addr;
3836
3837            self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&siblings);
3838            return siblings;
3839        }
3840
3841        if let Some(refusal) = self
3842            .happens_before
3843            .as_ref()
3844            .and_then(|hb| hb.relative_identity_refusal(caller, new_leader))
3845            && self.terminal_deadlock.is_none()
3846        {
3847            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
3848            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3849        }
3850
3851        self.thread_tree
3852            .transfer_exec_wait_owner(detpid, caller, new_leader);
3853
3854        let survivor_priority = match replay_resume {
3855            Some((next_tid, _)) if next_tid == new_leader => REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY,
3856            Some(_) => REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY,
3857            None => self
3858                .priorities
3859                .get(&caller)
3860                .copied()
3861                .or(reconnect_priority)
3862                .expect("exec caller must have a scheduler priority"),
3863        };
3864        let mut retired = siblings;
3865
3866        // The leader identity was occupied by a thread the kernel destroyed as
3867        // part of this exec. This is the one intentional exception to permanent
3868        // raw-TID tombstones: the pending exec record proves why Linux reused it.
3869        self.logically_killed_threads.remove(&new_leader);
3870        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&new_leader);
3871        self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
3872        assert!(
3873            self.next_turns
3874                .insert(
3875                    new_leader,
3876                    ThreadNextTurn {
3877                        dettid: new_leader,
3878                        child_tid_addr,
3879                        req: Ivar::new(),
3880                        resp: Ivar::new(),
3881                        protocol: Default::default(),
3882                    },
3883                )
3884                .is_none(),
3885            "retired exec leader still had a scheduler registration"
3886        );
3887        self.priorities.insert(new_leader, survivor_priority);
3888        if let Some((next_tid, timeslice)) = replay_resume
3889            && next_tid == new_leader
3890        {
3891            // Rebuild only the current cursor's decision. The removed entry
3892            // could have belonged to the displaced leader, while a prehook's
3893            // ContextSwitch(false, new_leader, ..) already refers to the
3894            // replacement. Neither priority nor the old entry distinguishes
3895            // those cases, and the cursor may have advanced in the meantime.
3896            self.timeslices.insert(new_leader, timeslice);
3897        }
3898        if let Some(writer) = &mut self.preemption_writer {
3899            writer.set_current(new_leader, survivor_priority);
3900        }
3901        // Post-exec reconnection can arrive asynchronously on backends whose
3902        // exec-child self-bootstraps outside a scheduler turn (DBT), so route
3903        // the new leader's admission (a run-queue *push*) through the
3904        // tentative-safe buffer rather than pushing directly.
3905        //
3906        // The exec caller's fresh next-turn request is the causal anchor. Step5
3907        // installed that empty Ivar before the caller began executing exec, so
3908        // the daemon cannot pass step1 while the successful exec is in flight.
3909        // This handler records the complete old-leader removal/replacement
3910        // admission pair before `logically_kill_thread(caller)` resolves that
3911        // request. The scheduler mutex then prevents step2 from observing only
3912        // half of the handoff. Host delay can move the handler relative to the
3913        // daemon's wait, but cannot change first-drain membership.
3914        //
3915        // The *removals* in this handler (`logically_kill_thread` ->
3916        // `run_queue.remove_tid`, for the exec caller and its siblings, above
3917        // and below) are likewise tentative-safe: `logically_kill_thread` now
3918        // routes the run-queue removal through `deschedule_or_defer`, which
3919        // buffers it to the same deterministic `step2` drain. The old leader's
3920        // removal is explicitly classified as `ReplaceThenAdmit`, so the drain
3921        // removes its physical queue slot without cancelling the new
3922        // incarnation. `are_all_quiesced` filters every pending removal key;
3923        // ordinary targets are logically dead, while the replacement key is not
3924        // runnable until that old slot has been removed and its admission
3925        // applied. No handler mutates the queue inside a tentative window.
3926        self.replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(new_leader, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
3927        self.started_up.try_put(());
3928
3929        self.logically_kill_thread(&caller, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
3930        self.timeslices.remove(&caller);
3931        retired.push(caller);
3932        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
3933        retired
3934    }
3935
3936    /// Install the barrier for a vfork parent whose `BlockingVfork` was just
3937    /// granted. State left by an earlier thread with the same TID is stale:
3938    /// that thread is gone, so a barrier it kept for its child, and a
3939    /// tombstone its child never settled, are dropped here, inside this
3940    /// committed turn.
3941    fn begin_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
3942        // The only barrier `parent` can still hold is one kept for a dead
3943        // thread with the same TID: a live parent's own barrier ends at its
3944        // continuation (step2a) before it can be granted another vfork.
3945        assert!(
3946            !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent)
3947                || self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent),
3948            "dettid {parent} began a vfork while its own live barrier stands"
3949        );
3950        self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
3951        self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent);
3952        self.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
3953    }
3954
3955    /// Remove `parent`'s barrier and every record about it.
3956    fn drop_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
3957        self.vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
3958        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
3959        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
3960        self.released_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
3961    }
3962
3963    /// `parent` is being logically killed. With no child registered yet, its
3964    /// barrier goes and a tombstone lets the child register as an orphan.
3965    /// With a registered child the barrier goes now if the child already
3966    /// reached a release edge or is gone, because then the child cannot be
3967    /// selected in its vfork role any more; otherwise it stays, marked
3968    /// parent-dead, until the child's next release edge. The outcome does not
3969    /// depend on whether this retirement arrives before or after that edge.
3970    fn retire_vfork_parent(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
3971        match self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent).copied() {
3972            None => {}
3973            Some(None) => {
3974                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
3975                self.dead_vfork_parents.insert(parent);
3976            }
3977            Some(Some(child))
3978                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
3979                    && !self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) =>
3980            {
3981                self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
3982            }
3983            Some(Some(_)) => self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent),
3984        }
3985    }
3986
3987    /// `child` reached a release edge: its `Exit` grant, its successful exec
3988    /// (`record_successful_exec`), or its logical kill. A barrier whose parent
3989    /// has died goes now. Otherwise the barrier is marked released, and step2a
3990    /// waits, committing nothing, until the parent's continuation or
3991    /// retirement, then drops it.
3992    pub(crate) fn release_vfork_child(&mut self, child: DetTid) {
3993        let parents: Vec<DetTid> = self
3994            .vfork_barriers
3995            .iter()
3996            .filter(|(_, registered)| **registered == Some(child))
3997            .map(|(parent, _)| *parent)
3998            .collect();
3999        for parent in parents {
4000            if self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) {
4001                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
4002            } else {
4003                self.released_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
4004            }
4005        }
4006    }
4007
4008    fn remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&mut self, retired: &[DetTid]) {
4009        self.vfork_barriers.retain(|parent, child| {
4010            !retired.contains(parent) && !child.is_some_and(|tid| retired.contains(&tid))
4011        });
4012        self.vfork_registration_origins
4013            .retain(|parent, _| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4014        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers
4015            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4016        self.released_vfork_barriers
4017            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4018    }

4068    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1023): Review fail-closed SaBRe thread tombstones.
4069    pub(crate) fn thread_is_logically_killed(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4070        self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
4071            && self.logically_killed_threads.contains(&dettid)
4072    }
4073
4074    /// Whether `dettid` is running in a turn the scheduler granted it, now:
4075    /// - it is the thread last granted a turn (`parked.running`, set only by
4076    ///   `unblock_guest`), and neither a backend failure nor a logical kill
4077    ///   has ended its run;
4078    /// - it has not filed its next request yet. `unblock_guest` installs a
4079    ///   fresh, empty request slot at the grant, and the thread's next
4080    ///   request fills it, which surrenders the turn;
4081    /// - the grant did not release it into the background. A thread running a
4082    ///   blocking call outside the runnable set (`external_io_blockers`, which
4083    ///   includes a copying vfork's parent, or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or
4084    ///   one woken there by a signal (`signaled_background`), does not hold
4085    ///   the turn even before the next grant moves `parked.running` away.
4086    pub(crate) fn holds_serial_grant(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4087        !self.backend_failed()
4088            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4089            && self.parked.running == Some(dettid)
4090            && self
4091                .next_turns
4092                .get(&dettid)
4093                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req.try_read().is_none())
4094            && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
4095            && !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
4096            && !self.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&dettid)
4097    }

4100        !self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&dettid)
4101            && self
4102                .exec_incarnations
4103                .get(&dettid)
4104                .is_none_or(|expected| *expected == mm)
4105    }

4107    /// A newborn may reach StartNewThread before its parent registers it. It
4108    /// must wait without publishing a clock until registration consumes this
4109    /// marker; ordinary messages cannot use startup as authority to clear it.
4110    pub(crate) fn transferred_exec_tid_requires_registration(&self, tid: DetTid) -> bool {
4111        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid)
4112    }
4113
4114    /// Called only by authenticated fresh child registration. A raw Linux TID
4115    /// can be reused after exec retired its former owner; an ordinary RPC
4116    /// cannot reopen it. Bind the new address space in the same transaction so
4117    /// delayed messages from a different old image remain rejected.
4118    pub(crate) fn register_reused_transferred_exec_tid(&mut self, tid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
4119        if !self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid) {
4120            return;
4121        }
4122        assert!(
4123            !self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid),
4124            "a reused exec caller must not have a live registration"
4125        );
4126        self.exec_incarnations.insert(tid, mm);
4127        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&tid);
4128        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.remove(&tid);
4129        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.remove(&tid);
4130    }

4140    /// Linearize failure with ordinary grants. Close the transaction here,
4141    /// before any awakened Tool can run consuming clear-TID/futex cleanup.
4142    /// The daemon observes the terminal state and must not undo it a second
4143    /// time. The caller sends the notification after releasing this mutex.
4144    pub(crate) fn report_backend_failure(
4145        &mut self,
4146        event: reverie::BackendFailure,
4147    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
4148        self.report_backend_failure_location(BackendFailureLocation {
4149            pid: event.pid,
4150            tid: Some(event.tid),
4151            phase: event.phase,
4152        })
4153    }
4154
4155    fn report_backend_failure_location(
4156        &mut self,
4157        event: BackendFailureLocation,
4158    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
4159        if self.backend_failed() {
4160            return None;
4161        }
4162        if self.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress() {
4163            self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
4164        }
4165        tracing::error!(
4166            "backend failure for process {}, task {:?}, phase {}",
4167            event.pid,
4168            event.tid,
4169            event.phase
4170        );
4171        self.backend_failure = Some(event);
4172        self.backend_failure_sender.take()
4173    }

4175    /// Construction does not imply scheduler registration: a backend may
4176    /// consume a child before its parent has sent CreateChildThread.
4177    pub(crate) fn thread_was_registered(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4178        self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.contains_key(&dettid)
4179    }

4181    /// Mark a physical exit cleanup as accounted. A transferred leader must
4182    /// consume each incarnation once even on a non-cancelling backend; other
4183    /// non-cancelling identities preserve their existing behavior.
4184    pub(crate) fn note_deregistration_accounted(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4185        // Remember an owner accounted before a later peer failure as well.
4186        // Ordinary non-cancelling behavior still accepts its prior callbacks.
4187        let first = self.deregistration_accounted.insert(dettid);
4188        (!self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
4189            && !self.backend_failed()
4190            && !self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.contains_key(&dettid))
4191            || first
4192    }

4194    /// Install a barrier between SaBRe's logical process-leader exit hook and the final ptrace
4195    /// wait status. Other backends retain their existing lifecycle behavior.
4196    pub(crate) fn begin_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4197        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
4198            && self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
4199        {
4200            // Monotone lifetime: an exit the backend already reported complete
4201            // (before its grant, or before a late deregistration) never
4202            // becomes pending again.
4203            return false;
4204        }
4205        if self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits
4206            || self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
4207        {
4208            self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
4209            let inserted = self.pending_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
4210            if inserted {
4211                trace!(
4212                    "[detcore, dpid {}] waiting for final physical process exit",
4213                    detpid
4214                );
4215            }
4216            inserted
4217        } else {
4218            false
4219        }
4220    }
4221
4222    /// Release the exact process barrier when the ptrace supervisor receives its final `Exited`
4223    /// or `Signaled` wait status. At that lifecycle point the process is physically waitable.
4224    /// The backend reports that the kernel has published `detpid`'s exit to
4225    /// its parent (`BackendCapabilities::reports_child_exit_publication`).
4226    /// Releases the hold the exit grant placed for a None or Discard
4227    /// notification; any other process is ignored. Returns whether a hold was
4228    /// released.
4229    pub(crate) fn complete_child_exit_publication(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4230        let released = self.child_exit_publications_pending.remove(&detpid);
4231        if !released {
4232            // No hold yet: the process was consumed before its Exit request
4233            // was granted (or has none). Remember it, so a stale grant does
4234            // not install a hold this report can no longer release.
4235            self.child_exit_publications_completed.insert(detpid);
4236        }
4237        released
4238    }
4239
4240    /// A successful exec by `process`, for the exit-signal rules it applies
4241    /// (`ThreadTree::record_successful_exec`).
4242    pub(crate) fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
4243        self.thread_tree.record_successful_exec(process);
4244        // The exec is a vfork child's release edge, while the exec caller
4245        // still owns its turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
4246        // A vfork child is a single-threaded process, so the caller is
4247        // `process`; an exec that retires a vfork child as a sibling or a
4248        // non-leader caller goes through `remove_exec_vfork_barriers`.
4249        self.release_vfork_child(process);
4250    }
4251
4252    /// Record (`Some`) or clear (`None`) the guest's own signal mask while
4253    /// Detcore holds `dettid` under a private blocking mask. Returns false for
4254    /// a thread the scheduler no longer knows.
4255    pub(crate) fn set_saved_guest_sigmask(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mask: Option<u64>) -> bool {
4256        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) {
4257            return false;
4258        }
4259        match mask {
4260            Some(mask) => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.insert(dettid, mask),
4261            None => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(&dettid),
4262        };
4263        true
4264    }
4265
4266    /// Classify `child`'s exit notification to `parent` at its exit grant, by
4267    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` rules (design: dev-hermit
4268    /// ignored/parity-green-sigchld/design-r7.md, design-r8.md).
4269    ///
4270    /// Only an effective SIGCHLD is classified: the child's clone exit signal
4271    /// must be SIGCHLD (a child created with another signal that later execs is
4272    /// left Undecided, conservatively). The receiving task is the creating
4273    /// thread Linux notifies (`wait_owner`); it must still belong to `parent`
4274    /// and be parked at the scheduler on an internal polling probe or a child
4275    /// wait, outside rt_sigsuspend and the temporary-mask syscalls (ppoll,
4276    /// pselect6, epoll_pwait), so its mask is stable and the guest's own. The parent's SIGCHLD disposition comes from
4277    /// /proc (ptrace guests are host processes whose dispositions Detcore
4278    /// passes through unchanged); the mask from the saved guest mask when
4279    /// Detcore holds a private one, else /proc. Anything unreadable is
4280    /// Undecided.
4281    pub(crate) fn classify_child_exit_notification(
4282        &self,
4283        child: DetPid,
4284        parent: DetPid,
4285    ) -> ChildExitNotification {
4286        let Some(wait) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
4287            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4288        };
4289        if self.thread_tree.notification_signal(child) != Some(libc::SIGCHLD) {
4290            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4291        }
4292        let receiving = wait.wait_owner;
4293        if self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&receiving) != Some(&parent) {
4294            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4295        }
4296        // Only the states the design covers (design-r8.md section 2): an
4297        // internal polling probe or a child wait, outside the temporary-mask
4298        // syscalls. Every other request (rt_sigsuspend, a signal in flight,
4299        // futexes, sleeps, external operations) and an unparked task stay
4300        // Undecided, with the synthetic SIGCHLD path as before.
4301        let covered = !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&receiving)
4302            && self
4303                .next_turns
4304                .get(&receiving)
4305                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
4306                .and_then(Result::ok)
4307                .is_some_and(|request| {
4308                    !request.resources.is_empty()
4309                        && request.resources.keys().all(|resource| {
4310                            matches!(
4311                                resource,
4312                                ResourceID::InternalIOPolling | ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }
4313                            )
4314                        })
4315                        && !matches!(request.fyi.as_str(), "ppoll" | "pselect6" | "epoll_pwait")
4316                });
4317        if !covered {
4318            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4319        }
4320        let Some(ignored) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigIgn") else {
4321            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4322        };
4323        let Some(caught) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigCgt") else {
4324            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
4325        };
4326        let blocked = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&receiving) {
4327            Some(mask) => *mask,
4328            None => match self.signal_mask_field(parent, Some(receiving), "SigBlk") {
4329                Some(mask) => mask,
4330                None => return ChildExitNotification::Undecided,
4331            },
4332        };
4333        let bit = 1_u64 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
4334        classify_sigchld_notification(ignored & bit != 0, caught & bit != 0, blocked & bit != 0)
4335    }
4336
4337    /// A /proc signal-mask field of a guest process or thread (the test-only
4338    /// table under `cfg(test)`).
4339    fn signal_mask_field(
4340        &self,
4341        pid: DetPid,
4342        tid: Option<DetTid>,
4343        field: &'static str,
4344    ) -> Option<u64> {
4345        #[cfg(test)]
4346        {
4347            self.test_signal_masks.get(&(pid, tid, field)).copied()
4348        }
4349        #[cfg(not(test))]
4350        {
4351            proc_status_signal_mask(pid, tid, field)
4352        }
4353    }

4355    pub(crate) fn complete_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4356        let removed = self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
4357        if removed {
4358            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
4359            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(detpid);
4360        } else if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
4361            // A completion that arrives before any grant (or after a death
4362            // without one) is kept, so a later begin is a no-op.
4363            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
4364        }
4365        removed
4366    }
4367
4368    /// The processes held between their exit grant and their physical exit,
4369    /// when exits complete asynchronously; otherwise none.
4370    pub(crate) fn pending_async_process_exits(&self) -> Vec<DetPid> {
4371        if !self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
4372            return Vec::new();
4373        }
4374        self.pending_physical_process_exits
4375            .iter()
4376            .copied()
4377            .collect()
4378    }
4379
4380    /// Whether the backend has reported `detpid` physically gone.
4381    pub(crate) fn process_physically_gone(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4382        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
4383    }
4384
4385    /// Begin the asynchronous-exit barrier for `process` at its Exit grant.
4386    /// The hold in `step2_drain_prefix` selects no further turn while any exit
4387    /// is pending, so a second grant cannot happen first: at most one process
4388    /// is ever pending.
4389    fn begin_exit_at_grant(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
4390        assert!(
4391            self.pending_physical_process_exits
4392                .iter()
4393                .all(|pending| *pending == process),
4394            "asynchronous exit completion: process {process} was granted an exit while {:?} is \
4395             still pending; the hold must allow at most one",
4396            self.pending_physical_process_exits
4397        );
4398        if self.begin_physical_process_exit(process) {
4399            trace!(
4400                "[detcore, dpid {}] holding turn selection until the exit completes",
4401                process
4402            );
4403        }
4404    }
4405
4406    /// Retire, at its completion, every registration of `detpid` that the
4407    /// process did not deregister itself: it died without finishing its exit
4408    /// hook (without an Exit grant, or between its grant and its
4409    /// `DeregisterThread`), at a moment the host chose. Returns whether anything
4410    /// was consumed; the caller then records determinism loss.
4411    ///
4412    /// A dead vfork parent's barrier is cancelled (by `logically_kill_thread`)
4413    /// so no other turn stays excluded. If its child has not registered yet, a
4414    /// tombstone lets the child's outstanding registration settle without the
4415    /// barrier.
4416    pub(crate) fn consume_unreported_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4417        // An admitted process can die before its parent's fork turn, or its
4418        // own startup, registers it. Then it has nothing to consume; the
4419        // completion still records it physically gone, so its registration
4420        // is refused when it arrives.
4421        if !self.thread_tree.contains(&detpid) {
4422            return false;
4423        }
4424        let unreported: Vec<DetTid> = self
4425            .thread_tree
4426            .my_thread_group(&detpid)
4427            .into_iter()
4428            .filter(|tid| {
4429                self.next_turns.contains_key(tid) && !self.deregistration_accounted.contains(tid)
4430            })
4431            .collect();
4432        for tid in &unreported {
4433            // A late DeregisterThread from the same incarnation, if one was
4434            // still in flight, is then acknowledged as already accounted.
4435            self.deregistration_accounted.insert(*tid);
4436            let mm = self
4437                .physical_thread_pidfds
4438                .get(tid)
4439                .map(|(mm, ..)| *mm)
4440                .unwrap_or(MmId::initial(*tid));
4441            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &detpid, mm);
4442        }
4443        !unreported.is_empty()
4444    }
4445
4446    /// Release every physical-exit barrier after the backend supervisor has drained all tracees.
4447    pub(crate) fn release_all_physical_process_exits(&mut self) -> usize {
4448        // Nothing can report a publication once every tracee is drained.
4449        self.child_exit_publications_pending.clear();
4450        self.child_exit_publications_completed.clear();
4451        let children = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_physical_process_exits);
4452        let released = children.len();
4453        for child in children {
4454            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(child);
4455            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(child);
4456        }
4457        released
4458    }
4459
4460    /// Remove entries from everywhere that non-runnable threads lurk.
4461    fn remove_blocking_entries(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid) {
4462        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(*dtid);
4463        let _ = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(dtid);
4464        self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(dtid);
4465        let _ = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(dtid);
4466        let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(dtid);
4467        self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(dtid);
4468        self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.remove(dtid);
4469        self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(dtid);
4470        self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(dtid);
4471        let _ = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(dtid);
4472        self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(dtid);
4473        self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(dtid);
4474        self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
4475            waiters.remove(dtid);
4476            !waiters.is_empty()
4477        });
4478        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(dtid);
4479        self.forget_poll_deadline(*dtid);
4480        let _ = self.remove_futex_waiter(dtid);
4481        // A killed thread must not keep the scheduler loop alive as a parked
4482        // happens-before thread. (`force_unblock_thread_at` never reaches here
4483        // for a parked thread: it leaves a held thread held.)
4484        if let Some(hb) = self.happens_before.as_mut() {
4485            hb.parked.remove(dtid);
4486            hb.held_at.remove(dtid);
4487            hb.holds.remove(dtid);
4488        }
4489    }
4490
4491    fn remove_futex_waiter(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid) -> bool {
4492        let mut removed = 0;
4493        self.blocked.futex_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
4494            let before = waiters.len();
4495            waiters.retain(|waiter| &waiter.dettid != dettid);
4496            removed += before - waiters.len();
4497            !waiters.is_empty()
4498        });
4499        assert!(removed <= 1, "thread was registered on multiple futexes");
4500        removed == 1
4501    }
4502
4503    /// Put a Futex waiter to sleep, to be awoken by `wake_futex_waiter`.
4504    pub fn sleep_futex_waiter(
4505        &mut self,
4506        dettid: &DetTid,
4507        futexid: FutexID,
4508        maybe_timeout: Option<LogicalTime>,
4509        bitset: u32,
4510        signal_watch: Option<FutexSignalWatch>,
4511    ) {
4512        let nxt = self
4513            .next_turns
4514            .get(dettid)
4515            .expect("Missing next_turns entry");
4516        let entry: &mut Vec<_> = self.blocked.futex_waiters.entry(futexid).or_default();
4517        entry.push(FutexWaiter {
4518            dettid: *dettid,
4519            response: nxt.resp.clone(),
4520            bitset,
4521            signal_watch,
4522        });
4523        // When we park, we use a resource request to signal WHAT we're blocking on.  But this is
4524        // not quite the same as when an active thread in the runqueue blocks on a resource, because
4525        // we're not actually waiting on the scheduler giving us the resource.  We're waiting in the
4526        // futex_waiters pool until a waker comes along.
4527        let mut rsrc = Resources::new(*dettid);
4528        rsrc.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
4529        nxt.req.put(Ok(rsrc));
4530        trace!(
4531            "[dtid {}] Waiter blocking on futex {:?}, now {} waiters, on {}",
4532            &dettid,
4533            &futexid,
4534            entry.len(),
4535            nxt.resp,
4536        );
4537        // A futex with timeout waits in both the futex_waiters and timed_events structures:
4538        if let Some(target_time) = maybe_timeout {
4539            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(target_time, *dettid);
4540        }
4541    }
4542
4543    /// Reschedule a single thread that has been blocked on futex.
4544    pub fn wake_futex_waiter(&mut self, waiter: FutexWaiter) {
4545        let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
4546        let waiter_ivar = waiter.response;
4547        debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(waiterid));
4548
4549        // If it was registered as a waiter-with-timeout, remove it:
4550        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
4551
4552        // Put the woken thread back into circulation:
4553        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waiterid);
4554        trace!(
4555            "[detcore] Woke one thread, dtid: {}, ivar {}, scheduled at position {}",
4556            &waiterid, &waiter_ivar, pos,
4557        );
4558        let nxt = self
4559            .next_turns
4560            .get_mut(&waiterid)
4561            .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
4562        assert_futex_request(nxt);
4563        // N.B. We don't write the response here.  That's for the scheduler to do.
4564        // But with a place in the queue, and a request filled, this thread
4565        // is ready to run in normal order.
4566    }
4567
4568    /// Move a waker to the back of its own priority band, under
4569    /// [`Config::yields_after_futex_wake`], so that it is behind the waiters
4570    /// its `FUTEX_WAKE` just queued when they share that band.
4571    ///
4572    /// The waker is the running thread, still in the run queue at the place
4573    /// its last committed turn left it, so ahead of the waiters
4574    /// [`Scheduler::wake_futex_waiter`] has just pushed. A yield request
4575    /// alone would be granted at once, and it would keep running. At the
4576    /// back of its band, its yield waits for the turns of every thread
4577    /// queued there, as at the end of any turn. It keeps its priority: a
4578    /// waiter in a lower-priority band still runs after it. (`--chaos`
4579    /// redraws priorities from the threads' chaos PRNGs, and a random
4580    /// heuristic does not select first in, first out.)
4581    /// The call comes in the waker's own wake request, in its turn, like the
4582    /// waiters' admission. A waker not in the run queue is left alone rather
4583    /// than asserted on: this runs with the scheduler locked, and a panic
4584    /// here would poison the lock.
4585    pub(crate) fn requeue_futex_waker(&mut self, waker: DetTid) {
4586        if !self.run_queue.remove_tid(waker) {
4587            warn!(
4588                "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} is not in the run queue; not requeued",
4589                waker
4590            );
4591            return;
4592        }
4593        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waker);
4594        trace!(
4595            "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} requeued to the back of its priority band at position {}",
4596            waker, pos
4597        );
4598    }
4599
4600    /// `--fuzz-futexes`: a random sample of `num_woken` of the matching waiters.
4601    fn choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(
4602        &mut self,
4603        vec: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>,
4604        num_woken: usize,
4605    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
4606        let rng = &mut self.fuzz_prng;
4607        debug!(
4608            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, pre shuffle: {:?}",
4609            num_woken,
4610            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
4611        );
4612
4613        // No need to actually use the results here since vec was mutated:
4614        let (_extracted, _remain) = &vec[..].partial_shuffle(rng, num_woken);
4615
4616        info!(
4617            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, post shuffle: {:?}",
4618            num_woken,
4619            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
4620        );
4621        // `partial_shuffle` leaves its random sample at the end of the slice.
4622        vec.split_off(vec.len() - num_woken)
4623    }
4624
4625    fn take_futex_wakees(
4626        &mut self,
4627        futexid: FutexID,
4628        max_to_wake: i32,
4629        wake_mask: u32,
4630    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
4631        // Linux's `futex_wake` (kernel/futex/waitwake.c) counts a matching waiter
4632        // before it compares the count, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`, and
4633        // `nr_wake` is the kernel's `int`. So a count of 0, or a `u32` count above
4634        // INT_MAX that is negative as an `int`, wakes one waiter, like a count of 1.
4635        // (Only futex2's FLAGS_STRICT returns early for a zero count, and futex2 is
4636        // refused before it reaches here.) FUTEX_WAKE_OP's two wakes share this
4637        // rule; FUTEX_REQUEUE's does not (0 wakes nobody), so
4638        // `requeue_futex_waiters` must never route its counts through here.
4639        let max_to_wake: usize = if max_to_wake <= 0 {
4640            1
4641        } else {
4642            max_to_wake as usize
4643        };
4644        let mut vec: Vec<FutexWaiter> = {
4645            match self.blocked.futex_waiters.get_mut(&futexid) {
4646                None => {
4647                    trace!(
4648                        "[detcore] Futex wake {} waiters FIZZLED -- none waiting",
4649                        max_to_wake
4650                    );
4651                    return Vec::new();
4652                }
4653                Some(r) => std::mem::take(r),
4654            }
4655        };
4656        trace!(
4657            "Waking up to {} Futex waiters, out of {} waiting.",
4658            max_to_wake,
4659            vec.len(),
4660        );
4661        let to_wake = if self.fuzz_futexes {
4662            let mut matching = take_matching_futex_waiters(&mut vec, wake_mask);
4663            let num_woken = std::cmp::min(matching.len(), max_to_wake);
4664            let to_wake = self.choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(&mut matching, num_woken);
4665            assert_eq!(to_wake.len(), num_woken);
4666            vec.extend(matching);
4667            to_wake
4668        } else {
4669            // Wake the longest waiters whose bitset matches first, as Linux does
4670            // for waiters of equal priority, and keep every other waiter in the
4671            // order it arrived: waiters are appended as their waits are committed,
4672            // so the list is in arrival order.
4673            let mut to_wake = Vec::new();
4674            let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(vec.len());
4675            for waiter in vec.drain(..) {
4676                if to_wake.len() < max_to_wake && waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0 {
4677                    to_wake.push(waiter);
4678                } else {
4679                    kept.push(waiter);
4680                }
4681            }
4682            vec = kept;
4683            to_wake
4684        };
4685        // Put back what wasn't woken up:
4686        if !vec.is_empty() {
4687            let junk = self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(futexid, vec);
4688            assert!(junk.unwrap().is_empty());
4689        }
4690        to_wake
4691    }
4692
4693    /// Reschedule all threads blocked on a particular futex.
4694    pub fn wake_futex_waiters(
4695        &mut self,
4696        _waker_dettid: DetTid,
4697        futexid: FutexID,
4698        max_to_wake: i32,
4699        wake_mask: u32,
4700    ) -> u64 {
4701        let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(futexid, max_to_wake, wake_mask);
4702        let num_woken = to_wake.len();
4703        for waiter in to_wake {
4704            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
4705        }
4706        num_woken as u64
4707    }
4708
4709    /// `FUTEX_REQUEUE` and `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE` on plain (non-PI) futexes, as
4710    /// Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) does them: walk the
4711    /// waiters of `from` in arrival order, stopping once
4712    /// `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`; wake the first `nr_wake`
4713    /// (`if (++task_count <= nr_wake)`) and move the rest onto `to`. Returns the
4714    /// numbers woken and moved; the call returns their sum. Bitsets are ignored,
4715    /// as `futex_requeue` ignores them. Unlike `futex_wake`, a `nr_wake` of 0
4716    /// wakes nobody here.
4717    ///
4718    /// A moved waiter joins the end of `to`'s waiters, in the order the moved
4719    /// waiters arrived, as `requeue_futex` appends it to the target hash chain
4720    /// with `plist_add`, so a later wake of `to` takes `to`'s earlier waiters
4721    /// first. Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody: `requeue_futex` only
4722    /// changes the waiter's key there. (When two different futexes share a Linux
4723    /// hash bucket the moved waiter keeps its place in the shared chain; that
4724    /// order depends on the kernel's hash of the addresses, which no guest can
4725    /// rely on, and Detcore uses the separate-bucket order.)
4726    ///
4727    /// The caller checks `nr_wake` and `nr_requeue` are not negative (`-EINVAL`)
4728    /// and, for `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE`, the futex word against `val3` (`-EAGAIN`).
4729    pub fn requeue_futex_waiters(
4730        &mut self,
4731        from: FutexID,
4732        to: FutexID,
4733        nr_wake: usize,
4734        nr_requeue: usize,
4735    ) -> (u64, u64) {
4736        let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.futex_waiters.remove(&from) else {
4737            return (0, 0);
4738        };
4739        let mut woken = Vec::new();
4740        let mut moved = Vec::new();
4741        let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(waiters.len());
4742        let mut task_count: usize = 0;
4743        for waiter in waiters {
4744            // `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`, in Linux's signed `int`s.
4745            if task_count as i128 - nr_wake as i128 >= nr_requeue as i128 {
4746                kept.push(waiter);
4747                continue;
4748            }
4749            task_count += 1;
4750            if task_count <= nr_wake {
4751                woken.push(waiter);
4752            } else if from == to {
4753                // Requeued onto the same key: it keeps its place.
4754                kept.push(waiter);
4755            } else {
4756                moved.push(waiter);
4757            }
4758        }
4759        let num_moved = (task_count - woken.len()) as u64;
4760        if !kept.is_empty() {
4761            self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(from, kept);
4762        }
4763        if !moved.is_empty() {
4764            self.blocked
4765                .futex_waiters
4766                .entry(to)
4767                .or_default()
4768                .extend(moved);
4769        }
4770        let num_woken = woken.len() as u64;
4771        for waiter in woken {
4772            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
4773        }
4774        trace!(
4775            "[detcore] futex requeue {:?} -> {:?}: woke {}, moved {}",
4776            from, to, num_woken, num_moved
4777        );
4778        (num_woken, num_moved)
4779    }
4780
4781    /// Record futex wakes delivered by a physical-exit callback for the next
4782    /// deterministic run-queue drain.
4783    pub(crate) fn wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(
4784        &mut self,
4785        wakes: &[(DetTid, FutexID)],
4786    ) -> Vec<u64> {
4787        wakes
4788            .iter()
4789            .map(|(_owner, futexid)| {
4790                let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(*futexid, 1, u32::MAX);
4791                let num_woken = to_wake.len();
4792                for waiter in to_wake {
4793                    let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
4794                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
4795                    let next_turn = self
4796                        .next_turns
4797                        .get_mut(&waiterid)
4798                        .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
4799                    assert_futex_request(next_turn);
4800                    self.admit_to_run_queue(waiterid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
4801                }
4802                num_woken as u64
4803            })
4804            .collect()
4805    }

4807    /// Simulate the effect of CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID.
4808    pub fn wake_futex_child_cleartid(&mut self, futid: FutexID, dettid: DetTid) {
4809        self.cleared_child_tids.insert(futid, dettid);
4810        debug!(
4811            "simulate CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID on futex {:?}, wake one",
4812            futid
4813        );
4814        // Wakes only one thread, as per:
4815        // https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/set_tid_address.2.html
4816        self.wake_futex_waiters(dettid, futid, 1, u32::MAX);
4817    }

4819    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4820    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review late CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID wait recovery.
4821    /// Whether a futex word still names the child that was logically cleared.
4822    pub(crate) fn child_tid_was_cleared(&self, futid: FutexID, observed: i32) -> bool {
4823        self.cleared_child_tids
4824            .get(&futid)
4825            .is_some_and(|dettid| dettid.as_raw() == observed)
4826    }
4827
4828    /// Step: Before we select which thread to run, first we check if some internal data
4829    /// structure maintenance is necessary, i.e. moving timed events from the waiting pool
4830    /// to the run queue. It manipulates scheduler data structures accordingly.
4831    fn step2_drain_prefix(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4832        // A terminal verdict recorded outside a turn (a global-request handler
4833        // such as the exec reconnect) ends the run once this turn returns:
4834        // select nothing, so no thread is granted a turn that would race the
4835        // exit.
4836        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
4837            return Err(SkipTurn);
4838        }
4839        // Apply run-queue mutations deferred by asynchronous global-request
4840        // handlers first, at this fixed deterministic point, before any early
4841        // return below and before step3 opens a tentative-pop window. Removals
4842        // drain before admissions so a thread killed while an admission was
4843        // still buffered is not re-enqueued.
4844        self.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
4845        self.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
4846        self.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
4847        // Re-admit happens-before threads whose gate a source opened in the
4848        // last committed turn, with the other deferred admissions: before
4849        // step2c harvests host-timed I/O continuations (so a ready one cannot
4850        // overtake a thread that is already runnable as far as the guest can
4851        // tell) and before step2d classifies an empty queue (so a source thread
4852        // that blocked right after firing is not reported as a futex deadlock,
4853        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
4854        self.hb_flush_wakes();
4855        self.hb_check_hold_budget()?;
4856        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
4857            && !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
4858        {
4859            // A granted exit has not completed physically yet: the exiting
4860            // process may still hold descriptors a peer would observe. Select
4861            // no turn until the backend reports it gone; the completion's host
4862            // timing decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
4863            std::thread::yield_now();
4864            return Err(SkipTurn);
4865        }
4866        if !self.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty() {
4867            // A child's exit grant left its notification to the kernel (None
4868            // or Discard). Select no turn until the backend reports the kernel
4869            // has published the exit to the parent; the report's host timing
4870            // decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
4871            std::thread::yield_now();
4872            return Err(SkipTurn);
4873        }
4874        if self
4875            .blocked
4876            .physical_child_waiters
4877            .keys()
4878            .any(|child| self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(child))
4879        {
4880            // A reaper has reached the deterministic logical-exit boundary.
4881            // Do not let runnable siblings advance while the backend catches
4882            // up to physical waitability; completion admits the waiter through
4883            // the next deterministic drain.
4884            std::thread::yield_now();
4885            return Err(SkipTurn);
4886        }
4887        self.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier()?;
4888        Ok(())
4889    }
4890
4891    fn step2_process_blocked(
4892        &mut self,
4893        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
4894    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4895        // Before anything can return or pop a timer (`sigalrm`).
4896        self.step2_sigalrm_ledger();
4897        self.step2_release_signaled_background()?;
4898        self.step2_drain_prefix()?;
4899        self.step2b_process_timed(global_time);
4900        self.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
4901        // A timed signal that just armed a background thread is followed by an
4902        // empty pass, so the barrier above requeues it at the top of the next
4903        // one whether or not its continuation is already posted.
4904        if self.backend_failed()
4905            || self.control_barrier()
4906            || !self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty()
4907        {
4908            return Err(SkipTurn);
4909        }
4910        self.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
4911        self.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
4912        self.step2d_handle_empty_queue(global_time)
4913    }
4914
4915    /// How long the release barrier waits for an armed thread's continuation
4916    /// before it refuses the run (see `step2_release_signaled_background`).
4917    const SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
4918
4919    /// How long step2a skips turns for a vfork barrier that waits for a
4920    /// backend event before it refuses the run (see
4921    /// `step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`). The same bound as the release
4922    /// barrier's.
4923    const VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
4924
4925    /// Requeue, at a fixed point, the background-pool threads that a committed
4926    /// signal armed (`BlockedPool::signaled_background`, set by
4927    /// `arm_signaled_background`).
4928    ///
4929    /// This runs first in every scheduler pass: before the drain prefix, any
4930    /// timer pop, and any selection. While an armed thread is still in its pool
4931    /// with no posted request, the kernel is still delivering its signal, and
4932    /// the pass does nothing else: it returns `SkipTurn`. Once every armed
4933    /// thread has posted its continuation (or left its pool, or exited), all of
4934    /// them are requeued in `DetTid` order exactly as
4935    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers` requeues a ready backgrounded call. No
4936    /// guest turn and no other scheduler event can commit between the signal
4937    /// and the requeue, so host delivery time decides only how many empty
4938    /// passes spin, never where the threads enter the run queue.
4939    ///
4940    /// The watchdog (`SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE`) only bounds how long the
4941    /// barrier waits; it never decides an admission. An armed thread is woken
4942    /// because its recorded mask does not block the signal and a traced thread
4943    /// is never spared a signal at generation, so it always stops and posts. If
4944    /// that ever fails to happen before the watchdog fires, the barrier keeps
4945    /// every arm, records a `SignaledBackgroundRefusal`, and the scheduler loop
4946    /// ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`. Dropping the arms instead
4947    /// would leave the threads for `step2c` to harvest behind runnable siblings:
4948    /// an admission order that host delivery time decides.
4949    fn step2_release_signaled_background(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4950        if self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty() {
4951            self.signaled_background_since = None;
4952            return Ok(());
4953        }
4954        let armed: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.signaled_background.iter().copied().collect();
4955        let mut unposted = Vec::new();
4956        for dtid in armed {
4957            let in_pool = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
4958                || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid);
4959            match self.next_turns.get(&dtid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read()) {
4960                Some(Some(Ok(_))) if in_pool => {}
4961                Some(None) if in_pool => unposted.push(dtid),
4962                // Left its pool, exited, or unregistered: nothing to order.
4963                _ => {
4964                    self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(&dtid);
4965                }
4966            }
4967        }
4968        if !unposted.is_empty() {
4969            let since = *self
4970                .signaled_background_since
4971                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
4972            let waited = since.elapsed();
4973            if waited < Self::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE {
4974                trace!(
4975                    "[step2] waiting for signaled background dtids {:?} to post their continuations",
4976                    unposted
4977                );
4978                std::thread::yield_now();
4979                return Err(SkipTurn);
4980            }
4981            // Fail closed: keep every arm, so nothing is admitted at a
4982            // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
4983            if self.signaled_background_refusal.is_none() {
4984                let refusal = SignaledBackgroundRefusal { unposted, waited };
4985                tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
4986                self.signaled_background_refusal = Some(refusal);
4987            }
4988            return Err(SkipTurn);
4989        }
4990        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.signaled_background);
4991        self.signaled_background_since = None;
4992        for dtid in ready {
4993            info!(
4994                "[step2] Reschedule signaled background dtid {:?} at its fixed point",
4995                dtid
4996            );
4997            let external = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&dtid);
4998            self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(&dtid);
4999            let sigsuspend = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&dtid);
5000            let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(&dtid);
5001            assert!(
5002                external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
5003                "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
5004            );
5005            self.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(dtid);
5006        }
5007        Ok(())
5008    }
5009
5010    /// Re-admit parents whose host-async `SIGCHLD` was parked in
5011    /// `blocked.sigchld_deferred` (see `block_for_one_resource`). Uses the same
5012    /// deterministic-work-first gate as `step2c_process_io_blockers`: a deferred
5013    /// signal is delivered only once the run queue holds no ordinary (non-poller)
5014    /// guest work, so its commit order is fixed by the scheduler rather than by
5015    /// host signal-arrival timing. Runs after external-IO harvesting so a ready
5016    /// IO continuation is always ordered ahead of a deferred signal.
5017    fn step2e_process_signal_deferred(&mut self) {
5018        if self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty() {
5019            return;
5020        }
5021        let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers();
5022        if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
5023            return;
5024        }
5025        // BTreeSet drains in sorted DetTid order, giving a canonical admission
5026        // order when several parents are owed a signal at the same quiescence.
5027        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.sigchld_deferred);
5028        for dtid in ready {
5029            info!("[step2] Re-admit deferred SIGCHLD for dtid {:?}", dtid);
5030            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dtid);
5031            self.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(dtid);
5032        }
5033    }
5034
5035    /// Keep scheduling inside an active vfork until the parent can continue.
5036    /// Before child registration no guest may run; afterward step 3 admits only
5037    /// the child. A failed clone reaches the parent continuation without a child.
5038    ///
5039    /// On the ptrace backend the kernel keeps the vfork parent blocked inside the injected
5040    /// `clone(2)` until the child execs or exits, so a registered child (barrier `Some`) is always
5041    /// present by the time the parent posts its continuation; an unfulfilled barrier (`None`) at
5042    /// that point therefore means the clone failed and the barrier must be dropped. On a backend
5043    /// that defers the child spawn (see `defers_vfork_child_registration`, e.g. KVM) the
5044    /// child registers only *after* the parent posts its continuation, so an unfulfilled barrier at
5045    /// parent continuation means the child is still on its way and the barrier must be kept.
5046    ///
5047    /// Two states make every pass skip its turn until a backend event arrives:
5048    /// a `Pending` barrier waits for its child's registration, and a
5049    /// `Released` one for its parent's continuation or retirement. No turn
5050    /// commits meanwhile, so the event's host timing decides only how many
5051    /// passes skip, never which turn is next. Each skip yields the scheduler
5052    /// thread, as the other step2 prefix skips do. The valve
5053    /// (`VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE`) bounds the wait without ever deciding a
5054    /// selection: if the event has not arrived when it expires, every barrier
5055    /// is kept, a `VforkBarrierRefusal` names the waiting barriers, and
5056    /// `sched_loop_inner` ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`
5057    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>). Dropping the
5058    /// barriers instead would let other threads be selected at a moment the
5059    /// host chose.
5060    fn step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
5061        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5062        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review deferred vfork child registration.
5063        let defers_registration = self.backend.defers_vfork_child_registration;
5064        let completed_parents: Vec<_> = self
5065            .vfork_barriers
5066            .iter()
5067            .filter_map(|(parent, registered_child)| {
5068                let child_registered = registered_child.is_some();
5069                let remove = match self
5070                    .next_turns
5071                    .get(parent)
5072                    .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
5073                {
5074                    // The parent exited: there will be no child; drop the barrier.
5075                    Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => true,
5076                    Some(Ok(resources)) => {
5077                        let vfork_failed = resources
5078                            .resources
5079                            .keys()
5080                            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::VforkFailed(_)));
5081                        let at_continue = resources.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
5082                            matches!(resource, ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_))
5083                        });
5084                        // A failed injected clone is an explicit deterministic outcome: no child
5085                        // can ever register, so cancel the barrier on every backend. Successful
5086                        // deferred spawns retain the ordinary continuation and keep waiting.
5087                        // At parent continuation, drop a fulfilled barrier as normal cleanup. An
5088                        // unfulfilled barrier is a failed clone only when the backend kept the
5089                        // parent blocked until the child registered; when the backend defers child
5090                        // registration the child is still coming, so keep waiting.
5091                        vfork_failed || (at_continue && (child_registered || !defers_registration))
5092                    }
5093                    _ => false,
5094                };
5095                remove.then_some(*parent)
5096            })
5097            .collect();
5098        for parent in completed_parents {
5099            self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
5100        }
5101
5102        // A pending barrier waits for its child's registration, a released one
5103        // for its parent's continuation or retirement; no turn commits
5104        // meanwhile, so when that host-timed event arrives cannot change the
5105        // schedule. A registered, unreleased barrier does not wait: step 3
5106        // admits its child.
5107        let waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait> = self
5108            .vfork_barriers
5109            .iter()
5110            .filter_map(|(parent, child)| {
5111                let state = if child.is_none() {
5112                    VforkBarrierState::Pending
5113                } else if self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(parent) {
5114                    VforkBarrierState::Released
5115                } else {
5116                    return None;
5117                };
5118                Some(VforkBarrierWait {
5119                    parent: *parent,
5120                    child: *child,
5121                    state,
5122                })
5123            })
5124            .collect();
5125        if waits.is_empty() {
5126            self.vfork_barrier_wait_since = None;
5127            return Ok(());
5128        }
5129        let since = *self
5130            .vfork_barrier_wait_since
5131            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
5132        let waited = since.elapsed();
5133        if waited < Self::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE {
5134            trace!("[step2a] waiting on vfork barriers {:?}", waits);
5135            std::thread::yield_now();
5136            return Err(SkipTurn);
5137        }
5138        // Fail closed: keep every barrier, so no other thread is selected at a
5139        // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
5140        if self.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none() {
5141            let refusal = VforkBarrierRefusal { waits, waited };
5142            tracing::error!("[step2a] {}", refusal);
5143            self.vfork_barrier_refusal = Some(refusal);
5144        }
5145        Err(SkipTurn)
5146    }
5147
5148    /// Record the timeout deadline of a poller that `step4_resource_block` just
5149    /// requeued backed off, replacing any earlier entry of the thread. Nothing
5150    /// is recorded under record/replay, whose schedule must not change, or
5151    /// under a heuristic that does not select in priority order (there a
5152    /// backed-off poller is never starved, and re-keying it would only remap
5153    /// seeds) (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
5154    fn note_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
5155        self.forget_poll_deadline(dettid);
5156        let Some(deadline) = rs.poll_deadline else {
5157            return;
5158        };
5159        if self.recordreplay_modes || !self.run_queue.is_priority_ordered() {
5160            return;
5161        }
5162        self.poll_deadlines.insert((deadline, dettid));
5163        self.poll_deadline_of.insert(dettid, deadline);
5164    }
5165
5166    fn forget_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
5167        if let Some(deadline) = self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid) {
5168            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
5169        }
5170    }
5171
5172    /// Restore the normal priority of every backed-off poller whose timeout
5173    /// deadline committed time has reached, so its next retry runs at the next
5174    /// selection and returns the timeout instead of waiting up to
5175    /// `POLLING_UPGRADE_INTERVAL` pushes for a poll upgrade
5176    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
5177    ///
5178    /// Each due entry resolves one of four ways:
5179    /// 1. the thread is gone, or its pending request no longer carries this
5180    ///    deadline (it ran, finished the call, or started another one): drop;
5181    /// 2. it is queued backed off: restore its priority, then drop;
5182    /// 3. it is queued but no longer backed off (`do_poll_upgrade`, or a
5183    ///    replayed priority change, restored it already): drop;
5184    /// 4. its request still carries the deadline but it is out of the run
5185    ///    queue: keep, so a later pass restores it once it is back. This is
5186    ///    defensive: the only suspension of a queued entry,
5187    ///    `take_validated_membership` for a parked alarm observation, accepts
5188    ///    no request that carries a poll deadline today.
5189    ///
5190    /// Deterministic: it reads only the deadlines threads computed in their own
5191    /// turns, `committed_time`, the run queue and the pending requests. It is
5192    /// idempotent for a given `committed_time` and monotone in it, so how many
5193    /// passes run between commits does not change its result; it is the same
5194    /// exposure `step2b_process_timed` already has to `committed_time`. A
5195    /// restore moves the entry to the back of its normal priority level: it
5196    /// takes a new back turn and counts toward the poll-upgrade interval
5197    /// (`RunQueue::restore_poller_priority`), so a poll upgrade can fire in the
5198    /// middle of this loop. Both are deterministic. It never admits or removes
5199    /// a thread.
5200    fn step2b_restore_due_pollers(&mut self) {
5201        let due: Vec<(LogicalTime, DetTid)> = self
5202            .poll_deadlines
5203            .iter()
5204            .take_while(|(deadline, _)| *deadline <= self.committed_time)
5205            .copied()
5206            .collect();
5207        for (deadline, dettid) in due {
5208            let still_waiting = self
5209                .next_turns
5210                .get(&dettid)
5211                .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
5212                .is_some_and(
5213                    |request| matches!(request, Ok(rs) if rs.poll_deadline == Some(deadline)),
5214                );
5215            if still_waiting {
5216                match self.run_queue.restore_poller_priority(dettid) {
5217                    PollerRestore::Restored => {
5218                        info!(
5219                            "[scheduler] dettid {} restored to its normal priority: its poll \
5220                             deadline {} has passed (committed time {})",
5221                            dettid, deadline, self.committed_time
5222                        );
5223                    }
5224                    PollerRestore::NotBackedOff => {}
5225                    PollerRestore::NotQueued => continue,
5226                }
5227            }
5228            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
5229            self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid);
5230        }
5231    }
5232
5233    /// Check whether it is time for the *earliest* time-based event to execute INSTEAD of
5234    /// dispatching from the normal run queue.  Manipulates scheduler data structures
5235    /// accordingly.
5236    /// Return whether an event was actually consumed, so a control refresh
5237    /// can distinguish an empty check from a spent maintenance budget.
5238    fn step2b_process_timed(&mut self, global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) -> bool {
5239        if let Some((time_ns, evt)) = self
5240            .blocked
5241            .timed_waiters
5242            .pop_if_before(self.committed_time)
5243        {
5244            match evt {
5245                TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(tid) => self.wake_timed_event(time_ns, tid),
5246                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, tid, sig) => {
5247                    let observed_now = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
5248                    self.dispatch_timed_signal(time_ns, id, tid, sig, true, observed_now)
5249                }
5250            }
5251            true
5252        } else {
5253            false
5254        }
5255    }
