5257    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5258    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
5259    fn fire_alarm(&mut self, dpid: DetPid, dtid: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
5260        // A guest-handled SIGALRM goes to the process's ledger, not the kernel.
5261        if self.divert_sigalrm(dpid, sig) {
5262            return;
5263        }
5264        #[cfg(test)]
5265        {
5266            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
5267        }
5268        let Some(target) = self.select_signal_target(dpid, Some(dtid)) else {
5269            info!(
5270                "[dpid {}] Alarm expired after its target exited; ignoring.",
5271                dpid
5272            );
5273            return;
5274        };
5275        info!(
5276            "[dtid {}] Alarm fired, delivering signal {} to guest.",
5277            target, sig
5278        );
5279        self.signal_guest(target, sig);
5280    }

5282    /// Snapshot eligibility is local to the exact outstanding sleep request.
5283    fn in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(
5284        &self,
5285        thread: DetTid,
5286    ) -> Option<(crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm, LogicalTime)> {
5287        if self.backend != BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST
5288            || self.registered_process(thread) != Some(thread)
5289            || self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) != [thread]
5290        {
5291            return None;
5292        }
5293        self.next_turns
5294            .get(&thread)?
5295            .req
5296            .try_read()?
5297            .ok()?
5298            .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
5299    }

5301    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(&self, thread: DetTid) -> bool {
5302        self.next_turns
5303            .get(&thread)
5304            .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
5305            .is_some_and(|request| {
5306                request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
5307                    resources.resources.len() == 1
5308                        && resources.resources.get(&ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm)
5309                            == Some(&Permission::W)
5310                })
5311            })
5312    }
5313
5314    /// Only a consumed one-shot Alarm identity may replace a parked sleep.
5315    /// Dispatch supplies the event timestamp and observed GlobalTime, since
5316    /// empty-queue skips and control hooks can advance that clock before
5317    /// committed_time is refreshed.
5318    fn divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
5319        &mut self,
5320        event_ns: LogicalTime,
5321        id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId,
5322        thread: DetTid,
5323        signal: Signal,
5324        observed_now: LogicalTime,
5325    ) -> bool {
5326        let timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(process) = id else {
5327            return false;
5328        };
5329        if signal != Signal::SIGALRM
5330            || process != thread
5331            || self.sigalrm_handled(process)
5332            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_state(process).is_some()
5333            || !matches!(self.thread_status(thread), ThreadStatus::NotRunning)
5334            || self
5335                .happens_before
5336                .as_ref()
5337                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&thread))
5338        {
5339            return false;
5340        }
5341        let Some((snapshot, deadline)) = self.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(thread) else {
5342            return false;
5343        };
5344        if !snapshot.ends_process()
5345            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(thread) != Some(deadline)
5346            || deadline <= self.committed_time.max(event_ns).max(observed_now)
5347        {
5348            return false;
5349        }
5350        let mut wake = Resources::new(thread);
5351        wake.insert(ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm, Permission::W);
5352        info!(
5353            "[dtid {}] one-shot SIGALRM expired during an in-guest sleep; staging fatal delivery in the target's turn.",
5354            thread
5355        );
5356        self.force_unblock_thread(thread, wake);
5357        true
5358    }

5360    /// Authenticate the retained caller request after the typed grant cleared
5361    /// its scheduler slot. This rejects a fabricated generic fatal resource,
5362    /// a stale address space, or a grant belonging to another task.
5363    pub(crate) fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
5364        &self,
5365        thread: DetTid,
5366        process: DetPid,
5367        mm: Option<MmId>,
5368        original: &Resources,
5369    ) -> bool {
5370        self.backend == BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST
5371            && thread == process
5372            && original.tid == thread
5373            && original
5374                .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
5375                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| snapshot.ends_process())
5376            && self.registered_process(thread) == Some(process)
5377            && self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) == [thread]
5378            && mm.is_some_and(|mm| self.rpc_incarnation_matches(thread, mm))
5379            && self.holds_serial_grant(thread)
5380    }
5381
5382    // Follow Linux semantics for delivering a signal to a thread within a process group.
5383    // Optionally take a hint on which tid detcore would *like* to deliver to, if it is available.
5384    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5385    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
5386    fn select_signal_target(&mut self, detpid: DetPid, m_dettid: Option<DetTid>) -> Option<DetTid> {
5387        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
5388            return None;
5389        }
5390
5391        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a process-directed signal may legally be
5392        // handled by any thread in the group that does not block it. Instead of
5393        // always steering it to the hinted/leader thread, pick a random eligible
5394        // thread to surface signal-timing races. This stays reproducible under a
5395        // fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
5396        if self.chaos_target_races {
5397            let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
5398            let eligible: Vec<DetTid> = group
5399                .into_iter()
5400                .filter(|t| !matches!(self.thread_status(*t), ThreadStatus::Gone))
5401                .collect();
5402            if let Some(chosen) = chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &eligible) {
5403                info!(
5404                    "[targeted-chaos] delivering process-directed signal to random group thread {} (of {:?})",
5405                    chosen, eligible
5406                );
5407                return Some(chosen);
5408            }
5409        }
5410
5411        if let Some(dettid) = m_dettid {
5412            match self.thread_status(dettid) {
5413                ThreadStatus::Gone => {}
5414                ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
5415                    return Some(dettid);
5416                }
5417            }
5418        }
5419        match self.thread_status(detpid) {
5420            ThreadStatus::Gone => self.process_signal_targets(detpid).into_iter().next(),
5421            ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => Some(detpid),
5422        }
5423    }
5424
5425    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5426    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
5427    /// Return the scheduler's live threads for a positive process ID.
5428    /// Is `dettid` a live thread, leader or not?
5429    ///
5430    /// `process_signal_targets` answers a DIFFERENT question and must not be
5431    /// reused for this one: it models `kill(2)`, so it returns nothing unless
5432    /// the id names a thread-group LEADER. `sched_setattr(2)` and its relatives
5433    /// resolve through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds any live task, so a
5434    /// non-leader thread's tid is a perfectly good target there. Answering that
5435    /// question with the kill resolver reports ESRCH for a thread that exists.
5436    ///
5437    /// Liveness is `next_turns`, the same membership `process_signal_targets`
5438    /// filters its own result by, so the two agree about what "live" means.
5439    pub fn thread_is_live(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5440        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid)
5441    }
5442
5443    /// Return scheduler-owned lifecycle state for an exact child-process wait.
5444    ///
5445    /// This deliberately models direct parentage and process liveness rather
5446    /// than `kill(2)` target resolution. It lets wait syscalls stop exposing
5447    /// the backend-dependent interval between logical exit and host waitability.
5448    pub fn exact_child_wait_state(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> ExactChildWaitState {
5449        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
5450            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
5451        }
5452
5453        let live = self
5454            .thread_tree
5455            .my_thread_group(&child)
5456            .into_iter()
5457            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
5458        if live {
5459            return ExactChildWaitState::Running;
5460        }
5461
5462        if !self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
5463            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
5464        }
5465
5466        if !self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits {
5467            ExactChildWaitState::LogicallyExited
5468        } else if self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(&child) {
5469            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicalExitPending
5470        } else {
5471            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicallyExited
5472        }
5473    }
5474
5475    fn child_matches_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
5476        let Some(metadata) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
5477            return false;
5478        };
5479        metadata.wait_parent == Some(parent)
5480            && spec.owner.is_none_or(|owner| metadata.wait_owner == owner)
5481            && match spec.exit_class {
5482                ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld => metadata.exit_signal == libc::SIGCHLD,
5483                ChildWaitExitClass::Clone => metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD,
5484                ChildWaitExitClass::Any => true,
5485            }
5486            && match spec.selector {
5487                ChildWaitSelector::Exact(expected) => child == expected,
5488                ChildWaitSelector::Any => true,
5489                ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group) => metadata.process_group == group,
5490            }
5491    }
5492
5493    /// True, in a happens-before run with a thread held at a gate, when there
5494    /// is at least one child wait and every one of them can only be satisfied
5495    /// by stuck children: children whose live threads are all held at gates,
5496    /// parked in a futex wait, or themselves in a child wait on stuck
5497    /// children. None of these runs again until some other thread does (an
5498    /// anchor firing, a futex wake, a child exit), so with nothing runnable,
5499    /// no timer and no outstanding external I/O, such waits can never end
5500    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904). A chain of waits
5501    /// down to a held child is stuck too, so an ancestor's ordinary wait does
5502    /// not hide the cycle below it. A wait with no matching child, a child
5503    /// with any other live thread or none, a child that has already exited,
5504    /// and a child a committed SIGKILL has doomed (it will die at a host-timed
5505    /// point, so its wait is real) are treated as able to end, as before.
5506    fn child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children(&self) -> bool {
5507        let Some(hb) = self.happens_before.as_ref() else {
5508            return false;
5509        };
5510        if self.unresolved_sigkill || hb.parked.is_empty() || self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty()
5511        {
5512            return false;
5513        }
5514        // The stuck processes, as a least fixed point: a process becomes stuck
5515        // once each of its live threads is held, futex-parked, or waiting only
5516        // on processes already found stuck. Growing the set only makes more
5517        // processes qualify, so the iteration ends; the process tree has no
5518        // cycles, so a chain is found one level per round.
5519        let mut stuck: BTreeSet<DetPid> = BTreeSet::new();
5520        loop {
5521            let next: BTreeSet<DetPid> = self
5522                .thread_tree
5523                .process_wait
5524                .keys()
5525                .copied()
5526                .filter(|child| self.child_is_stuck(hb, *child, &stuck))
5527                .collect();
5528            if next == stuck {
5529                break;
5530            }
5531            stuck = next;
5532        }
5533        self.blocked
5534            .child_waiters
5535            .values()
5536            .all(|(parent, spec)| self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, &stuck))
5537    }
5538
5539    /// True when the child wait of `parent` with `spec` has at least one
5540    /// matching child and every matching child is in `stuck`.
5541    fn child_wait_is_stuck(
5542        &self,
5543        parent: DetPid,
5544        spec: ChildWaitSpec,
5545        stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>,
5546    ) -> bool {
5547        let mut children = self
5548            .thread_tree
5549            .process_wait
5550            .keys()
5551            .copied()
5552            .filter(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
5553            .peekable();
5554        children.peek().is_some() && children.all(|child| stuck.contains(&child))
5555    }
5556
5557    /// True when process `child` can run again only after some other thread
5558    /// does, given the processes already known to be `stuck`
5559    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`]).
5560    fn child_is_stuck(&self, hb: &HbRuntime, child: DetPid, stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>) -> bool {
5561        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(child.as_raw());
5562        // A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is killed by the
5563        // kernel when its parent thread exits, at a moment set by host
5564        // timing. The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the
5565        // caller's committed turn and never forgotten, so such a process
5566        // never counts as stuck (the second Claude re-check of
5567        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013).
5568        if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child)
5569            || self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&child)
5570            || !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&leader)
5571            || self.host_timed_signals(leader) & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) != 0
5572        {
5573            return false;
5574        }
5575        // The thread tree keeps every thread a process ever had. A thread no
5576        // longer registered that left by its own committed exit is gone
5577        // harmlessly; one that left any other way died of a signal or with its
5578        // process, so the process is going down and its wait is real. The
5579        // dying thread's deregistration is ordered (the scheduler waits for a
5580        // running thread to quiesce); the held thread's is not, so only the
5581        // dying sibling can tell.
5582        let (live, gone): (Vec<DetTid>, Vec<DetTid>) = self
5583            .thread_tree
5584            .my_thread_group(&leader)
5585            .into_iter()
5586            .partition(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
5587        gone.iter().all(|tid| self.committed_exits.contains(tid))
5588            && !live.is_empty()
5589            && live.iter().all(|tid| {
5590                hb.parked.contains(tid)
5591                    || self.parked_futex_waiter(*tid).is_some()
5592                    || self
5593                        .blocked
5594                        .child_waiters
5595                        .get(tid)
5596                        .is_some_and(|(parent, spec)| {
5597                            self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, stuck)
5598                        })
5599            })
5600    }
5601
5602    pub fn ready_child_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> Option<DetPid> {
5603        self.logically_exited_processes
5604            .iter()
5605            .copied()
5606            .find(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
5607    }
5608
5609    pub fn has_child_wait_target(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
5610        self.thread_tree
5611            .process_wait
5612            .keys()
5613            .copied()
5614            .any(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, spec))
5615    }
5616
5617    pub fn consume_child_wait(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> bool {
5618        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
5619            return false;
5620        }
5621        self.wake_child_waiters(parent, child);
5622        self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&child);
5623        self.sigkilled_processes.remove(&child);
5624        self.thread_tree.process_parent.remove(&child);
5625        self.thread_tree.process_wait.remove(&child);
5626        self.thread_tree.child_subreapers.remove(&child);
5627        self.thread_tree.init_orphans.remove(&child);
5628        self.thread_tree.granted_exits.remove(&child);
5629        self.logically_exited_processes.remove(&child)
5630    }
5631
5632    fn wake_child_waiters(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) {
5633        let waiters: Vec<DetTid> = self
5634            .blocked
5635            .child_waiters
5636            .iter()
5637            .filter_map(|(dettid, (wait_parent, spec))| {
5638                (*wait_parent == parent && self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, *spec))
5639                    .then_some(*dettid)
5640            })
5641            .collect();
5642        for dettid in waiters {
5643            self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(&dettid);
5644            debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid));
5645            self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
5646        }
5647    }
5648
5649    fn wake_physical_child_waiters(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
5650        if let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.remove(&child) {
5651            for dettid in waiters {
5652                self.blocked.physical_child_ready.insert(dettid);
5653                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) && !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
5654                    self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
5655                }
5656            }
5657        }
5658    }
5659
5660    pub fn process_signal_targets(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
5661        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
5662            return Vec::new();
5663        }
5664        let mut targets = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
5665        targets.retain(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
5666        targets.sort();
5667        targets
5668    }
5669
5670    fn wake_timed_event(&mut self, time_ns: LogicalTime, dettid: DetTid) {
5671        let futex_timed_out = {
5672            let next_turn = self
5673                .next_turns
5674                .get(&dettid)
5675                .expect("internal invariant broken");
5676            is_futex_request(next_turn)
5677        };
5678        if futex_timed_out {
5679            assert!(self.remove_futex_waiter(&dettid));
5680            assert!(self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid));
5681        }
5682
5683        if enabled!(Level::TRACE) {
5684            if futex_timed_out {
5685                info!(
5686                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}, committed time {}) - futex wait timed out!",
5687                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
5688                );
5689            } else {
5690                info!(
5691                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}) jumping back to the head of it's priority at global(committed) time {}",
5692                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
5693                );
5694            }
5695        }
5696        self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
5697    }
5698
5699    /// Send a signal to the guest. A scheduler-parked thread is made runnable immediately. SaBRe
5700    /// external syscalls remain blocked until the signal interrupts them and their real
5701    /// continuation RPC becomes visible; other backends retain their existing immediate requeue.
5702    fn signal_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal) {
5703        debug!(
5704            "[dtid {}] deliver signal {} physically to guest thread.",
5705            dettid, signal
5706        );
5707        let result = if let Some((_, _, _, pidfd)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid) {
5708            let rc = unsafe {
5709                libc::syscall(
5710                    libc::SYS_pidfd_send_signal,
5711                    pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
5712                    signal as libc::c_int,
5713                    std::ptr::null::<libc::siginfo_t>(),
5714                    0,
5715                )
5716            };
5717            if rc < 0 {
5718                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
5719            } else {
5720                Ok(())
5721            }
5722        } else if self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
5723            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
5724                format!(
5725                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot deliver signal {} to dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
5726                    signal, dettid,
5727                )
5728            });
5729            return;
5730        } else {
5731            let pid = Pid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()); // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
5732            signal::kill(pid, signal)
5733        };
5734        match result {
5735            Ok(()) => {}
5736            // ⚠️ ESRCH IS AN EXPECTED OUTCOME HERE, NOT AN ERROR. The target
5737            // chose to exit between the moment it was selected and the moment
5738            // the signal was sent; that window is inherent and cannot be closed
5739            // by locking, because the thread's exit is the guest's decision.
5740            // There is no one left to signal and nothing left to wake, so the
5741            // correct behaviour is to say so and carry on.
5742            //
5743            // This is NOT a retry and NOT a widened catch: exactly ESRCH is
5744            // absorbed, and every other errno still panics, because a signal
5745            // rejected for any other reason means the scheduler's model of the
5746            // guest is wrong and continuing would compound it.
5747            //
5748            // WHY IT MATTERED. Before this, the unconditional `expect` turned
5749            // that ordinary race into a panic on the scheduler task -- and a
5750            // panicking scheduler does not fail the run, it HANGS it, because
5751            // every guest thread is waiting on a task that no longer exists.
5752            // Measured 2026-08-25: `hermit --backend kvm run --strict --verify`
5753            // on a bash process-substitution pipeline ran 420 s with empty
5754            // stdout and never exited. The pipeline's short-lived subshells hit
5755            // this window repeatedly. Found only once the 22 `run_kvm_` cli
5756            // tests were scheduled; nothing had ever run them.
5757            Err(nix::errno::Errno::ESRCH) => {
5758                info!(
5759                    "[dtid {}] signal {} not delivered: the thread exited before it landed. \
5760                     Expected race; nothing to deliver and nothing to wake.",
5761                    dettid, signal
5762                );
5763                return;
5764            }
5765            Err(errno) => panic!("signal::kill to go through, got {errno}"),
5766        }
5767        self.wake_signaled_guest(dettid, signal);
5768    }
5769
5770    /// Record `signal`, just sent at a committed point, for a thread still
5771    /// stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask does not
5772    /// block it (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`). A later signal
5773    /// of the same kind adds nothing: either one wakes the call.
5774    fn note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal) {
5775        let Some(Some(Ok(request))) = self.next_turns.get(&dettid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read())
5776        else {
5777            return;
5778        };
5779        let suspends = request
5780            .resources
5781            .keys()
5782            .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)));
5783        let unblocked = matches!(
5784            request.blocked_signal_mask,
5785            Some(mask) if mask & kernel_signal_bit(signal as i32) == 0
5786        );
5787        if suspends && unblocked {
5788            self.blocked
5789                .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
5790                .entry(dettid)
5791                .or_insert(signal);
5792        }
5793    }
5794
5795    /// `wake_signaled_guest` for a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
5796    /// the run queue (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers` or `external_io_blockers`) on a
5797    /// traced backend, just sent `signal` at a committed point.
5798    ///
5799    /// Linux wakes a thread sleeping interruptibly when a signal it does not
5800    /// block is queued for it, and a traced thread is never spared one at
5801    /// generation (`sig_ignored` is false under ptrace), so it stops for
5802    /// delivery and the backend posts its `InboundSignal` continuation. Such a
5803    /// thread is armed for the release barrier
5804    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), which requeues it at the top of
5805    /// the next pass once that continuation is posted. A `SIGCHLD` target is
5806    /// also marked `sigchld_ready`, so its delivery commits rather than being
5807    /// deferred behind runnable siblings.
5808    ///
5809    /// Not armed, and left in its pool for `step2c` exactly as before, is a
5810    /// thread the signal does not wake at a known point: a vfork parent (it
5811    /// sleeps killable, so a non-fatal signal does not wake it) and a thread
5812    /// whose recorded sleeping mask is unknown or blocks the signal.
5813    fn arm_signaled_background(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal) {
5814        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal as i32);
5815        let wakes = !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&dettid)
5816            && matches!(
5817                self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&dettid),
5818                Some(Some(mask)) if mask & bit == 0
5819            );
5820        if !wakes {
5821            debug!(
5822                "[dtid {}] signal {} does not wake its background call at a known point; leaving it to step2c.",
5823                dettid, signal
5824            );
5825            return;
5826        }
5827        info!(
5828            "[dtid {}] signal {} armed signaled background thread; awaiting its continuation.",
5829            dettid, signal
5830        );
5831        self.blocked.signaled_background.insert(dettid);
5832        if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD {
5833            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
5834        }
5835    }
5836
5837    /// Wake a scheduler-parked target after another guest has successfully
5838    /// queued a physical signal for it. The signal itself is not sent here;
5839    /// this only prevents an internal polling request from hiding a pending
5840    /// signal indefinitely.
5841    fn wake_signaled_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal) {
5842        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
5843            return;
5844        }
5845        // The physical send has already happened. Preserve its real kernel
5846        // pending/ignored semantics, but never invent an interrupted sleep
5847        // for an alarm this exact owner snapshot blocks or ignores. This
5848        // covers both filed requests and sleeps already outside the queue.
5849        if signal == Signal::SIGALRM
5850            && self
5851                .in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(dettid)
5852                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| {
5853                    snapshot.blocked
5854                        || snapshot.disposition
5855                            == crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Ignored
5856                })
5857        {
5858            return;
5859        }
5860        debug!(
5861            "[dtid {}] make pending signal {} visible to the scheduler.",
5862            dettid, signal
5863        );
5864        // `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` joins `external_io_blockers` here per main's
5865        // rt_sigsuspend work; both mean the thread is parked outside the
5866        // scheduler and must await its own continuation.
5867        let has_external_blocker = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
5868            || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid);
5869        if self.models_signal_targets && !has_external_blocker {
5870            self.note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(dettid, signal);
5871        }
5872        let await_external_continuation =
5873            self.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls && has_external_blocker;
5874        // Where the scheduler models signal targets (`models_signal_targets`),
5875        // such a thread awaits its own continuation too. Its request was
5876        // consumed when it was backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited
5877        // for it; the scheduler orders the continuation the signal provokes
5878        // instead.
5879        if self.models_signal_targets && has_external_blocker && !await_external_continuation {
5880            self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
5881            return;
5882        }
5883        // A scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
5884        // DBT, KVM) has nothing to arm, and the thread still runs its call
5885        // outside the scheduler. Its request was consumed when it was
5886        // backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited for it either: it
5887        // rejoins through its own continuation (`BlockedExternalContinue`),
5888        // and the physical signal has already reached it. Before, a debug
5889        // build asserted below and a release build counterfeited a request
5890        // for a thread still in its pool, as
5891        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146 found for the traced
5892        // backend. In-guest LiteInst reached this when a vfork child's exit
5893        // signalled its parent, which the child had just killed, before the
5894        // parent's death was retired; host load widens that window.
5895        if has_external_blocker {
5896            return;
5897        }
5898        if cfg!(debug_assertions) && !await_external_continuation {
5899            let nxtturn = self
5900                .next_turns
5901                .get(&dettid)
5902                .expect("internal invariant broken");
5903            assert!(
5904                nxtturn.req.try_read().is_some(),
5905                "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler"
5906            );
5907        }
5908        if await_external_continuation {
5909            return;
5910        }
5911
5912        // Now that the thread is signaled, it needs to be runnable for the scheduler to continue it.
5913        match self.thread_status(dettid) {
5914            ThreadStatus::Gone => {
5915                panic!(
5916                    "signal_guest: should not have just delivered a signal to a nonexistent thread..."
5917                );
5918            }
5919            ThreadStatus::Running => {
5920                let is_internal_io_polling = self
5921                    .next_turns
5922                    .get(&dettid)
5923                    .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
5924                    .is_some_and(|request| {
5925                        request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
5926                            resources
5927                                .resources
5928                                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
5929                        })
5930                    });
5931
5932                if is_internal_io_polling {
5933                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
5934                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
5935                    rsrcs.insert(
5936                        ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(signal)),
5937                        Permission::W,
5938                    );
5939                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, rsrcs);
5940                }
5941                // TODO(T137242449): other runnable requests could be reprioritized to run
5942                // sooner, but for now we leave their priorities alone.
5943            }
5944            ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
5945                // This is a commit point. The only callers are a timed pop in
5946                // step2b (`dispatch_timed_signal` -> `fire_alarm` ->
5947                // `signal_guest`) or the empty-queue time skip, both on the
5948                // scheduler thread while no guest thread holds the turn. So the
5949                // dispositions read here are the ones in force at this point in
5950                // the global order, with the exceptions named at
5951                // `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`. That is where Linux
5952                // decides delivery: a caught, unblocked signal wakes the sleeper
5953                // with EINTR, and an ignored one is discarded and never wakes it.
5954                //
5955                // The woken waiter is queued to run next, so it is the first
5956                // thread to resume and dequeue the signal. Its futex handler
5957                // still checks, in its own turn, that an interrupting signal is
5958                // pending for it. If none is, because a sibling made the signal
5959                // ignored or, under a chaos schedule, resumed first and took it,
5960                // the waiter parks again with its original absolute deadline,
5961                // as a Linux waiter that the signal never reached would still be
5962                // waiting.
5963                if let Some(interrupting) =
5964                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, kernel_signal_bit(signal as i32))
5965                {
5966                    if interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal as i32) == 0 {
5967                        // Blocked, ignored, or default-ignored for this waiter now,
5968                        // or a signal the wait holds until the call returns
5969                        // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`): the kernel
5970                        // discards an ignored signal or keeps the others pending,
5971                        // and the wait stays registered with its original
5972                        // absolute deadline. So does a default job-control stop
5973                        // that the wait defers (`FutexSignalWatch`), which the
5974                        // kernel delivers or discards when the call returns.
5975                        debug!(
5976                            "[dtid {}] signal {} does not interrupt its futex wait; leaving it parked.",
5977                            dettid, signal
5978                        );
5979                        return;
5980                    }
5981                    // The wake is committed for this signal. That commit is the
5982                    // deterministic delivery point; the woken waiter goes to the
5983                    // front of its band, so it is the next thread to resume and
5984                    // dequeue the signal (`force_unblock_thread_at`).
5985                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
5986                    rsrcs.insert(
5987                        ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(signal)),
5988                        Permission::W,
5989                    );
5990                    self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
5991                    return;
5992                }
5993                let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
5994                rsrcs.insert(
5995                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(signal)),
5996                    Permission::W,
5997                );
5998                self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, rsrcs);
5999            }
6000        }
6001    }
6002
6003    /// Classify a request that still represents the same in-flight waitid.
6004    /// A signal may arrive before its polling request is rewritten or after a prior
6005    /// notification has already materialized its scheduler wakeup.
6006    fn waitid_signal_request(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<WaitidSignalRequest> {
6007        let resources = self
6008            .next_turns
6009            .get(&dettid)
6010            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
6011            .and_then(Result::ok)?;
6012        // The two ways to be parked inside wait4/waitid: the legacy kernel
6013        // polling loop, and the scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle resource
6014        // added by the typed WaitChild work. Both must be woken; neither implies
6015        // anything about run-queue residency, which the drain decides.
6016        let waiting_on_child = resources
6017            .resources
6018            .keys()
6019            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }));
6020        let legacy_polling = resources.fyi == "waitid"
6021            && resources
6022                .resources
6023                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling);
6024        if legacy_polling || waiting_on_child {
6025            return Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked);
6026        }
6027        // Signals already materialized on this waitid request by an earlier
6028        // drain. A marked `WaitidSignals` resource instead belongs to an
6029        // interrupted InternalIOPolling request and is classified below.
6030        if resources.signal_interrupt_errno().is_some() {
6031            return None;
6032        }
6033        resources
6034            .resources
6035            .keys()
6036            .find_map(|resource| match resource {
6037                ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals) => {
6038                    Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(signals.clone()))
6039                }
6040                _ => None,
6041            })
6042    }
6043
6044    fn restartable_internal_io_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<SigWrapper>> {
6045        if !self.backend.supports_parked_write_signal_interruption {
6046            return None;
6047        }
6048        self.next_turns
6049            .get(&dettid)
6050            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
6051            .and_then(Result::ok)
6052            .and_then(|resources| {
6053                if resources.resources.len() != 1
6054                    || resources.signal_interrupt_errno() != Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
6055                {
6056                    return None;
6057                }
6058                match resources.resources.keys().next() {
6059                    Some(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling) => Some(Vec::new()),
6060                    Some(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals)) => Some(signals.clone()),
6061                    _ => None,
6062                }
6063            })
6064    }
6065
6066    /// Whether `dettid` is asleep in a precise-mode futex wait: its request is the
6067    /// bare `FutexWait` park and it is still registered as a waiter. A waiter that
6068    /// a `FUTEX_WAKE` or its timeout already requeued is not: that outcome was
6069    /// committed first, so the wait completes with it and the kernel delivers the
6070    /// pending signal when the syscall returns, as Linux does after a wakeup.
6071    #[cfg(test)]
6072    fn is_parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
6073        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid).is_some()
6074    }
6075
6076    fn parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<&FutexWaiter> {
6077        if !self.next_turns.get(&dettid).is_some_and(is_futex_request) {
6078            return None;
6079        }
6080        self.blocked
6081            .futex_waiters
6082            .values()
6083            .find_map(|waiters| waiters.iter().find(|waiter| waiter.dettid == dettid))
6084    }
6085
6086    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter's mask leaves unblocked, when
6087    /// its backend reported them. A cross-task signal outside this set cannot
6088    /// interrupt the wait whatever the dispositions become, so it is not admitted
6089    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
6090    fn parked_futex_unblocked_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
6091        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)
6092            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
6093            .map(|watch| watch.unblocked)
6094    }
6095
6096    /// The signals that end a parked precise-mode futex waiter's wait NOW, when its
6097    /// backend reports the kernel's signal state: unblocked by its mask, and caught
6098    /// or fatal-by-default under the dispositions the kernel holds at this moment
6099    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Never `SIGCHLD`, which a
6100    /// gated wait holds until the call returns (`futex_wait_held_signals`),
6101    /// unless the scheduler sends it at this commit point (`committed`).
6102    ///
6103    /// ⚠️ CALL THIS ONLY WHERE A WAKE IS COMMITTED: the step2 drain of cross-task
6104    /// signals and the scheduler-sent signal paths in step2b and the empty-queue
6105    /// time skip. There no guest thread holds the turn: every thread the
6106    /// scheduler controls is stopped, its request filled or parked. A
6107    /// disposition changes only when a guest thread runs: `rt_sigaction` in its
6108    /// turn, or `exec`, or a fault or `SA_RESETHAND` delivery in its turn. So the
6109    /// value read here is a function of the deterministic schedule, not of when
6110    /// the host ran the read.
6111    ///
6112    /// Two kinds of thread are the exception. One blocked in a call the backend
6113    /// runs outside the scheduler (`external_io_blockers`, non-sequentialized
6114    /// IO) or in `rt_sigsuspend` (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) sits in the kernel,
6115    /// not in a ptrace stop, so a signal can be delivered to it at a host-timed
6116    /// moment. An `SA_RESETHAND` handler delivered that way resets its
6117    /// process's disposition outside any turn, and this read can race it. What
6118    /// such a race can change is bounded: a waiter woken for a signal that no
6119    /// longer interrupts it finds nothing pending when its futex handler checks
6120    /// in its own turn, and parks again with its original absolute deadline.
6121    ///
6122    /// Linux decides interruption the same way, from the disposition when the
6123    /// signal is delivered, and an ignored signal is discarded rather than ending
6124    /// the wait. A disposition changed after the wait began therefore counts: a
6125    /// signal that became caught wakes the waiter, and one that became ignored
6126    /// leaves it registered with its original absolute deadline. The earlier
6127    /// design, a disposition snapshot taken when the wait began, got both wrong:
6128    /// it could leave an untimed waiter parked forever with a ready handler, and
6129    /// it restarted a timed wait with a fresh relative timeout.
6130    ///
6131    /// A read error (the thread is gone, or the file is unparseable) falls back to
6132    /// every unblocked signal. A waiter woken that way reads its own signal state
6133    /// in its turn (`handle_futex_blocking`). If that read succeeds and finds no
6134    /// interrupting signal pending, it parks again with its original absolute
6135    /// deadline, so a false wake costs one extra turn. If that read fails too,
6136    /// it is handled as a wait's first read is (`read_wait_signal_state`): a
6137    /// thread that no longer exists ends the call with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which
6138    /// nothing observes, and otherwise the run ends with a diagnostic, never an
6139    /// errno the futex call cannot return. Leaving a waiter parked for a signal
6140    /// that does interrupt it could instead deadlock it.
6141    ///
6142    /// `committed` names a signal the scheduler sends at this commit point
6143    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, from `signal_guest`), such as a `SIGCHLD` from a
6144    /// child's child-exit timer, or from a POSIX timer whose signal is
6145    /// `SIGCHLD`: the wait does not hold it unless a
6146    /// host-timed source can post it too
6147    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
6148    fn parked_futex_interrupting_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid, committed: u64) -> Option<u64> {
6149        let watch = self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)?.signal_watch?;
6150        let held =
6151            self.futex_wait_held_signals(dettid) & !(committed & !self.host_timed_signals(dettid));
6152        #[cfg(test)]
6153        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
6154            return Some(
6155                state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held,
6156            );
6157        }
6158        match read_kernel_signal_state(
6159            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.pid),
6160            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.tid),
6161        ) {
6162            Ok(state) => {
6163                Some(state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held)
6164            }
6165            Err(errno) => {
6166                debug!(
6167                    "[dtid {}] cannot read the signal state of parked futex waiter {}/{} ({}); \
6168                     treating every unblocked signal it does not hold as interrupting.",
6169                    dettid, watch.pid, watch.tid, errno
6170                );
6171                Some(watch.unblocked & !held)
6172            }
6173        }
6174    }
6175
6176    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter holds until its call
6177    /// returns, whatever its mask and dispositions: `SIGCHLD`, whoever sent it,
6178    /// and every signal a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to its
6179    /// process (`host_timed_signals`). A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to
6180    /// the waiter at a commit point is the exception
6181    /// (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`' `committed`,
6182    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). The kernel posts these at a moment set
6183    /// by host timing (`SIGCHLD` for a child's exit, stop or continue), and the
6184    /// waiter cannot tell that copy from one sent at a deterministic point. The
6185    /// guest side holds the same signals in its own checks (`KernelSignalWait`,
6186    /// and the futex pre-check in `handle_futex_blocking`)
6187    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
6188    fn futex_wait_held_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> u64 {
6189        kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | self.host_timed_signals(dettid)
6190    }
6191
6192    /// Records that `caller`, in its turn, armed a host-timed source of
6193    /// `signals`: a source the kernel fires at a moment set by host timing,
6194    /// such as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. From then on no gated wait of a process in
6195    /// `scope` ends for any of `signals`, whoever sends it
6196    /// (`host_timed_signals`). Returns what `caller`'s waits now hold.
6197    ///
6198    /// An entry is never removed: not when the guest disarms the source, nor
6199    /// at `exec`, nor when the source has fired. Hermit cannot tell a copy
6200    /// posted by the source from one a guest sends with `kill`, and a source
6201    /// that fired once may stay armed. Holding a signal too long keeps the
6202    /// behaviour gated waits had before signal interruption
6203    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>); ending a wait for a
6204    /// host-timed copy makes the run depend on host timing.
6205    ///
6206    /// The entry is keyed by the caller's process, so every thread of it is
6207    /// covered: Linux sends a parent-death signal process-directed, and the
6208    /// kernel picks the thread. A forked child starts with no entry, as it
6209    /// starts with no parent-death signal.
6210    pub fn record_host_timed_signals(
6211        &mut self,
6212        caller: DetTid,
6213        scope: HostTimedSignalScope,
6214        signals: u64,
6215    ) -> u64 {
6216        match scope {
6217            HostTimedSignalScope::Caller => {
6218                let process = self.sigchld_process(caller);
6219                *self.host_timed_signals.entry(process).or_default() |= signals;
6220            }
6221            HostTimedSignalScope::Container => self.host_timed_signals_everywhere |= signals,
6222        }
6223        self.host_timed_signals(caller)
6224    }
6225
6226    /// The signals that no gated wait of `thread` ends for, because a
6227    /// host-timed source a guest armed can post them to its process
6228    /// (`record_host_timed_signals`), or a terminal the guest may have
6229    /// inherited can (`startup_host_timed_signals`). Gated waits read this in
6230    /// their own turn.
6231    pub fn host_timed_signals(&self, thread: DetTid) -> u64 {
6232        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
6233        self.host_timed_signals_everywhere
6234            | self.host_timed_signals.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
6235    }
6236
6237    // `SIGCHLD` AND GATED WAITS
6238    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146)
6239    //
6240    // A gated wait decides interruption from the kernel's pending set in
6241    // `/proc`: the precise futex pre-check and the parked waiter's wake
6242    // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`), and the polling waits that read
6243    // the kernel's signal state each turn (`KernelSignalWait`). None of them
6244    // ends for a `SIGCHLD` that only `/proc` reports. The kernel posts `SIGCHLD` to a
6245    // parent for a child's exit, stop or continue at a moment set by host
6246    // timing (under ptrace, when the tracer releases the dying child), and
6247    // `/proc` cannot tell that copy from one a guest or the scheduler sent at
6248    // a deterministic point. The signal stays pending in the kernel and is
6249    // delivered when the call returns for another reason. Linux would end the
6250    // wait; that part of the issue is given up until Reverie reports every
6251    // delivery it holds.
6252    //
6253    // The exception is a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to the thread at
6254    // a commit point through `signal_guest`, the one a child's `ChildExit`
6255    // timer sends, or a POSIX timer whose signal is `SIGCHLD`: the resume that
6256    // names it lifts the hold for that turn
6257    // alone, so the wait ends at a point the schedule fixes
6258    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). A death without that
6259    // timer (a child killed by a signal, or leaving through `exit` in its last
6260    // thread) still leaves the signal held.
6261    //
6262    // The waits of `select`, and of `pselect6` without a temporary mask, read
6263    // the same state but hold nothing (`KernelSignalWait::for_select`), so a
6264    // pending caught `SIGCHLD` still ends them at a turn host timing can
6265    // choose: a known gap that these waits had before.
6266    //
6267    // What follows models which thread of a process the kernel gives a
6268    // `SIGCHLD` that the scheduler sends for a child's exit
6269    // (`kernel_sigchld_target`), under `models_signal_targets`.
6270
6271    /// The process whose shared queue a `SIGCHLD` for `thread` joins.
6272    fn sigchld_process(&self, thread: DetTid) -> DetPid {
6273        self.registered_process(thread).unwrap_or(thread)
6274    }
6275
6276    /// The thread of `process` that the kernel gives a `SIGCHLD` queued on the
6277    /// process's shared queue, with `preferred` the thread it tries first (the
6278    /// child's creator).
6279    ///
6280    /// Linux's `complete_signal` takes `preferred` if it does not block the
6281    /// signal, and otherwise looks for another thread that does not. Under a
6282    /// tracer, a thread held in a ptrace stop does not qualify, and the kernel
6283    /// instead leaves the signal pending for whichever thread resumes first
6284    /// without blocking it. The order here is `preferred`, then the rest in
6285    /// thread-ID order, which stands in for the kernel's round-robin
6286    /// `curr_target`. Only a chosen thread that sleeps outside the runnable
6287    /// set is woken (`arm_signaled_background`). A chosen parked futex waiter
6288    /// is not woken by the drain: its wait holds `SIGCHLD` until the call
6289    /// returns (`futex_wait_held_signals`), unless the `ChildExit` timer's own
6290    /// send names it (`wake_signaled_guest`). A running thread counts as much
6291    /// as a parked one.
6292    ///
6293    /// Every mask this uses is a function of the schedule, so the choice is
6294    /// too. Call this only at the step2 drain or a step2b timed pop, where no
6295    /// guest thread holds the turn. A thread then falls in one of two kinds:
6296    ///
6297    /// * One the scheduler controls is stopped at a request, filled or
6298    ///   parked. Its mask changes only when it runs, in its own turn, so the
6299    ///   mask read now is the one it stopped with.
6300    /// * One sleeping in a call outside the runnable set
6301    ///   (`external_io_blockers`, `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) is not stopped:
6302    ///   `rt_sigsuspend`, `ppoll` and `pselect6` install their temporary mask
6303    ///   after the scheduler released the thread, and a handler delivered to
6304    ///   it runs under a wider one, both at host-timed moments. Its live mask
6305    ///   is never read here; the mask recorded when the scheduler committed
6306    ///   its call is used instead (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`).
6307    ///
6308    /// A thread whose mask cannot be read is not a target, and only a thread
6309    /// that no longer exists has one: a stopped thread's `/proc` entry stays
6310    /// readable, and an out-of-scheduler thread's live mask is never read. A
6311    /// thread the guest kills is retired at the turn that kills it
6312    /// (`logically_kill_thread`), which takes it out of
6313    /// `process_signal_targets` before it dies. So an unreadable thread was
6314    /// killed from outside the container at a host-timed moment, the same
6315    /// envelope as any signal sent from outside; the kernel does not choose a
6316    /// dying thread either (`wants_signal` skips `PF_EXITING`). Returns `None`
6317    /// when every thread blocks the signal.
6318    fn kernel_sigchld_target(&self, process: DetPid, preferred: DetTid) -> Option<DetTid> {
6319        let sigchld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
6320        let mut threads = self.process_signal_targets(process);
6321        // Stable, so the rest stay in thread-ID order.
6322        threads.sort_by_key(|thread| *thread != preferred);
6323        threads.into_iter().find(|thread| {
6324            self.thread_signal_mask(*thread)
6325                .is_some_and(|mask| mask & sigchld == 0)
6326        })
6327    }
6328
6329    /// `thread`'s signal mask: the one its parked futex wait reported, which only
6330    /// it can change and so cannot change while it is parked; for a thread
6331    /// sleeping outside the runnable set, the one recorded when its call was
6332    /// committed (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`); and otherwise the
6333    /// kernel's (`SigBlk`) for a thread stopped at a request.
6334    fn thread_signal_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
6335        if let Some(watch) = self
6336            .parked_futex_waiter(thread)
6337            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
6338        {
6339            return Some(!watch.unblocked);
6340        }
6341        if let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&thread) {
6342            return *recorded;
6343        }
6344        self.read_thread_blocked_mask(thread)
6345    }
6346
6347    /// `thread`'s current signal mask (`SigBlk`), read from the kernel; `None`
6348    /// when it cannot be read. Ordered by the schedule only while `thread` is
6349    /// stopped at a request (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
6350    fn read_thread_blocked_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
6351        #[cfg(test)]
6352        self.test_kernel_mask_reads
6353            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
6354        #[cfg(test)]
6355        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&thread) {
6356            return Some(state.blocked);
6357        }
6358        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
6359        match read_kernel_signal_state(
6360            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
6361            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
6362        ) {
6363            Ok(state) => Some(state.blocked),
6364            Err(errno) => {
6365                debug!(
6366                    "[dtid {}] cannot read its signal mask ({}); it is not a SIGCHLD target.",
6367                    thread, errno
6368                );
6369                None
6370            }
6371        }
6372    }
6373
6374    /// Record an unambiguous cross-task signal that was physically queued while
6375    /// its target was parked in waitid, restartable internal IO polling, or a
6376    /// precise-mode futex wait, or slept in a real `rt_sigsuspend` or waited
6377    /// for its grant (`in_rt_sigsuspend`), or in an emulated `pause` or
6378    /// `nanosleep` (`sleep_signal`). The
6379    /// request rewrite is deferred to step2 so an asynchronous backend cannot
6380    /// mutate beneath a tentative selection. A futex waiter is admitted on its mask
6381    /// alone, and a sleep on its request alone; the drain, the commit point,
6382    /// decides on the rest.
6383    pub(crate) fn notify_signal_pending(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
6384        if self.waitid_signal_request(dettid).is_some()
6385            || self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid).is_some()
6386            || self
6387                .parked_futex_unblocked_signals(dettid)
6388                .is_some_and(|signals| signals & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0)
6389            || self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid)
6390            || self.admits_sleep_signal(dettid, signal)
6391        {
6392            let signals = self.pending_cross_task_signals.entry(dettid).or_default();
6393            if !signals.contains(&signal) {
6394                signals.push(signal);
6395            }
6396        }
6397    }
6398
6399    /// Whether `dettid` sleeps in a real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the run queue
6400    /// (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or waits for the grant of that call's
6401    /// request, where a signal sent now still reaches the call
6402    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`).
6403    fn in_rt_sigsuspend(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
6404        self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
6405            || self
6406                .next_turns
6407                .get(&dettid)
6408                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
6409                .and_then(Result::ok)
6410                .is_some_and(|request| {
6411                    request
6412                        .resources
6413                        .keys()
6414                        .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)))
6415                })
6416    }
6417
6418    // Force a thread out blocking and into the runnable state, replacing its resource request.
6419    fn force_unblock_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources) {
6420        self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, false);
6421    }
6422
6423    /// [`Scheduler::force_unblock_thread`], queuing the thread at the front of its
6424    /// priority band when `front` is set. A precise futex waiter woken for a
6425    /// signal goes to the front, so it is the next thread to resume and dequeue
6426    /// the signal it was woken for, which is the thread the scheduler chose for
6427    /// it (`kernel_sigchld_target`, and the cross-task sender's own target). A
6428    /// sibling queued ahead of it and not blocking the signal would otherwise
6429    /// resume first and take it, leaving the waiter a wake with nothing to be
6430    /// interrupted by (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
6431    ///
6432    /// A thread held at a happens-before gate is left held. Its pending
6433    /// request is the gate's checkpoint, and the guest does not re-check the
6434    /// gate after a substituted resume, so replacing that request would let
6435    /// the thread past a hard edge before its BEFORE anchor fired. A held
6436    /// thread is runnable as far as Linux is concerned, only not scheduled:
6437    /// the signal stays pending in the kernel and is delivered when the gate
6438    /// opens and the thread resumes, as for any runnable thread that is not
6439    /// running.
6440    fn force_unblock_thread_at(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources, front: bool) {
6441        // The consumed alarm already owns this exact response. A later
6442        // physical signal must not replace its fatal continuation.
6443        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
6444            return;
6445        }
6446        if self
6447            .happens_before
6448            .as_ref()
6449            .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dettid))
6450        {
6451            info!(
6452                "[dtid {}] held at a happens-before gate; leaving it held, its signal pending",
6453                dettid
6454            );
6455            return;
6456        }
6457        info!(
6458            "[dtid {}] removing blocking entries and requeuing thread",
6459            dettid
6460        );
6461        self.remove_blocking_entries(&dettid);
6462        // The substituted request resolves any polling wait the thread was in.
6463        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid);
6464
6465        if let Some(nxt) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) {
6466            // Counterfeit the entry as though the thread had requested this resource from the start:
6467            nxt.req = Ivar::full(Ok(rsrcs));
6468        }
6469
6470        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a force-unblocked thread (e.g. woken by a
6471        // signal or ready I/O) is normally requeued at the back of its priority
6472        // level, so it runs after everything already queued. Randomizing whether
6473        // it jumps to the front instead varies the order in which a just-woken
6474        // thread races the threads it was contending with -- surfacing
6475        // lock-ordering / wakeup-ordering races. Reproducible under `--fuzz-seed`.
6476        //
6477        // Chaos keeps its draw for a signal-woken futex waiter too, so the same
6478        // PRNG stream is consumed. A waiter that then resumes after a sibling
6479        // took its signal parks again with its original deadline.
6480        let to_front = if self.chaos_target_races {
6481            chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &[true, false]).unwrap_or(false)
6482        } else {
6483            front
6484        };
6485        if to_front {
6486            self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
6487        } else {
6488            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
6489        }
6490    }
6491
6492    /// Check on threads executing blocking syscalls outside the runnable set.
6493    fn step2c_process_io_blockers(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6494        if !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
6495            || !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
6496        {
6497            // A nondeterministic snapshot of which backgrounded actions are ready right now:
6498            let mut blockers: Vec<(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)> = self
6499                .blocked
6500                .external_io_blockers
6501                .iter()
6502                .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(dtid)))
6503                .chain(
6504                    self.blocked
6505                        .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
6506                        .iter()
6507                        .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, true)),
6508                )
6509                .collect();
6510            blockers.sort_by_key(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid);
6511            let ready: Vec<DetTid> = blockers
6512                .iter()
6513                .filter(|(dtid, op_id, signal_can_complete)| {
6514                    let nt = self
6515                        .next_turns
6516                        .get(dtid)
6517                        .expect("internal invariant broken");
6518                    if let Some(Ok(req)) = nt.req.try_read() {
6519                        blocking_request_is_ready(&req, *op_id, *signal_can_complete)
6520                    } else {
6521                        false
6522                    }
6523                })
6524                .map(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid)
6525                .collect();
6526            debug!(
6527                "Nondeterministic status of backgrounded operations: out of {}, completed on {}, dtids: {:?}",
6528                blockers.len(),
6529                ready.len(),
6530                ready
6531            );
6532
6533            let requeue_ready = |scheduler: &mut Self, ready: &[DetTid]| {
6534                for ready_dtid in ready {
6535                    info!(
6536                        "[step2] Reschedule formerly backgrounded dtid {:?}",
6537                        ready_dtid
6538                    );
6539                    let external = scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
6540                    scheduler.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(ready_dtid);
6541                    let sigsuspend = scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
6542                    let _ = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(ready_dtid);
6543                    assert!(
6544                        external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
6545                        "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
6546                    );
6547                    scheduler.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(*ready_dtid);
6548                }
6549            };
6550
6551            // FIXME TODO (T137183027): for record/replay to work properly, we need to ALLOW the
6552            // "Nondeterminstic algorithm" below, but record & replay those scheduler events. In
6553            // the meantime, use a deterministic eager policy once there is no other runnable work.
6554            if self.recordreplay_modes {
6555                // A call that replay serves from the recording cannot block, but it
6556                // changes guest state while it runs: the stand-in for an accepted
6557                // connection takes a descriptor slot. Commit no other turn until every
6558                // such call has finished, so that each takes effect right after its own
6559                // turn rather than among other threads' turns at a host-timed point.
6560                // Waiting changes only how long the scheduler spins, not what it commits
6561                // next. It also makes the readiness of these calls below independent of
6562                // host timing.
6563                let log_served: Vec<DetTid> =
6564                    self.blocked.replay_log_served.iter().copied().collect();
6565                if log_served.iter().any(|dtid| !ready.contains(dtid)) {
6566                    trace!(
6567                        "[step2] waiting for background calls replay serves from the log, dtids {:?}",
6568                        log_served
6569                    );
6570                    std::thread::yield_now();
6571                    return Err(SkipTurn);
6572                }
6573
6574                // Only *real* deterministic work should defer external-IO harvesting.
6575                // Internal pollers sit at LAST_PRIORITY and are frequently spinning on
6576                // the very result an external-IO blocker will produce (e.g. the reader
6577                // side of `echo hi | cat`, where one stage uses InternalIOPolling while
6578                // its peer is backgrounded on BlockingExternalIO). Treat a run queue
6579                // that holds only pollers as "no deterministic work" so we still harvest
6580                // completed IO below; a queued poller must not starve a ready blocker.
6581                let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers();
6582
6583                // Deterministic work is runnable: let it proceed. Waiting here while such
6584                // work exists can deadlock thread creation -- the parent and new child
6585                // cannot complete clone while an existing worker blocks indefinitely in
6586                // epoll_wait.
6587                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
6588                    return Ok(());
6589                }
6590
6591                // Replay readmits each call at the turn the recording logged, not when
6592                // it finishes (see `rejoin_log`).
6593                if self.rejoin_replay.is_some() {
6594                    return self.step2c_replay_rejoin(&blockers, &ready, requeue_ready);
6595                }
6596
6597                // Readmit those calls first, in thread order; every one has finished.
6598                // Other background calls are readmitted below once none of them remain.
6599                if !log_served.is_empty() {
6600                    requeue_ready(self, &log_served);
6601                    return Ok(());
6602                }
6603
6604                // Reschedule every blocker whose IO has completed so its continuation can
6605                // consume the recorded result. Harvesting all ready blockers (not just the
6606                // first) and doing so even when pollers are queued is what breaks the
6607                // record-mode pipe livelock: previously a queued poller made this branch
6608                // return early forever, so the completed read/write was never rescheduled
6609                // and the poller spun on data that never arrived.
6610                //
6611                // Which pass finds a call finished depends on host timing, so record
6612                // logs the turn of each readmission for replay to follow.
6613                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
6614                if !ready.is_empty() {
6615                    self.log_rejoin(&blockers, &ready);
6616                    requeue_ready(self, &ready);
6617                    return Ok(());
6618                }
6619
6620                // `rt_sigsuspend` has no spontaneous completion: with no real
6621                // external IO left, continue to step2d so a finite timer can
6622                // fire or the signal-less wait can receive a terminal verdict.
6623                if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
6624                    return Ok(());
6625                }
6626
6627                // No completed IO yet, but pollers are queued: let one poll. A poller
6628                // can be what the blocker waits for, not only the other way round: a
6629                // client's read on a TCP connection waits for the server's accept, and
6630                // the server polls that accept in turn
6631                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880). Spinning here would
6632                // never run it. Readiness is still checked, and a ready blocker
6633                // harvested, before every poll. Whether a call had finished before
6634                // this poll is host-timed; the rejoin log above makes replay agree.
6635                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() {
6636                    return Ok(());
6637                }
6638
6639                // No completed IO yet and nothing queued, but a thread sleeps
6640                // until a reachable deadline: let step2d move virtual time
6641                // there, as `hermit run` does below. The blocked call can wait
6642                // on that thread, a client that sleeps before it connects or
6643                // writes, and spinning would never wake it
6644                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3881). Whether the
6645                // call finished before this move is host-timed; the rejoin log
6646                // records the wake count with the turn so replay agrees.
6647                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
6648                if self.next_deadline_is_reachable() {
6649                    return Ok(());
6650                }
6651
6652                // No completed IO yet, and nothing to run. The
6653                // blocking syscalls are executing in the host kernel; go around the loop
6654                // and re-check readiness. (Still a busy-wait; see T137183027 for the
6655                // record-the-nondeterministic-event fix.)
6656                trace!(
6657                    "[step2] eagerly waiting on external IO for dtids {:?}. spinning.",
6658                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
6659                );
6660                std::thread::yield_now();
6661                return Err(SkipTurn);
6662            } // End region which should be deleted.
6663
6664            // Use the same deterministic-work-first policy as record/replay. Host
6665            // completion timing must not decide whether a ready continuation overtakes
6666            // guest work that was already runnable. Pollers are excluded because they
6667            // commonly wait for the completed operation and would otherwise starve it.
6668            let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers();
6669            if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
6670                return Ok(());
6671            }
6672
6673            if !ready.is_empty() {
6674                requeue_ready(self, &ready);
6675            }
6676            if self.run_queue.is_empty()
6677                && self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty()
6678                && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
6679            {
6680                // TODO (T137184765): for now we just WAIT eagerly whenever there is blocking
6681                // external IO and else to do. We implement a busy-wait by going around the
6682                // scheduler loop again.
6683                trace!(
6684                    "[step2] TEMPORARY2: eagerly blocking on external IO for dtids {:?}.  SPINNING!",
6685                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
6686                );
6687                std::thread::yield_now();
6688                Err(SkipTurn)
6689            } else {
6690                // Productive work to do, irrespcetive of what's blocked, so let's get to it.
6691                Ok(())
6692            }
6693        } else {
6694            Ok(())
6695        }
6696    }
6697
6698    /// `hermit record`: log that `step2c_process_io_blockers` readmits the
6699    /// finished calls of `ready` at this turn (see `rejoin_log`).
6700    fn log_rejoin(&mut self, blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)], ready: &[DetTid]) {
6701        let Some(writer) = self.rejoin_writer.as_mut() else {
6702            return;
6703        };
6704        let rejoin = Rejoin {
6705            turn: self.turn,
6706            wakes: self.empty_queue_wakes,
6707            calls: ready
6708                .iter()
6709                .map(|dtid| {
6710                    let (_, op_id, _) = blockers
6711                        .iter()
6712                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
6713                        .expect("a ready thread is a blocker");
6714                    (*dtid, op_id.sequence)
6715                })
6716                .collect(),
6717        };
6718        writer
6719            .append(&rejoin)
6720            .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("cannot write the rejoin log: {err}"));
6721    }
6722
6723    /// How long replay waits, with nothing runnable and no readmission due, for
6724    /// work to appear, or at a logged readmission for its calls to finish,
6725    /// before it refuses (see `step2c_replay_rejoin`).
6726    const REJOIN_STALL_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
6727
6728    /// `hermit replay`: readmit backgrounded calls at the turns the recording
6729    /// logged (see `rejoin_log`). Called where record readmits finished calls,
6730    /// after the checks the two runs share.
6731    ///
6732    /// - A readmission logged for this turn waits until each of its calls has
6733    ///   finished, without committing a turn, then readmits them in the logged
6734    ///   order. Record readmitted them in a pass at this turn, before any other
6735    ///   turn could commit. A call still unfinished after `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE`
6736    ///   is refused rather than waited on forever.
6737    /// - Until then a finished call stays parked, and queued threads run as
6738    ///   they did in record.
6739    /// - Replay refuses if it reaches a later turn than a logged readmission,
6740    ///   or if the parked call is not the logged one.
6741    ///   With nothing runnable and no readmission due, record spun until a call
6742    ///   finished; replay waits `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE` for other work to appear
6743    ///   (a thread admission, say) and then refuses rather than hang.
6744    ///
6745    /// By induction on turns, the two schedules agree up to the next logged
6746    /// turn: everything host-timed before it (poll results, readmissions) is
6747    /// in the recording, so whatever let the call finish in record has also
6748    /// happened in replay by then.
6749    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
6750    fn step2c_replay_rejoin(
6751        &mut self,
6752        blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)],
6753        ready: &[DetTid],
6754        requeue_ready: impl Fn(&mut Self, &[DetTid]),
6755    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6756        let next = match self.rejoin_replay.as_ref() {
6757            Some(rejoins) => rejoins.front().cloned(),
6758            None => unreachable!("only replay follows the rejoin log"),
6759        };
6760        let describe = |rejoin: &Rejoin| {
6761            rejoin
6762                .calls
6763                .iter()
6764                .map(|(dtid, sequence)| format!("thread {} call {}", dtid.as_raw(), sequence))
6765                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
6766                .join(", ")
6767        };
6768        let point = (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes);
6769        if let Some(next) = next {
6770            if next.point() < point {
6771                let reason = format!(
6772                    "the recording readmitted {} at turn {} after {} timer wakes, and replay \
6773                     reached turn {} after {} first",
6774                    describe(&next),
6775                    next.turn,
6776                    next.wakes,
