6777                    self.turn,
6778                    self.empty_queue_wakes
6779                );
6780                return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
6781            }
6782            if next.point() == point {
6783                for (dtid, sequence) in &next.calls {
6784                    let parked = blockers
6785                        .iter()
6786                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
6787                        .map(|(_, op_id, _)| op_id.sequence);
6788                    if parked != Some(*sequence) {
6789                        let reason = format!(
6790                            "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, but replay has {} parked there",
6791                            describe(&next),
6792                            next.turn,
6793                            parked.map_or("no such call".to_string(), |parked| format!(
6794                                "call {parked} of thread {}",
6795                                dtid.as_raw()
6796                            ))
6797                        );
6798                        return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
6799                    }
6800                }
6801                let due: Vec<DetTid> = next.calls.iter().map(|(dtid, _)| *dtid).collect();
6802                if due.iter().all(|dtid| ready.contains(dtid)) {
6803                    self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
6804                    if let Some(rejoins) = self.rejoin_replay.as_mut() {
6805                        rejoins.pop_front();
6806                    }
6807                    requeue_ready(self, &due);
6808                    return Ok(());
6809                }
6810                let since = *self
6811                    .rejoin_stalled_since
6812                    .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
6813                if since.elapsed() >= Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
6814                    let reason = format!(
6815                        "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, and replay waited {} s there \
6816                         for those calls to finish",
6817                        describe(&next),
6818                        next.turn,
6819                        Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE.as_secs()
6820                    );
6821                    return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
6822                }
6823                trace!(
6824                    "[step2] waiting at turn {} for the logged readmission of {:?}",
6825                    self.turn, due
6826                );
6827                std::thread::yield_now();
6828                return Err(SkipTurn);
6829            }
6830        }
6831        // Record readmitted nothing in this pass. `rt_sigsuspend` alone goes on
6832        // to step2d, queued pollers run, and step2d wakes a reachable timed
6833        // event, as in record.
6834        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
6835            || !self.run_queue.is_empty()
6836            || self.next_deadline_is_reachable()
6837        {
6838            self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
6839            return Ok(());
6840        }
6841        let since = *self
6842            .rejoin_stalled_since
6843            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
6844        if since.elapsed() < Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
6845            std::thread::yield_now();
6846            return Err(SkipTurn);
6847        }
6848        let reason = format!(
6849            "at turn {} nothing can run, and the next logged readmission is {}",
6850            self.turn,
6851            match self
6852                .rejoin_replay
6853                .as_ref()
6854                .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
6855            {
6856                Some(next) => format!("{} at turn {}", describe(next), next.turn),
6857                None => "none".to_string(),
6858            }
6859        );
6860        self.refuse_rejoin(reason)
6861    }
6862
6863    /// Whether step2d, with the run queue empty, would wake a timed event: one
6864    /// is pending, and the earliest is not `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`.
6865    fn next_deadline_is_reachable(&self) -> bool {
6866        self.blocked
6867            .timed_waiters
6868            .next_deadline()
6869            .is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_indefinite())
6870    }
6871
6872    /// Replay's refusal of a run that ends with logged readmissions it never
6873    /// reached: the recording's schedule went on past where replay's ended.
6874    fn unreplayed_rejoins(&self) -> Option<RejoinRefusal> {
6875        let rejoins = self.rejoin_replay.as_ref()?;
6876        let next = rejoins.front()?;
6877        Some(RejoinRefusal {
6878            reason: format!(
6879                "the run ended at turn {} with {} logged readmissions not replayed, the first at \
6880                 turn {}",
6881                self.turn,
6882                rejoins.len(),
6883                next.turn
6884            ),
6885        })
6886    }
6887
6888    /// Record a `RejoinRefusal` for the scheduler loop to end the run with.
6889    fn refuse_rejoin(&mut self, reason: String) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6890        if self.rejoin_refusal.is_none() {
6891            let refusal = RejoinRefusal { reason };
6892            tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
6893            self.rejoin_refusal = Some(refusal);
6894        }
6895        Err(SkipTurn)
6896    }
6897
6898    /// Render one blocked thread's pending request, with a stable resource order.
6899    ///
6900    /// `Resources::resources` is a `HashMap`, so its iteration order is not
6901    /// reproducible; sort the rendered entries. Reads the `Ivar`'s contents
6902    /// rather than `Debug`-printing the `Ivar`, whose parked `Waker` carries raw
6903    /// host pointers.
6904    fn render_pending_request(req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>) -> String {
6905        match req.try_read() {
6906            None => "<no request pending>".to_owned(),
6907            Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => "<thread exited>".to_owned(),
6908            Some(Ok(rsrc)) => {
6909                let mut held: Vec<String> = rsrc
6910                    .resources
6911                    .iter()
6912                    .map(|(rid, perm)| match rid {
6913                        // Spell the sentinel out. Its derived `Debug` is
6914                        // `SleepUntil(LogicalTime(18446744073709551615))`, and a
6915                        // reader who has to decode that number by hand is
6916                        // exactly the reader this report failed.
6917                        ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline) if deadline.is_indefinite() => {
6918                            format!("SleepUntil(INDEFINITE): {:?}", perm)
6919                        }
6920                        _ => format!("{:?}: {:?}", rid, perm),
6921                    })
6922                    .collect();
6923                held.sort();
6924                let mut rendered = if held.is_empty() {
6925                    "<no resources>".to_owned()
6926                } else {
6927                    held.join(", ")
6928                };
6929                if rsrc.poll_attempt != 0 {
6930                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (poll_attempt {})", rsrc.poll_attempt);
6931                }
6932                if !rsrc.fyi.is_empty() {
6933                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (fyi {:?})", rsrc.fyi);
6934                }
6935                rendered
6936            }
6937        }
6938    }
6939
6940    /// Render a futex key with its guest address in hex.
6941    ///
6942    /// `FutexID`'s derived `Debug` prints the address in decimal, which is
6943    /// deterministic but unusable: a reader has to match it against a guest
6944    /// symbol or a `futex(...)` line in the DETLOG, and both are hex.
6945    fn render_futex_id(futex_id: &FutexID) -> String {
6946        match futex_id {
6947            FutexID::Private { mm, address } => {
6948                format!("private {:?} address {:#x}", mm, address)
6949            }
6950            FutexID::Shared { object, offset } => {
6951                format!("shared {:?} offset {:#x}", object, offset)
6952            }
6953        }
6954    }
6955
6956    /// Render a `LogicalTime` deadline, naming the no-deadline sentinel.
6957    fn render_deadline(deadline: LogicalTime) -> String {
6958        if deadline.is_indefinite() {
6959            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)".to_owned()
6960        } else {
6961            deadline.to_string()
6962        }
6963    }
6964
6965    /// Name every blocked class that is actually holding the run.
6966    ///
6967    /// Derived from state rather than passed in by the caller, so the headline
6968    /// cannot contradict the body it sits above. Branch order alone would
6969    /// mis-file a genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer
6970    /// registered: `step2d_handle_empty_queue` reaches the indefinite arm
6971    /// whenever *any* timed waiter exists, so a caller-supplied headline would
6972    /// read "waiting indefinitely" while the futex pool is the real story. The
6973    /// body always listed both; the headline is what lands in a bug report.
6974    fn describe_terminal_waiters(&self) -> String {
6975        let mut classes: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
6976        if !self.blocked.no_futex_waiters() {
6977            classes.push("thread(s) waiting on futex");
6978        }
6979        if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
6980            classes.push(
6981                "thread(s) waiting indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time)",
6982            );
6983        }
6984        if !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
6985            classes.push("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal");
6986        }
6987        if self
6988            .happens_before
6989            .as_ref()
6990            .is_some_and(|hb| !hb.parked.is_empty())
6991        {
6992            classes.push("thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire");
6993        }
6994        if classes.is_empty() {
6995            // Defensive: every caller fires with at least one class present.
6996            "thread(s) blocked with no possible wake".to_owned()
6997        } else {
6998            classes.join(", and ")
6999        }
7000    }
7001
7002    /// Build the deadlock report. **Must be byte-identical across runs of the
7003    /// same program**: this text reaches stderr, and emitting a
7004    /// host-dependent string from a deterministic execution engine is a defect
7005    /// in its own right, whether or not any comparator currently catches it.
7006    ///
7007    /// The obvious implementation -- `{:?}` of `run_queue`, `next_turns` and
7008    /// `blocked` -- is *not* reproducible. Three independent sources of
7009    /// run-to-run variation hide in those structures:
7010    ///
7011    /// 1. `ThreadNextTurn` and `FutexWaiter` hold [`Ivar`]s whose `Debug` prints
7012    ///    the parked waker as `Waker { data: 0x55.., vtable: 0x55.. }` -- raw
7013    ///    host pointers that move with ASLR on every run.
7014    /// 2. `BlockedPool::futex_waiters` is a `HashMap` and
7015    ///    `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, so both iterate in a
7016    ///    randomized order whenever they hold more than one entry.
7017    /// 3. `Resources::resources` is itself a `HashMap`, so even a single
7018    ///    thread's resource list is unordered.
7019    ///
7020    /// So every collection below is sorted on a stable key, and only
7021    /// guest-level identities are printed: dettids, resource ids, futex keys and
7022    /// logical deadlines, all of which Detcore already guarantees to be
7023    /// deterministic. No host pointer is emitted.
7024    fn format_terminal_deadlock(&self) -> String {
7025        // ⚠️ ADDING A SECTION HERE? RENDER `dtid` OR A STABLE ORDINAL, NEVER A
7026        // DEBUG-FORMATTED ID. The rule is stated in full in the doc comment above
7027        // and repeated here because that is not where authors edit: the doc
7028        // comment already warned that the obvious `{:?}` implementation is not
7029        // reproducible, and a later change added a section that did it anyway.
7030        //
7031        // A host-influenced counter is the failure that survives review, because
7032        // it LOOKS like a small integer. `{:?}` of a wrapper type, a raw thread
7033        // id, an allocation counter or anything seeded from host state will differ
7034        // run to run while reading like an ordinary index.
7035        //
7036        // Print only identities Detcore already determinizes: dettids, resource
7037        // ids, futex keys, logical deadlines, or a position computed by sorting on
7038        // one of those.
7039        //
7040        // ⚠️ AND EXTEND THE FIXTURE. The determinism test cannot see a section its
7041        // fixture never renders, so a section that only appears under state
7042        // `deadlocked_scheduler` does not build is UNGUARDED however good the
7043        // banned list is. If your section needs different scheduler state, add
7044        // that state to the fixture in the same change.
7045        let mut out = format!(
7046            "Deadlock detected: {}, but no runnable threads left.\n",
7047            self.describe_terminal_waiters()
7048        );
7049        let _ = writeln!(
7050            out,
7051            "  turn {}, committed time {}",
7052            self.turn, self.committed_time
7053        );
7054        let _ = writeln!(out, "  run queue: {} runnable", self.run_queue.len());
7055
7056        let _ = writeln!(out, "  threads ({}), by dettid:", self.next_turns.len());
7057        // `next_turns` is a BTreeMap, so this walk is already ordered.
7058        for (dettid, next_turn) in self.next_turns.iter() {
7059            let _ = writeln!(
7060                out,
7061                "    dtid {}: {}",
7062                dettid,
7063                Self::render_pending_request(&next_turn.req)
7064            );
7065        }
7066
7067        let mut futexes: Vec<String> = self
7068            .blocked
7069            .futex_waiters
7070            .iter()
7071            .filter(|(_, waiters)| !waiters.is_empty())
7072            .map(|(futex_id, waiters)| {
7073                let mut parked: Vec<String> = waiters
7074                    .iter()
7075                    .map(|w| format!("dtid {} (bitset {:#010x})", w.dettid, w.bitset))
7076                    .collect();
7077                parked.sort();
7078                format!(
7079                    "    {}: {}",
7080                    Self::render_futex_id(futex_id),
7081                    parked.join(", ")
7082                )
7083            })
7084            .collect();
7085        futexes.sort();
7086        if futexes.is_empty() {
7087            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters: none");
7088        } else {
7089            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters ({}), by futex:", futexes.len());
7090            for line in futexes {
7091                let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", line);
7092            }
7093        }
7094
7095        let mut timed_out: Vec<DetTid> = self
7096            .blocked
7097            .timed_out_futex_waiters
7098            .iter()
7099            .copied()
7100            .collect();
7101        timed_out.sort();
7102        let _ = writeln!(
7103            out,
7104            "  timed-out futex waiters: {}",
7105            render_tid_list(&timed_out)
7106        );
7107
7108        let timed: Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)> = self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect();
7109        if timed.is_empty() {
7110            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters: none");
7111        } else {
7112            // `TimedEvents` is backed by a BTreeMap keyed on the deadline, so
7113            // this is already in deadline order.
7114            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters ({}), by deadline:", timed.len());
7115            for (deadline, evt) in timed {
7116                let _ = writeln!(out, "    {}: {}", Self::render_deadline(deadline), evt);
7117            }
7118        }
7119
7120        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
7121            let _ = writeln!(out, "  external IO blockers: none");
7122        } else {
7123            // BTreeMap: already ordered by dettid.
7124            let _ = writeln!(
7125                out,
7126                "  external IO blockers ({}), by dettid:",
7127                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len()
7128            );
7129            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.external_io_blockers.iter() {
7130                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
7131            }
7132        }
7133
7134        if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
7135            let _ = writeln!(out, "  rt_sigsuspend blockers: none");
7136        } else {
7137            let _ = writeln!(
7138                out,
7139                "  rt_sigsuspend blockers ({}), by dettid:",
7140                self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len()
7141            );
7142            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.iter() {
7143                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
7144                // The mask recorded when the call was committed, when the
7145                // scheduler models signal targets: a signal it blocks cannot
7146                // end the wait, which is often why nothing can.
7147                if let Some(Some(mask)) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(dettid) {
7148                    let _ = writeln!(out, "      temporary mask {:#x}", mask);
7149                }
7150            }
7151        }
7152
7153        // Both are BTreeSets, so already ordered.
7154        let deferred: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.iter().copied().collect();
7155        let ready: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.iter().copied().collect();
7156        let _ = writeln!(
7157            out,
7158            "  sigchld deferred: {}; sigchld ready: {}",
7159            render_tid_list(&deferred),
7160            render_tid_list(&ready)
7161        );
7162        out
7163    }
7164
7165    /// Report a permanently blocked guest and abort the run.
7166    ///
7167    /// Reached only when the run queue is empty *and* every remaining thread is
7168    /// blocked on something no future scheduler turn can supply. In a
7169    /// sequentialized deterministic run the scheduler is the only source of
7170    /// wakeups, so "no thread can be woken now" is also "no thread can ever be
7171    /// woken": the condition is permanent, not transient. Linux would leave such
7172    /// a process hung forever; reporting it is strictly more useful than
7173    /// reproducing the hang, and it is the established Detcore behaviour for the
7174    /// futex case (`docs/ERROR_CATALOG.md`).
7175    ///
7176    /// `waiters` names *what* is blocked; everything else is shared, so every
7177    /// deadlock class prints the same reproducible shape.
7178    ///
7179    /// Records the report and returns [`SkipTurn`] rather than panicking.
7180    /// `sched_loop_inner` picks it up and exits the container, next to the two
7181    /// existing `--stop-after-*` fatal exits. A panic here would NOT end the
7182    /// run: the scheduler is a `tokio::spawn`ed task whose panic the harness
7183    /// captures, leaving every guest thread parked forever on an
7184    /// `Ivar<SchedResponse>` only the scheduler could fill, so the process hangs
7185    /// until an external timeout kills it. Unwinding out of
7186    /// `do_a_turn_blocking` would also poison the scheduler mutex.
7187    fn report_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> SkipTurn {
7188        let report = self.format_terminal_deadlock();
7189        // A terminal state with threads held at happens-before gates that can
7190        // never open is a fault of the spec, not of Hermit: refuse it by naming
7191        // the BEFORE anchors that never fired, with the deadlock report below
7192        // for diagnosis.
7193        let refusal = self
7194            .happens_before
7195            .as_ref()
7196            .and_then(HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal);
7197        // Keep the first verdict: it names the state that actually wedged.
7198        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
7199            if let Some(refusal) = refusal {
7200                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!("{}\n{}", refusal, report));
7201                self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
7202            } else {
7203                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(report);
7204            }
7205        }
7206        SkipTurn
7207    }
7208
7209    /// Take the pending terminal-deadlock report, if the scheduler produced one.
7210    fn take_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
7211        self.terminal_deadlock.take()
7212    }

7214    /// Test seam: see [`SchedLoopPoint`].
7215    #[cfg(not(test))]
7216    #[inline(always)]
7217    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, _point: SchedLoopPoint) {}
7218
7219    /// Test seam: run the current thread's installed loop probe, if any.
7220    #[cfg(test)]
7221    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, point: SchedLoopPoint) {
7222        test::fire_loop_probe(point, self);
7223    }
7224
7225    fn step2d_handle_empty_queue(
7226        &mut self,
7227        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
7228    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7229        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue);
7230        let decision = self.step2d_decide_empty_queue(global_time);
7231        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue);
7232        decision
7233    }
7234
7235    fn step2d_decide_empty_queue(
7236        &mut self,
7237        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
7238    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7239        // Threads whose gate opened were re-admitted by `step2_drain_prefix`;
7240        // threads still parked wait on a source that has not fired. They are
7241        // blocked, not gone: an empty queue with only them (and no timer or
7242        // external input that could let a source run) is a deadlock to report,
7243        // not an exit to fizzle into
7244        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149). A child wait counts
7245        // as input that may still arrive, unless every child it could reap is
7246        // held at a gate: such a child can only exit after it runs, so with
7247        // nothing runnable the wait is part of the deadlock
7248        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
7249        let hb_parked_empty = self
7250            .happens_before
7251            .as_ref()
7252            .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty());
7253        let timed_empty = self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty();
7254        let external_waits_empty = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
7255            && self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty()
7256            && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
7257        let external_waits_settled = external_waits_empty
7258            || (self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
7259                && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
7260                && self.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
7261        let rt_sigsuspend_empty = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty();
7262        let futex_empty = self.blocked.no_futex_waiters();
7263
7264        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
7265            let logically_empty = futex_empty
7266                && timed_empty
7267                && external_waits_empty
7268                && rt_sigsuspend_empty
7269                && hb_parked_empty;
7270            // Report the empty state from logical state alone, BEFORE the
7271            // physical-exit wait below and once per empty state. Both halves are
7272            // what make the line a function of Detcore scheduling.
7273            //
7274            // Before the physical-exit wait: that wait holds the loop for the
7275            // ptrace supervisor's final wait status, which arrives at a
7276            // host-chosen moment. When the report sat after the wait, it was
7277            // logged only if the status had landed before this step ran, and
7278            // otherwise the loop exited without it -- zero or one lines for the
7279            // same logical execution
7280            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360).
7281            //
7282            // Once per empty state: the loop can reach this step again before it
7283            // exits, while it waits for that status or drains a removal queued
7284            // by a dead thread's second, reactive exit hook. How many times it
7285            // does is host timing, and neither thing it waits for is a thread,
7286            // so the state it reports has not changed
7287            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223). See
7288            // `empty_queue_kick_turn`.
7289            //
7290            // The branch's control flow is unchanged: the wait still gates the
7291            // deadlock report and the timer fast-forward, and every path below
7292            // still skips this turn. Only where and how often the line is
7293            // logged changed; the guest cannot observe either.
7294            if !logically_empty {
7295                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
7296            } else if self.empty_queue_kick_turn != Some(self.turn) {
7297                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = Some(self.turn);
7298                // `info!`, and that level is load-bearing. Restored from `trace!`
7299                // by owner ruling after 08ff51a33e demoted it.
7300                //
7301                // THE DEMOTION'S ARGUMENT AND WHY IT WAS REJECTED. It ran: how
7302                // many times this branch is reached depends on when the host
7303                // delivers a child's final wait status, that is an external
7304                // real-time event, an INFO line driven by one is a determinism
7305                // hazard by construction, so keep the loop sub-INFO. The
7306                // measurement offered with it was real -- over 312 concurrent
7307                // SaBRe cell-runs, 4 diverged, and in each the whole difference
7308                // was this line plus one unrelated WARN.
7309                //
7310                // The owner's ruling: this fizzle is part of the deterministic
7311                // scheduling model, not record/replay external-IO terrain, so it
7312                // SHOULD be a deterministic function of detcore scheduling. If it
7313                // is not, that is a hermit DEFECT, and demoting the line hid the
7314                // defect instead of fixing it. The previous note ended "do not
7315                // promote this back without making the host's wait-status
7316                // delivery deterministic, which is not possible" -- but making it
7317                // deterministic is exactly the work owed, not a reason to stop
7318                // reporting it.
7319                //
7320                // AND THE DEFECT IS REAL AND LARGER THAN THIS LINE. Measured
7321                // 2026-08-24 on the CI-staged SaBRe artifact: a guest that forks
7322                // and reaps its child with `wait4(WNOHANG)` diverges 36 of 50
7323                // under `--verify-strict`, while ptrace is 0 of 50 on the same
7324                // guest. The divergence is not confined to logging -- the guest
7325                // ITSELF executes different work, 355 syscalls with 4 `wait4`
7326                // calls in one run against 354 with 3 in the other. The
7327                // scheduler's committed non-poll decisions are byte-identical
7328                // (68 in both), so what varies is how many times the parent is
7329                // told "not yet". Silencing this line would have left that
7330                // unreported.
7331                //
7332                // If this line is noisy again, the fix is to make a child's exit
7333                // become observable to its parent at a deterministic point, not
7334                // to lower the level.
7335                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
7336                    let record_suffix = crate::detlog::record_suffix(
7337                        crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerEmptyQueueKick,
7338                    );
7339                    info!(
7340                        "scheduler (step2_process_blocked): zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.{}",
7341                        record_suffix
7342                    );
7343                }
7344            }
7345            if !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty() {
7346                // The SaBRe plugin has run the child process's logical exit hook, but the ptrace
7347                // supervisor has not received its final wait status. Fast-forwarding the next
7348                // timer here can fire a parent's timeout before the child becomes waitable.
7349                trace!(
7350                    "waiting for physical process exits before empty-queue timer fast-forward: {:?}",
7351                    self.pending_physical_process_exits
7352                );
7353                std::thread::yield_now();
7354                return Err(SkipTurn);
7355            }
7356            // When the run queue is empty, we sometimes need to give things a kick.
7357            if logically_empty {
7358                return Err(SkipTurn);
7359            } else if timed_empty
7360                && external_waits_settled
7361                && (!futex_empty || !rt_sigsuspend_empty || !hb_parked_empty)
7362            {
7363                return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock());
7364            } else if !timed_empty {
7365                // Only a *reachable* deadline justifies fast-forwarding the clock.
7366                // `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` is the sentinel a `pause(2)` (or a
7367                // far-future timer that saturated the clock) registers to mean "no
7368                // deadline; wake me on a signal". Because the map is ordered, an
7369                // indefinite front entry means every pending timed event is
7370                // indefinite, so no amount of virtual time can fire any of them.
7371                // Popping it anyway would jump global virtual time by ~584 years and
7372                // grant the sleep as a `ResumeStatus::Normal` wake, which is exactly
7373                // the internal violation `Detcore::handle_pause` refuses to accept.
7374                let next_deadline = self
7375                    .blocked
7376                    .timed_waiters
7377                    .next_deadline()
7378                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
7379                if next_deadline.is_indefinite() {
7380                    if !external_waits_empty {
7381                        // Blocking external IO may still complete and produce the
7382                        // signal/wake the indefinite waiter needs, so this is not a
7383                        // deadlock yet. Spin as step2c does for the same reason.
7384                        trace!(
7385                            "[scheduler] empty run-queue with only indefinite waiters, but external IO is outstanding for dtids {:?}. SPINNING!",
7386                            &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
7387                        );
7388                        std::thread::yield_now();
7389                        return Err(SkipTurn);
7390                    }
7391                    return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock());
7392                }
7393                debug!(
7394                    "[scheduler] Deadlock avoidance! Empty run-queue, so waking next timed event."
7395                );
7396                let (event_ns, evt) = self
7397                    .blocked
7398                    .timed_waiters
7399                    .pop()
7400                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
7401                debug_assert_eq!(event_ns, next_deadline);
7402                self.empty_queue_wakes += 1;
7403                let observed_now = {
7404                    let mut gt = global_time.lock().unwrap();
7405                    let gt_now_ns = gt.as_nanos();
7406                    if event_ns > gt_now_ns {
7407                        info!("[scheduler] Skipping global time ahead to {}.", event_ns);
7408                        let delta = event_ns.duration_since(gt_now_ns);
7409                        detlog_debug!(
7410                            "[sched] add extra global time for deadlock avoidance {:?} on current time {}",
7411                            delta,
7412                            gt_now_ns,
7413                        );
7414                        gt.add_extra_time(delta);
7415                    } else {
7416                        // A control hook may have crossed this deadline after
7417                        // maintenance consumed its one event. Keep the separate
7418                        // empty-queue wake/SkipTurn, without rewinding the clock.
7419                        info!(
7420                            "[scheduler] Waking elapsed timed event at {} with global time {} unchanged.",
7421                            event_ns, gt_now_ns,
7422                        );
7423                    }
7424                    gt.as_nanos()
7425                };
7426
7427                match evt {
7428                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dtid) => self.wake_timed_event(event_ns, dtid),
7429                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, dtid, sig) => {
7430                        self.dispatch_timed_signal(event_ns, id, dtid, sig, false, observed_now)
7431                    }
7432                }
7433                return Err(SkipTurn);
7434            }
7435        } else {
7436            // A queued thread ends any empty state.
7437            self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
7438        }
7439        Ok(())
7440    }
7441
7442    /// Step: Find the next thread to run for this scheduling run.
7443    /// Sometimes the next thread is from the run queue, but it can also be a timed event.
7444    /// Return `None` if the queue is empty.
7445    ///
7446    /// This is a "peek" in the sense that it leaves the thread in the run queue.
7447    fn step3_peek(&mut self) -> Option<(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>)> {
7448        // Re-admit any happens-before threads whose gate opened since last turn.
7449        // Must precede `tentative_pop_next`: the run queue forbids pushes while a
7450        // selection transaction is live.
7451        self.hb_flush_wakes();
7452        debug!(
7453            "[sched-step3] Stepping scheduler, queue len {}, current turn {}, committed_time {}",
7454            self.run_queue.len(),
7455            self.turn,
7456            self.committed_time
7457        );
7458
7459        // Enable for FULL detail:
7460        {
7461            trace!(
7462                "[sched-step3] queue {:?}, io-blocked {:?}, next_turns: ",
7463                &self.run_queue, self.blocked.external_io_blockers
7464            );
7465            for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
7466                trace!(" ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}", dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp);
7467            }
7468            if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
7469                trace!("Timed events: {:?}", self.blocked.timed_waiters);
7470            }
7471        }
7472
7473        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
7474            None
7475        } else {
7476            let next_dtid = if self.vfork_barriers.is_empty() {
7477                self.run_queue.tentative_pop_next().expect("impossible")
7478            } else {
7479                let child = self
7480                    .vfork_barriers
7481                    .values()
7482                    .flatten()
7483                    .find(|child| self.run_queue.contains_tid(**child))
7484                    .copied()?;
7485                self.run_queue
7486                    .tentative_pop_tid(child)
7487                    .expect("vfork child disappeared from run queue")
7488            };
7489            let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
7490                panic!(
7491                "[sched-step3] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
7492                    next_dtid
7493            )
7494            });
7495            Some((next_dtid, nextturn.req.clone(), nextturn.resp.clone()))
7496        }
7497    }
7498
7499    /// Deschedule, but do not clear request/response. This should be used when
7500    /// the turn was skipped because the blocked-on resource is still blocking.
7501    fn skip_turn_blocked(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7502        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Started in step3.
7503        assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while we wait.
7504        trace!(
7505            "[dtid {}] after removal, run queue: {:?}",
7506            dettid, &self.run_queue
7507        );
7508        self.skip_turn()
7509    }
7510
7511    /// Post-await re-check: the selected thread parked (its request resolved
7512    /// `Ok`), but did its `next_turns` entry survive until the daemon got the
7513    /// lock back? If not, the turn must be abandoned.
7514    ///
7515    /// Returns `Err(SkipTurn)` for the abandoned case, after closing the
7516    /// tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Two things hang on that `Err`:
7517    ///
7518    /// * The tentative pop is undone rather than committed, so the selection
7519    ///   does not outlive the turn and the next pass's step2 removal drain does
7520    ///   not call `remove_tid` against a live `tentative_selection` (the same
7521    ///   hygiene the `Err(ThreadExited)` arm needs).
7522    /// * The caller reports a SKIP, not a completed turn. This branch bypasses
7523    ///   steps 4-7, so nothing is blocked, unblocked or re-enqueued -- yet
7524    ///   `bump_global_time` suppresses its advance only on `last_turn.is_err()`
7525    ///   ("if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped").
7526    ///   Reporting `Ok` here therefore added a DETLOG-visible virtual-time tick
7527    ///   for work that never happened, and whether this branch is reached at all
7528    ///   depends on whether teardown cleared `next_turns` inside the host-timed
7529    ///   gap between the await resolving and the re-lock -- so the same logical
7530    ///   execution could gain that tick in one run and not the next.
7531    fn abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7532        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&next_dtid) {
7533            return Ok(());
7534        }
7535        info!(
7536            "[sched-daemon] thread {} exited, skipping over...",
7537            &next_dtid
7538        );
7539        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
7540        Err(SkipTurn)
7541    }
7542
7543    /// Simply advance the turn. This does NOT remove any threads from the
7544    /// runqueue; callers must maintain `run_queue`/`blocking` invariants.
7545    fn skip_turn(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7546        self.turn += 1; // Skipping the turn advances the turn.
7547        Err(SkipTurn)
7548    }
7549
7550    /// Step: Determine if action will block based on current information.  E.g. will it block
7551    /// on a pipe read with no writer? If so, register it in the blocked_pool and issue a "skip".
7552    /// We can go ahead and take resource locks and physically issue the blocking effect if we
7553    /// like.  It's immaterial whether we do that now or later.
7554    ///
7555    /// Postcondition:
7556    ///  - If returning SkipTurn, this function ENDS the Scheduler turn, advancing to the
7557    ///    next (skipping subsequent steps within theturn).  Otherwise, it waits for a
7558    ///    later step end the turn.
7559    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)]
7560    fn step4_resource_block(
7561        &mut self,
7562        dettid: DetTid,
7563        rs: &Resources,
7564        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
7565    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7566        if rs.poll_attempt > 0 {
7567            // The thread is polling and hasn't been "remade" as runnable yet.
7568            info!(
7569                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} polling resource {:?}",
7570                self.turn, dettid, rs
7571            );
7572            // Requeue the thread as a poller
7573            let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
7574            assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
7575            self.run_queue
7576                .push_poller(dettid, self.get_priority(dettid), rs.poll_attempt);
7577            // Before the count reset below hides that this is a retry.
7578            self.note_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid, rs);
7579            trace!(
7580                "[dtid {}] after deprioritizing polling request, run queue: {:?}",
7581                dettid, &self.run_queue
7582            );
7583            self.upgrade_polled_to_runnable(dettid, rs); // Indicate the thread gets to run next time
7584            self.note_poll_deadline(dettid, rs);
7585            self.skip_turn()
7586        } else {
7587            match rs.resources.len() {
7588                0 => Ok(()),
7589                1 => {
7590                    let (rid, perm) = rs.resources.iter().next().unwrap();
7591                    let blocked = self.block_for_one_resource(
7592                        dettid,
7593                        rid,
7594                        perm,
7595                        rs.signal_interrupt_errno(),
7596                        rs.blocked_signal_mask,
7597                        resp,
7598                    );
7599                    if rs.replay_served_from_log
7600                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
7601                        && self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
7602                    {
7603                        self.blocked.replay_log_served.insert(dettid);
7604                    }
7605                    if rs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown
7606                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
7607                        && let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get_mut(&dettid)
7608                    {
7609                        // The call sleeps under a mask this turn could not
7610                        // read faithfully (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`).
7611                        *recorded = None;
7612                    }
7613                    blocked
7614                }
7615                _ => {
7616                    panic!(
7617                        "Requests for more than one resource at a time are not supported yet: {:?}",
7618                        rs
7619                    )
7620                }
7621            }
7622        }
7623    }
7624
7625    /// Replace the request Ivar for `dettid` with a copy with `poll_attempt = 0`,
7626    /// indicating the poll request is runnable on the next trip through the run queue.
7627    ///
7628    /// Precondition: The guest is stopped, so that no one is potentially using the request Ivar.
7629    /// The request Ivar should also be full with the passed resources
7630    fn upgrade_polled_to_runnable(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
7631        let mut retry_rs = rs.clone();
7632        retry_rs.poll_attempt = 0;
7633        let runnable_req = Ivar::full(Ok(retry_rs.clone()));
7634        let req = &mut self
7635            .next_turns
7636            .get_mut(&dettid)
7637            .expect("nextturn present")
7638            .req;
7639        debug_assert!(req.try_read().unwrap().is_ok()); // Ivar should be full
7640        trace!(
7641            "[dtid {}] Upgrading polled resource request in {} to runnable non-polled in {}",
7642            dettid, req, runnable_req
7643        );
7644        let previous = std::mem::replace(req, runnable_req.clone());
7645        // This is the same logical operation with a fresh scheduler request.
7646        // Keep parked ownership attached while the daemon holds exclusive access.
7647        self.rebind_parked_request(dettid, &previous, &runnable_req, rs, &retry_rs);
7648    }
7649
7650    /// Helper function. Same postcondition as step4_resource_block
7651    fn block_for_one_resource(
7652        &mut self,
7653        dettid: DetTid,
7654        rid: &ResourceID,
7655        _perm: &Permission,
7656        signal_interrupt_errno: Option<i32>,
7657        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
7658        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
7659    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7660        match rid {
7661            ResourceID::SleepUntil(target_ns) => {
7662                if *target_ns <= self.committed_time {
7663                    trace!(
7664                        "[dtid {}] time-based action ready to execute, target time {} is before committed global time {}",
7665                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
7666                    );
7667                    Ok(())
7668                } else if target_ns.is_indefinite() && self.admit_pause_with_due_sigalrm(dettid) {
7669                    // A pause admitted with a due guest-handled SIGALRM returns
7670                    // in this turn instead of parking (`sigalrm`).
7671                    Ok(())
7672                } else {
7673                    trace!(
7674                        "[dtid {}] time-based action not ready yet, registering waiter at future time {}. Current time is {}",
7675                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
7676                    );
7677                    info!(
7678                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} which wanted resource {:?} (blocking)",
7679                        self.turn, dettid, rid
7680                    );
7681                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(*target_ns, dettid);
7682                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
7683                }
7684            }
7685
7686            // Thread BEGINS a blocking syscall outside the runnable set.
7687            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id)
7688            | ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op_id)
7689            | ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id) => {
7690                if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingVfork(_)) {
7691                    self.begin_vfork_barrier(dettid);
7692                    if let Some(origin) = self.next_turns[&dettid].protocol.origin {
7693                        self.vfork_registration_origins.insert(dettid, origin.mm);
7694                    }
7695                }
7696                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(dettid.as_raw(), false);
7697                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
7698                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
7699                        self.turn,
7700                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
7701                        false,
7702                        false,
7703                    );
7704                    info!(
7705                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, BACKGROUND dettid {} (maybe-blocking){}",
7706                        self.turn, dettid, record_suffix
7707                    );
7708                }
7709                // Here we allow the action to execute asynchrounously, in the
7710                // background. The protocol is that it must:
7711                //   (1) not interfere with other internal/external actions (independence),
7712                //   (2) Request a BlockedExternalContinue as the first thing after the external IO is complete.
7713                self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3
7714                assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while in background.
7715
7716                // TODO: Register the action that is occuring in the background:
7717                // let act = self.new_action(Ivar::new());
7718                // self.bg_action_pool.insert(act.action_id, act);
7719
7720                // Unblock guest so that potentially-blocking IO action can get
7721                // started. This intentionally races with subsequent turns the
7722                // scheduler commits, and thus it leans on an assumption of
7723                // non-interference, or on interference *only* affecting the external
7724                // actions that will be recorded anyway.
7725                //
7726                // Record the mask the thread will sleep under BEFORE releasing it:
7727                // its call's own temporary mask, read in its turn, or else its
7728                // current mask, which only it can change and cannot change while
7729                // it is still stopped at this request. Once released, its live
7730                // mask is host-timed (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
7731                //
7732                // Only a scheduler with `models_signal_targets` reads or records
7733                // that mask. Its two readers, `kernel_sigchld_target` (through
7734                // `thread_signal_mask`) and `arm_signaled_background`, run only
7735                // under that flag, and the flag needs
7736                // `backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`, which a
7737                // backend sets only when its `DetTid`s are the host thread IDs
7738                // that `/proc` names (`prepare_backend_config` in
7739                // `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs`). On a backend whose IDs are
7740                // guest-virtual, a `/proc` read of `dettid` would name an
7741                // unrelated host thread or none at all.
7742                let sleeping_mask = self
7743                    .models_signal_targets
7744                    .then(|| blocked_signal_mask.or_else(|| self.read_thread_blocked_mask(dettid)));
7745                self.run_queue.consume_yield_exclusion();
7746                self.unblock_guest(dettid, resp)?;
7747
7748                // Only once the ivars are cleared and the guest is ready to issue
7749                // BlockedExternalContinue do we record which blocked pool owns it.
7750                let old = if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)) {
7751                    self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
7752                } else {
7753                    self.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
7754                };
7755                assert!(old.is_none(), "thread started a second external operation");
7756                if let Some(mask) = sleeping_mask {
7757                    self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.insert(dettid, mask);
7758                }
7759                if let Some(signal) = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(&dettid) {
7760                    self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
7761                }
7762                Err(SkipTurn)
7763            }
7764
7765            // Thread CONTINUES after completing [potentially] blocking IO.
7766            ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(_) => {
7767                // We leave the thread out of the run-queue.  At the point we put it back
7768                // in, this resource request is immediately granted.
7769                Ok(())
7770            }
7771
7772            ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec } => {
7773                if self.ready_child_wait(*parent, *spec).is_some()
7774                    || !self.has_child_wait_target(*parent, *spec)
7775                {
7776                    Ok(())
7777                } else {
7778                    info!(
7779                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for child {:?}",
7780                        self.turn, dettid, spec
7781                    );
7782                    assert!(
7783                        self.blocked
7784                            .child_waiters
7785                            .insert(dettid, (*parent, *spec))
7786                            .is_none()
7787                    );
7788                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
7789                }
7790            }
7791
7792            ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child) => {
7793                if self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(&dettid) {
7794                    Ok(())
7795                } else {
7796                    info!(
7797                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for physical child {}",
7798                        self.turn, dettid, child
7799                    );
7800                    let completion_already_observed =
7801                        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(child);
7802                    assert!(
7803                        self.blocked
7804                            .physical_child_waiters
7805                            .entry(*child)
7806                            .or_default()
7807                            .insert(dettid)
7808                    );
7809                    let skipped = self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
7810                    if completion_already_observed {
7811                        self.wake_physical_child_waiters(*child);
7812                    }
7813                    skipped
7814                }
7815            }
7816
7817            // Thread requests change in priority
7818            ResourceID::PriorityChangePoint(prio, change_time, rcbs, epochs) => {
7819                self.perform_priority_changepoint(dettid, *prio, *change_time, *rcbs, epochs)
7820            }
7821
7822            // For now, all other resource types are immediately granted.
7823            // (TODO/FIXME: handle the entire set of resource requests.)
7824            ResourceID::FileContents(_) => Ok(()),
7825            ResourceID::FileMetadata(_) => Ok(()),
7826            ResourceID::DirectoryContents(_) => Ok(()),
7827            ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(_) => Ok(()),
7828            ResourceID::Path(_) => Ok(()),
7829            ResourceID::PathsTransitive(_) => Ok(()),
7830            ResourceID::Device(_) => Ok(()),
7831            // The scheduler-ordered `Exit` grant is the deterministic moment a
7832            // child process leaves the run set. Register a one-shot child-exit
7833            // `SIGCHLD` for the reaping parent, to be delivered at a deterministic
7834            // logical time by `step2b_process_timed`, instead of relying on the
7835            // host-async kernel `SIGCHLD` whose arrival time is host-timed (the
7836            // `make -jN` / redis `--strict --verify` nondeterminism source).
7837            // A backend that registered a PIDFD_THREAD already preserves the
7838            // kernel's native child-exit signal. Sending another SIGCHLD through
7839            // that pidfd would make the application observe both CLD_EXITED and
7840            // SI_TKILL for one child, so only the scheduler wait readiness is
7841            // synthesized on that path.
7842            ResourceID::Exit { group, process, mm } => {
7843                let reserve_mode = match self.reserve_exit_boundary(dettid, *process, *mm, *group) {
7844                    Ok(mode) => mode,
7845                    Err(failure) => {
7846                        self.fail_parked(dettid, failure);
7847                        // fail_parked linearizes terminal failure and closes
7848                        // the tentative selection. Do not undo it a second
7849                        // time through skip_turn_blocked.
7850                        return Err(SkipTurn);
7851                    }
7852                };
7853                // A grant that ends its process fixes the process's logical
7854                // exit between committed turns (`reparent_orphans`). The
7855                // process is the one the thread tree registered the exiting
7856                // thread in: for a raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit
7857                // signal, the backend's `process` names its creator instead.
7858                if let Some(exiting) = self.registered_process(dettid)
7859                    && (*group
7860                        || !self
7861                            .thread_tree
7862                            .my_thread_group(&exiting)
7863                            .into_iter()
7864                            .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid)))
7865                {
7866                    self.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(exiting);
7867                }
7868                // The grant is a vfork child's release edge: a barrier whose
7869                // parent has died ends here, inside this committed turn.
7870                self.release_vfork_child(dettid);
7871                // The thread leaves by its own committed exit, not by dying
7872                // with its process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
7873                self.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
7874                // An exit that ends its process leaves the host some time after
7875                // this grant. Hold turn selection from here until the backend
7876                // reports the process physically gone (asynchronous exit
7877                // completion), so no peer observes its descriptors still open.
7878                if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
7879                    && (*group
7880                        || !self
7881                            .thread_tree
7882                            .my_thread_group(process)
7883                            .into_iter()
7884                            .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid)))
7885                {
7886                    self.begin_exit_at_grant(*process);
7887                }
7888                if reserve_mode == signal_control::ExitReserveMode::Uncontrolled
7889                    && *group
7890                    && let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(process)
7891                    && self.should_synthesize_child_exit_signal(parent)
7892                {
7893                    // The hold waits for the backend's report that `process`
7894                    // is consumed, so it is sound only if this grant ends that
7895                    // process: the exiting thread must belong to it in the
7896                    // thread tree. A backend can name another process here: a
7897                    // raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own
7898                    // process in the tree, but ptrace reports it with its
7899                    // creator's pid, so its exit_group names the creator, which
7900                    // keeps running and is never reported. Such a grant keeps
7901                    // the synthetic timer it had before Phase A.
7902                    let ends_named_process =
7903                        if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&dettid) {
7904                            dettid == *process
7905                        } else {
7906                            self.registered_process(dettid) == Some(*process)
7907                        };
7908                    let notification =
7909                        if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
7910                            self.classify_child_exit_notification(*process, parent)
7911                        } else {
7912                            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
7913                        };
7914                    match notification {
7915                        // Linux generates nothing (explicit SIG_IGN) or discards
7916                        // the signal at generation (default-ignored, unblocked),
7917                        // so the guest observes no SIGCHLD from Linux. Send no
7918                        // synthetic one: no alarm, no physical send, no wake of
7919                        // the parent. The traced parent still receives the
7920                        // kernel's own notification, which this hold places at
7921                        // the first scheduling pass after the backend reports its
7922                        // publication.
7923                        ChildExitNotification::None | ChildExitNotification::Discard => {
7924                            // A publication already reported (the process was
7925                            // consumed before this grant) needs no hold: the
7926                            // kernel has already notified the parent.
7927                            if !self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(process) {
7928                                self.child_exit_publications_pending.insert(*process);
7929                            }
7930                        }
7931                        // Caught, blocked, other exit signals and every state
7932                        // Hermit cannot classify keep the synthetic SIGCHLD.
7933                        ChildExitNotification::Deliver | ChildExitNotification::Undecided => {
7934                            // Fire strictly after the current committed time so the event
7935                            // is dispatched on a subsequent scheduler pass.
7936                            //
7937                            // Linux sends the child's exit signal to its parent thread,
7938                            // the one that created it, and prefers that thread when it
7939                            // picks which thread of the process takes the signal
7940                            // (`do_notify_parent` -> `complete_signal`). Where gated
7941                            // waits model interruption, the timer carries that thread
7942                            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146), so a
7943                            // creator that does not block `SIGCHLD` takes it and the
7944                            // leader's wait is left alone. Elsewhere it keeps naming
7945                            // the leader (DetTid == DetPid for a group leader).
7946                            let deadline = self.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
7947                            let parent_thread = if self.models_signal_targets {
7948                                self.thread_tree
7949                                    .process_wait
7950                                    .get(process)
7951                                    .map_or(parent, |metadata| metadata.wait_owner)
7952                            } else {
7953                                parent
7954                            };
7955                            // Where the kernel also sends its own, the first of the
7956                            // two delivered stands for the exit, the other is
7957                            // dropped, and the scheduler's gets Linux's siginfo
7958                            // (`child_exit_sigchld`).
7959                            if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
7960                                self.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, *process);
7961                            }
7962                            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
7963                                deadline,
7964                                *process,
7965                                parent,
7966                                parent_thread,
7967                            );
7968                        }
7969                    }
7970                }
7971                if *group {
7972                    self.child_exit_sigchld.forget_exit_status(*process);
7973                }
7974                Ok(())
7975            }
7976            ResourceID::ParentContinue { .. } => Ok(()),
7977            ResourceID::InternalIOPolling => Ok(()),
7978            ResourceID::FutexWait => Ok(()),
7979            ResourceID::TraceReplay => Ok(()),
7980            ResourceID::SchedYield => Ok(()),
7981            ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm => Ok(()),
7982
7983            // A guest thread checking in at a happens-before anchor point. Delegate
7984            // to the enforcement logic, which either grants passage (firing anchors)
7985            // or parks the thread until its gating BEFORE anchor fires.
7986            ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(count) => self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, &[]),
7987            ResourceID::HappensBeforeSyscallCheckpoint { count, anchors } => {
7988                self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, anchors)
7989            }
7990            ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
7991                count,
7992                anchors,
7993                code,
7994            } => self.hb_posthook_interrupted(dettid, *count, anchors, code),
7995
7996            // A host-async SIGCHLD (a guest child process exited) is delivered to
7997            // the parent at a moment decided by host timing. Committing that turn
7998            // immediately makes the signal race whatever guest work was already
7999            // runnable (e.g. a `make -jN` jobserver `pselect6` continuation),
8000            // which diverges under `--strict --verify`. Defer it deterministic-
8001            // work-first: park the parent out of the run queue and let
8002            // `step2e_process_signal_deferred` re-admit it once no ordinary guest
8003            // work remains, mirroring the `external_io_blockers` policy. Signals
8004            // that the scheduler itself synthesizes deterministically (timers via
8005            // `fire_alarm`) are never SIGCHLD and are unaffected.
8006            ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_) => Ok(()),
8007            ResourceID::InboundSignal(sig) => {
8008                // `sigchld_ready` marks a parent step2e has already re-admitted,
8009                // or a delivery the scheduler already placed; grant it now rather
8010                // than deferring it (a second time).
8011                let already_readmitted = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&dettid);
8012                if sig.signal() == Some(Signal::SIGCHLD)
8013                    && signal_interrupt_errno.is_none()
8014                    && !already_readmitted
8015                    && self.run_queue.has_runnable_besides(dettid)
8016                {
8017                    self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
8018                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
8019                    self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(dettid);
8020                    Err(SkipTurn)
8021                } else {
8022                    Ok(())
8023                }
8024            }
8025        }
8026    }

8028    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-868): Review the vfork registration scheduler barrier.
8029    pub(crate) fn complete_vfork_registration(&mut self, parent: DetTid, child: DetTid) {
8030        if self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent) {
8031            // The parent died before this registration; its barrier is already
8032            // cancelled. The child registers as any orphan does.
8033            self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
8034            return;
8035        }
8036        let registered_child = self
8037            .vfork_barriers
8038            .get_mut(&parent)
8039            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("vfork child registered without a pending parent {parent}"));
8040        assert!(registered_child.replace(child).is_none());
8041        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
8042    }
8043
8044    /// Authenticate the child address space against the exact parent grant,
8045    /// before a reused child TID has a registration of its own. The caller also
8046    /// checks the immutable RPC sender and the backend's vfork/serialized-fork
8047    /// mode; this predicate neither consumes the barrier nor opens admission.
8048    pub(crate) fn pending_vfork_registration_matches(
8049        &self,
8050        parent: DetTid,
8051        process: DetPid,
8052        child: DetTid,
8053        child_mm: MmId,
8054        shares_vm: bool,
8055    ) -> bool {
8056        let Some(parent_mm) = self.vfork_registration_origins.get(&parent).copied() else {
8057            return false;
8058        };
8059        parent != child
8060            && self.registered_process(parent) == Some(process)
8061            && self.next_turns.contains_key(&parent)
8062            && !self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
8063            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(parent)
8064            && self.rpc_incarnation_matches(parent, parent_mm)
8065            && self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent) == Some(&None)
8066            && MmId::for_clone(parent_mm, child, shares_vm) == child_mm
8067    }

8069    /// Inner helper for just the core priority changing.
8070    fn requeue_with_new_priority(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, new_priority: Priority) {
8071        // TODO: do we want to record in preemption_writer if we are in schedule-trace-replay mode?
8072        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
8073        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
8074        let _old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
8075        let present = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
8076        if present {
8077            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
8078        }
8079        trace!(
8080            "[dettid {}] requeue: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
8081            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
8082        );
8083    }
8084
8085    /// Helper for priority changepoint logic
8086    ///
8087    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
8088    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
8089    ///
8090    /// Postcondition: Same as block_for_one_resource. However, always returns SkipTurn, because the
8091    /// priority changepoint may not allow the current thread to continue in a regular turn (i.e.
8092    /// doing actual work).
8093    fn perform_priority_changepoint(
8094        &mut self,
8095        dettid: DetTid,
8096
8097        new_priority: Priority,
8098        guest_time: LogicalTime,
8099        guest_rcbs: u64,
8100        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8101        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1151)
8102        chaos_epochs: &[crate::resources::ChaosEpochTransition],
8103    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
8104        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
8105        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
8106        let old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
8107
8108        // Do not attempt to record preemptions/priorities when we're dictated by a raw schedule replay.
8109        if self.replayer.is_none()
8110            && let Some(pw) = &mut self.preemption_writer
8111        {
8112            let old_prio = old_priority.unwrap();
8113            debug!(
8114                "[dtid {}] Recording preemption point, current time {} prior priority {} (next priority {})",
8115                dettid, guest_time, old_prio, new_priority
8116            );
8117            for transition in chaos_epochs {
8118                pw.insert_chaos_epoch(dettid, *transition);
8119            }
8120            pw.insert_reprioritization(dettid, guest_time, guest_rcbs, old_prio, new_priority);
8121            pw.set_current(dettid, new_priority);
8122        }
8123
8124        let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
8125        assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
8126        self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
8127        trace!(
8128            "[dettid {}] changepoint: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
8129            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
8130        );
8131
8132        // Update request to be empty so the thread is unconditionally
8133        // runnable when it next comes up in the queue.
8134        let empty_req = Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(dettid)));
8135        trace!(
8136            "[dettid {}] Priority change point emplaced empty resource request at new {}",
8137            dettid, empty_req
8138        );
8139        self.next_turns
8140            .get_mut(&dettid)
8141            .expect("nextturn present")
8142            .req = empty_req;
8143        info!(
8144            "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, dettid {} changed priority to {}",
8145            self.turn, dettid, new_priority
8146        );
8147        self.skip_turn() // The thread shouldn't run.
8148    }
8149
8150    fn step1_check_quiescence(
8151        &mut self,
8152        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
8153        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
8154    ) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
8155        // TODO: actually check resource availability to enable asynchronous background activities!
8156        let outstanding = self.are_all_quiesced();
8157        if outstanding.is_none() {
8158            self.bump_global_time(global_time, last_turn);
8159        }
8160        outstanding
8161    }
