8163    fn is_internal_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
8164        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::TraceReplay)
8165    }
8166
8167    /// A turn that only grants `InternalIOPolling`, i.e. a retry of a nonblocking
8168    /// poll/epoll/select/futex/recv/... injected by the blocking-via-polling machinery
8169    /// (see `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`). The *number* of such retries before a
8170    /// file descriptor becomes ready is wall-clock dependent when the readiness is driven
8171    /// by an external actor (e.g. a child linker process draining a pipe), so it varies
8172    /// between otherwise-identical runs.
8173    fn is_polling_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
8174        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
8175    }
8176
8177    /// A backend whose internal pipe turns are host-timed (today SaBRe) discovers an
8178    /// inherited stdio pipe as a device resource before the inner
8179    /// `InternalIOPolling` request. Both turns belong to one host-timing-sensitive pipe
8180    /// operation, so their logical-time logging must use the same retry normalization.
8181    fn is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
8182        rsrcs.fyi == HOST_TIMED_INTERNAL_PIPE_IO_FYI
8183    }
8184
8185    /// A strong yield issued, on a backend whose loopback pollers yield to their peers
8186    /// (today SaBRe), before a zero-timeout poll while the task owns a
8187    /// loopback connection. Its count is kernel-readiness timing, not guest-visible progress.
8188    fn is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
8189        rsrcs.fyi == LOOPBACK_POLL_YIELD_FYI
8190    }
8191
8192    fn is_x_turn(rsrcs: &Resources, x: &ResourceID) -> bool {
8193        if rsrcs.resources.contains_key(x) {
8194            if rsrcs.resources.len() > 1 {
8195                panic!(
8196                    "is_x_turn: not expecting an {:?} mixed in with other resource requests: {:?}",
8197                    x, rsrcs
8198                );
8199            }
8200            true
8201        } else {
8202            false
8203        }
8204    }
8205
8206    /// Tick global logical time due to represent the work of the scheduler itself.
8207    /// Also, update committed time.
8208    /// Prerequisite: all threads are parked, with their time contributions frozen.
8209    fn bump_global_time(
8210        &mut self,
8211        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
8212        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
8213    ) {
8214        // An internal IO-polling retry (see `is_polling_turn`) must still advance logical
8215        // time -- finite poll/epoll/select/futex timeouts are enforced by comparing observed
8216        // logical time against the deadline in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`, so freezing
8217        // time here would turn a timed wait into an infinite spin. But because the *count* of
8218        // these retries is host-timing nondeterministic, we keep their time-advance out of the
8219        // determinism log (DETLOG). This makes the `--verify` deterministic comparison
8220        // insensitive to retry count; the matching `{InternalIOPolling: ...}` COMMIT turn is
8221        // likewise excluded in `logdiff::is_internal_io_poll_commit`. Time values still shift
8222        // between runs, but those are numerically normalized before comparison.
8223        let last_turn_was_polling = last_turn
8224            .as_ref()
8225            .map(|resources| {
8226                Self::is_polling_turn(resources)
8227                    || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(resources)
8228                    || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(resources)
8229            })
8230            .unwrap_or(false);
8231
8232        // At this moment, when threads are parked, we know that the global_time is
8233        // frozen and we can read it without any race.
8234        let snapshot: LogicalTime = {
8235            let mut gtime = global_time.lock().unwrap();
8236
8237            if self.run_queue.is_empty() && self.blocked.only_external_blocked() {
8238                // TODO(T112017687): rationalize the occurence of
8239                // BlockingExternalIO in strict runs. For example, we should
8240                // probably inject nanosleep and actually wait the intervening
8241                // time, so we don't appear too fast to external observers.
8242                trace!(
8243                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because we're ONLY waiting for external events"
8244                );
8245            } else if last_turn.is_err() {
8246                // Note: if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped. But since we
8247                // can't see the future, we just cancel out the bump by not doing a bump this turn.
8248                trace!(
8249                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn did not progress (i.e. SkipTurn)"
8250                );
8251            } else if last_turn
8252                .as_ref()
8253                .map(Self::is_internal_turn)
8254                .unwrap_or(false)
8255            {
8256                trace!(
8257                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn was an internal book-keeping one"
8258                );
8259            } else if !last_turn_was_polling
8260                && last_turn
8261                    .as_ref()
8262                    .map(|resources| resources.backend_runtime_bootstrap)
8263                    .unwrap_or(false)
8264            {
8265                // The turn served a syscall that a backend-resident runtime made
8266                // inside its bootstrap window and whose syscall cost is withheld
8267                // (`ThreadState::charge_syscall_time`). Per Reverie's
8268                // `Guest::is_backend_runtime_bootstrap` contract that work is not
8269                // the guest's, so its turn must not advance the guest's clock
8270                // either: a backend without such a runtime never makes this turn,
8271                // so charging it would add time that only one backend's guests
8272                // see. An IO-polling retry is
8273                // excluded above and still advances, because finite poll and
8274                // futex timeouts are enforced against this clock. The decision is
8275                // a function of the request alone, which the guest's own
8276                // execution determines, so both runs of --verify and a replay
8277                // make it identically.
8278                trace!(
8279                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld"
8280                );
8281            } else {
8282                let newtime = match gtime.add_scheduler_time() {
8283                    Ok(newtime) => newtime,
8284                    Err(exhausted) => {
8285                        // Keep the first report; the clock did not move.
8286                        self.terminal_clock_exhaustion
8287                            .get_or_insert_with(|| exhausted.to_string());
8288                        gtime.as_nanos()
8289                    }
8290                };
8291                if last_turn_was_polling {
8292                    // Advance time (needed for timeout enforcement) but keep it off the DETLOG.
8293                    trace!(
8294                        "[sched] advance global time for internal IO-polling retry (suppressed from detlog), new time {:?}",
8295                        newtime,
8296                    );
8297                } else {
8298                    detlog_debug!(
8299                        "[sched] advance global time for scheduler turn, new time {:?}",
8300                        newtime,
8301                    );
8302                }
8303            }
8304            gtime.as_nanos()
8305        };
8306
8307        match snapshot.cmp(&self.committed_time) {
8308            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
8309                panic!(
8310                    "bump_global_time: invariant broken, global time went backwards from {} to {}",
8311                    self.committed_time, snapshot
8312                );
8313            }
8314            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
8315            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
8316                // NB: `committed_time` still tracks the (host-timing-perturbed) global clock,
8317                // including the time advanced by suppressed IO-polling retries above, so this
8318                // line's presence is retry-count sensitive. It is therefore excluded from the
8319                // deterministic `--verify` comparison in `logdiff::is_scheduler_committed_time`
8320                // (it is redundant with the per-turn "advance global time" DETLOG anyway).
8321                detlog_debug!(
8322                    event = crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommittedTime;
8323                    "[sched-step1] advancing committed_time from {} to {}",
8324                    self.committed_time,
8325                    snapshot
8326                );
8327                self.committed_time = snapshot;
8328            }
8329        }
8330    }
8331
8332    /// Step 4: unblock enabled actions to actually, physically run.
8333    fn step5_guest_unblock(
8334        &mut self,
8335        next_dtid: DetTid,
8336        rsrcs: &Resources,
8337        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
8338    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
8339        match self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid) {
8340            None => {
8341                info!(
8342                    "Scheduler was about to schedule {} for a turn (resources {:?}), but it died first.",
8343                    &next_dtid, rsrcs.resources
8344                );
8345                Err(SkipTurn)
8346            }
8347            Some(nxt) => {
8348                assert_eq!(resp, &nxt.resp);
8349                // Refuse an exhausted transport identity before recording a
8350                // COMMIT or consuming any response state.
8351                if nxt.protocol.epoch.checked_add(1).is_none() {
8352                    self.fail_parked(next_dtid, parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow);
8353                    return Err(SkipTurn);
8354                }
8355                // N.B.: these prints themselves should be deterministic between
8356                // runs.  They are part of the "detlog".
8357                // The records this thread's in-guest Tool forwarded before the request
8358                // this turn serves go to the log here, at a point the schedule fixes
8359                // (the order rule at `detlog::set_forwarded_source`).
8360                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(next_dtid.as_raw(), true);
8361                let normalization_marker = if self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs) {
8362                    " [sabre-internal-pipe-io]"
8363                } else if self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs) {
8364                    " [sabre-loopback-poll-zero-timeout]"
8365                } else {
8366                    ""
8367                };
8368                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
8369                    let internal_io_poll =
8370                        rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
8371                            || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs)
8372                            || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs);
8373                    let runtime_maps_read = rsrcs.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
8374                        matches!(
8375                            resource,
8376                            ResourceID::Path(path)
8377                                if path.as_path() == std::path::Path::new("/proc/self/maps")
8378                        )
8379                    });
8380                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
8381                        self.turn,
8382                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
8383                        internal_io_poll,
8384                        runtime_maps_read,
8385                    );
8386                    info!(
8387                        "[sched-step5] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, dettid {} using resources {:?}, on previously committed {}{}{}",
8388                        self.turn,
8389                        next_dtid,
8390                        rsrcs.resources,
8391                        self.committed_time,
8392                        normalization_marker,
8393                        record_suffix,
8394                    );
8395                }
8396                self.unblock_guest(next_dtid, resp)?;
8397                Ok(())
8398            }
8399        }
8400    }
8401
8402    /// Unblock the guest to run, clear its ivars for the next turn, and increment the turn counter.
8403    ///
8404    /// Precondition: guest is stopped.
8405    /// Postcondition: guest is running concurrently with this scheduler/tracer thread.
8406    fn unblock_guest(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
8407        trace!(
8408            "[sched-step5] Guest unblocking (via {}); clear ivars for the next turn on dettid {}",
8409            &resp, &dtid
8410        );
8411        let signals = self.inbound_signals(dtid); // Peek before we clear the ivars.
8412        let fatal_alarm = self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dtid);
8413        let futex_timed_out = self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(&dtid);
8414        if let Err(error) = self.clear_nextturn(dtid) {
8415            self.fail_parked(dtid, error);
8416            return Err(SkipTurn);
8417        }
8418        self.turn += 1;
8419        let answer = if fatal_alarm {
8420            SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm
8421        } else if !signals.is_empty() {
8422            SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))
8423        } else if futex_timed_out {
8424            SchedResponse::Go(Some(SchedValue::TimeOut))
8425        } else {
8426            let timeslice = self.timeslices.remove(&dtid).flatten();
8427            // TODO(T137799529): use a more strongly typed representation rather than reusing
8428            // SchedValue/u64:
8429            let as_schedvalue = timeslice
8430                .as_ref()
8431                .map(LogicalTime::as_nanos)
8432                .map(SchedValue::Value);
8433            SchedResponse::Go(as_schedvalue)
8434        };
8435        self.parked.running = Some(dtid);
8436        resp.put(answer);
8437        Ok(())
8438    }
8439
8440    fn inbound_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Vec<SigWrapper> {
8441        let req = &self.next_turns.get(&dettid).unwrap().req;
8442        let mut signals = Vec::new();
8443        if let Some(Ok(resources)) = req.try_read() {
8444            for resource in resources.resources.keys() {
8445                match resource {
8446                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal) => signals.push(*signal),
8447                    ResourceID::WaitidSignals(batch) => signals.extend(batch.iter().copied()),
8448                    _ => {}
8449                }
8450            }
8451        }
8452        // A signal can legitimately appear in both an `InboundSignal` and a
8453        // merged `WaitidSignals` batch. Sort then dedup so the reported set is a
8454        // canonical function of WHICH signals are pending, not of how many
8455        // resources happen to carry each one or of the order they arrived in.
8456        signals.sort_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
8457        signals.dedup_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
8458        signals
8459    }
8460
8461    /// Clear the thread's nextturn, installing fresh ivars.
8462    ///
8463    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
8464    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
8465    fn clear_nextturn(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), parked::ProtocolFailure> {
8466        let epoch = self
8467            .next_turns
8468            .get(&dtid)
8469            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Identity)?
8470            .protocol
8471            .epoch
8472            .checked_add(1)
8473            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow)?;
8474        self.settle_parked_grant(dtid);
8475        self.clear_ready_polled_read(dtid);
8476        // The granted request is consumed; so is any polling wait it continued.
8477        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dtid);
8478        let nextturn = self
8479            .next_turns
8480            .get_mut(&dtid)
8481            .expect("clear_nextturn: Thread should be available in next_turns");
8482        nextturn.req = Ivar::new();
8483        nextturn.resp = Ivar::new();
8484        nextturn.protocol.epoch = epoch;
8485        nextturn.protocol.origin = None;
8486        Ok(())
8487    }
8488
8489    /// Step: reenqueue the thread that just had a turn.
8490    fn step6_reenquue(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid, sched_yield: bool) {
8491        // We delay popping till here, so while holding the lock we "atomically" move the
8492        // thread from the front to the back of the queue.
8493        let dt2 = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop_completed_turn();
8494        assert_eq!(next_dtid, dt2);
8495        // SchedYield is emitted in normal execution and non-chaos preemption replay. Its
8496        // queue placement is transient, so persistent priorities remain unchanged.
8497        let pos = if sched_yield {
8498            let priority = self.get_priority(next_dtid);
8499            self.run_queue.push_yielded(next_dtid, priority)
8500        } else {
8501            self.runqueue_push_back(next_dtid)
8502        };
8503        debug!(
8504            "[sched-step6] dettid {} going back into queue at position {}.",
8505            next_dtid, pos
8506        );
8507    }
8508
8509    /// Add a simulated "post hook" for exit calls which we're about to let through.
8510    /// ALTERNATIVE: this could happen later when the thread_exit hook comes through.
8511    fn step7_simulate_exit_posthook(
8512        &mut self,
8513        dettid: DetTid,
8514        placeholder_syscall: Syscall,
8515        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
8516    ) {
8517        let replay = self.replayer.is_some();
8518        let record = self.preemption_writer.is_some();
8519        if !(replay || record) {
8520            return;
8521        }
8522        let thread_duration = global_time.lock().unwrap().threads_duration(dettid);
8523        debug!(
8524            "simulate exit posthook on tid {}, thread time {}: {:?}",
8525            dettid, thread_duration, placeholder_syscall
8526        );
8527
8528        let ev = SchedEvent::syscall(dettid, placeholder_syscall.number(), SyscallPhase::Posthook)
8529            .with_time(thread_duration);
8530        let print_stack1 = if replay {
8531            let ConsumeResult {
8532                keep_running,
8533                print_stack,
8534                event_ix: _,
8535                timeslice_remaining: _,
8536            } = self.consume_schedevent(&ev);
8537            // We should not ever need to background the thread when it is going to exit anyway.
8538            if !keep_running {
8539                tracing::warn!(
8540                    "simulate_exit_posthook: unexpectedly asked to background the current, exiting thread {}",
8541                    dettid
8542                );
8543            }
8544            print_stack
8545        } else {
8546            None
8547        };
8548        let print_stack2 = if record { self.record_event(&ev) } else { None };
8549        if print_stack1.is_some() || print_stack2.is_some() {
8550            crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
8551                ":: Guest tid {}, at thread time {}, backtrace requested but not available post-exit!\n",
8552                dettid,
8553                thread_duration
8554            );
8555        }
8556    }
8557
8558    /// Get the priority for a thread; panic if absent.
8559    fn get_priority(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Priority {
8560        *self
8561            .priorities
8562            .get(&dettid)
8563            .expect("get_priority: all threads should have a persistent priority")
8564    }
8565
8566    /// Push_back a thread onto the runqueue, respecting its persistent priority
8567    /// value. This should be the ordinary way threads are pushed onto the queue.
8568    pub fn runqueue_push_back(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
8569        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
8570        self.run_queue.push_back(dettid, priority)
8571    }
8572
8573    /// Push a thread to the front of its persistent priority band.
8574    ///
8575    /// This is reserved for protocol handoffs where the queued thread must run
8576    /// before an equal-priority peer, such as ordinary clone child startup.
8577    pub(crate) fn runqueue_push_front(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
8578        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
8579        self.run_queue.push_front(dettid, priority)
8580    }
8581
8582    /// Record an intent to admit `dtid` to the run queue, applied by the daemon
8583    /// at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
8584    ///
8585    /// Global-request handlers (`recv_create_child_thread`,
8586    /// `reconnect_after_exec`) hold the scheduler lock but run on whichever
8587    /// backend worker fielded the RPC, not on the scheduler daemon's turn. The
8588    /// point in the daemon's loop at which such a handler acquires the lock is
8589    /// host-timing-dependent on asynchronous backends (e.g. DBT): it may land
8590    /// inside the tentative-pop window (between `step3_peek` and `step4`'s
8591    /// commit, where the lock is released across `req.get().await`) *or* outside
8592    /// it (during the quiescence-wait / backoff awaits at the top of
8593    /// `do_a_turn_blocking`, where `tentative_selection` is `None`). A design
8594    /// that pushed directly whenever the window happened to be closed would make
8595    /// the *admission order* — and, under `RunsPostFork::Random`, the PRNG draw
8596    /// order — a function of that host timing: two equal-priority admissions
8597    /// could enter the queue in either relative order across otherwise-identical
8598    /// runs, and a fixed seed could explore different schedules.
8599    ///
8600    /// So admission is *always* deferred, never applied directly here. Handlers
8601    /// only record the unresolved [`AdmitIntent`]; the daemon resolves the side
8602    /// (drawing any `RunsPostFork::Random` value) and pushes the run queue at the
8603    /// single `step2` drain, in canonical `DetTid` order, before `step3` opens a
8604    /// tentative window. Draining is also the only place `remove_tid`'s tentative
8605    /// guard is guaranteed to hold.
8606    ///
8607    /// # What this does and does not make deterministic
8608    ///
8609    /// **Synchronous backends (ptrace): fully deterministic, and byte-identical
8610    /// to the pre-deferral behavior.** Handlers run post-commit, one per turn, so
8611    /// at most one admission is buffered per turn and it drains at the next
8612    /// `step2` — before that turn's `step3` selection — yielding the same
8613    /// selection sequence and the same one-draw-per-fork PRNG order as an
8614    /// immediate push.
8615    ///
8616    /// **Asynchronous backends: every production admission site has a causal or
8617    /// explicit barrier that fixes its drain, and order within that drain is
8618    /// canonical.** A bare off-turn handler would still be insufficient: a
8619    /// `BTreeMap` only canonicalizes items already in one snapshot. The current
8620    /// sites additionally bind snapshot membership to deterministic scheduler
8621    /// state:
8622    ///
8623    /// * **Ordinary clone — anchored, causally.** `CreateChildThread` issues the
8624    ///   parent's `ParentContinue` request only *after* buffering the child's
8625    ///   admission, so no thread can run between the two and the admission
8626    ///   cannot straddle a drain boundary.
8627    /// * **`vfork` — anchored, by barrier.** `vfork_barriers` /
8628    ///   [`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`] hold the parent until the
8629    ///   child has registered, which fixes the drain.
8630    /// * **Multi-threaded exec reconnect — anchored, causally.** Step5 installs
8631    ///   the caller's empty next-turn request before it executes exec. The
8632    ///   reconnect handler atomically buffers the old-leader removal and new
8633    ///   incarnation admission, then retires the caller and resolves that
8634    ///   request. Step1 therefore cannot release step2 before the complete pair
8635    ///   exists. [`Scheduler::replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation`] binds the
8636    ///   same-raw-TID handoff explicitly.
8637    ///
8638    /// Thus both membership and within-drain resolution are functions of
8639    /// deterministic state for all current sites. The exec regression test
8640    /// forces the daemon to wait before reconnect, varies host yields, and
8641    /// compares the exact first-drain queue plus the next post-fork PRNG draw.
8642    pub(crate) fn admit_to_run_queue(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
8643        let prev = self.pending_run_queue_admissions.insert(dtid, intent);
8644        debug_assert!(
8645            prev.is_none(),
8646            "thread {:?} recorded for run-queue admission twice before draining",
8647            dtid
8648        );
8649    }
8650
8651    /// Atomically classify a same-raw-TID exec handoff and record its fresh
8652    /// admission. The scheduler mutex serializes this method with `step2`, so a
8653    /// drain can never observe only one half of the handoff.
8654    fn replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
8655        let disposition = self
8656            .pending_run_queue_removals
8657            .get_mut(&dtid)
8658            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
8659                panic!(
8660                    "exec replacement {:?} has no retired run-queue incarnation",
8661                    dtid
8662                )
8663            });
8664        assert_eq!(
8665            *disposition,
8666            RemovalDisposition::Retire,
8667            "exec replacement {:?} was classified more than once",
8668            dtid
8669        );
8670        *disposition = RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit;
8671        assert!(
8672            self.pending_run_queue_admissions
8673                .insert(dtid, intent)
8674                .is_none(),
8675            "exec replacement {:?} already had a pending admission",
8676            dtid
8677        );
8678    }
8679
8680    /// Resolve an [`AdmitIntent`] to a concrete [`AdmitSide`], consuming the
8681    /// post-fork PRNG draw for `RunsPostFork::Random`.
8682    ///
8683    /// Called at the drain rather than in the handler, so the draw is never
8684    /// consumed in host *RPC arrival* order, and the draws taken within one
8685    /// drain follow canonical `DetTid` order. This function only canonicalizes
8686    /// draws within a fixed drain; each admission site must separately bind its
8687    /// drain membership to deterministic scheduler state. See
8688    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the causal and explicit barriers
8689    /// that provide that binding for all current production sites.
8690    fn resolve_admit_intent(&mut self, intent: AdmitIntent) -> AdmitSide {
8691        match intent {
8692            AdmitIntent::Fixed(side) => side,
8693            AdmitIntent::PostFork(mode) => {
8694                if self.child_runs_first_post_fork(mode) {
8695                    AdmitSide::Front
8696                } else {
8697                    AdmitSide::Back
8698                }
8699            }
8700        }
8701    }
8702
8703    /// Record an intent to remove `dtid` from the run queue, applied by the
8704    /// daemon at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
8705    ///
8706    /// The mirror of [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the removal side, and
8707    /// deferred for the same reason: a global-request handler
8708    /// (`reconnect_after_exec` -> `logically_kill_thread`) runs on a backend
8709    /// worker and may hold the lock inside the daemon's tentative-pop window,
8710    /// where `RunQueue::remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` assert
8711    /// would trip and poison the scheduler mutex. Recording the removal and
8712    /// applying it at `step2` (window closed, guard holds) avoids that. The
8713    /// caller has already made the thread logically dead (cleared `next_turns`,
8714    /// resolved its request to `ThreadExited`), so leaving its stale run-queue
8715    /// entry in place until the drain is inert: the daemon skips it for any
8716    /// intervening turn (`step3`'s pick is validated against `next_turns`) and
8717    /// `are_all_quiesced` filters it out. On ptrace the drain runs at the next
8718    /// `step2`, before that turn's `step3` selection, so the removal is
8719    /// observationally immediate — the dead thread is never selected.
8720    fn deschedule_or_defer(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) {
8721        // A later logical death of a not-yet-drained exec replacement must
8722        // override `ReplaceThenAdmit`: `remove_blocking_entries` clears its
8723        // admission and this `Retire` disposition prevents resurrection.
8724        self.pending_run_queue_removals
8725            .insert(dtid, RemovalDisposition::Retire);
8726    }
8727
8728    /// Apply queued cross-task signal notifications at the deterministic
8729    /// run-queue mutation point. Re-check the request because a target may have
8730    /// exited or completed its wait before this drain.
8731    fn drain_pending_cross_task_signals(&mut self) {
8732        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_cross_task_signals);
8733        for (dettid, mut signals) in pending {
8734            if self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid) {
8735                // A guest's signal reached a thread asleep in a real
8736                // `rt_sigsuspend`, or stopped at that call's request, at host
8737                // speed. Linux wakes the call if its mask lets the signal
8738                // through, and the wake's signal stop is posted when the host
8739                // gets to it. Placing it here, at this fixed point, as for a
8740                // signal the scheduler sends (`wake_signaled_guest`: the release
8741                // barrier, or the record its grant arms), makes the scheduler
8742                // wait for that stop. Before, nothing did, and on a slow host
8743                // an empty run queue was reported as a deadlock first.
8744                signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
8745                signals.dedup();
8746                for signal in signals.iter().filter_map(SigWrapper::signal) {
8747                    self.wake_signaled_guest(dettid, signal);
8748                }
8749                continue;
8750            }
8751            match self.waitid_signal_request(dettid) {
8752                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked) => {
8753                    // This legacy wake completes the child-wait resource and
8754                    // replaces it with an ordinary signal grant. Retire its
8755                    // parked capability at the same ownership boundary; a
8756                    // shared alarm may become due later in this very pass.
8757                    if let Err(error) = self.retire_child_wait_signal_request(dettid) {
8758                        self.fail_parked(dettid, error);
8759                        continue;
8760                    }
8761                    // Decide run-queue residency HERE, by asking the queue, and
8762                    // never by inferring it from which resource the thread
8763                    // holds. A thread can hold either park request while already
8764                    // queued: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without
8765                    // clearing its `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue`
8766                    // pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues its
8767                    // next request. `force_unblock_thread` ends in
8768                    // `runqueue_push_*`, so pushing an already-queued thread
8769                    // trips the run-queue invariant under `debug_assertions`
8770                    // and, worse, SILENTLY double-enqueues in release — one
8771                    // thread selected twice. This mirrors `wake_signaled_guest`,
8772                    // which likewise consults `thread_status` before removing.
8773                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
8774                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
8775                        debug_assert!(
8776                            removed,
8777                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
8778                        );
8779                    }
8780                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
8781                    signals.dedup();
8782                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
8783                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
8784                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, resources);
8785                }
8786                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(existing)) => {
8787                    signals.extend(existing);
8788                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
8789                    signals.dedup();
8790                    // One resource, always. `step4_resource_block` and
8791                    // `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert a request carries
8792                    // exactly one, so this must replace the request rather than
8793                    // add to it. Only a request whose sole resource is already
8794                    // `WaitidSignals` reaches here, so nothing is discarded.
8795                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
8796                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
8797                    let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
8798                        continue;
8799                    };
8800                    next_turn.req = Ivar::full(Ok(resources));
8801                }
8802                None if let Some(interrupting) =
8803                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, 0) =>
8804                {
8805                    // A precise-mode futex waiter sleeps in `futex_waiters`, outside
8806                    // the run queue, so nothing else would ever let the physically
8807                    // pending signal interrupt it
8808                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Take it out
8809                    // of the futex and requeue it with the signal set, exactly as a
8810                    // scheduler-sent signal does in `wake_signaled_guest`: its turn
8811                    // answers `Signaled`, which the futex handler reports as the
8812                    // wait's restart errno, and the kernel then applies the guest's
8813                    // disposition. `WaitidSignals` is the one-resource form for a
8814                    // signal set, and later batches merge into it before it runs.
8815                    //
8816                    // This drain is the commit point. Admission checked only the
8817                    // waiter's mask; `interrupting` is computed from the
8818                    // dispositions the kernel holds now, with no guest thread
8819                    // holding the turn (see `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
8820                    // A signal that the sender, or a sibling later in the same
8821                    // turn, made ignored is dropped here, as the kernel drops it,
8822                    // and a waiter left with none stays registered with its
8823                    // original deadline.
8824                    signals.retain(|signal| interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0);
8825                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
8826                    signals.dedup();
8827                    if signals.is_empty() {
8828                        continue;
8829                    }
8830                    // The waiter runs next, so it is the thread that resumes
8831                    // and dequeues the signal. Its futex handler re-checks in
8832                    // its turn and parks again if nothing is pending for it.
8833                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
8834                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
8835                    self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, resources, true);
8836                }
8837                None if let Some(sleep) = self.signal_sleep(dettid) => {
8838                    // An emulated `pause` or `nanosleep`, parked in the timed
8839                    // waiters or still queued with its request
8840                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
8841                    self.drain_sleep_signals(dettid, sleep, signals);
8842                }
8843                None => {
8844                    let Some(existing) = self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid) else {
8845                        continue;
8846                    };
8847                    // ERESTARTSYS is the existing contract by which the kernel
8848                    // decides whether this physically pending signal is
8849                    // blocked, ignored, restarts the syscall, or interrupts it
8850                    // for a handler. Replace the polling request rather than
8851                    // adding a second resource; step4 accepts exactly one.
8852                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
8853                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
8854                        debug_assert!(
8855                            removed,
8856                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
8857                        );
8858                    }
8859                    signals.extend(existing);
8860                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
8861                    signals.dedup();
8862                    if signals.is_empty() {
8863                        continue;
8864                    }
8865                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
8866                    // `WaitidSignals` is already the scheduler's one-resource
8867                    // representation for a complete signal identity set. The
8868                    // ERESTARTSYS marker distinguishes this write wakeup from a
8869                    // waitid request and survives later notification batches.
8870                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
8871                    resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
8872                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, resources);
8873                }
8874            }
8875        }
8876    }
8877
8878    /// Drain removals deferred by [`Scheduler::deschedule_or_defer`] at the same
8879    /// deterministic `step2` point as admissions, and *before* them, so a thread
8880    /// killed while an admission was still buffered is not re-enqueued. The
8881    /// window is closed here (`tentative_selection` is `None`), so
8882    /// `remove_tid`'s guard holds. The `BTreeMap` makes removal order canonical;
8883    /// each disposition determines whether a same-raw-TID admission is stale or
8884    /// is the explicitly paired exec replacement.
8885    fn drain_pending_run_queue_removals(&mut self) {
8886        if self.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty() {
8887            return;
8888        }
8889        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_removals);
8890        for (dtid, disposition) in pending {
8891            match disposition {
8892                RemovalDisposition::Retire => {
8893                    // Ordinary logical death cancels a buffered admission for
8894                    // the same thread incarnation.
8895                    self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(&dtid);
8896                }
8897                RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit => {
8898                    assert!(
8899                        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid),
8900                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its scheduler registration",
8901                        dtid
8902                    );
8903                    assert!(
8904                        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid),
8905                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its paired admission",
8906                        dtid
8907                    );
8908                    assert!(
8909                        !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid),
8910                        "logically dead exec replacement {:?} reached the drain",
8911                        dtid
8912                    );
8913                }
8914            }
8915            // Always remove the old physical queue slot before a replacement
8916            // admission is applied. This prevents the new image from inheriting
8917            // the destroyed leader's round-robin position.
8918            let _ = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dtid);
8919        }
8920    }
8921
8922    /// Push `dtid` onto the run queue immediately, idempotently: a thread
8923    /// already queued is left in place rather than enqueued twice.
8924    fn admit_now(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, side: AdmitSide) {
8925        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
8926            return;
8927        }
8928        match side {
8929            AdmitSide::Front => {
8930                let _ = self.runqueue_push_front(dtid);
8931            }
8932            AdmitSide::Back => {
8933                let _ = self.runqueue_push_back(dtid);
8934            }
8935        }
8936    }
8937
8938    /// Drain admissions deferred by [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] into the
8939    /// run queue at a single deterministic point: the very start of `step2`,
8940    /// before `step3_peek` opens a tentative window (so `tentative_selection` is
8941    /// guaranteed `None` here). Draining a `BTreeMap` visits `DetTid`s in sorted
8942    /// order, so the resulting run-queue state is a pure function of the
8943    /// deterministic schedule rather than of RPC/lock-acquisition timing.
8944    fn drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(&mut self) {
8945        if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty() {
8946            return;
8947        }
8948        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_admissions);
8949        // `pending` is a `BTreeMap`, so iteration visits `DetTid`s in sorted
8950        // order. Resolving each intent here (rather than at the racing handler)
8951        // means any `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw is consumed in this
8952        // canonical order, so both the admission order *and* the chosen side are
8953        // pure functions of deterministic state.
8954        for (dtid, intent) in pending {
8955            // A thread retired (exec/kill) between record and drain is skipped.
8956            // `remove_blocking_entries` also clears the buffer on teardown, so
8957            // this guard is defensive against any teardown path that does not.
8958            if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid) {
8959                trace!(
8960                    "[step2] skipping deferred admission of retired thread {:?}",
8961                    dtid
8962                );
8963                continue;
8964            }
8965            let side = self.resolve_admit_intent(intent);
8966            self.admit_now(dtid, side);
8967        }
8968    }
8969
8970    /// Decide which side gets the first post-fork turn for an ordinary clone.
8971    pub(crate) fn child_runs_first_post_fork(&mut self, mode: RunsPostFork) -> bool {
8972        match mode {
8973            RunsPostFork::Child => true,
8974            RunsPostFork::Parent => false,
8975            RunsPostFork::Random => self.post_fork_prng.random(),
8976        }
8977    }
8978
8979    /// Check if a thread is alive, but removed from run queue.
8980    fn thread_status(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> ThreadStatus {
8981        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
8982            ThreadStatus::Running
8983        } else {
8984            // Check all the places a blocked thread could be hiding.
8985            // TODO: this O(N) search could be made more efficient with more indexing structures.
8986            for v in self.blocked.futex_waiters.values() {
8987                for waiter in v {
8988                    if waiter.dettid == dtid {
8989                        return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
8990                    }
8991                }
8992            }
8993            for (_, evt) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
8994                match evt {
8995                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dt) => {
8996                        if dt == dtid {
8997                            return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
8998                        }
8999                    }
9000                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(_, _, _) => {}
9001                }
9002            }
9003            if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid) {
9004                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
9005            }
9006            if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
9007                || self.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&dtid)
9008                || self
9009                    .blocked
9010                    .physical_child_waiters
9011                    .values()
9012                    .any(|waiters| waiters.contains(&dtid))
9013            {
9014                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
9015            }
9016            if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid) {
9017                return ThreadStatus::Running;
9018            }
9019            // Held at a happens-before gate: alive, out of the run queue until
9020            // a source fires. Reporting it as gone made a signal sent to it
9021            // (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) panic `wake_signaled_guest`.
9022            if self
9023                .happens_before
9024                .as_ref()
9025                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dtid))
9026            {
9027                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
9028            }
9029            ThreadStatus::Gone
9030        }
9031    }

9035    /// Fold an exiting thread's completed-timeslice distribution into the
9036    /// scheduler's per-thread record, to be reported in the final run summary.
9037    pub fn record_timeslice_stats(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, stats: TimesliceStats) {
9038        if stats.is_empty() {

9047    /// Record an exiting thread's final completed-syscall count.
9048    pub fn record_syscall_count(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) {
9049        let consumed = self
9050            .transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
9051            .get(&dettid)
9052            .copied()
9053            .unwrap_or(0);
9054        let total = consumed
9055            .checked_add(count)
9056            .expect("transferred exec syscall count overflow");
9057        self.per_thread_syscalls.insert(dettid, total);
9058    }

9060    /// Summarize the run after completion, as a RunSummary. This is partial because the Scheduler
9061    /// does not have all the necessary information.
9062    ///
9063    /// Side Effects: This also flushes the in-memory PreemptionWriter to disk.
9064    #[cfg(test)]
9065    pub fn generate_partial_run_summary(
9066        &mut self,
9067        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
9068    ) -> anyhow::Result<RunSummary> {
9069        self.generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(preemptions_to)
9070            .map(|(summary, _)| summary)
9071    }
9072
9073    /// Build the full report and the INFO preemption description together.
9074    /// The latter retains counts/history but excludes the host output filename.
9075    /// This performs one generation and flush.
9076    pub(crate) fn generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(
9077        &mut self,
9078        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
9079    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RunSummary, Option<String>)> {
9080        let schedevent_replayed = self
9081            .replayer
9082            .as_ref()
9083            .map(|r| r.events_popped)
9084            .unwrap_or_default();
9085        let total_desync_stats = self
9086            .replayer
9087            .as_ref()
9088            .map(|r| {
9089                r.desync_counts
9090                    .values()
9091                    .fold(Default::default(), |x: DesyncStats, y: &DesyncStats| x + *y)
9092            })
9093            .unwrap_or_default();
9094
9095        let total_desyncs = total_desync_stats.soft + total_desync_stats.hard;
9096        let desync_descrip = if total_desyncs > 0 {
9097            let mut buf = String::new();
9098            write!(
9099                buf,
9100                "  Encountered {} soft desyncs, {} hard (with {} at context switch points), {} resyncs ({}/{} insertion/deletion).\n  Per thread (soft,hard,@switch,resync): ",
9101                total_desync_stats.soft,
9102                total_desync_stats.hard,
9103                total_desync_stats.at_context_switch,
9104                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions + total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
9105                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions,
9106                total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
9107            )?;
9108            if let Some(ref replayer) = self.replayer {
9109                for (tid, desync_stats) in replayer.desync_counts.iter() {
9110                    write!(
9111                        buf,
9112                        "{}=>({},{},{},{}) ",
9113                        tid,
9114                        desync_stats.soft,
9115                        desync_stats.hard,
9116                        desync_stats.at_context_switch,
9117                        desync_stats.resync_insertions + desync_stats.resync_deletions,
9118                    )?;
9119                }
9120            }
9121            writeln!(buf)?;
9122            Some(buf)
9123        } else {
9124            None
9125        };
9126
9127        let (reprio_descrip, info_reprio_descrip) = if let Some(pw) = self.preemption_writer.take()
9128        {
9129            let mut buf = String::new();
9130            writeln!(
9131                buf,
9132                "Record of {} preemption and reprioritization events:",
9133                pw.len()
9134            )?;
9135            let info_description;
9136            if let Some(path) = preemptions_to {
9137                // Preserve the full human/JSON description; build the INFO
9138                // description before adding the host artifact destination.
9139                info_description = buf.clone();
9140                writeln!(buf, "  (Writing to file {:?})", path)?;
9141                if let Err(str) = pw.flush() {
9142                    tracing::warn!("{}", str);
9143                }
9144            } else {
9145                // Recording, but not outputting to file, so this is the only (partial) record of it:
9146                writeln!(buf, "{}", truncated(200, pw.into_string()))?;
9147                info_description = buf.clone();
9148            }
9149            (Some(buf), Some(info_description))
9150        } else {
9151            (None, None)
9152        };
9153
9154        let num_processes = self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.len() as u64;
9155        let num_threads = self.thread_tree.size() as u64;
9156        let threads_descrip = format!("{}", self.thread_tree);
9157
9158        // Aggregate the per-thread timeslice distributions collected at thread
9159        // exit. BTreeMap gives a deterministic (dettid-sorted) ordering.
9160        let per_thread_timeslice: Vec<(DetTid, TimesliceStats)> = self
9161            .per_thread_timeslice
9162            .iter()
9163            .map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v))
9164            .collect();
9165        let mut timeslice_stats = TimesliceStats::default();
9166        for (_, st) in &per_thread_timeslice {
9167            timeslice_stats.merge(st);
9168        }
9169        let syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.values().copied().sum();
9170
9171        Ok((
9172            RunSummary {
9173                sched_turns: self.turn,
9174                schedevent_replayed,
9175                schedevent_recorded: self.recorded_event_count,
9176                schedevent_desynced: total_desyncs,
9177                // schedevent_desynced_at_context_switch: total_desyncs.at_context_switch,
9178                desync_descrip,
9179                reprio_descrip,
9180                threads_descrip,
9181                num_processes,
9182                num_threads,
9183                syscalls: Some(syscalls),
9184                virttime_elapsed: 0, // Cannot fill.
9185                virttime_final: 0,   // Cannot fill.
9186                realtime_elapsed: None,
9187                timeslice_stats,
9188                per_thread_timeslice,
9189                // The backend, not the scheduler, measures dispatch.
9190                dispatch_stats: None,
9191            },
9192            info_reprio_descrip,
9193        ))
9194    }

9196    /// Summarize the state of the scheduler while executing (verbose).
9197    pub fn full_summary(&self) -> String {
9198        let mut buf = String::new();
9199        write!(&mut buf, "  {}", self.run_queue).unwrap();
9200
9201        let total_futex_blocked: usize = self.blocked.futex_waiters.iter().map(|v| v.1.len()).sum();
9202        writeln!(
9203            &mut buf,
9204            "\n  Futex-waiters, {} blocked on {} futexes:",
9205            total_futex_blocked,
9206            self.blocked.futex_waiters.len()
9207        )
9208        .unwrap();
9209        // Sorted, and no `Ivar` Debug. `format_terminal_deadlock` above already
9210        // documents the two sources this avoids, and this function had neither
9211        // guard: `futex_waiters` is a `HashMap`, so it iterates in a randomized
9212        // order once it holds more than one entry, and `FutexWaiter`'s derived
9213        // `Debug` prints its `Ivar`'s parked waker as raw host pointers.
9214        //
9215        // Measured before this change, three runs of
9216        // `--stop-after-turn=15 -- rustbin_futex_and_print`, which reaches this
9217        // function through the `--stop-after-turn` warning:
9218        //   Waker { data: 0x564ea2a82c80
9219        //   Waker { data: 0x55f2120b9c80
9220        //   Waker { data: 0x56163deeec80
9221        // Three runs, three host addresses, in a WARN record that
9222        // `--verify-strict` compares.
9223        //
9224        // Only guest-level identities are printed here: the futex key, the
9225        // waiting dettid and the bitset are all values Detcore already
9226        // determinizes.
9227        let mut futex_rows: Vec<String> = self
9228            .blocked
9229            .futex_waiters
9230            .iter()
9231            .map(|(futex, waiters)| {
9232                let mut dettids: Vec<String> =
9233                    waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid.to_string()).collect();
9234                dettids.sort();
9235                let mut bitsets: Vec<u32> = waiters.iter().map(|w| w.bitset).collect();
9236                bitsets.sort_unstable();
9237                format!(
9238                    "    {:?} => {} waiter(s), dettids [{}], bitsets {:?}",
9239                    futex,
9240                    waiters.len(),
9241                    dettids.join(", "),
9242                    bitsets
9243                )
9244            })
9245            .collect();
9246        futex_rows.sort();
9247        for row in futex_rows {
9248            writeln!(&mut buf, "{}", row).unwrap();
9249        }
9250
9251        writeln!(
9252            &mut buf,
9253            "\n  Timed-waiters, {}:",
9254            self.blocked.timed_waiters.len()
9255        )
9256        .unwrap();
9257        for (time, dtid) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
9258            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {} => {}", time, dtid).unwrap();
9259        }
9260
9261        writeln!(
9262            &mut buf,
9263            "\n  External-IO-blocked, {}:",
9264            self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len(),
9265        )
9266        .unwrap();
9267        for x in &self.blocked.external_io_blockers {
9268            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
9269        }
9270
9271        writeln!(
9272            &mut buf,
9273            "\n  Rt-sigsuspend-blocked, {}:",
9274            self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len(),
9275        )
9276        .unwrap();
9277        for x in &self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers {
9278            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
9279        }
9280
9281        writeln!(&mut buf, "\n  Next_turns: ").unwrap();
9282        for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
9283            writeln!(
9284                &mut buf,
9285                " ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}",
9286                dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp
9287            )
9288            .unwrap();
9289        }
9290        buf
9291    }

9293    // Return whether we should print the stacktrace after recording this event.
9294    // This is redundant with the consume_schedevent logic but allows us to print on either
9295    // recording or replay.
9296    pub fn record_event(&mut self, ev: &SchedEvent) -> MaybePrintStack {
9297        debug!(
9298            "[dtid {}] Record scheduled event #{}: {:?}",
9299            &ev.dettid, self.recorded_event_count, ev
9300        );
9301        let pw = self
9302            .preemption_writer
9303            .as_mut()
9304            .expect("trace_schedevent should be called only when preemption_writer is set");
9305        pw.insert_schedevent(ev.clone());
9306
9307        let print_stack = self.try_pop_stacktrace_event(self.recorded_event_count, ev);
9308        self.recorded_event_count += 1;
9309        print_stack
9310    }

9312    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
9313    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
9314    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#869)
9315    // Returns the logical duration until any previously scheduled alarm, if any (zero otherwise).
9316    pub fn register_alarm(
9317        &mut self,
9318        detpid: DetPid,
9319        dettid: DetTid,
9320        now: LogicalTime,
9321        duration: LogicalTime,
9322        interval: LogicalTime,
9323        sig: Signal,
9324    ) -> (LogicalTime, LogicalTime) {
9325        let old = if duration == LogicalTime::ZERO {
9326            // Alarm of 0 cancels any pending signal.
9327            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_alarm(detpid)
9328        } else {
9329            let target_time = now + duration;
9330            self.blocked
9331                .timed_waiters
9332                .insert_alarm(target_time, detpid, dettid, sig, interval)
9333        };
9334        if let Some((old_target_time, old_interval)) = old {
9335            let remain_ns = old_target_time.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos());
9336            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(remain_ns), old_interval)
9337        } else {
9338            // Return 0 if no previous alarm, as per https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/alarm.2.html
9339            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::ZERO)
9340        }
9341    }

9343    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
9344    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#869)
9345    pub fn register_posix_timer(
9346        &mut self,
9347        detpid: DetPid,
9348        dettid: DetTid,
9349        timer_id: i32,
9350        deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
9351        interval: LogicalTime,
9352        sig: timed_waiters::TimerSignal,
9353    ) {
9354        if let Some(deadline) = deadline {
9355            self.blocked
9356                .timed_waiters
9357                .insert_posix_timer(deadline, detpid, dettid, timer_id, sig, interval);
9358        } else {
9359            self.blocked
9360                .timed_waiters
9361                .remove_posix_timer(detpid, timer_id);
9362        }
9363    }

9365    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
9366    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-841): Review logical ITIMER_REAL state queries.
9367    pub fn alarm_remaining(&self, detpid: DetPid, now: LogicalTime) -> LogicalTime {
9368        self.blocked
9369            .timed_waiters
9370            .alarm_time(detpid)
9371            .map(|deadline| {
9372                LogicalTime::from_nanos(deadline.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos()))
9373            })
9374            .unwrap_or(LogicalTime::ZERO)
9375    }

9424    #[test]
9425    fn chaos_pick_is_seed_deterministic_and_covers_all_choices() {
9426        let choices = [10, 20, 30, 40];
9427
9428        // Same seed => identical sequence of picks (the reproducibility that
9429        // targeted chaos relies on).
9430        let mut a = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
9431        let mut b = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
9432        for _ in 0..64 {
9433            assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut a, &choices), chaos_pick(&mut b, &choices));
9434        }
9435
9436        // Over enough draws every choice is reachable (the bias actually explores
9437        // the space rather than pinning one option).
9438        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(9);
9439        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
9440        for _ in 0..256 {
9441            seen.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &choices).unwrap());
9442        }
9443        assert_eq!(
9444            seen,
9445            choices.iter().copied().collect(),
9446            "chaos_pick should be able to return every choice"
9447        );
9448
9449        // An empty slice yields None rather than panicking.
9450        assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[] as &[i32]), None);
9451
9452        // The front/back coin flip used by force_unblock_thread reaches both.
9453        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(7);
9454        let mut both = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
9455        for _ in 0..64 {
9456            both.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[true, false]).unwrap());
9457        }
9458        assert_eq!(both, [false, true].into_iter().collect());
9459    }

9578    /// A four-generation chain of single-threaded processes, each live in the
9579    /// run set: root 1, its child 2, grandchild 3 and great-grandchild 4.
9580    /// Process 4 is a clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal.
9581    fn process_chain() -> Scheduler {
9582        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
9583        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9584        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
9585        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
9586        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
9587        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
9588            middle,
9589            orphan,
9590            true,
9591            false,
9592            libc::SIGUSR1,
9593        );
9594        for pid in [root, inner, middle, orphan] {
9595            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
9596        }
9597        scheduler
9598    }
9599
9600    /// The exit of single-threaded `pid` after its Exit grant: what an
9601    /// `exit_group` does.
9602    fn exit_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, pid: DetPid) {
9603        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(pid);
9604        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&pid, &pid, MmId::initial(pid));
9605    }
9606
9607    /// `logically_kill_thread` runs again for a process that is already dead,
9608    /// from a thread's late exit hook at a moment the host chooses. An orphan
9609    /// already given to init is not searched for a subreaper again, even if a
9610    /// subreaper has appeared since, so the outcome is the first decision's.
9611    #[test]
9612    fn a_late_second_exit_record_does_not_re_decide_an_init_orphan() {
9613        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9614        let [root, _, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9615        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9616        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9617
9618        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9619        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
9620
9621        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9622        assert_eq!(
9623            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9624            Some(middle)
9625        );
9626        assert!(
9627            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
9628        );
9629    }
9630
9631    /// A parent that died without an Exit grant (killed) is recorded at its
9632    /// host-timed deregistration, and so is a subreaper's adoption of its
9633    /// orphans (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). The adoption
9634    /// records a determinism loss instead of passing as deterministic.
9635    #[test]
9636    fn adopting_the_orphans_of_a_killed_parent_records_a_determinism_loss() {
9637        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9638        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9639        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9640        assert!(!scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&middle));
9641
9642        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
9643
9644        assert_eq!(
9645            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9646            Some(inner)
9647        );
9648        assert_eq!(scheduler.determinism_losses.len(), 1);
9649        assert!(
9650            scheduler.determinism_losses[0].contains("without an Exit grant"),
9651            "{:?}",
9652            scheduler.determinism_losses
9653        );
9654    }
9655
9656    /// A subreaper outside a PID namespace never adopts from inside it: the
9657    /// search stops where the depth changes. An inner process's orphan, and
9658    /// the orphan of the namespace's own init, are left to init.
9659    #[test]
9660    fn a_subreaper_does_not_adopt_across_a_pid_namespace_boundary() {
9661        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9662        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9663        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9664        // `inner` is a namespace init; `middle` and `orphan` live inside it.
9665        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
9666        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
9667        tree.add_child(root, root, true);
9668        tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
9669        tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
9670        tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
9671        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(inner), 1);
9672        assert_eq!(
9673            tree.pid_ns_depth(middle),
9674            1,
9675            "a child inherits its creator's depth"
9676        );
9677        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(root), 0);
9678        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
9679        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
9680
9681        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9682        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9683        assert!(
9684            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
9685        );
9686
9687        // The namespace init itself dies: its children are not adopted by the
9688        // outer subreaper either.
9689        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9690        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9691        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
9692        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
9693        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9694        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9695    }
9696
9697    /// Orphans are decided in ascending pid order whatever order the hash map
9698    /// holds them in: 64 children, so a hash order that happens to be sorted
9699    /// is out of the question.
9700    #[test]
9701    fn orphans_are_decided_in_pid_order() {
9702        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
9703        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(1);
9704        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
9705        let children: Vec<DetPid> = (0..64).map(|i| DetPid::from_raw(1000 - 7 * i)).collect();
9706        for child in &children {
9707            tree.add_child(parent, *child, true);
9708        }
9709        let mut expected = children.clone();
9710        expected.sort();
9711        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected);
9712        tree.orphan_to_init(expected[0]);
9713        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected[1..]);
9714    }

9716    /// A normal exit records no loss: its Exit grant fixed it between turns.
9717    #[test]
9718    fn adopting_the_orphans_of_an_exited_parent_records_no_determinism_loss() {
9719        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9720        let [_, inner, middle, _] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9721        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9722        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9723        assert!(scheduler.determinism_losses.is_empty());
9724    }

9726    /// A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process in
9727    /// the thread tree, but the backend reports its exit with its creator's
9728    /// pid. Its orphans are still decided when its last thread leaves.
9729    #[test]
9730    fn a_raw_clone_processs_exit_re_parents_its_orphans() {
9731        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
9732        let [root, creator, raw, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9733        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
9734        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, creator, true);
9735        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
9736            creator,
9737            raw,
9738            true,
9739            false,
9740            libc::SIGUSR1,
9741        );
9742        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(raw, orphan, true);
9743        for pid in [root, creator, raw, orphan] {
9744            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
9745        }
9746        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(creator, true);
9747        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(raw);
9748
9749        // The backend names the creator, which is still live.
9750        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&raw, &creator, MmId::initial(creator));
9751
9752        assert_eq!(
9753            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9754            Some(creator)
9755        );
9756        assert!(scheduler.determinism_losses.is_empty());
9757    }

9759    /// The Exit grant records the granted exit under the process the thread
9760    /// tree registered the exiting thread in: the raw clone child itself, not
9761    /// the creator the backend names.
9762    #[test]
9763    fn an_exit_grant_marks_the_registered_process_as_granted() {
9764        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9765        let middle = DetPid::from_raw(3);
9766        grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, middle);
9767        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&middle));
9768
9769        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
9770        let [root, creator, raw] = [1, 2, 3].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9771        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
9772        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, creator, true);
9773        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
9774            creator,
9775            raw,
9776            true,
9777            false,
9778            libc::SIGUSR1,
9779        );
9780        for pid in [root, creator, raw] {
9781            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
9782        }
9783        grant_group_exit_from(&mut scheduler, raw, creator);
9784        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&raw));
9785        assert!(!scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&creator));
9786    }

9788    /// A reused pid starts without the old process's subreaper flag, init
9789    /// orphan mark or granted exit.
9790    #[test]
9791    fn a_reused_pid_starts_without_the_old_processes_subreaper_state() {
9792        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
9793        let [root, child] = [1, 2].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9794        tree.add_child(root, root, true);
9795        tree.add_child(root, child, true);
9796        tree.set_child_subreaper(child, true);
9797        tree.orphan_to_init(child);
9798        tree.granted_exits.insert(child);
9799        tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(child);
9800
9801        tree.add_child(root, child, true);
9802
9803        assert!(!tree.is_child_subreaper(child));
9804        assert!(!tree.is_init_orphan(child));
9805        assert!(!tree.granted_exits.contains(&child));
9806        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(child), 0);

9809    /// When its parent's process exits, an orphan's wait parent becomes the
9810    /// nearest live child subreaper, as Linux's `forget_original_parent`
9811    /// does, with SIGCHLD as its exit signal (`reparent_leader`)
9812    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3997).
9813    #[test]
9814    fn an_orphan_goes_to_its_nearest_live_child_subreaper() {
9815        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9816        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9817        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9818        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9819        let orphan_wait = normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan));
9820        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
9821
9822        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9823
9824        assert!(scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
9825
9826        let metadata = scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan];
9827        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_parent, Some(inner));
9828        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_owner, inner);
9829        assert_eq!(metadata.exit_signal, libc::SIGCHLD);
9830        assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_tree.parent_process(&orphan), Some(inner));
9831        assert_eq!(
9832            scheduler.thread_tree.notification_signal(orphan),
9833            Some(libc::SIGCHLD)
9834        );
9835        assert_eq!(
9836            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(inner, orphan),
9837            ExactChildWaitState::Running
9838        );
9839        assert_eq!(
9840            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(middle, orphan),
9841            ExactChildWaitState::Unknown
9842        );
9843
9844        // The orphan exits: its new parent can wait for it.
9845        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
9846        assert_eq!(
9847            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
9848            Some(middle),
9849            "the exited child, the lower pid, is selected first"
9850        );
9851        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, middle));
9852        assert_eq!(
9853            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
9854            Some(orphan)
9855        );
9856        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, orphan));
9857        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)));
9858    }
9859
9860    /// An orphan that has already exited when its parent does becomes
9861    /// waitable by the subreaper at that moment.
9862    #[test]
9863    fn an_exited_orphan_becomes_waitable_by_the_subreaper() {
9864        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9865        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9866        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9867        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
9868        assert_eq!(
9869            scheduler.ready_child_wait(middle, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
9870            None,
9871            "a clone child does not match a SIGCHLD-class wait"
9872        );
9873
9874        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9875
9876        assert_eq!(
9877            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
9878            Some(orphan),
9879            "re-parenting made it a SIGCHLD child of the subreaper"
9880        );
9881    }

9883    /// Without a live subreaper among its ancestors an orphan has no guest
9884    /// parent (the container's init). A subreaper with no live thread is
9885    /// skipped, and clearing the flag takes a process out of the search.
9886    #[test]
9887    fn an_orphan_without_a_live_subreaper_has_no_guest_parent() {
9888        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9889        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9890        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9891        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, false);
9892        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9893        // The record still names the dead parent, as before subreapers were
9894        // modeled, and no live process can wait for the orphan.
9895        assert_eq!(
9896            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9897            Some(middle)
9898        );
9899        assert_eq!(
9900            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].exit_signal,
9901            libc::SIGUSR1
9902        );
9903        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9904        for parent in [root, inner] {
9905            assert!(
9906                !scheduler
9907                    .has_child_wait_target(parent, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
9908            );
9909        }
9910
9911        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9912        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9913        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9914        // The inner subreaper has left the run set but is still its parent
9915        // in the record.
9916        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&inner);
9917        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9918        assert_eq!(
9919            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9920            Some(root)
9921        );
9922    }
