9924    /// An orphan that went to the container's init keeps naming its dead
9925    /// parent, but its real parent is init. So when it exits in turn, its own
9926    /// children go to init too, even if a process above the dead parent has
9927    /// become a subreaper since.
9928    #[test]
9929    fn an_init_orphans_children_do_not_climb_the_stale_parent_chain() {
9930        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9931        let [root, _, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9932        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(5);
9933        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(orphan, grandchild, true);
9934        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, grandchild);
9935        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9936        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
9937
9938        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9939        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
9940
9941        assert_eq!(
9942            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&grandchild].wait_parent,
9943            Some(orphan)
9944        );
9945        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(grandchild));
9946        assert!(
9947            !scheduler
9948                .has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(grandchild)))
9949        );
9950    }

9952    /// When a subreaper itself exits, the orphans it had inherited move on to
9953    /// the next subreaper up the chain, through the edges already moved.
9954    #[test]
9955    fn a_subreapers_inherited_orphans_move_on_when_it_exits() {
9956        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9957        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9958        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
9959        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9960        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9961        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, middle));
9962
9963        exit_process(&mut scheduler, inner);
9964
9965        assert_eq!(
9966            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
9967            Some(root)
9968        );
9969        assert_eq!(
9970            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&inner].wait_parent,
9971            Some(root)
9972        );
9973        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(root, inner));
9974        assert!(!scheduler.thread_tree.is_child_subreaper(inner));
9975    }

9977    /// A parked waiter of the subreaper wakes when an exited orphan is
9978    /// re-parented to it.
9979    #[test]
9980    fn re_parenting_an_exited_orphan_wakes_the_subreapers_waiter() {
9981        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
9982        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
9983        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
9984        let spec = normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan));
9985        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(inner, (inner, spec));
9986        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
9987        assert!(scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&inner));
9988
9989        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
9990
9991        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&inner));
9992        assert!(scheduler.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&inner));
9993    }

9995    #[test]
9996    fn dbt_process_sigkill_completes_registered_child_lifecycle() {
9997        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
9998            backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
9999        });
10000        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
10001        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(37);
10002        let child = DetTid::from_raw(38);
10003        let child_mm = MmId::for_clone(MmId::initial(parent), child, false);
10004        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
10005        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
10006        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
10007        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
10008        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
10009        scheduler
10010            .register_physical_thread(child, child_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
10011            .expect("PIDFD_THREAD must bind the current test thread");
10012
10013        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(child, child);
10014
10015        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&child));
10016        assert!(!scheduler.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&child));
10017        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child));
10018    }

10020    fn install_runnable_exec_group(
10021        sched: &mut Scheduler,
10022        leader: DetTid,
10023        caller: DetTid,
10024    ) -> (DetPid, MmId, Ivar<SchedRequest>) {
10025        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
10026        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
10027        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
10028        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
10029        register_known_thread(sched, leader);
10030        register_known_thread(sched, caller);
10031        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
10032        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
10033        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
10034        (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request)
10035    }

10073    fn exec_replay(
10074        caller: DetTid,
10075        next: DetTid,
10076        following: DetTid,
10077        branches: Option<u32>,
10078    ) -> (Replayer, SchedEvent) {
10079        let prehook = SchedEvent::syscall(caller, Sysno::execve, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
10080            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000));
10081        let mut events = vec![prehook.clone()];
10082        if let Some(count) = branches {
10083            let branch = SchedEvent::branches(next, count)
10084                .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000) + LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
10085            let other = SchedEvent {
10086                op: detcore_model::schedule::Op::OtherInstructions,
10087                count: 1,
10088                ..branch.clone()
10089            };
10090            events.extend([branch, other]);
10091        } else {
10092            events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
10093                next,
10094                Sysno::getpid,
10095                SyscallPhase::Prehook,
10096            ));
10097        }
10098        events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
10099            following,
10100            Sysno::getpid,
10101            SyscallPhase::Prehook,
10102        ));
10103        (Replayer::new(events), prehook)
10104    }

10106    #[tokio::test]
10107    async fn transferred_exec_reconnect_restores_replay_pre_hook_continuation_grant() {
10108        for branches in [Some(123), None] {
10109            let config = Config::default();
10110            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
10111            let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
10112            let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
10113            let unrelated = DetTid::from_raw(31);
10114            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request) =
10115                install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
10116            register_known_thread(&mut sched, unrelated);
10117            sched.runqueue_push_back(unrelated);
10118            let (replayer, prehook) = exec_replay(caller, leader, unrelated, branches);
10119            sched.replayer = Some(replayer);
10120            let duration = branches.map(|count| LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
10121
10122            // Exercise the actual prehook ContextSwitch(false, leader, ..),
10123            // including the priority and pending duration it stages.
10124            let consumed = sched.consume_schedevent(&prehook);
10125            assert!(consumed.keep_running);
10126            assert_eq!(consumed.event_ix, 0);
10127            assert_eq!(consumed.timeslice_remaining, duration);
10128            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&caller], REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
10129            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
10130            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
10131
10132            // The backend consumes the displaced leader before post-exec.
10133            // That removes its priority, but not its pending timeslice.
10134            sched.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
10135            let caller_request = sched.next_turns[&caller].req.clone();
10136            sched.turn = 41;
10137            sched.committed_time = GlobalTime::new(&config).as_nanos();
10138            let before = (sched.turn, sched.committed_time);
10139            let next_event = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap().cursor.peek().cloned();
10140            reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
10141
10142            assert_eq!((sched.turn, sched.committed_time), before);
10143            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
10144            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
10145            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&caller));
10146            assert!(matches!(caller_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
10147            assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
10148            assert_ne!(sched.next_turns[&leader].req, old_leader_request);
10149            let replayer = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap();
10150            assert_eq!(replayer.traced_event_count, 1);
10151            assert_eq!(replayer.events_popped, 1);
10152            assert_eq!(replayer.cursor.peek(), next_event.as_ref());
10153            assert_eq!(
10154                replayer.desync_counts,
10155                BTreeMap::from([(caller, replayer::DesyncStats::default())])
10156            );
10157
10158            for tid in [leader, unrelated] {
10159                let mut resources = Resources::new(tid);
10160                resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(tid), Permission::RW);
10161                sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(resources));
10162            }
10163            let continuation = sched.next_turns[&leader].resp.clone();
10164            let unrelated_response = sched.next_turns[&unrelated].resp.clone();
10165            assert!(continuation.try_read().is_none());
10166            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
10167            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
10168            let granted = tokio::time::timeout(
10169                Duration::from_secs(5),
10170                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
10171            )
10172            .await
10173            .expect("the continuation grant must not stall")
10174            .expect("the replay continuation must be runnable");
10175            assert_eq!(granted.tid, leader);
10176            let Some(SchedResponse::Go(granted_duration)) = continuation.try_read() else {
10177                panic!("replacement did not receive an ordinary continuation grant");
10178            };
10179            assert_eq!(
10180                granted_duration,
10181                duration.map(|time| SchedValue::Value(time.as_nanos()))
10182            );
10183            assert!(unrelated_response.try_read().is_none());
10184            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
10185            assert_eq!(sched.turn, before.0 + 1);
10186            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&leader));
10187            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
10188            assert_eq!(
10189                sched.run_queue.tids().filter(|tid| **tid == leader).count(),
10190                1
10191            );
10192        }
10193    }

10197        let config = Config::default();

10209        sched.replayer = Some(replayer);

10504    /// F1/F2: an admission deferred while a tentative_pop window is live must
10505    /// resolve its side -- including the `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw -- at
10506    /// the `DetTid`-ordered drain, so the drained run queue is a pure function of
10507    /// deterministic state, independent of the order in which racing handlers
10508    /// buffered the admissions.
10509    #[test]
10510    fn deferred_admission_side_is_arrival_order_independent() {
10511        let config = Config {
10512            sched_seed: Some(0xABCD),
10513            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
10514            ..Default::default()
10515        };
10516        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
10517        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
10518
10519        // Buffer the two children in `order`, optionally while a tentative
10520        // window is live, then drain. Return the drained relative order of the
10521        // two children (the anchor is filtered out because it is consumed by the
10522        // window in the `open_window` case but not otherwise -- what must be
10523        // deterministic is the children's order and chosen sides).
10524        let drained_order = |order: [DetTid; 2], open_window: bool| -> Vec<DetTid> {
10525            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
10526            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
10527            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
10528            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
10529            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
10530            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
10531
10532            if open_window {
10533                assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
10534                assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
10535            }
10536            for tid in order {
10537                sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
10538            }
10539            // Admission ALWAYS defers -- window or not -- so nothing is pushed or
10540            // resolved (no side chosen, no PRNG drawn) until the drain.
10541            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&lower));
10542            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&higher));
10543            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(lower));
10544            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(higher));
10545
10546            if open_window {
10547                let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
10548            }
10549            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
10550            sched
10551                .run_queue
10552                .tids()
10553                .copied()
10554                .filter(|t| *t == lower || *t == higher)
10555                .collect()
10556        };
10557
10558        // The drained order/side is independent of BOTH host-timing inputs the
10559        // old immediate path was sensitive to: the arrival (buffering) order of
10560        // the racing handlers, and whether a tentative window happened to be
10561        // live when each handler ran.
10562        let baseline = drained_order([lower, higher], true);
10563        assert_eq!(
10564            baseline,
10565            drained_order([higher, lower], true),
10566            "arrival order"
10567        );
10568        assert_eq!(
10569            baseline,
10570            drained_order([lower, higher], false),
10571            "window state"
10572        );
10573        assert_eq!(baseline, drained_order([higher, lower], false), "both");
10574        assert!(baseline.contains(&lower) && baseline.contains(&higher));
10575    }

10577    #[test]
10578    fn robust_list_wake_batches_are_arrival_order_independent() {
10579        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
10580        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
10581        let first_owner = DetTid::from_raw(31);
10582        let second_owner = DetTid::from_raw(33);
10583        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(5));
10584        let lower_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100);
10585        let higher_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200);
10586
10587        let deliver = |reverse: bool| {
10588            let mut first = ThreadState::<()>::new(first_owner, &Config::default(), ());
10589            let mut second = first.clone();
10590            second.dettid = second_owner;
10591            first.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404100));
10592            second.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404200));
10593            first.stage_robust_list_wakes(
10594                RobustListExit::ExitGroup,
10595                vec![
10596                    (
10597                        second_owner,
10598                        vec![RobustListWake {
10599                            futex: higher_futex,
10600                        }],
10601                    ),
10602                    (first_owner, vec![RobustListWake { futex: lower_futex }]),
10603                ],
10604            );
10605            let first_time = DetTime::default();
10606            let mut second_time = first_time.clone();
10607            second_time.add_syscall();
10608            let ready = if reverse {
10609                assert_eq!(
10610                    second.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time.clone()),
10611                    None,
10612                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
10613                );
10614                first
10615                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time)
10616                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
10617                    .1
10618            } else {
10619                assert_eq!(
10620                    first.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time),
10621                    None,
10622                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
10623                );
10624                second
10625                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time)
10626                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
10627                    .1
10628            };
10629            let request: Vec<_> = ready
10630                .into_iter()
10631                .map(|(owner, wake)| (owner, wake.futex))
10632                .collect();
10633            assert_eq!(
10634                request,
10635                vec![(first_owner, lower_futex), (second_owner, higher_futex)],
10636                "one owner/futex-sorted request must carry the complete group"
10637            );
10638
10639            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
10640            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
10641            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
10642            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
10643            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
10644            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
10645            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&lower, lower_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
10646            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&higher, higher_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
10647
10648            assert_eq!(sched.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&request), vec![1, 1]);
10649
10650            let pending: Vec<_> = sched
10651                .pending_run_queue_admissions
10652                .iter()
10653                .map(|(tid, intent)| (*tid, *intent))
10654                .collect();
10655            assert_eq!(
10656                pending,
10657                vec![
10658                    (lower, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
10659                    (higher, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
10660                ]
10661            );
10662            assert_eq!(
10663                sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
10664                vec![anchor],
10665                "physical-exit wakes must wait for the deterministic drain"
10666            );
10667
10668            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
10669            let drained = sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>();
10670            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
10671            (pending, drained)
10672        };
10673
10674        let forward = deliver(false);
10675        let reverse = deliver(true);
10676        assert_eq!(forward, reverse);
10677        assert_eq!(forward.1, vec![DetTid::from_raw(5), lower, higher]);
10678    }

10680    /// F3: a run-queue removal requested while a tentative_pop window is live
10681    /// (an asynchronous exec reconnect racing the daemon) must be deferred, not
10682    /// applied through `remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` guard, and
10683    /// a pending-removal thread whose `next_turns` entry is already gone must not
10684    /// crash `are_all_quiesced`. The removal lands at the next drain.
10685    /// ITEM 1 REGRESSION: a NON-LEADER thread is live, even though it is not a
10686    /// kill target.
10687    ///
10688    /// `process_signal_targets` models `kill(2)`, whose first act is to refuse
10689    /// anything that is not a thread-group leader. `sched_setattr(2)` and its
10690    /// relatives resolve through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds any live
10691    /// task. Answering the second question with the first resolver reports
10692    /// ESRCH for a thread that is plainly running, so the two must stay
10693    /// distinguishable -- this test fails the moment `thread_is_live` is
10694    /// reduced to the kill resolver.
10695    #[test]
10696    fn a_non_leader_thread_is_live_without_being_a_kill_target() {
10697        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
10698        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(11);
10699        let member = DetTid::from_raw(12);
10700        let stranger = DetTid::from_raw(13);
10701        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
10702        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, member, false);
10703        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
10704        register_known_thread(&mut sched, member);
10705
10706        assert!(sched.thread_is_live(leader), "the leader is obviously live");
10707        assert!(
10708            sched.thread_is_live(member),
10709            "a non-leader thread of a live group is live; sched_setattr must reach it"
10710        );
10711        assert!(
10712            !sched.thread_is_live(stranger),
10713            "a tid that was never registered is not live"
10714        );
10715
10716        // The distinction being preserved: the kill resolver still declines the
10717        // non-leader, which is correct for kill(2) and wrong for sched_setattr.
10718        assert!(
10719            sched.process_signal_targets(member).is_empty(),
10720            "kill(2) semantics: a non-leader is not a signal target, which is \
10721             exactly why it is the wrong resolver for a tid lookup"
10722        );
10723        assert!(
10724            !sched.process_signal_targets(leader).is_empty(),
10725            "the leader is a signal target, so the fixture is wired correctly"
10726        );
10727    }
10728
10729    #[test]
10730    fn deferred_removal_survives_tentative_window_and_drains() {
10731        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
10732        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
10733        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
10734        register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
10735        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
10736        sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
10737        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim);
10738
10739        // Daemon peeks the anchor and releases the lock (window open).
10740        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
10741        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
10742
10743        // A racing handler descheduling the victim must buffer, not panic.
10744        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
10745        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
10746        assert!(
10747            sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim),
10748            "removal is deferred, so the stale entry lingers until the drain"
10749        );
10750
10751        // The handler has also made the victim logically dead: its next_turns
10752        // entry is gone. Iterating quiescence must SKIP the victim (filtered by
10753        // pending_run_queue_removals) rather than panic in check_request on the
10754        // missing next_turns entry -- without the filter this call panics.
10755        sched.next_turns.remove(&victim);
10756        let _ = sched.are_all_quiesced();
10757
10758        // Close the window and drain: the victim is gone, the anchor remains.
10759        let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
10760        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
10761        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
10762        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
10763    }
10764
10765    /// Always-defer invariant (codex finding 1/2): even with NO tentative window
10766    /// live, a global-request handler NEVER pushes or pops the run queue
10767    /// directly -- both admission and removal are buffered and take effect only
10768    /// at the deterministic step2 drain. This removes the host-timing-dependent
10769    /// immediate path: whichever daemon phase a handler happened to race, it only
10770    /// records intent, so the run-queue mutation is applied at one fixed point in
10771    /// DetTid order regardless of host arrival timing.
10772    #[test]
10773    fn run_queue_mutations_always_defer_to_the_drain() {
10774        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
10775        let keep = DetTid::from_raw(7);
10776        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
10777        register_known_thread(&mut sched, keep);
10778        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
10779        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim); // already queued; to be removed
10780        assert!(!sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
10781
10782        // No window live, yet both mutations buffer rather than apply.
10783        sched.admit_to_run_queue(keep, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
10784        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
10785        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&keep));
10786        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
10787        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep), "admission deferred");
10788        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim), "removal deferred");
10789
10790        // The daemon applies them at the drain (removals first, then admissions).
10791        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
10792        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
10793        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep));
10794        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
10795        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
10796        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
10797    }

10799    /// A thread admitted and then killed before the drain must end up neither
10800    /// queued nor pending: removals drain first and the retired-thread skip in
10801    /// the admission drain drops the buffered admission for a thread with no
10802    /// next_turns entry.
10803    #[test]
10804    fn buffered_admission_cancelled_by_buffered_removal() {
10805        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
10806        let tid = DetTid::from_raw(11);
10807        register_known_thread(&mut sched, tid);
10808
10809        sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
10810        sched.deschedule_or_defer(tid);
10811
10812        // The thread is retired before the drain: its next_turns entry is gone.
10813        sched.next_turns.remove(&tid);
10814        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
10815        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
10816
10817        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(tid));
10818        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
10819        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
10820    }

10822    /// A successful nonleader exec retires the old process leader and reuses
10823    /// its raw TID for the caller's replacement image.  The old-leader removal
10824    /// and replacement-leader admission therefore share a `DetTid`, but they do
10825    /// not name the same thread incarnation: the drain must remove the former
10826    /// without cancelling the latter.
10827    #[test]
10828    fn nonleader_exec_removal_preserves_replacement_admission() {
10829        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
10830            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
10831            backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
10832        });
10833        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
10834        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
10835        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
10836        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
10837        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
10838
10839        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
10840        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
10841        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
10842        register_known_thread(&mut sched, caller);
10843        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
10844        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
10845
10846        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
10847        let post_exec_mm = pre_exec_mm.for_exec(detpid);
10848        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
10849        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
10850        sched
10851            .register_physical_thread(leader, pre_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
10852            .expect("old leader PIDFD_THREAD registration must succeed");
10853        sched
10854            .register_physical_thread(leader, post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
10855            .expect("post-exec PIDFD_THREAD registration must replace the old address space");
10856        let retired = sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
10857            caller,
10858            new_leader: leader,
10859            detpid,
10860            pre_exec_mm,
10861            post_exec_mm,
10862            child_tid_addr: 0,
10863            reconnect_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
10864        });
10865
10866        assert_eq!(retired, vec![leader, caller]);
10867        assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
10868        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
10869        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&leader));
10870        assert_eq!(
10871            sched.physical_thread_identity(leader),
10872            Some((post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)),
10873            "old-leader cleanup must not remove the replacement leader's PIDFD_THREAD"
10874        );
10875
10876        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
10877        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
10878
10879        assert_eq!(
10880            sched
10881                .run_queue
10882                .tids()
10883                .filter(|dettid| **dettid == leader)
10884                .count(),
10885            1,
10886            "the first eligible drain must contain exactly one replacement leader"
10887        );
10888        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
10889        assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
10890        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
10891        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
10892    }

10971    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
10972    enum ExecReconnectTiming {
10973        BeforeDaemon,
10974        AfterCallerWait { yields: usize },
10975        CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect,
10976    }
10977
10978    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
10979    struct ExecDrainObservation {
10980        queue: Vec<DetTid>,
10981        next_post_fork_draw: bool,
10982        turn: u64,
10983        old_leader_registration_survived: bool,
10984    }
10985
10986    async fn observe_exec_reconnect_drain(timing: ExecReconnectTiming) -> ExecDrainObservation {
10987        let config = Config {
10988            sched_seed: Some(0x5107),
10989            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
10990            ..Config::default()
10991        }
10992        .with_backend(|backend| {
10993            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
10994        });
10995        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
10996        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
10997        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
10998        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
10999        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(31);
11000        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(37);
11001        let barrier_parent = DetTid::from_raw(99);
11002        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
11003        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
11004
11005        let (caller_request, old_leader_request) = {
11006            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
11007            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
11008            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
11009            register_known_thread(&mut s, leader);
11010            register_known_thread(&mut s, caller);
11011            // Give the destroyed leader a visibly different queue band. The
11012            // replacement must use the caller's priority at the ordinary tail.
11013            s.priorities.insert(leader, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
11014            s.runqueue_push_back(leader);
11015            s.runqueue_push_back(caller);
11016            s.next_turns
11017                .get(&leader)
11018                .unwrap()
11019                .req
11020                .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
11021
11022            register_known_thread(&mut s, lower);
11023            register_known_thread(&mut s, higher);
11024            s.admit_to_run_queue(lower, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
11025            s.admit_to_run_queue(higher, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
11026            // `step2` drains first, then this unresolved barrier returns
11027            // `SkipTurn`, exposing the exact first-drain queue before step3 can
11028            // tentatively select or rotate it.
11029            s.vfork_barriers.insert(barrier_parent, None);
11030            (
11031                s.next_turns.get(&caller).unwrap().req.clone(),
11032                s.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone(),
11033            )
11034        };
11035
11036        if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon) {
11037            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
11038                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
11039                leader,
11040                caller,
11041                detpid,
11042                pre_exec_mm,
11043            );
11044        } else if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
11045            caller_request.put(Ok(Resources::new(caller)));
11046        }
11047
11048        let turn_sched = sched.clone();
11049        let turn_time = global_time.clone();
11050        let turn = tokio::spawn(async move {
11051            let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
11052            do_a_turn_blocking(turn_sched, turn_time, &last).await
11053        });
11054
11055        if let ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields } = timing {
11056            let mut saw_waiter = false;
11057            for _ in 0..1_000 {
11058                if caller_request.to_string() == "<ivar HasWaiter>" {
11059                    saw_waiter = true;
11060                    break;
11061                }
11062                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
11063            }
11064            assert!(saw_waiter, "daemon never waited on the exec caller request");
11065            for _ in 0..yields {
11066                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
11067            }
11068            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
11069                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
11070                leader,
11071                caller,
11072                detpid,
11073                pre_exec_mm,
11074            );
11075        }
11076
11077        assert!(turn.await.expect("scheduler task panicked").is_err());
11078        let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
11079        let observation = ExecDrainObservation {
11080            queue: s.run_queue.tids().copied().collect(),
11081            next_post_fork_draw: s.child_runs_first_post_fork(RunsPostFork::Random),
11082            turn: s.turn,
11083            old_leader_registration_survived: s
11084                .next_turns
11085                .get(&leader)
11086                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req == old_leader_request),
11087        };
11088        if !matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
11089            assert_eq!(
11090                observation
11091                    .queue
11092                    .iter()
11093                    .filter(|tid| **tid == leader)
11094                    .count(),
11095                1
11096            );
11097            assert!(!observation.queue.contains(&caller));
11098            assert!(!observation.old_leader_registration_survived);
11099            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
11100            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
11101        }
11102        observation
11103    }
11104
11105    #[tokio::test]
11106    async fn exec_reconnect_caller_gate_fixes_first_drain_membership_and_prng() {
11107        let canonical = observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon).await;
11108        for yields in [0, 1, 64] {
11109            assert_eq!(
11110                canonical,
11111                observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields }).await,
11112                "host delay of {yields} yields changed the first eligible drain"
11113            );
11114        }
11115
11116        let broken =
11117            observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect).await;
11118        assert!(broken.old_leader_registration_survived);
11119        assert_ne!(
11120            canonical.queue, broken.queue,
11121            "the deliberate caller-gate violation was inert"
11122        );
11123    }

11125    /// With `--scheduler-turn-cost`, a charge refused because it would pass the
11126    /// end of representable virtual time ends an ordinary turn at once: the
11127    /// runnable thread is not selected or granted, so the terminal report can
11128    /// exit without waiting on any guest
11129    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3885). Before the fix the turn
11130    /// went on to select and grant thread 100.
11131    #[tokio::test]
11132    async fn a_refused_turn_charge_returns_before_an_ordinary_grant() {
11133        let config = Config {
11134            sequentialize_threads: true,
11135            epoch: "2554-07-21T23:34:32.709051615Z".parse().unwrap(),
11136            scheduler_turn_cost: std::num::NonZeroU64::new(1_000_000_000),
11137            ..Config::default()
11138        };
11139        let mut s = Scheduler::new(&config);
11140        let ready = DetTid::from_raw(100);
11141        register_known_thread(&mut s, ready);
11142        s.next_turns[&ready].req.put(Ok(Resources::new(ready)));
11143        s.runqueue_push_back(ready);
11144        let mut time = GlobalTime::new(&config);
11145        // One accepted charge leaves 500,615 ns of representable time.
11146        let now = time.add_scheduler_time().unwrap();
11147        assert_eq!(now.as_nanos(), u64::MAX - 500_615);
11148        s.committed_time = now;
11149        let response = s.next_turns[&ready].resp.clone();
11150        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(s));
11151        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(time));
11152
11153        let outcome = do_a_turn_blocking(
11154            sched.clone(),
11155            global_time.clone(),
11156            &Ok(Resources::new(ready)),
11157        )
11158        .await;
11159        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
11160        assert!(s.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some());
11161        assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(SkipTurn)), "{outcome:?}");
11162        assert_eq!(
11163            global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
11164            now,
11165            "a refused charge adds nothing"
11166        );
11167        assert!(
11168            response.try_read().is_none(),
11169            "the runnable thread was not granted"
11170        );
11171        assert!(!s.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
11172        assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(ready));
11173    }
11174
11175    /// F6 (real-path regression): when the thread `step3_peek` tentatively
11176    /// selected dies while the daemon awaits its request, `do_a_turn_blocking`
11177    /// takes the `Err(ThreadExited)` fizzle arm. That arm MUST undo the tentative
11178    /// pop so the selection does not outlive the turn; otherwise the next pass's
11179    /// step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is
11180    /// still `Some`, tripping the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect
11181    /// panic moved one pass" defect (reachable in NORMAL async-DBT operation, not
11182    /// just the reviewed edge case: any thread that exits during the await window
11183    /// races here). This drives the ACTUAL async daemon function end to end
11184    /// rather than poking `RunQueue` directly, which is the coverage gap the
11185    /// pre-existing tests left. Positive control: after the fizzle the window is
11186    /// closed and the following real step2 removal drain does not panic.
11187    #[tokio::test]
11188    async fn reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_safe() {
11189        let config = Config::default();
11190        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
11191        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
11192        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
11193        {
11194            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
11195            s.priorities.insert(dead, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11196            s.next_turns.insert(
11197                dead,
11198                ThreadNextTurn {
11199                    dettid: dead,
11200                    child_tid_addr: 0,
11201                    // Request already resolved to `ThreadExited`: the daemon will
11202                    // observe the thread died the moment it awaits `req.get()`.
11203                    req: Ivar::full(Err(ThreadExited)),
11204                    resp: Ivar::new(),
11205                    protocol: Default::default(),
11206                },
11207            );
11208            s.runqueue_push_back(dead);
11209        }
11210        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
11211
11212        // Pass 1: step1 sees a filled request (quiescent), step3 tentatively
11213        // pops `dead`, then `req.get().await` yields `Err(ThreadExited)`. The
11214        // fizzle arm returns `SkipTurn` and undoes the tentative pop.
11215        let first = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
11216        assert!(first.is_err(), "fizzled reconnect turn skips");
11217        assert!(
11218            !sched.lock().unwrap().run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
11219            "the ThreadExited arm must undo the tentative pop"
11220        );
11221
11222        // Pass 2: the dead thread's run-queue removal is now buffered, exactly
11223        // as a reconnect/kill handler would leave it. Because pass 1 closed the
11224        // window, the real step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` with
11225        // `tentative_selection == None` and does NOT trip the guard. Pre-fix
11226        // (window left open) this call panicked.
11227        {
11228            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
11229            s.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
11230            s.next_turns.remove(&dead);
11231            let _ = s.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
11232            assert!(!s.run_queue.contains_tid(dead), "dead thread drained out");
11233            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
11234        }
11235    }
11236
11237    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle), part 1: the branch itself, both ways.
11238    ///
11239    /// NEGATIVE -- the defect. A selected thread whose `next_turns` entry
11240    /// vanished during the daemon's post-await window must abandon the turn:
11241    /// report `SkipTurn` (it commits nothing -- steps 4-7 are bypassed) AND
11242    /// close the tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Before the fix this
11243    /// branch fell through to `Ok(rsrcs)`, which `bump_global_time` reads as a
11244    /// completed turn and answers with a virtual-time advance.
11245    /// POSITIVE -- not inert. A thread that is still registered proceeds: `Ok`,
11246    /// with its tentative selection left open for step4 to commit. Without this
11247    /// side an `abort_turn_if_thread_vanished` that simply always skipped would
11248    /// pass the negative and silently stall the scheduler.
11249    #[test]
11250    fn a_vanished_thread_aborts_its_turn_and_a_live_one_does_not() {
11251        let config = Config::default();
11252        let vanishing = DetTid::from_raw(11);
11253        let live = DetTid::from_raw(13);
11254
11255        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
11256        register_known_thread(&mut sched, vanishing);
11257        register_known_thread(&mut sched, live);
11258        sched.runqueue_push_back(vanishing);
11259        sched.runqueue_push_back(live);
11260
11261        // NEGATIVE: retire `vanishing` after its selection was tentatively
11262        // popped, exactly as teardown does inside the post-await window.
11263        assert_eq!(
11264            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(vanishing),
11265            Some(vanishing)
11266        );
11267        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
11268        sched.next_turns.remove(&vanishing);
11269        assert!(
11270            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(vanishing).is_err(),
11271            "a turn that bypasses steps 4-7 must report SkipTurn, never success: \
11272             reporting Ok lets bump_global_time advance virtual time for a turn \
11273             that committed nothing"
11274        );
11275        assert!(
11276            !sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
11277            "the abandoned turn must also close its tentative window"
11278        );
11279
11280        // POSITIVE: a still-registered thread is untouched and proceeds to
11281        // step4 with its selection still open to commit.
11282        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(live), Some(live));
11283        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
11284        assert!(
11285            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(live).is_ok(),
11286            "a live thread's turn must proceed"
11287        );
11288        assert!(
11289            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
11290            "a proceeding turn must keep its tentative selection open for step4"
11291        );
11292    }
11293
11294    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle must not advance virtual time): both sides of
11295    /// the consequence, stated directly against `bump_global_time` -- the code
11296    /// that turns a turn's returned `Result` into a virtual-time decision.
11297    ///
11298    /// The defect: the fizzle arm where `req.get()` resolved `Ok` but the
11299    /// thread's `next_turns` entry vanished before the daemon re-acquired the
11300    /// lock skips steps 4-7, commits nothing, and used to fall through to
11301    /// `Ok(rsrcs)` -- landing in the advancing branch below and adding a
11302    /// DETLOG-visible tick for work that never happened. It now reports
11303    /// `Err(SkipTurn)` like its `ThreadExited` sibling, so this pair of
11304    /// assertions is what that fix buys.
11305    ///
11306    /// Deliberately NOT an end-to-end test of that arm. Reaching it requires
11307    /// teardown to clear `next_turns` inside the host-scheduling gap between the
11308    /// await resolving and the re-lock, and that gap is not constructible from a
11309    /// test: the daemon quiescence check only proceeds once every thread's request
11310    /// is already filled, so `req.get()` never suspends and there is no window a
11311    /// test can hold open. An attempt to win the lock in that gap is a genuine
11312    /// race that would usually lose (and deadlocks outright on a current-thread
11313    /// runtime, where the daemon's blocking `sched.lock()` stalls the whole
11314    /// executor). F6's `reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_
11315    /// safe` does drive the real `do_a_turn_blocking` for the sibling arm.
11316    ///
11317    /// NEGATIVE: a skipped turn leaves virtual time exactly where it was. That is
11318    /// what the F8 fix buys; before it, the non-committing arm reported `Ok` and
11319    /// landed in the advancing branch.
11320    /// POSITIVE: a committed, non-internal turn *does* advance it. Without this
11321    /// side the negative would pass vacuously for a `bump_global_time` that had
11322    /// simply stopped advancing time at all.
11323    #[test]
11324    fn virtual_time_advances_for_a_committed_turn_and_not_for_a_skipped_one() {
11325        let config = Config::default();
11326        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
11327
11328        // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external events"
11329        // guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
11330        let mut advancing = Scheduler::new(&config);
11331        advancing.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11332        advancing.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
11333        let advancing_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
11334        let before_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11335        advancing.bump_global_time(&advancing_time, &Ok(Resources::new(runnable)));
11336        let after_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11337        assert!(
11338            after_commit > before_commit,
11339            "a committed turn must advance virtual time ({before_commit:?} -> {after_commit:?})"
11340        );
11341
11342        let mut skipping = Scheduler::new(&config);
11343        skipping.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11344        skipping.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
11345        let skipping_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
11346        let before_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11347        skipping.bump_global_time(&skipping_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
11348        let after_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11349        assert_eq!(
11350            after_skip, before_skip,
11351            "a skipped turn must not advance virtual time"
11352        );
11353    }
11354
11355    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3517: a committed turn that
11356    /// served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld does not
11357    /// advance virtual time. The identical request without the mark does, so the
11358    /// negative is not vacuous, and a marked IO-polling retry still does, because
11359    /// finite poll and futex timeouts are enforced against this clock.
11360    #[test]
11361    fn bootstrap_syscall_turn_withholds_scheduler_time_except_for_polling_retries() {
11362        let config = Config::default();
11363        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
11364        let advance = |request: Resources| {
11365            // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external
11366            // events" guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
11367            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
11368            sched.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11369            sched.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
11370            let time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
11371            let before = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11372            sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(request));
11373            let after = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
11374            assert_eq!(sched.committed_time, after);
11375            (before, after)
11376        };
11377        let file = ResourceID::Path("/proc/self/maps".into());
11378
11379        let mut guest_turn = Resources::new(runnable);
11380        guest_turn.resources.insert(file.clone(), Permission::R);
11381        let (before, after) = advance(guest_turn.clone());
11382        assert!(
11383            after > before,
11384            "an unmarked committed turn must advance virtual time ({before:?} -> {after:?})"
11385        );
11386        let per_turn = after - before;
11387
11388        let mut bootstrap_turn = guest_turn;
11389        bootstrap_turn.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
11390        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_turn);
11391        assert_eq!(
11392            after, before,
11393            "a turn serving an uncharged bootstrap syscall must not advance virtual time"
11394        );
11395
11396        let mut bootstrap_poll = Resources::new(runnable);
11397        bootstrap_poll
11398            .resources
11399            .insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
11400        bootstrap_poll.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
11401        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_poll);
11402        assert_eq!(
11403            after - before,
11404            per_turn,
11405            "a marked IO-polling retry must still advance virtual time by one turn"
11406        );
11407    }

11409    /// Liveness (negative control) for the F6 fix above: proves the guard the
11410    /// fizzle arm protects is real, so the positive test is not vacuous. If a
11411    /// fizzled turn does NOT undo its tentative pop (the pre-fix behavior), the
11412    /// next pass's step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while
11413    /// `tentative_selection` is `Some`, and the run queue's transaction guard
11414    /// panics. This is precisely the panic `undo_tentative_pop` prevents.
11415    #[test]
11416    #[should_panic(expected = "tentative_selection.is_none()")]
11417    fn removal_drain_panics_if_tentative_window_left_open() {
11418        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11419        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
11420        register_known_thread(&mut sched, dead);
11421        sched.runqueue_push_back(dead);
11422
11423        // Simulate step3_peek selecting `dead` with the turn neither committing
11424        // nor undoing -- i.e., the fizzle arm WITHOUT its undo.
11425        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(dead));
11426        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
11427
11428        // Next pass buffers the removal and drains: remove_tid trips the guard.
11429        sched.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
11430        sched.next_turns.remove(&dead);
11431        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
11432    }
11433
11434    /// F7 (adjacent-snapshot sensitivity): this fixture directly places two
11435    /// admissions in adjacent step2 drains; it does not model a production
11436    /// handler protocol. Every current asynchronous admission site separately
11437    /// fixes snapshot membership: ordinary clone buffers before the parent's
11438    /// `ParentContinue`, `vfork` uses its registration barrier, and exec
11439    /// reconnect buffers before retiring and resolving the caller request. See
11440    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for those causal bindings.
11441    ///
11442    /// The synthetic split remains a negative/sensitivity bracket for that
11443    /// requirement. Replaying one fixed split at one seed is reproducible, but
11444    /// swapping which child occupies the first drain changes the resolved queue
11445    /// order. Thus a future unanchored admission site would make host-selected
11446    /// membership observable; this test must not be read as evidence that any
11447    /// current production site is unanchored.
11448    #[test]
11449    fn deferred_admission_binds_to_snapshot_membership_across_adjacent_drains() {
11450        let config = Config {
11451            sched_seed: Some(0x5107),
11452            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
11453            ..Default::default()
11454        };
11455        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11456        let a = DetTid::from_raw(31);
11457        let b = DetTid::from_raw(37);
11458
11459        // Admit `first` in drain 1 and `second` in drain 2 (two adjacent step2
11460        // drains) and return the final run-queue order relative to a fixed
11461        // anchor, which encodes each child's resolved front/back side.
11462        let split = |first: DetTid, second: DetTid| -> Vec<DetTid> {
11463            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
11464            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
11465            register_known_thread(&mut sched, a);
11466            register_known_thread(&mut sched, b);
11467            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
11468
11469            sched.admit_to_run_queue(first, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
11470            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(); // drain 1
11471            sched.admit_to_run_queue(second, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
11472            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(); // drain 2 (adjacent)
11473
11474            sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect()
11475        };
11476
11477        // Fixed synthetic membership is deterministic across identical replays.
11478        let canonical = split(a, b);
11479        assert_eq!(
11480            canonical,
11481            split(a, b),
11482            "identical schedule -> identical result"
11483        );
11484        assert!(canonical.contains(&a) && canonical.contains(&b) && canonical.contains(&anchor));
11485
11486        // Sensitivity control: changing synthetic snapshot membership changes
11487        // the outcome for this seed, so a missing production anchor would be
11488        // observable rather than inert.
11489        assert_ne!(
11490            split(a, b),
11491            split(b, a),
11492            "swapping snapshot membership changes the resolved order"
11493        );
11494    }

11496    #[test]
11497    fn vfork_registration_barrier_blocks_until_child_registration() {
11498        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11499        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11500        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11501        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
11502
11503        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11504        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
11505        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11506        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
11507    }

11509    /// A vfork parent killed while its registered child's barrier is up takes
11510    /// the barrier with it. Otherwise, once the child is gone, `step3_peek`
11511    /// selects nothing while another thread is runnable
11512    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
11513    #[test]
11514    fn a_killed_vfork_parent_takes_its_barrier_with_it() {
11515        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11516        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11517        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11518        let other = DetTid::from_raw(7);
11519        for tid in [parent, other] {
11520            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11521            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11522                tid,
11523                ThreadNextTurn {
11524                    dettid: tid,
11525                    child_tid_addr: 0,
11526                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
11527                    resp: Ivar::new(),
11528                    protocol: Default::default(),
11529                },
11530            );
11531        }
11532        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
11533        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11534        assert!(
11535            scheduler.step3_peek().is_none(),
11536            "with the child gone, the barrier selects nobody"
11537        );
11538
11539        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
11540        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
11541        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11542        assert!(!scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.contains(&parent));
11543        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the other thread runs");
11544        assert_eq!(selected, other);
11545        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
11546    }
11547
11548    /// A vfork parent killed while its registered child can still run keeps
11549    /// its barrier, marked parent-dead, so the next selection is the child's
11550    /// whether the parent's retirement arrives before or after the child's
11551    /// turn. The child's next release edge (here its logical kill) drops the
11552    /// barrier, and only then can another thread be selected
11553    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
11554    #[test]
11555    fn a_killed_vfork_parents_barrier_lasts_until_its_childs_release_edge() {
11556        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11557        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11558        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11559        let other = DetTid::from_raw(7);
11560        for tid in [parent, child, other] {
11561            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
11562            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11563            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11564                tid,
11565                ThreadNextTurn {
11566                    dettid: tid,
11567                    child_tid_addr: 0,
11568                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
11569                    resp: Ivar::new(),
11570                    protocol: Default::default(),
11571                },
11572            );
11573        }
11574        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
11575        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11576        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11577
11578        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
11579        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
11580        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the child runs");
11581        assert_eq!(selected, child, "not the bystander queued first");
11582        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
11583
11584        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
11585        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11586        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11587        scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().unwrap();
11588        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the bystander runs");
11589        assert_eq!(selected, other);
11590        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
11591    }

11593    /// The child's `Exit` grant is a release edge: inside that committed turn
11594    /// the barrier of its killed parent ends.
11595    #[test]
11596    fn a_vfork_childs_exit_grant_releases_its_dead_parents_barrier() {
11597        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11598        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11599        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11600        for tid in [parent, child] {
11601            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
11602            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11603            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11604                tid,
11605                ThreadNextTurn {
11606                    dettid: tid,
11607                    child_tid_addr: 0,
11608                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
11609                    resp: Ivar::new(),
11610                    protocol: Default::default(),
11611                },
11612            );
11613        }
11614        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
11615        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
11616        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
11617
11618        assert!(
11619            scheduler
11620                .block_for_one_resource(
11621                    child,
11622                    &ResourceID::Exit {
11623                        group: true,
11624                        process: child,
11625                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
11626                    },
11627                    &Permission::RW,
11628                    None,
11629                    None,
11630                    &Ivar::new(),
11631                )
11632                .is_ok()
11633        );
11634        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11635        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11636    }

11638    /// A scheduler with vfork parent 3 and its registered child 5, both alive,
11639    /// for the release-edge tests below.
11640    fn live_vfork_pair() -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid) {
11641        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11642        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11643        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11644        for tid in [parent, child] {
11645            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
11646            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
11647            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11648                tid,
11649                ThreadNextTurn {
11650                    dettid: tid,
11651                    child_tid_addr: 0,
11652                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
11653                    resp: Ivar::new(),
11654                    protocol: Default::default(),
11655                },
11656            );
11657        }
11658        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
11659        (scheduler, parent, child)
11660    }
11661
11662    /// The child's successful exec is a release edge even while its parent is
11663    /// alive: step2a then waits, committing nothing, until the parent's fate is
11664    /// known. Here the parent's retirement arrives after the exec edge, the
11665    /// order in which the barrier used to outlive the exec; it drops the
11666    /// barrier, exactly as a retirement before the edge does
11667    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
11668    #[test]
11669    fn a_vfork_parent_retired_after_its_childs_exec_releases_the_barrier() {
11670        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
11671        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
11672        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent));
11673        assert!(
11674            scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err(),
11675            "waits for the parent's fate"
11676        );
11677
11678        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
11679        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11680        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11681        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11682        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11683    }
11684
11685    /// After the child's exec edge, the live parent's continuation ends the
11686    /// released barrier.
11687    #[test]
11688    fn a_released_vfork_barrier_ends_at_the_parents_continuation() {
11689        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
11690        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
11691        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11692
11693        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
11694        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
11695        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
11696        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
11697        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11698        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11699        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11700    }

11702    /// Backdates the start of step2a's wait past its valve: an injected clock,
11703    /// so the production bound needs no test knob.
11704    fn expire_vfork_barrier_valve(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) {
11705        scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since = Some(
11706            std::time::Instant::now()
11707                .checked_sub(Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE + Duration::from_secs(1))
11708                .expect("the monotonic clock has run longer than the valve"),
11709        );
11710    }
11711
11712    /// A pending barrier whose child never registers is refused by name once
11713    /// the valve expires, and the barrier stays, so no other thread is
11714    /// selected at a moment the host chose
11715    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999).
11716    #[test]
11717    fn a_pending_vfork_barrier_past_its_valve_refuses_the_run_and_stays() {
11718        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11719        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11720        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
11721
11722        // Inside the valve, the first pass starts the clock and only waits.
11723        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11724        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_some());
11725        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
11726
11727        expire_vfork_barrier_valve(&mut scheduler);
11728        for _ in 0..2 {
11729            assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11730            assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&None));
11731        }
11732        let refusal = scheduler
11733            .vfork_barrier_refusal
11734            .take()
11735            .expect("an expired wait records a typed refusal");
11736        assert_eq!(
11737            refusal.waits,
11738            vec![VforkBarrierWait {
11739                parent,
11740                child: None,
11741                state: VforkBarrierState::Pending,
11742            }]
11743        );
11744        assert!(refusal.waited >= Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE);
11745        let text = refusal.to_string();
11746        assert!(text.starts_with("hermit refused to continue the run"));
11747        assert!(text.contains(
11748            "parent 3 (no child registered) Pending, awaiting the child's registration;"
11749        ));
11750    }
11751
11752    /// A released barrier whose parent never posts its continuation, and is
11753    /// never retired, is refused by name once the valve expires, and the
11754    /// barrier stays released.
11755    #[test]
11756    fn a_released_vfork_barrier_past_its_valve_refuses_the_run_and_stays() {
11757        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
11758        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
11759        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11760        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
11761
11762        expire_vfork_barrier_valve(&mut scheduler);
11763        for _ in 0..2 {
11764            assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11765            assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
11766            assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent));
11767        }
11768        let refusal = scheduler
11769            .vfork_barrier_refusal
11770            .take()
11771            .expect("an expired wait records a typed refusal");
11772        assert_eq!(
11773            refusal.waits,
11774            vec![VforkBarrierWait {
11775                parent,
11776                child: Some(child),
11777                state: VforkBarrierState::Released,
11778            }]
11779        );
11780        assert!(refusal.to_string().contains(
11781            "parent 3 (child 5) Released, awaiting the parent's continuation or retirement;"
11782        ));
11783    }

11785    /// Control: when the awaited event arrives inside the valve, the barrier
11786    /// ends as before, the clock stops and nothing is refused; a later wait
11787    /// starts its own clock rather than inheriting the earlier one.
11788    #[test]
11789    fn a_vfork_barrier_event_inside_the_valve_proceeds_and_stops_the_clock() {
11790        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
11791        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
11792        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11793        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_some());
11794
11795        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
11796        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
11797        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
11798        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
11799        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11800        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11801        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_none());
11802        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
11803
11804        // A new wait, for another parent, starts its own clock.
11805        let other_parent = DetTid::from_raw(9);
11806        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(other_parent, None);
11807        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11808        let since = scheduler
11809            .vfork_barrier_wait_since
11810            .expect("the new wait starts the clock");
11811        assert!(since.elapsed() < Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE);
11812        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
11813    }

11815    /// A barrier kept for a dead parent's still-running child is stale once
11816    /// that TID begins a new vfork: the new grant replaces it instead of
11817    /// asserting.
11818    #[test]
11819    fn a_new_vfork_by_a_reused_tid_replaces_a_kept_barrier() {
11820        let (mut scheduler, parent, _child) = live_vfork_pair();
11821        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
11822        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent));
11823        scheduler.begin_vfork_barrier(parent);
11824        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&None));
11825        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11826    }

11828    /// A tombstone left by a dead vfork parent is stale once a later thread
11829    /// with the same TID begins a vfork of its own: that thread's child must
11830    /// fill the new barrier, not be swallowed by the old record.
11831    #[test]
11832    fn a_new_vfork_by_a_reused_tid_clears_a_stale_tombstone() {
11833        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
11834        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11835        let child = DetTid::from_raw(9);
11836        scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.insert(parent);
11837        scheduler.begin_vfork_barrier(parent);
11838        assert!(!scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.contains(&parent));
11839        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
11840        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
11841    }

11843    /// A vfork parent killed before its child registered leaves a tombstone,
11844    /// so the child's late registration settles as an orphan's.
11845    #[test]
11846    fn a_killed_vfork_parent_with_an_unregistered_child_leaves_a_tombstone() {

11848        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11849        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);

11854        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());

11885    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
11886    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review deferred vfork child registration.
11887    #[test]
11888    fn vfork_registration_barrier_waits_for_deferred_child_at_continuation() {
11889        // On a backend that defers the child spawn (e.g. KVM), the parent posts its continuation
11890        // BEFORE the child registers. An unfulfilled barrier at continuation must be kept, not
11891        // torn down as a failed clone; otherwise the late child panics on registration.
11892        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
11893            backend.defers_vfork_child_registration = true;
11894        });
11895        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
11896        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11897        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
11898        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
11899        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
11900        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
11901
11902        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
11903        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11904            parent,
11905            ThreadNextTurn {
11906                dettid: parent,
11907                child_tid_addr: 0,
11908                req: Ivar::full(Ok(continuation)),
11909                resp: Ivar::new(),
11910                protocol: Default::default(),
11911            },
11912        );
11913
11914        // Parent is at its continuation but the child has not registered: keep waiting, keep the
11915        // barrier (the failed-clone teardown must NOT fire on a deferring backend).
11916        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
11917        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&None));
11918
11919        // The deferred child registers; now the barrier is fulfilled and released.
11920        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
11921        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11922        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11923    }
