11925    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review failed deferred-vfork cancellation.
11926    #[test]
11927    fn vfork_registration_barrier_releases_deferred_failed_clone() {
11928        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
11929            backend.defers_vfork_child_registration = true;
11930        });
11931        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
11932        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11933        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
11934        let mut failure = Resources::new(parent);
11935        failure.insert(ResourceID::VforkFailed(op_id), Permission::RW);
11936
11937        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
11938        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(parent, op_id);
11939        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
11940            parent,
11941            ThreadNextTurn {
11942                dettid: parent,
11943                child_tid_addr: 0,
11944                req: Ivar::full(Ok(failure)),
11945                resp: Ivar::new(),
11946                protocol: Default::default(),
11947            },
11948        );
11949
11950        // The explicit failure proves that no deferred child is coming, so step2a cancels the
11951        // barrier instead of waiting forever. The ordinary external-continuation path can then
11952        // requeue the parent, whose syscall handler still owns and returns the original errno.
11953        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
11954        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
11955        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
11956        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
11957        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
11958    }

11973            .blocked

11975            .insert(signal_waiter, op_id);

11998    /// Under record, a client's read can wait for a server that polls its
11999    /// accept in turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880). With
12000    /// the client's read unfinished and only the poller queued, the scheduler
12001    /// must let the poller run rather than wait for the read.
12002    #[test]
12003    fn record_lets_a_poller_run_while_external_io_is_unfinished() {
12004        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12005        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
12006        let client = DetTid::from_raw(21);
12007        let server = DetTid::from_raw(3);
12008        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(client, 3);
12009
12010        scheduler.priorities.insert(client, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
12011        scheduler.priorities.insert(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
12012        scheduler
12013            .run_queue
12014            .push_poller(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
12015        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.is_empty() && scheduler.run_queue.only_pollers());
12016        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(client, op_id);
12017        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
12018            client,
12019            ThreadNextTurn {
12020                dettid: client,
12021                child_tid_addr: 0,
12022                req: Ivar::new(),
12023                resp: Ivar::new(),
12024                protocol: Default::default(),
12025            },
12026        );
12027
12028        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
12029        assert_eq!(
12030            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&client),
12031            Some(&op_id)
12032        );
12033        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(server));
12034    }

12036    /// A record/replay scheduler with `client` backgrounded on call `op_id`,
12037    /// finished when `finished`, and the poller `server`, if any, queued.
12038    fn rejoin_fixture(op_id: ExternalOpId, server: Option<DetTid>, finished: bool) -> Scheduler {
12039        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12040        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
12041        let client = op_id.tid;
12042        scheduler.priorities.insert(client, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
12043        if let Some(server) = server {
12044            scheduler.priorities.insert(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
12045            scheduler
12046                .run_queue
12047                .push_poller(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
12048        }
12049        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(client, op_id);
12050        let mut continuation = Resources::new(client);
12051        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
12052        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
12053            client,
12054            ThreadNextTurn {
12055                dettid: client,
12056                child_tid_addr: 0,
12057                req: if finished {
12058                    Ivar::full(Ok(continuation))
12059                } else {
12060                    Ivar::new()
12061                },
12062                resp: Ivar::new(),
12063                protocol: Default::default(),
12064            },
12065        );
12066        scheduler
12067    }

12069    /// Record logs the turn at which a finished backgrounded call rejoins,
12070    /// with the call's ordinal (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3908).
12071    #[test]
12072    fn record_logs_the_turn_a_backgrounded_call_rejoins() {
12073        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

12076        scheduler.rejoin_writer = Some(RejoinWriter::create(dir.path()).unwrap());
12077        scheduler.turn = 12;
12078
12079        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
12080        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
12081        assert_eq!(
12082            rejoin_log::read(dir.path()).unwrap(),
12083            std::collections::VecDeque::from([Rejoin {
12084                turn: 12,
12085                wakes: 0,
12086                calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12087            }])
12088        );
12089    }

12091    fn replaying(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, rejoins: &[Rejoin]) {
12092        scheduler.rejoin_replay = Some(rejoins.iter().cloned().collect());
12093    }

12095    /// Replay keeps a finished call parked until its logged turn, letting the
12096    /// queued poller run as record did, then readmits it at that turn.
12097    #[test]
12098    fn replay_readmits_a_finished_call_only_at_its_logged_turn() {
12099        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
12100        let server = DetTid::from_raw(3);
12101        let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, Some(server), true);
12102        let logged = Rejoin {
12103            turn: 12,
12104            wakes: 0,
12105            calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12106        };
12107        replaying(&mut scheduler, std::slice::from_ref(&logged));
12108        scheduler.turn = 11;
12109
12110        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
12111        assert_eq!(
12112            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
12113            Some(&op_id)
12114        );
12115        assert!(scheduler.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
12116
12117        scheduler.turn = 12;
12118        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
12119        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
12120        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(op_id.tid));
12121        assert!(matches!(&scheduler.rejoin_replay, Some(left) if left.is_empty()));
12122        assert_eq!(scheduler.unreplayed_rejoins(), None);
12123    }

12125    /// At its logged turn, replay waits for an unfinished call without
12126    /// running the poller, because record readmitted it before any other turn,
12127    /// and refuses once the call is still unfinished after the valve.
12128    #[test]
12129    fn replay_waits_at_the_logged_turn_for_an_unfinished_call() {
12130        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
12131        let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, Some(DetTid::from_raw(3)), false);
12132        replaying(
12133            &mut scheduler,
12134            &[Rejoin {
12135                turn: 12,
12136                wakes: 0,
12137                calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12138            }],
12139        );
12140        scheduler.turn = 12;
12141
12142        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_err());
12143        assert!(scheduler.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
12144        assert_eq!(
12145            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
12146            Some(&op_id)
12147        );
12148
12149        // It does not wait forever: past the valve, it refuses.
12150        scheduler.rejoin_stalled_since =
12151            std::time::Instant::now().checked_sub(Scheduler::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE);
12152        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_err());
12153        assert!(scheduler.rejoin_refusal.is_some());
12154    }

12156    /// Replay refuses a log it cannot follow: a logged point already passed,
12157    /// by turn or by timer wakes within the turn, or a different call parked.
12158    /// (An unreadable log is refused before the scheduler runs, and one left
12159    /// unexhausted when the run ends; see
12160    /// `replay_refuses_a_run_that_ends_before_its_log`.)
12161    #[test]
12162    fn replay_refuses_a_rejoin_log_it_cannot_follow() {
12163        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
12164        let server = DetTid::from_raw(3);
12165        let cases = [
12166            (
12167                "passed",
12168                (13, 0),
12169                vec![Rejoin {
12170                    turn: 12,
12171                    wakes: 0,
12172                    calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12173                }],
12174            ),
12175            (
12176                "passed by a wake",
12177                (12, 1),
12178                vec![Rejoin {
12179                    turn: 12,
12180                    wakes: 0,
12181                    calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12182                }],
12183            ),
12184            (
12185                "other call",
12186                (12, 0),
12187                vec![Rejoin {
12188                    turn: 12,
12189                    wakes: 0,
12190                    calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 8)],
12191                }],
12192            ),
12193        ];
12194        for (name, (turn, wakes), log) in cases {
12195            let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, Some(server), true);
12196            scheduler.rejoin_replay = Some(log.into_iter().collect());
12197            scheduler.turn = turn;
12198            scheduler.empty_queue_wakes = wakes;
12199            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_err(), "{name}");
12200            assert!(scheduler.rejoin_refusal.is_some(), "{name}");
12201            assert_eq!(
12202                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
12203                Some(&op_id),
12204                "{name}"
12205            );
12206        }
12207    }

12209    /// A replay that ends with logged readmissions left is refused, naming
12210    /// the first one; an exhausted log, or a run that is not a replay, is not.
12211    #[test]
12212    fn replay_refuses_a_run_that_ends_before_its_log() {

12217        assert_eq!(scheduler.unreplayed_rejoins(), None);

12219            &mut scheduler,
12220            &[Rejoin {
12221                turn: 999_999_999,
12222                wakes: 0,
12223                calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 1)],
12224            }],
12225        );
12226        let refusal = scheduler.unreplayed_rejoins().expect("no refusal");

12230                .contains("1 logged readmissions not replayed, the first at turn 999999999"),

12235    /// `scheduler` with `sleeper` asleep until 1 µs from now; returns the clock
12236    /// and the deadline.
12237    fn add_sleeper(
12238        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
12239        sleeper: DetTid,
12240    ) -> (Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>, LogicalTime) {
12241        let config = Config::default();
12242        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
12243        let deadline = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos() + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
12244        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, sleeper);
12245        scheduler.priorities.insert(sleeper, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
12246        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
12247            sleeper,
12248            ThreadNextTurn {
12249                dettid: sleeper,
12250                child_tid_addr: 0,
12251                req: Ivar::new(),
12252                resp: Ivar::new(),
12253                protocol: Default::default(),
12254            },
12255        );
12256        (global_time, deadline)
12257    }

12259    /// With a backgrounded call unfinished and nothing queued, record wakes a
12260    /// thread sleeping in virtual time instead of spinning: the call may wait
12261    /// on that thread (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3881).
12262    #[test]
12263    fn record_wakes_a_sleeper_while_a_backgrounded_call_runs() {
12264        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
12265        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(5);
12266        let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, false);
12267        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut scheduler, sleeper);
12268
12269        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
12270        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
12271        assert_eq!(scheduler.empty_queue_wakes, 1);
12272        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(sleeper));
12273        assert_eq!(
12274            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
12275            Some(&op_id)
12276        );
12277    }

12279    /// Replay readmits a finished call at its logged turn and wake count. At
12280    /// an earlier wake count in that turn it wakes the sleeper as record did,
12281    /// leaving the call parked; at the logged point it readmits the call
12282    /// without waking anyone.
12283    #[test]
12284    fn replay_follows_the_wake_count_within_a_turn() {
12285        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
12286        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(5);
12287        let logged = Rejoin {
12288            turn: 12,
12289            wakes: 1,
12290            calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
12291        };
12292
12293        let mut early = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, true);
12294        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut early, sleeper);
12295        replaying(&mut early, std::slice::from_ref(&logged));
12296        early.turn = 12;
12297        assert!(early.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
12298        assert!(early.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
12299        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
12300        assert_eq!(early.empty_queue_wakes, 1);
12301        assert_eq!(
12302            early.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
12303            Some(&op_id)
12304        );
12305
12306        let mut due = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, true);
12307        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut due, sleeper);
12308        replaying(&mut due, std::slice::from_ref(&logged));
12309        due.turn = 12;
12310        due.empty_queue_wakes = 1;
12311        assert!(due.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_ok());
12312        assert!(due.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
12313        assert!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos() < deadline);
12314        assert!(due.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
12315        assert!(due.run_queue.contains_tid(op_id.tid));
12316    }

12447    /// A cross-task signal must interrupt a precise-mode futex waiter, which sleeps
12448    /// outside the run queue (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12449    #[test]
12450    fn pending_signal_interrupts_a_parked_futex_waiter() {
12451        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12452        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
12453        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
12454        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
12455        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12456            &target,
12457            futex,
12458            None,
12459            u32::MAX,
12460            Some(signal_watch(usr_signals())),
12461        );
12462        scheduler
12463            .test_kernel_signal_states
12464            .insert(target, signal_state(usr_signals(), 0));
12465        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12466        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12467
12468        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
12469        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
12470        // Nothing moves until the deterministic step2 drain.
12471        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12472        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12473        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12474
12475        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
12476        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12477        assert!(scheduler.blocked.no_futex_waiters());
12478        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12479        assert_eq!(
12480            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12481            vec![
12482                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
12483                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
12484            ]
12485        );
12486        // A futex wake that arrives afterwards finds no waiter to take.
12487        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(target, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 0);
12488    }
12489
12490    fn usr_signals() -> u64 {
12491        kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2)
12492    }
12493
12494    /// A precise-mode futex waiter's report in a unit test. The `/proc` identity
12495    /// names no live thread, so a test that installs no kernel signal state for
12496    /// the waiter exercises the read-error fallback.
12497    fn signal_watch(unblocked: u64) -> FutexSignalWatch {
12498        FutexSignalWatch {
12499            unblocked,
12500            defers_default_stops: false,
12501            pid: i32::MAX,
12502            tid: i32::MAX,
12503        }
12504    }
12505
12506    /// Kernel dispositions with `caught` handled and `ignored` set to `SIG_IGN`;
12507    /// every other signal keeps its default action.
12508    fn signal_state(caught: u64, ignored: u64) -> KernelSignalState {
12509        KernelSignalState {
12510            caught,
12511            ignored,
12512            ..Default::default()
12513        }
12514    }
12515
12516    fn parked_futex_target(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) -> (DetTid, FutexID) {
12517        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
12518        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
12519        (
12520            target,
12521            FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110),
12522        )
12523    }
12524
12525    /// A cross-task signal the waiter blocks, ignores, or ignores by default leaves
12526    /// a precise-mode futex waiter parked with its original deadline, alongside one
12527    /// that does interrupt it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12528    #[test]
12529    fn non_interrupting_signal_leaves_a_parked_futex_waiter_parked() {
12530        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12531        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12532        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
12533        // SIGTERM is blocked. SIGUSR1 is caught, SIGUSR2 is ignored, and SIGWINCH
12534        // and SIGCHLD keep their default action, which ignores them.
12535        let unblocked =
12536            usr_signals() | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12537        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12538            &target,
12539            futex,
12540            Some(deadline),
12541            u32::MAX,
12542            Some(signal_watch(unblocked)),
12543        );
12544        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
12545            target,
12546            signal_state(
12547                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
12548                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
12549            ),
12550        );
12551
12552        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
12553        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH));
12554        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM));
12555        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12556        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR2);
12557        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
12558        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTERM);
12559
12560        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
12561        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12562        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12563        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
12564        assert_eq!(
12565            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
12566            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
12567        );
12568
12569        // The one signal that interrupts the wait still ends it.
12570        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
12571        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12572        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12573        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
12574        assert_eq!(
12575            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12576            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
12577        );
12578    }
12579
12580    /// A timed `FUTEX_WAIT`, whose restart would start its relative timeout again,
12581    /// stays parked with its original deadline when a default `SIGTSTP` arrives:
12582    /// Linux discards that stop in an orphaned process group and the wait goes on.
12583    /// `SIGSTOP` and a caught `SIGTSTP` still end it, and a wait that does not
12584    /// defer default stops is ended by the default `SIGTSTP` too (review of
12585    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361 at `cbb36408`, finding 4).
12586    #[test]
12587    fn a_default_job_control_stop_leaves_a_rearming_futex_wait_parked() {
12588        let stops = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP)
12589            | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTTIN)
12590            | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTTOU);
12591        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
12592        let park = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, defers_default_stops: bool, caught: u64| {
12593            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(scheduler);
12594            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12595                &target,
12596                futex,
12597                Some(deadline),
12598                u32::MAX,
12599                Some(FutexSignalWatch {
12600                    defers_default_stops,
12601                    ..signal_watch(stops | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP))
12602                }),
12603            );
12604            scheduler
12605                .test_kernel_signal_states
12606                .insert(target, signal_state(caught, 0));
12607            target
12608        };
12609        let assert_parked = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid| {
12610            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12611            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12612            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
12613            assert_eq!(
12614                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
12615                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
12616            );
12617        };
12618        let assert_woken = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid, signal: Signal| {
12619            assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12620            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12621            assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
12622            assert_eq!(
12623                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12624                vec![SigWrapper::from(signal)]
12625            );
12626        };
12627
12628        // Through the drain of cross-task signals and through scheduler sends.
12629        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12630        let target = park(&mut scheduler, true, 0);
12631        for signal in [Signal::SIGTSTP, Signal::SIGTTIN, Signal::SIGTTOU] {
12632            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(signal));
12633        }
12634        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12635        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
12636        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
12637        assert_parked(&scheduler, target);
12638        // SIGSTOP always stops the process, so it still ends the wait.
12639        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGSTOP);
12640        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGSTOP);
12641
12642        // A handler makes SIGTSTP an ordinary caught signal.
12643        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12644        let target = park(&mut scheduler, true, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP));
12645        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
12646        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
12647
12648        // A wait whose restart keeps its deadline takes the default stop at once.
12649        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12650        let target = park(&mut scheduler, false, 0);
12651        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
12652        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
12653    }
12654
12655    /// A precise-mode futex waiter is admitted on its mask alone. The dispositions
12656    /// are not consulted until the drain commits the wake, so a signal that is
12657    /// ignored now is still recorded, and a blocked one is not
12658    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12659    #[test]
12660    fn a_parked_futex_waiter_is_admitted_on_its_mask_alone() {
12661        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12662        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12663        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12664            &target,
12665            futex,
12666            None,
12667            u32::MAX,
12668            Some(signal_watch(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1))),
12669        );
12670        scheduler
12671            .test_kernel_signal_states
12672            .insert(target, signal_state(0, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1)));
12673
12674        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
12675        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
12676
12677        assert_eq!(
12678            scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.get(&target),
12679            Some(&vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)])
12680        );
12681        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12682    }
12683
12684    /// A handler a sibling installs over `SIG_IGN` after the wait began ends the
12685    /// wait when the signal arrives, as on Linux. The earlier design read the
12686    /// dispositions when the wait began and left this waiter parked; an untimed
12687    /// wait then never ended (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12688    #[test]
12689    fn a_signal_caught_after_a_futex_wait_began_ends_it() {
12690        // Through the step2 drain of a cross-task signal.
12691        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12692        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12693        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
12694        scheduler
12695            .test_kernel_signal_states
12696            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
12697        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
12698        // The sibling's `rt_sigaction` runs in its turn, before it signals.
12699        scheduler
12700            .test_kernel_signal_states
12701            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
12702        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
12703        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12704
12705        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12706        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12707        assert_eq!(
12708            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12709            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
12710        );
12711
12712        // Through a scheduler send (a timer), for SIGWINCH, which is ignored by
12713        // default until a handler is installed. A SIGCHLD ends the wait only
12714        // when the scheduler sends it
12715        // (`a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it`).
12716        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12717        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12718        let winch = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH);
12719        scheduler
12720            .test_kernel_signal_states
12721            .insert(target, signal_state(0, 0));
12722        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(winch)));
12723        scheduler
12724            .test_kernel_signal_states
12725            .insert(target, signal_state(winch, 0));
12726        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGWINCH);
12727
12728        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12729        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12730        assert_eq!(
12731            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12732            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
12733        );
12734    }
12735
12736    /// A signal a sibling sets to `SIG_IGN` after the wait began leaves the waiter
12737    /// parked, registered with its original absolute deadline, because Linux
12738    /// discards an ignored signal without ending the wait. The earlier design woke
12739    /// the waiter, and the restarted `FUTEX_WAIT` began a fresh relative timeout
12740    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12741    #[test]
12742    fn a_signal_ignored_after_a_futex_wait_began_keeps_its_deadline() {
12743        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12744        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12745        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
12746        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
12747        scheduler
12748            .test_kernel_signal_states
12749            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
12750        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12751            &target,
12752            futex,
12753            Some(deadline),
12754            u32::MAX,
12755            Some(signal_watch(usr1)),
12756        );
12757        scheduler
12758            .test_kernel_signal_states
12759            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
12760
12761        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
12762        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12763        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
12764
12765        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
12766        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12767        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12768        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
12769        assert_eq!(
12770            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
12771            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
12772        );
12773        // A FUTEX_WAKE still finds the waiter.
12774        assert_eq!(
12775            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(101), futex, 1, u32::MAX),
12776            1
12777        );
12778    }

12780    /// When the waiter's signal state cannot be read at the commit point, every
12781    /// signal its mask leaves unblocked ends the wait. A needless wake costs one
12782    /// turn: the waiter re-checks its signals in its own turn and parks again
12783    /// with its original absolute deadline. A missed wake can leave the waiter
12784    /// parked forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
12785    #[test]
12786    fn an_unreadable_signal_state_ends_a_parked_futex_wait() {
12787        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12788        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
12789        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
12790            &target,
12791            futex,
12792            None,
12793            u32::MAX,
12794            Some(signal_watch(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH))),
12795        );
12796        assert!(!scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.contains_key(&target));
12797
12798        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH));
12799        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
12800
12801        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
12802        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
12803        assert_eq!(
12804            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
12805            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
12806        );
12807    }

12809    /// A backend that does not report the guest's signal state keeps the base

12858    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of one waiter wakes the longest waiter, as Linux does for
12859    /// waiters of equal priority. Waking the newest one let a thread that re-waits
12860    /// after every wake take every wake, and an older waiter never ran
12861    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3917).
12862    #[test]
12863    fn a_futex_wake_takes_the_longest_waiter_first() {
12864        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12865        let waiters = [100, 101, 102].map(DetTid::from_raw);
12866        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
12867        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
12868        for waiter in waiters {
12869            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
12870            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
12871        }
12872        for (woken, waiter) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
12873            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
12874            for (index, other) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
12875                assert_eq!(
12876                    scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(other),
12877                    index > woken,
12878                    "after wake {woken}, waiter {other:?}"
12879                );
12880            }
12881            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
12882        }
12883    }
12884
12885    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` count of 0, or a count that is negative as the kernel's
12886    /// `int nr_wake` (-1, which is `u32::MAX` as the guest passes it), wakes one
12887    /// waiter, the longest one, as Linux's `futex_wake` does: it counts a waiter
12888    /// before comparing, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`
12889    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3957). A count of 0 used to wake
12890    /// nobody, and a negative count panicked the scheduler.
12891    #[test]
12892    fn a_futex_wake_count_of_zero_or_below_wakes_one_waiter() {
12893        for count in [0, -1, u32::MAX as i32, i32::MIN] {
12894            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12895            let waiters = [100, 101].map(DetTid::from_raw);
12896            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
12897            for waiter in waiters {
12898                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
12899                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
12900            }
12901            assert_eq!(
12902                scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, count, u32::MAX),
12903                1,
12904                "count {count}"
12905            );
12906            assert!(
12907                !scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[0]),
12908                "count {count}"
12909            );
12910            assert!(
12911                scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[1]),
12912                "count {count}"
12913            );
12914        }
12915        // With no waiter, such a wake still wakes nobody.
12916        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12917        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
12918        assert_eq!(
12919            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, 0, u32::MAX),
12920            0
12921        );
12922    }
12923
12924    /// A count of 0 still skips waiters whose bitset does not match, and wakes
12925    /// the first one that does, as `futex_wake`'s `continue` before `++ret`.
12926    #[test]
12927    fn a_futex_wake_bitset_count_of_zero_wakes_the_first_matching_waiter() {
12928        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12929        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
12930        let waiters = [(100, 0b10), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b01)]
12931            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
12932        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
12933            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
12934            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
12935        }
12936        assert_eq!(
12937            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(103), futex, 0, 0b01),
12938            1
12939        );
12940        let parked = waiters.map(|(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
12941        assert_eq!(parked, [true, false, true]);
12942    }
12943
12944    /// Helper: `n` waiters (raw tids from `first`) parked on `futex` with `bitset`.
12945    fn park_futex_waiters(
12946        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
12947        futex: FutexID,
12948        first: i32,
12949        n: i32,
12950        bitset: u32,
12951    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
12952        (first..first + n)
12953            .map(|raw| {
12954                let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(raw);
12955                register_known_thread(scheduler, waiter);
12956                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
12957                waiter
12958            })
12959            .collect()
12960    }
12961
12962    fn futex_waiter_order(scheduler: &Scheduler, futex: FutexID) -> Vec<DetTid> {
12963        scheduler
12964            .blocked
12965            .futex_waiters
12966            .get(&futex)
12967            .map(|waiters| waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid).collect())
12968            .unwrap_or_default()
12969    }
12970
12971    /// FUTEX_REQUEUE wakes the first `nr_wake` waiters in arrival order and moves
12972    /// the next `nr_requeue`, which join the end of the target's waiters in their
12973    /// arrival order, as Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) with
12974    /// `requeue_futex` appending to the target chain
12975    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3958).
12976    #[test]
12977    fn a_futex_requeue_wakes_the_oldest_and_moves_the_next_in_order() {
12978        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12979        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
12980        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
12981        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
12982        let on_to = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, to, 100, 1, u32::MAX);
12983        let on_from = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 101, 4, u32::MAX);
12984        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, 1, 2), (1, 2));
12985        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_from[0]));
12986        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, from), vec![on_from[3]]);
12987        assert_eq!(
12988            futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
12989            vec![on_to[0], on_from[1], on_from[2]]
12990        );
12991        // A later wake of the target takes its own earlier waiter first.
12992        assert_eq!(
12993            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(99), to, 1, u32::MAX),
12994            1
12995        );
12996        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_to[0]));
12997    }
12998
12999    /// `futex_requeue`'s loop: `if (task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue) break;`
13000    /// before counting, and `if (++task_count <= nr_wake)` to wake. So nothing is
13001    /// done for 0 and 0, a `nr_wake` of 0 wakes nobody (unlike `futex_wake`), and
13002    /// bitsets do not matter.
13003    #[test]
13004    fn futex_requeue_counts_follow_linux() {
13005        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
13006        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
13007        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
13008        for (nr_wake, nr_requeue, expected) in [
13009            (0, 0, (0, 0)),
13010            (0, 1, (0, 1)),
13011            (2, 0, (2, 0)),
13012            (5, 5, (3, 0)),
13013        ] {
13014            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13015            let waiters = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 100, 3, 0b01);
13016            assert_eq!(
13017                scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, nr_wake, nr_requeue),
13018                expected,
13019                "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue}"
13020            );
13021            let (woken, moved) = expected;
13022            let (woken, moved) = (woken as usize, moved as usize);
13023            for (index, &waiter) in waiters.iter().enumerate() {
13024                assert_eq!(
13025                    scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter),
13026                    index < woken,
13027                    "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue} waiter {index}"
13028                );
13029            }
13030            assert_eq!(
13031                futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
13032                waiters[woken..woken + moved].to_vec()
13033            );
13034        }
13035    }
13036
13037    /// Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody (`requeue_futex` only rewrites
13038    /// the key): the counted waiters keep their places, and only the woken leave.
13039    #[test]
13040    fn a_futex_requeue_onto_itself_keeps_waiters_in_place() {
13041        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13042        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
13043        let waiters = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, futex, 100, 3, u32::MAX);
13044        assert_eq!(
13045            scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 0, i32::MAX as usize),
13046            (0, 3)
13047        );
13048        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters);
13049        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 1, 1), (1, 1));
13050        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters[1..].to_vec());
13051    }

13053    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of several wakes the longest waiters, and they join the

13056    fn a_futex_wake_of_several_takes_the_longest_waiters_in_order() {
13057        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());

13079    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE_BITSET` that matches only some waiters leaves the others
13080    /// in the order they arrived, so a later wake still takes the longest
13081    /// waiter (Linux `futex_wake` walks one list in arrival order and skips
13082    /// the waiters whose bitset does not match).
13083    #[test]
13084    fn a_partial_bitset_wake_keeps_the_other_waiters_in_arrival_order() {
13085        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13086        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
13087        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
13088        let waiters = [(100, 0b01), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b10)]
13089            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
13090        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
13091            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
13092            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
13093        }
13094        let parked = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
13095            waiters
13096                .iter()
13097                .map(|&(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter))
13098                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
13099        };
13100        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, 0b01), 1);
13101        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, true, true]);
13102        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
13103        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, true]);
13104        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
13105        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, false]);
13106    }

13108    /// The wakes Detcore issues for an exiting thread also take the longest

13110    /// joining one) and the one-waiter wake of a robust-list futex.

13112    fn exit_wakes_take_the_longest_waiter_first() {

13132    /// Under `--futex-wake-yields` a waker that woke a waiter goes
13133    /// behind it, and behind every thread already queued, so its yield at the
13134    /// syscall's post-hook is granted only after their turns
13135    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3874). By default the waker
13136    /// keeps its place ahead of the waiter it woke.
13137    #[test]
13138    fn a_futex_waker_is_requeued_behind_the_waiters_it_woke() {
13139        for requeue in [false, true] {
13140            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13141            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
13142            let waker = DetTid::from_raw(101);
13143            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(102);
13144            for tid in [waiter, waker, runnable] {
13145                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
13146            }
13147            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waker);
13148            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
13149            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
13150            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
13151
13152            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
13153            if requeue {
13154                scheduler.requeue_futex_waker(waker);
13155            }
13156            let expected = if requeue {
13157                vec![runnable, waiter, waker]
13158            } else {
13159                vec![waker, runnable, waiter]
13160            };
13161            assert_eq!(
13162                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
13163                expected
13164            );
13165        }
13166    }
13167
13168    /// The scheduler under the condition that turns on its model of which thread
13169    /// a signal reaches (`models_signal_targets`): serialized threads and a
13170    /// backend that decides blocked-wait interruption from the kernel's signal
13171    /// state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13172    fn gated_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
13173        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
13174            sequentialize_threads: true,
13175            backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption: true,
13176            ..Config::default()
13177        });
13178        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
13179        scheduler
13180    }
13181
13182    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` ends a parked precise-mode futex wait only when the
13183    /// scheduler sends it to the waiter at a commit point (`wake_signaled_guest`,
13184    /// as a `ChildExit` timer does): the waiter is woken with the signal, as
13185    /// Linux ends the wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
13186    /// Through the drain of a cross-task signal, which only says a `SIGCHLD` is
13187    /// pending, or when a host-timed source a guest armed can post `SIGCHLD`
13188    /// too, the waiter stays parked with its original deadline, and the signal
13189    /// stays pending in the kernel until the call returns for another reason:
13190    /// `/proc` cannot tell a `SIGCHLD` sent at a deterministic point from the
13191    /// one the kernel posts for a child event at a moment set by host timing
13192    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). A caught `SIGUSR1`
13193    /// still ends the same wait.
13194    #[test]
13195    fn a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it() {
13196        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13197        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
13198        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
13199        for (scheduler_send, host_timed) in [(false, false), (true, false), (true, true)] {
13200            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
13201            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
13202            if host_timed {
13203                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
13204            }
13205            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
13206                &target,
13207                futex,
13208                Some(deadline),
13209                u32::MAX,
13210                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
13211            );
13212            scheduler
13213                .test_kernel_signal_states
13214                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
13215            assert_eq!(
13216                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(target, 0),
13217                Some(usr1),
13218                "a caught SIGCHLD is not among the signals that end the wait"
13219            );
13220
13221            if scheduler_send {
13222                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
13223            } else {
13224                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
13225                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13226            }
13227            let case = format!("scheduler_send={scheduler_send} host_timed={host_timed}");
13228            if scheduler_send && !host_timed {
13229                assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
13230                assert_eq!(
13231                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
13232                    vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)],
13233                    "{case}"
13234                );
13235                continue;
13236            }
13237            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
13238            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
13239            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{case}");
13240            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
13241            assert_eq!(
13242                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
13243                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
13244                "{case}"
13245            );
13246
13247            if scheduler_send {
13248                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
13249            } else {
13250                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
13251                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13252            }
13253            assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
13254            assert_eq!(
13255                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
13256                vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
13257                "{case}"
13258            );
13259        }
13260    }
13261
13262    /// A signal recorded as host-timed for a process, as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`
13263    /// records its signal in the arming thread's turn, never ends a parked
13264    /// precise-mode futex wait of any thread of that process, although the
13265    /// waiter catches it, and a later disarm does not remove the record. A
13266    /// forked child's wait still ends for it; a container-wide record holds
13267    /// it in every process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13268    #[test]
13269    fn a_host_timed_signal_never_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_of_its_process() {
13270        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
13271        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
13272        let term = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM);
13273        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13274        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
13275            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), 0, "nothing armed yet");
13276        }
13277
13278        // The creator, not its process's leader, arms SIGUSR1.
13279        assert_eq!(
13280            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(creator, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr1),
13281            usr1
13282        );
13283        assert_eq!(
13284            scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent),
13285            usr1,
13286            "the record covers every thread of the arming process"
13287        );
13288        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(creator), usr1);
13289        assert_eq!(
13290            scheduler.host_timed_signals(child),
13291            0,
13292            "a forked child starts without its parent's record"
13293        );
13294        // A disarm (signal 0) records nothing and removes nothing.
13295        assert_eq!(
13296            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(parent, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, 0),
13297            usr1
13298        );
13299        // A container-wide source holds its signal in every process.
13300        assert_eq!(
13301            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(child, HostTimedSignalScope::Container, usr2),
13302            usr2
13303        );
13304        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), usr1 | usr2);
13305        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(child), usr2);
13306
13307        // Parked futex waiters that catch all three signals: only SIGTERM ends
13308        // the parent's wait, and SIGUSR1 and SIGTERM end the child's.
13309        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
13310            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
13311                &thread,
13312                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
13313                None,
13314                u32::MAX,
13315                Some(signal_watch(usr1 | usr2 | term)),
13316            );
13317            scheduler
13318                .test_kernel_signal_states
13319                .insert(thread, signal_state(usr1 | usr2 | term, 0));
13320        }
13321        assert_eq!(
13322            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(parent, 0),
13323            Some(term)
13324        );
13325        assert_eq!(
13326            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(child, 0),
13327            Some(usr1 | term)
13328        );
13329    }
13330
13331    /// A launch that may pass the guest a terminal records every signal a
13332    /// terminal sends as host-timed for every process before the guest runs:
13333    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT for a hangup, SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the
13334    /// interrupt, quit and suspend characters, SIGWINCH for a resize, and
13335    /// SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU for a background read or write. So a parked
13336    /// precise-mode futex wait that catches all of them ends for none, in the
13337    /// first process and in a forked child alike. Nothing is recorded without
13338    /// that terminal, or on a backend whose blocked waits do not read the
13339    /// kernel's signal state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13340    /// Round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
13341    /// interruption" on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361: only
13342    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT were recorded, so a resize ended such a wait at a
13343    /// turn the host chose.
13344    #[test]
13345    fn a_launch_that_may_pass_a_terminal_holds_the_terminal_signals_from_the_start() {
13346        let terminal = [
13347            libc::SIGHUP,
13348            libc::SIGCONT,
13349            libc::SIGINT,
13350            libc::SIGQUIT,
13351            libc::SIGTSTP,
13352            libc::SIGWINCH,
13353            libc::SIGTTIN,
13354            libc::SIGTTOU,
13355        ]
13356        .into_iter()
13357        .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal));
13358        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
13359        let gated = |guest_may_inherit_a_terminal| Config {
13360            sequentialize_threads: true,
13361            backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption: true,
13362            guest_may_inherit_a_terminal,
13363            ..Config::default()
13364        };
13365        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(true)), terminal);
13366        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(false)), 0);
13367        assert_eq!(
13368            startup_host_timed_signals(&Config {
13369                guest_may_inherit_a_terminal: true,
13370                ..Config::default()
13371            }),
13372            0,
13373            "a backend whose waits do not read the kernel's signal state records nothing"
13374        );
13375
13376        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(true));
13377        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
13378        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
13379        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
13380        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
13381        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
13382        for thread in [parent, child] {
13383            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
13384        }
13385        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
13386            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), terminal);
13387            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
13388                &thread,
13389                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
13390                None,
13391                u32::MAX,
13392                Some(signal_watch(terminal | usr1)),
13393            );
13394            scheduler
13395                .test_kernel_signal_states
13396                .insert(thread, signal_state(terminal | usr1, 0));
13397            assert_eq!(
13398                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(thread, 0),
13399                Some(usr1),
13400                "only SIGUSR1 ends the wait of {thread:?}"
13401            );
13402        }
13403
13404        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(false));
13405        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), 0);
13406    }
13407
13408    /// A parent process 100 whose second thread 101 created child process 200
13409    /// with `exit_signal`, on the gated scheduler.
13410    fn sigchld_family(exit_signal: libc::c_int) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid, DetTid) {
13411        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
13412        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
13413        let creator = DetTid::from_raw(101);
13414        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
13415        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
13416        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, creator, false);
13417        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
13418            creator,
13419            child,
13420            true,
13421            false,
13422            exit_signal,
13423        );
13424        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
13425            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
13426        }
13427        (scheduler, parent, creator, child)
13428    }
13429
13430    fn park_for_sigchld(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, unblocked: u64) {
13431        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
13432        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
13433            &thread,
13434            futex,
13435            None,
13436            u32::MAX,
13437            Some(signal_watch(unblocked)),
13438        );
13439        scheduler
13440            .test_kernel_signal_states
13441            .insert(thread, signal_state(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0));
13442    }
13443
13444    /// A child's death itself wakes no parked futex waiter of its parent,
13445    /// although the waiter catches `SIGCHLD`: a child killed by a signal, or
13446    /// leaving through `exit` in its last thread, has no `ChildExit` timer, and
13447    /// the kernel posts its own `SIGCHLD` at a moment set by host timing, so the
13448    /// signal stays pending until the waiter's call returns for another reason.
13449    /// Before, the death made the signal eligible and the drain woke that
13450    /// waiter (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The scheduler
13451    /// still names the thread Linux would give it to (`kernel_sigchld_target`),
13452    /// the child's creator first, and the `SIGCHLD` a `ChildExit` timer sends to
13453    /// that thread wakes it, and only it
13454    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
13455    #[test]
13456    fn a_child_exit_wakes_only_the_parked_futex_waiter_its_timer_signals() {
13457        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13458        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13459        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
13460        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, chld);
13461        assert_eq!(
13462            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13463            Some(creator)
13464        );
13465
13466        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13467        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13468        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
13469        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
13470        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
13471        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
13472        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(creator).is_empty());
13473
13474        // The SIGCHLD a `ChildExit` timer sends to the creator wakes it, and
13475        // leaves the leader parked.
13476        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
13477        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
13478        assert_eq!(
13479            scheduler.inbound_signals(creator),
13480            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)]
13481        );
13482        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
13483        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
13484    }
13485
13486    /// The kernel gives a shared-queue `SIGCHLD` to the first thread that does
13487    /// not block it, the child's creator first, whether that thread is parked or
13488    /// running, and `kernel_sigchld_target` names that thread: a `ChildExit`
13489    /// timer signals it. No parked waiter is woken for the child's death,
13490    /// whichever thread is the target (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13491    #[test]
13492    fn a_child_exit_sigchld_goes_to_the_first_thread_that_does_not_block_it() {
13493        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13494
13495        // The creator runs and does not block SIGCHLD: it takes the signal, and
13496        // the leader's wait is left alone.
13497        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13498        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
13499        scheduler
13500            .test_kernel_signal_states
13501            .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
13502        assert_eq!(
13503            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13504            Some(creator)
13505        );
13506        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13507        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13508        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
13509        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
13510
13511        // The creator blocks SIGCHLD and the leader runs without blocking it: the
13512        // leader comes first in thread-ID order and takes it, so a waiter after
13513        // it is not woken.
13514        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13515        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(102);
13516        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, waiter, false);
13517        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
13518        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, waiter, chld);
13519        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
13520        scheduler
13521            .test_kernel_signal_states
13522            .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
13523        assert_eq!(
13524            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13525            Some(parent)
13526        );
13527        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13528        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13529        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
13530        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
13531
13532        // Every thread blocks it: nobody is chosen and nobody is woken.
13533        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13534        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
13535        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
13536            parent,
13537            KernelSignalState {
13538                blocked: chld,
13539                ..signal_state(chld, 0)
13540            },
13541        );
13542        assert_eq!(scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator), None);
13543        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13544        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13545        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
13546    }
13547
13548    /// Commit `thread`'s request to begin a blocking call outside the runnable
13549    /// set, as step3 does, with `mask` the call's own temporary mask.
13550    fn commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13551        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
13552        thread: DetTid,
13553        rid: ResourceID,
13554        mask: Option<u64>,
13555    ) {
13556        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(thread);
13557        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(thread), Some(thread));
13558        assert!(
13559            scheduler
13560                .block_for_one_resource(thread, &rid, &Permission::RW, None, mask, &Ivar::new())
13561                .is_err()
13562        );
13563    }
13564
13565    /// A thread sleeping in `rt_sigsuspend` or in other IO outside the runnable
13566    /// set is not stopped, so its live mask changes at host-timed moments:
13567    /// `rt_sigsuspend` installs its temporary mask only after the scheduler
13568    /// released the thread. The `SIGCHLD` target is chosen from the mask the
13569    /// scheduler recorded when it committed the call, the call's own mask or
13570    /// else the mask read while the thread was still stopped at its request.
13571    /// Before, the live mask was read when the child died, so whether the
13572    /// creator or a sibling parked in a precise futex wait took the signal
13573    /// depended on host timing; the target is also the thread a `ChildExit`
13574    /// timer signals (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
13575    #[test]
13576    fn a_sigchld_target_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_uses_the_mask_recorded_at_its_commit() {
13577        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13578        let blocking = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
13579            blocked,
13580            ..signal_state(chld, 0)
13581        };
13582        let family_with_parked_sibling = || {
13583            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13584            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
13585            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
13586            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
13587            park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, sibling, chld);
13588            // The leader runs with SIGCHLD blocked, and so does the creator
13589            // until its call installs a mask of its own.
13590            scheduler
13591                .test_kernel_signal_states
13592                .insert(parent, blocking(chld));
13593            scheduler
13594                .test_kernel_signal_states
13595                .insert(creator, blocking(chld));
13596            (scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling)
13597        };
13598
13599        // The creator suspends with an rt_sigsuspend mask that unblocks SIGCHLD.
13600        // Whether or not the host has installed that mask yet, the creator takes
13601        // the signal, so the sibling's precise futex wait is left alone.
13602        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
13603        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
13604        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13605            &mut scheduler,
13606            creator,
13607            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
13608            Some(0),
13609        );
13610        assert_eq!(
13611            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
13612            Some(&op)
13613        );
13614        assert_eq!(
13615            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
13616            Some(&Some(0))
13617        );
13618        for live in [chld, 0] {
13619            scheduler
13620                .test_kernel_signal_states
13621                .insert(creator, blocking(live));
13622            assert_eq!(
13623                scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13624                Some(creator)
13625            );
13626        }
13627        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13628        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13629        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
13630
13631        // Other external IO sleeps under the thread's own mask, read while it is
13632        // still stopped at its request: SIGCHLD blocked. A later change of its
13633        // live mask does not make it the target. The sibling is the target, but
13634        // its wait holds SIGCHLD, so it stays parked.
13635        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
13636        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13637            &mut scheduler,
13638            creator,
13639            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 2)),
13640            None,
13641        );
13642        assert_eq!(
13643            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
13644            Some(&Some(chld))
13645        );
13646        scheduler
13647            .test_kernel_signal_states
13648            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
13649        assert_eq!(
13650            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13651            Some(sibling)
13652        );
13653        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
13654        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13655        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
13656        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(sibling).is_empty());
13657
13658        // A mask that could not be recorded is not a target, whatever the live
13659        // one says, and the record goes when the thread leaves its pool.
13660        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
13661        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13662            &mut scheduler,
13663            creator,
13664            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 3)),
13665            Some(0),
13666        );
13667        scheduler
13668            .blocked
13669            .out_of_scheduler_masks
13670            .insert(creator, None);
13671        scheduler
13672            .test_kernel_signal_states
13673            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
13674        assert_eq!(
13675            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13676            Some(sibling)
13677        );
13678        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&creator);
13679        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
13680        assert_eq!(
13681            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
13682            Some(creator)
13683        );
13684    }
13685
13686    /// A signal the scheduler sends while a thread is still stopped at its
13687    /// `rt_sigsuspend` request reaches the call: the thread may block it now,
13688    /// but the call's temporary mask does not, so the kernel delivers it as
13689    /// soon as the call starts. Committing the call arms the thread for the
13690    /// release barrier, which waits for its signal stop, as for a signal sent
13691    /// after the commit. Before, the thread entered the pool as a sleeper no
13692    /// signal could reach, and the next pass reported a deadlock. That is how
13693    /// dash's `wait` failed: a `ChildExit` timer fired between its
13694    /// `wait4(WNOHANG)` and its `rt_sigsuspend`, while it blocked every signal.
13695    /// A signal the temporary mask blocks arms nothing.
13696    #[test]
13697    fn a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
13698        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13699        for (temporary_mask, armed) in [(0, true), (chld, false)] {
13700            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13701            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
13702            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
13703            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
13704            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
13705            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
13706            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
13707            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
13708
13709            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
13710            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
13711            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13712                &mut scheduler,
13713                creator,
13714                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
13715                Some(temporary_mask),
13716            );
13717            assert_eq!(
13718                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
13719                Some(&op)
13720            );
13721            assert_eq!(
13722                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
13723                armed,
13724                "temporary mask {temporary_mask:#x}"
13725            );
13726            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator), armed);
13727            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty());
13728        }
13729    }

13731    /// A guest's signal to a thread asleep in a real `rt_sigsuspend`
13732    /// (`kill`, `tgkill` and `tkill` report it with `notify_signal_pending`)
13733    /// is placed at the next drain as a signal the scheduler sends is: the
13734    /// thread is armed for the release barrier when its sleeping mask lets the
13735    /// signal through, and not when it blocks it; a thread still stopped at
13736    /// its `rt_sigsuspend` request gets the record its grant arms. Before, such
13737    /// a signal was not recorded at all, the scheduler did not wait for the
13738    /// wake's signal stop, and on a slow host it reported a deadlock first.
13739    #[test]
13740    fn a_guest_signal_to_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_arms_the_release_barrier() {
13741        let usr1 = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
13742        for (sleeping_mask, armed) in [(0, true), (kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1), false)] {
13743            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13744            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13745                &mut scheduler,
13746                creator,
13747                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 5)),
13748                Some(sleeping_mask),
13749            );
13750            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, usr1);
13751            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13752            assert_eq!(
13753                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
13754                armed,
13755                "sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
13756            );
13757        }
13758
13759        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13760        let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
13761        request.insert(
13762            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 6)),
13763            Permission::RW,
13764        );
13765        request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
13766        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
13767        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
13768        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, usr1);
13769        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
13770        assert_eq!(
13771            scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
13772            Some(&Signal::SIGUSR1)
13773        );
13774    }
