13776    /// A scheduler that does not model signal targets (`models_signal_targets`)
13777    /// neither reads a committed thread's sleeping mask from `/proc` nor records
13778    /// one. Nothing on such a scheduler consumes the record, and on a backend
13779    /// whose `DetTid` is not a host thread ID the read would name an unrelated
13780    /// host thread or none. The gated scheduler, for contrast, records the
13781    /// call's own mask, or else reads the thread's
13782    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13783    /// A background call whose temporary mask its turn cannot vouch for
13784    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`: a pselect6 in record and
13785    /// replay) has no recorded sleeping mask, so a committed signal never arms
13786    /// it, whatever the thread's ordinary mask, and it is not a `SIGCHLD`
13787    /// target. Taking the ordinary mask for such a call armed it for a SIGALRM
13788    /// the call's own mask blocks, and the release barrier waited for a wake
13789    /// Linux never delivers (Codex review of
13790    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3989). The same call without the
13791    /// flag is armed, from the ordinary mask read while it was stopped.
13792    #[test]
13793    fn a_background_call_with_an_unknown_sleeping_mask_is_never_armed() {
13794        for unknown in [false, true] {
13795            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13796            // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
13797            scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
13798            scheduler
13799                .test_kernel_signal_states
13800                .insert(creator, signal_state(0, 0));
13801            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
13802            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
13803            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op), Permission::RW);
13804            request.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = unknown;
13805            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
13806            assert_eq!(
13807                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
13808                Some(creator)
13809            );
13810            assert!(
13811                scheduler
13812                    .step4_resource_block(creator, &request, &Ivar::new())
13813                    .is_err()
13814            );
13815            assert_eq!(
13816                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
13817                Some(&op)
13818            );
13819            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGALRM);
13820            let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
13821            let armed = scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator);
13822            if unknown {
13823                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&None));
13824                assert!(!armed);
13825                assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_signal_mask(creator), None);
13826            } else {
13827                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(0)));
13828                assert!(armed);
13829            }
13830        }
13831    }
13832
13833    #[test]
13834    fn a_scheduler_that_does_not_model_signal_targets_reads_and_records_no_sleeping_mask() {
13835        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
13836        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13837        for models in [false, true] {
13838            for (seq, rt_sigsuspend, call_mask) in [(1, false, None), (2, true, Some(0))] {
13839                let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13840                scheduler.models_signal_targets = models;
13841                scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
13842                    creator,
13843                    KernelSignalState {
13844                        blocked: chld,
13845                        ..signal_state(chld, 0)
13846                    },
13847                );
13848                let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, seq);
13849                let rid = if rt_sigsuspend {
13850                    ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op)
13851                } else {
13852                    ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
13853                };
13854                let before = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
13855                commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, call_mask);
13856                let reads = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed) - before;
13857                let case = format!("models={models} rt_sigsuspend={rt_sigsuspend}");
13858
13859                // Either way the thread sleeps in its pool.
13860                let pool = if rt_sigsuspend {
13861                    &scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers
13862                } else {
13863                    &scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers
13864                };
13865                assert_eq!(pool.get(&creator), Some(&op), "{case}");
13866                let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
13867                if models {
13868                    assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(call_mask.unwrap_or(chld))), "{case}");
13869                    assert_eq!(reads, usize::from(call_mask.is_none()), "{case}");
13870                } else {
13871                    assert_eq!(recorded, None, "{case}");
13872                    assert!(
13873                        scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty(),
13874                        "{case}"
13875                    );
13876                    assert_eq!(reads, 0, "{case}");
13877                }
13878            }
13879        }
13880    }

13882    /// Post `signal`'s delivery stop for `thread`, as its backend does when the
13883    /// kernel wakes it for the signal.
13884    fn post_inbound_signal(
13885        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
13886        thread: DetTid,
13887        signal: libc::c_int,
13888        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
13889    ) {
13890        let req = scheduler.next_turns.get(&thread).unwrap().req.clone();
13891        let mut delivered = Resources::new(thread);
13892        delivered.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(signal)), Permission::W);
13893        scheduler.request_put(&req, delivered, global_time);
13894    }
13895
13896    /// A committed signal to a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
13897    /// the run queue, on a traced backend, counterfeits no request for it: its
13898    /// request was consumed when it was backgrounded. The thread is armed, and
13899    /// every scheduler pass is empty until the delivery stop the signal
13900    /// provokes is posted; the next pass then requeues it, before anything
13901    /// else, and its `SIGCHLD` delivery is granted rather than deferred behind
13902    /// a runnable sibling. Before, a debug build asserted here and a release
13903    /// build counterfeited a request for a thread still in its pool
13904    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
13905    #[test]
13906    fn a_signal_to_a_thread_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_is_requeued_after_its_own_stop() {
13907        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
13908        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13909        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
13910        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
13911            &mut scheduler,
13912            creator,
13913            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
13914            Some(0),
13915        );
13916        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
13917
13918        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
13919        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
13920        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
13921        assert!(
13922            scheduler
13923                .next_turns
13924                .get(&creator)
13925                .unwrap()
13926                .req
13927                .try_read()
13928                .is_none()
13929        );
13930        assert_eq!(
13931            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
13932            Some(&op)
13933        );
13934        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
13935
13936        // The kernel has not delivered yet: every pass is empty.
13937        for _ in 0..3 {
13938            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
13939            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
13940        }
13941
13942        // The thread's own stop posts its continuation; the next pass requeues it.
13943        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
13944        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
13945        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
13946        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
13947        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
13948        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
13949        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
13950
13951        // Its delivery commits although the leader is runnable.
13952        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
13953        assert_eq!(
13954            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
13955            Some(creator)
13956        );
13957        assert!(
13958            scheduler
13959                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
13960                .is_ok()
13961        );
13962        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
13963    }

13965    /// On a scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
13966    /// DBT, KVM), a committed signal to a thread asleep in a call outside the
13967    /// scheduler (a blocking external call, or a vfork parent waiting for its
13968    /// child) neither arms the thread nor counterfeits a request: the thread
13969    /// stays in its pool, awaiting its own continuation. Before, a debug build
13970    /// panicked here ("thread should be parked in the scheduler"). In-guest
13971    /// LiteInst hit it when a vfork child's exit signalled the parent it had
13972    /// just killed, and the panic poisoned the scheduler and hung the run.
13973    #[test]
13974    fn a_signal_to_a_backgrounded_thread_on_a_scheduler_without_signal_targets_waits_for_its_continuation()
13975     {
13976        for vfork in [false, true] {
13977            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
13978            scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
13979            assert!(!scheduler.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls);
13980            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
13981            let rid = if vfork {
13982                ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op)
13983            } else {
13984                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
13985            };
13986            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, None);
13987            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
13988
13989            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
13990            let case = format!("vfork={vfork}");
13991            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
13992            assert!(
13993                scheduler
13994                    .next_turns
13995                    .get(&creator)
13996                    .unwrap()
13997                    .req
13998                    .try_read()
13999                    .is_none(),
14000                "{case}: a request was counterfeited"
14001            );
14002            assert_eq!(
14003                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
14004                Some(&op),
14005                "{case}"
14006            );
14007            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
14008            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent), "{case}");
14009        }
14010    }

14012    /// When the release barrier's watchdog expires with an armed thread that
14013    /// has still not posted its continuation, the barrier must not drop the
14014    /// arm and resume scheduling: that would leave the thread for `step2c` to
14015    /// harvest behind runnable siblings, an admission order that host delivery
14016    /// time decides. The watchdog's start is backdated here (an injected clock),
14017    /// so the production bound needs no test knob.
14018    #[test]
14019    fn an_expired_release_barrier_keeps_the_arm_and_refuses_the_run() {
14020        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14021        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
14022        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14023            &mut scheduler,
14024            creator,
14025            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
14026            Some(0),
14027        );
14028        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
14029        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
14030        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
14031
14032        // The first empty pass starts the watchdog.
14033        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
14034        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
14035        scheduler.signaled_background_since = Some(
14036            std::time::Instant::now()
14037                .checked_sub(Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE + Duration::from_secs(1))
14038                .expect("the monotonic clock has run longer than the watchdog bound"),
14039        );
14040
14041        // Expired: the pass is still refused, the arm and the pool entry stay,
14042        // and nothing is requeued for a later harvest.
14043        for _ in 0..2 {
14044            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
14045            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
14046            assert_eq!(
14047                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
14048                Some(&op)
14049            );
14050            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14051        }
14052        // The typed refusal names the thread, and the scheduler loop ends the
14053        // run with it rather than scheduling on.
14054        let refusal = scheduler
14055            .signaled_background_refusal
14056            .take()
14057            .expect("an expired barrier records a typed refusal");
14058        assert_eq!(refusal.unposted, vec![creator]);
14059        assert!(refusal.waited >= Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE);
14060        assert!(
14061            refusal
14062                .to_string()
14063                .starts_with("hermit refused to continue the run")
14064        );
14065        // A whole pass is refused as well, so step2c cannot harvest the thread.
14066        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14067        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
14068        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14069        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_refusal.is_some());
14070    }
14071
14072    /// Armed threads are released together, only once every one has posted,
14073    /// in an order fixed by thread ID alone: the barrier pushes them in
14074    /// ascending DetTid order to the front of the run queue (as `step2e` admits
14075    /// deferred parents), so the highest DetTid runs first. Which stop the host
14076    /// reports first does not decide the order: both posting orders give the
14077    /// same run-queue order. A thread that leaves its pool another way (here it
14078    /// exits) is dropped rather than waited for.
14079    #[test]
14080    fn signaled_background_threads_are_released_together_in_thread_id_order() {
14081        for creator_posts_first in [false, true] {
14082            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14083            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14084            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
14085            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
14086            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
14087            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14088                &mut scheduler,
14089                creator,
14090                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
14091                Some(0),
14092            );
14093            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14094                &mut scheduler,
14095                sibling,
14096                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(sibling, 1)),
14097                Some(0),
14098            );
14099            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14100                &mut scheduler,
14101                child,
14102                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(child, 1)),
14103                Some(0),
14104            );
14105            for thread in [sibling, child, creator] {
14106                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(thread, Signal::SIGUSR1);
14107            }
14108            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.len(), 3);
14109            assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.is_empty());
14110
14111            let (first, last) = if creator_posts_first {
14112                (creator, sibling)
14113            } else {
14114                (sibling, creator)
14115            };
14116            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, first, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
14117            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
14118            scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
14119            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
14120            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(first));
14121            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
14122
14123            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, last, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
14124            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
14125            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14126            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
14127            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(sibling));
14128            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), sibling);
14129            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(creator));
14130            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), creator);
14131            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(child));
14132            assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
14133            assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
14134            assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
14135        }
14136    }

14138    /// A signal that does not wake a background call at a known point arms
14139    /// nothing and counterfeits nothing: the thread stays in its pool for
14140    /// `step2c` to harvest. That is a vfork parent, which sleeps killable, and
14141    /// a thread whose recorded sleeping mask blocks the signal or is unknown.
14142    #[test]
14143    fn a_signal_that_cannot_wake_a_background_call_leaves_it_in_its_pool() {
14144        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
14145        let cases: [(&str, Option<u64>, bool); 3] = [
14146            ("vfork parent", Some(0), true),
14147            ("blocked", Some(chld), false),
14148            ("unknown mask", None, false),
14149        ];
14150        for (case, mask, vfork_parent) in cases {
14151            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14152            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
14153            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14154                &mut scheduler,
14155                creator,
14156                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
14157                Some(0),
14158            );
14159            scheduler
14160                .blocked
14161                .out_of_scheduler_masks
14162                .insert(creator, mask);
14163            if vfork_parent {
14164                scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
14165            }
14166            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
14167            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
14168            assert!(
14169                !scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator),
14170                "{case}"
14171            );
14172            assert_eq!(
14173                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
14174                Some(&op),
14175                "{case}"
14176            );
14177            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
14178            assert!(
14179                scheduler
14180                    .next_turns
14181                    .get(&creator)
14182                    .unwrap()
14183                    .req
14184                    .try_read()
14185                    .is_none(),
14186                "{case}"
14187            );
14188            assert!(
14189                scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok(),
14190                "{case}"
14191            );
14192        }
14193    }
14194
14195    /// A signal another guest sends in its own turn (`notify_signal_pending`)
14196    /// while a thread is still stopped at its posted `rt_sigsuspend` request
14197    /// reaches the call, as a timer's send at that point does
14198    /// (`a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes`):
14199    /// the send is queued, the step2 drain notes it without arming anything,
14200    /// and committing the call arms the thread for the release barrier. A
14201    /// signal the temporary mask blocks is not noted, and nothing arms. Coverage
14202    /// of main: its drain notes the send
14203    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
14204    /// note.
14205    #[test]
14206    fn a_sibling_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
14207        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
14208        for (case, signal, temporary_mask, armed) in [
14209            ("admitted", Signal::SIGUSR1, 0, true),
14210            // Gap: main's drain drops a realtime signal sent at an rt_sigsuspend request.
14211            ("blocked", Signal::SIGUSR1, usr1, false),
14212            // Gap: main notes SIGKILL sent at an rt_sigsuspend request (open policy question).
14213        ] {
14214            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14215            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
14216            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
14217            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
14218            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
14219            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
14220            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
14221            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
14222
14223            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper::from(signal));
14224            assert_eq!(
14225                scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.get(&creator),
14226                Some(&vec![SigWrapper::from(signal)]),
14227                "{case}"
14228            );
14229            assert!(
14230                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
14231                "{case}"
14232            );
14233            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
14234            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
14235            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
14236            assert_eq!(
14237                scheduler
14238                    .blocked
14239                    .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
14240                    .get(&creator)
14241                    .copied(),
14242                armed.then_some(signal),
14243                "{case}"
14244            );
14245            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator), "{case}");
14246            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14247                &mut scheduler,
14248                creator,
14249                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
14250                Some(temporary_mask),
14251            );
14252            assert_eq!(
14253                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
14254                Some(&op),
14255                "{case}"
14256            );
14257            assert_eq!(
14258                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
14259                armed,
14260                "{case}"
14261            );
14262            assert!(
14263                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
14264                "{case}"
14265            );
14266        }
14267    }

14269    /// A signal a sibling sends while the waiter's `rt_sigsuspend` request is
14270    /// posted but not yet granted is delivered by the kernel as soon as the
14271    /// granted call installs its temporary mask, and the waiter's delivery stop
14272    /// is its report. The step2 drain notes the send and granting the request
14273    /// arms the waiter, so every pass is empty until that stop is posted, and
14274    /// the release barrier then requeues the waiter ahead of the runnable
14275    /// sibling: no sibling runs between the grant and the waiter's return.
14276    /// Coverage of main: its drain notes the send
14277    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
14278    /// note. Adapted from https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3224, where a
14279    /// hold on every other thread gave this order.
14280    #[tokio::test]
14281    async fn a_sibling_signal_sent_before_the_rt_sigsuspend_grant_requeues_the_waiter_first() {
14282        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14283        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14284        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
14285        let rid = ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op);
14286        let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
14287        request.insert(rid.clone(), Permission::RW);
14288        request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
14289        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&creator].req.clone();
14290        scheduler.request_put(&req, request, &global_time);
14291        // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
14292        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
14293
14294        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1));
14295        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
14296        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
14297        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14298        assert_eq!(
14299            scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
14300            Some(&Signal::SIGUSR1)
14301        );
14302
14303        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
14304        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, Some(0));
14305        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&parent].req.clone();
14306        scheduler.request_put(&req, Resources::new(parent), &global_time);
14307        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
14308        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(scheduler));
14309        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
14310
14311        for _ in 0..3 {
14312            let pass = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
14313            assert!(pass.is_err(), "the sibling ran before the waiter reported");
14314            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14315            assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
14316            assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
14317        }
14318        post_inbound_signal(
14319            &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
14320            creator,
14321            libc::SIGUSR1,
14322            &global_time,
14323        );
14324        let turn = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last)
14325            .await
14326            .expect("the waiter's delivery turn");
14327        assert_eq!(turn.tid, creator);
14328        assert!(
14329            turn.resources
14330                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1)))
14331        );
14332        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14333        assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
14334        assert!(s.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
14335        assert!(s.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14336    }

14338    /// The invariant that guards the counterfeit request still holds for every

14340    /// parked at a posted request.

14342    #[should_panic(expected = "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler")]
14343    fn a_signal_to_an_unposted_thread_outside_the_background_pools_still_asserts() {
14344        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14345        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
14346    }

14348    /// The resources of `thread`'s posted request, or `None` while it has
14349    /// posted nothing.
14350    fn request_resources(scheduler: &Scheduler, thread: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<ResourceID>> {
14351        scheduler.next_turns[&thread]
14352            .req
14353            .try_read()
14354            .map(|request| request.unwrap().resources.keys().cloned().collect())
14355    }

14357    /// A synthesized `SIGCHLD` that reaches a vfork parent still inside its real
14358    /// vfork (its request is empty) arms nothing and counterfeits nothing. A
14359    /// vfork parent sleeps killable, so the signal stays pending; a counterfeit
14360    /// request would put a thread that cannot answer on the run queue and lose
14361    /// the continuation that releases the vfork barrier. Once the child has
14362    /// exited, the parent's own continuation arrives and the ordinary barrier
14363    /// and blocker paths return it to the run queue.
14364    #[test]
14365    fn child_exit_signal_leaves_vfork_parent_waiting_for_its_continuation() {
14366        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14367        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
14368        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14369            &mut scheduler,
14370            creator,
14371            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
14372            Some(0),
14373        );
14374        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
14375
14376        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
14377
14378        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14379        assert_eq!(
14380            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
14381            Some(&op)
14382        );
14383        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14384        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, creator), None);
14385
14386        let mut continuation = Resources::new(creator);
14387        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op), Permission::RW);
14388        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
14389        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
14390        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
14391        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
14392        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
14393        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14394        assert_eq!(
14395            request_resources(&scheduler, creator),
14396            Some(vec![ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op)])
14397        );
14398    }

14529    /// A signal the waiter's temporary mask blocks cannot end its
14530    /// `rt_sigsuspend`, so it must not arm the waiter: the scheduler would then
14531    /// wait for a report that never comes. Left in its pool, a waiter that
14532    /// nothing else can wake gets the terminal deadlock verdict instead of a
14533    /// hang, and the verdict names the mask.
14534    #[test]
14535    fn signal_blocked_by_the_rt_sigsuspend_mask_leaves_the_wait_in_its_pool() {
14536        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
14537        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14538        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
14539        let op = ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291);
14540        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
14541        let alarm_bit = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
14542        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14543            &mut scheduler,
14544            waiter,
14545            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
14546            Some(alarm_bit),
14547        );
14548
14549        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, Signal::SIGALRM);
14550
14551        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14552        assert_eq!(
14553            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&waiter),
14554            Some(&op)
14555        );
14556        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
14557        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, waiter), None);
14558        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
14559        let report = scheduler
14560            .take_terminal_deadlock()
14561            .expect("a waiter whose mask blocks the only signal is a terminal deadlock");
14562        assert!(
14563            report.contains("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal"),
14564            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
14565        );
14566        assert!(
14567            report.contains(&format!("temporary mask {:#x}", alarm_bit)),
14568            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
14569        );
14570    }

14572    /// The scheduler's sigset bits are the kernel's: signal n is bit n - 1, so
14573    /// realtime signal 64 is bit 63, and a number outside 1..=64 has no bit.
14574    /// The mask recorded for an `rt_sigsuspend` waiter is the one the kernel
14575    /// installs, which never blocks SIGKILL or SIGSTOP (the syscall layer's
14576    /// `kernel_installed_signal_mask`, tested with it). A signal that mask
14577    /// admits arms the waiter; one it blocks does not.
14578    #[test]
14579    fn rt_sigsuspend_mask_uses_kernel_sigset_bits_and_cannot_block_kill_or_stop() {
14580        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
14581        assert_eq!(usr1, 1_u64 << (libc::SIGUSR1 - 1));
14582        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(64), 1_u64 << 63);
14583        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(63), 1_u64 << 62);
14584        for out_of_range in [0, 65, -1, i32::MIN] {
14585            assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(out_of_range), 0, "{out_of_range}");
14586        }
14587        // The widest mask the kernel installs.
14588        let everything = !(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP));
14589        assert_ne!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM), 0);
14590        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL), 0);
14591        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP), 0);
14592
14593        let cases = [
14594            (usr1, Signal::SIGUSR1, false),
14595            (usr1, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
14596            (0, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
14597            (everything, Signal::SIGALRM, false),
14598        ];
14599        for (mask, signal, armed) in cases {
14600            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
14601            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
14602            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
14603            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14604                &mut scheduler,
14605                waiter,
14606                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291)),
14607                Some(mask),
14608            );
14609            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, signal);
14610            assert_eq!(
14611                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&waiter),
14612                armed,
14613                "mask {mask:#x}, signal {signal}"
14614            );
14615        }
14616    }

14618    /// A child-exit timer whose creator already dequeued the kernel's own
14619    /// `SIGCHLD` for the process, and had that delivery deferred, commits that
14620    /// delivery instead of sending a second signal. Before, only the leader was
14621    /// looked up, so the timer sent again and found the deferred creator in no
14622    /// pool (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
14623    #[test]
14624    fn a_child_exit_timer_commits_a_deferred_creator_delivery_without_sending() {
14625        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14626        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14627        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
14628        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
14629        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
14630        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
14631        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
14632        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
14633        assert_eq!(
14634            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
14635            Some(creator)
14636        );
14637        assert!(
14638            scheduler
14639                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
14640                .is_err()
14641        );
14642        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&creator));
14643        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14644
14645        let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
14646        scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
14647            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
14648            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
14649            creator,
14650            Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
14651            true,
14652            scheduler.committed_time,
14653        );
14654        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, attempts);
14655        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
14656        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
14657        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
14658        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14659    }

14661    /// The barrier runs before anything else in a pass: while an armed thread
14662    /// has posted nothing, a due timer is not popped and the pass is empty;
14663    /// once it has posted, the pass requeues it first and then goes on.
14664    #[test]
14665    fn the_signaled_background_barrier_runs_before_any_timer_pop() {
14666        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
14667        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14668        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
14669        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
14670        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
14671            &mut scheduler,
14672            creator,
14673            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
14674            Some(0),
14675        );
14676        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGUSR1);
14677        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
14678            LogicalTime::from_nanos(0),
14679            child,
14680            parent,
14681            creator,
14682        );
14683        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
14684        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 1);
14685        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14686
14687        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
14688        let _ = scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
14689        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
14690        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
14691        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
14692        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 0);
14693    }

14695    /// A `SIGCHLD` delivery that no scheduler decision placed is deferred behind
14696    /// a runnable sibling, as a host-async signal is, so the sibling's work runs
14697    /// first. A committed futex wake no longer places one: no `SIGCHLD` ends a
14698    /// gated wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
14699    #[test]
14700    fn an_unplaced_sigchld_delivery_is_deferred_behind_a_runnable_sibling() {
14701        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
14702        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14703        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
14704        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
14705        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
14706        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(parent), Some(parent));
14707        assert!(
14708            scheduler
14709                .block_for_one_resource(parent, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
14710                .is_err()
14711        );
14712        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&parent));
14713        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
14714        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
14715    }

14717    /// A precise futex waiter woken for a signal is queued ahead of a thread that
14718    /// was already runnable, so it is the thread that resumes and dequeues the
14719    /// signal (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
14720    #[test]
14721    fn a_signal_woken_futex_waiter_runs_before_an_already_runnable_thread() {
14722        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
14723        for scheduler_send in [false, true] {
14724            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
14725            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
14726            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(101);
14727            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, runnable);
14728            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
14729            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
14730            scheduler
14731                .test_kernel_signal_states
14732                .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
14733            if scheduler_send {
14734                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
14735            } else {
14736                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
14737                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
14738            }
14739            assert_eq!(
14740                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
14741                vec![target, runnable]
14742            );
14743        }
14744    }

14746    /// A child whose `exit_group` was granted has a `ChildExit` timer that sends
14747    /// the parent's `SIGCHLD` at a fixed logical time. Its logical death leaves
14748    /// the timer armed and sends nothing itself, and the timer names the thread
14749    /// that created the child, the one Linux prefers
14750    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
14751    #[test]
14752    fn a_child_exit_timer_names_the_thread_that_created_the_child() {
14753        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
14754        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD));
14755        let child_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
14756        let deadline = scheduler.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
14757        assert!(
14758            scheduler
14759                .block_for_one_resource(
14760                    child,
14761                    &ResourceID::Exit {
14762                        group: true,
14763                        process: child_process,
14764                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
14765                    },
14766                    &Permission::RW,
14767                    None,
14768                    None,
14769                    &Ivar::new(),
14770                )
14771                .is_ok()
14772        );
14773
14774        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
14775
14776        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
14777        assert_eq!(
14778            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
14779            vec![(
14780                deadline,
14781                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(
14782                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit {
14783                        child: child_process,
14784                        parent,
14785                    },
14786                    creator,
14787                    Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
14788                ),
14789            )]
14790        );
14791    }

14793    /// The first `SIGCHLD` delivered for an owned child's exit stands for it
14794    /// (`child_exit_sigchld`): once the kernel's copy was delivered, the
14795    /// child's `ChildExit` timer sends none, which before was a second
14796    /// `SIGCHLD` for that exit. Without that delivery the timer sends its own.
14797    #[test]
14798    fn a_child_exit_timer_sends_nothing_after_the_kernels_copy() {
14799        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
14800        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
14801        for kernel_copy_first in [false, true] {
14802            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14803            let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
14804            let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
14805            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
14806            assert_eq!(
14807                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
14808                    child,
14809                    ChildExitSigchldControl::ExitStatus {
14810                        code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
14811                        status: 7,
14812                        uid: 0,
14813                    },
14814                ),
14815                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
14816            );
14817            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
14818            if kernel_copy_first {
14819                assert_eq!(
14820                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
14821                        parent,
14822                        ChildExitSigchldControl::ClaimKernelCopy { child },
14823                    ),
14824                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(false),
14825                    "the kernel's copy is the first, and is delivered"
14826                );
14827            }
14828            let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
14829            scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
14830                scheduler.committed_time,
14831                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
14832                parent,
14833                Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
14834                true,
14835                scheduler.committed_time,
14836            );
14837            assert_eq!(
14838                scheduler.host_signal_attempts - attempts,
14839                u64::from(!kernel_copy_first),
14840                "kernel copy first: {kernel_copy_first}"
14841            );
14842        }
14843    }

14951    #[test]
14952    fn pending_signals_preserve_a_restartable_internal_write_pollers_signal_set() {
14953        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14954        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);

14964        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
14965        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();

14967        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
14968        assert_eq!(
14969            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
14970            vec![
14971                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),

14973            ]

14983            resources

14985                .contains_key(&ResourceID::WaitidSignals(vec![

14996        // of the same one-resource response rather than being dropped.
14997        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM));
14998        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();

15000            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),

15002                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),

15008        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();

15010        assert_eq!(selected, target);

15012            scheduler

15014                .is_ok()

15017            scheduler
15018                .step5_guest_unblock(target, &resources, &selected_response)
15019                .is_ok()
15020        );
15021        assert!(matches!(
15022            response.try_read(),
15023            Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals)))
15024                if signals == vec![
15025                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
15026                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2),
15027                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM),
15028                ]
15029        ));

15033    fn restartable_io_sigchld_bypasses_host_async_signal_deferral() {

15047        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();

15049        let resources = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
15050            .req
15051            .try_read()

15060            scheduler
15061                .block_for_one_resource(
15062                    target,

15074    /// `step4_resource_block` and `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert that a
15075    /// request carries exactly one resource. The drain must never violate that.
15076    ///
15077    /// An earlier revision merged a pending signal into a request that already
15078    /// held an `InboundSignal`, producing a two-resource request. The scheduler
15079    /// daemon then panicked and the container hung — on a guest containing no
15080    /// `waitid` at all, because `{InboundSignal}` is exactly what `signal_guest`
15081    /// installs for an ordinary cross-thread signal.
15082    #[test]
15083    fn drain_never_builds_a_multi_resource_request() {
15084        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15085        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15086        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
15087        // The shape that crashed: an ordinary delivered signal, nothing to do
15088        // with waitid.
15089        let mut inbound = Resources::new(target);
15090        inbound.insert(
15091            ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)),
15092            Permission::W,
15093        );
15094        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(inbound));
15095        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
15096
15097        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
15098        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
15099
15100        let resources = scheduler
15101            .next_turns
15102            .get(&target)
15103            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
15104            .and_then(Result::ok)
15105            .expect("the target should still hold a request");
15106        assert!(
15107            resources.resources.len() <= 1,
15108            "the drain produced a {}-resource request, which step4 asserts against: {:?}",
15109            resources.resources.len(),
15110            resources.resources,
15111        );
15112    }
15113
15114    /// A thread can hold a `WaitChild` request while ALREADY in the run queue:
15115    /// `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its request, and
15116    /// `step6_reenqueue` pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues
15117    /// its next request. An earlier revision inferred "blocked" from the
15118    /// resource and skipped the run-queue removal, so the drain pushed a
15119    /// second copy of the thread.
15120    ///
15121    /// That failure is worse than it looks: `RunQueue`'s duplicate check is
15122    /// `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, so debug builds panic with "Invariant
15123    /// violation! Tried to add ... already present" while RELEASE builds
15124    /// silently enqueue the thread twice and select it twice.
15125    #[test]
15126    fn pending_signal_does_not_double_queue_a_runnable_child_waiter() {
15127        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15128        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15129        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
15130        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
15131        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
15132            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
15133            owner: None,
15134            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15135        };
15136        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
15137        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
15138        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
15139        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
15140        // The distinguishing state: holds WaitChild AND is runnable, with no
15141        // `child_waiters` entry -- exactly what a just-woken waiter looks like.
15142        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
15143        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
15144        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target));
15145
15146        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
15147        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
15148
15149        let occurrences = scheduler
15150            .run_queue
15151            .tids()
15152            .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
15153            .count();
15154        assert_eq!(
15155            occurrences, 1,
15156            "the signalled child waiter must appear in the run queue exactly once"
15157        );
15158    }
15159
15160    /// A thread parked on a scheduler-managed child wait is blocked in
15161    /// `child_waiters`, never in the run queue, so the run-queue removal the
15162    /// polling disposition performs does not apply to it. Before this case was
15163    /// handled, a signal aimed at such a thread was recorded nowhere and a wait
15164    /// on a child that never exits could not be interrupted at all.
15165    #[test]
15166    fn pending_signal_unblocks_a_managed_child_waiter() {
15167        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15168        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15169        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
15170        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
15171        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
15172            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
15173            owner: None,
15174            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15175        };
15176        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
15177        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
15178        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
15179        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
15180        // Parked, not runnable: exactly how `WaitChild` leaves a thread.
15181        scheduler
15182            .blocked
15183            .child_waiters
15184            .insert(target, (parent, spec));
15185        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
15186
15187        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
15188        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
15189
15190        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
15191
15192        assert!(
15193            scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target),
15194            "the signalled child waiter must be requeued"
15195        );
15196        assert!(
15197            !scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target),
15198            "its child-wait blocking entry must be cleared"
15199        );
15200        assert_eq!(
15201            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
15202            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
15203            "the resume must name the signal that woke it"
15204        );
15205    }

15207    #[test]
15208    fn pending_signal_replaces_an_internal_poller_request() {
15209        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15210        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15211        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
15212        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
15213        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
15214        polling.fyi("waitid");
15215        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
15216        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
15217
15218        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
15219
15220        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
15221        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
15222        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
15223        assert_eq!(
15224            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
15225            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)]
15226        );
15227
15228        // A later signal must merge into the already-materialized waitid wakeup.
15229        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
15230        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
15231        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
15232        assert_eq!(
15233            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
15234            vec![
15235                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
15236                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
15237            ]
15238        );
15239    }

15241    /// A scheduler for a backend whose process exits complete asynchronously
15242    /// (in-guest LiteInst), with killed-thread RPC cancellation as that backend
15243    /// has it.
15244    fn async_exit_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
15245        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15246            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
15247            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
15248        });
15249        Scheduler::new(&config)
15250    }
15251
15252    /// Registers single-threaded process `tid` with an empty pending request.
15253    fn register_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
15254        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
15255        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15256            tid,
15257            ThreadNextTurn {
15258                dettid: tid,
15259                child_tid_addr: 0,
15260                req: Ivar::new(),
15261                resp: Ivar::new(),
15262                protocol: Default::default(),
15263            },
15264        );
15265    }

15267    #[test]
15268    fn async_exit_holds_selection_from_the_grant_until_completion() {
15269        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
15270        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
15271        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
15272        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
15273        assert_eq!(
15274            scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits,
15275            BTreeSet::from([process])
15276        );
15277        // What the backend's watchdog reads.
15278        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits(), [process]);
15279        // Every pass skips while the exit is pending, however many there are.
15280        for _ in 0..3 {
15281            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
15282        }
15283        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
15284        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
15285        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
15286        assert!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits().is_empty());
15287    }

15301    #[test]
15302    fn async_exit_lifetime_is_monotone() {
15303        // A completion that arrives first is kept, and a later begin, from the
15304        // grant or from a late deregistration, is a no-op.
15305        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
15306        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
15307        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
15308        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
15309        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
15310        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(process));
15311        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
15312        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
15313
15314        // After a grant and its completion, a late begin is a no-op too.
15315        let other = DetPid::from_raw(200);
15316        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(other);
15317        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(other));
15318        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(other));
15319        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
15320    }

15330    #[test]
15331    fn completion_consumes_only_registrations_the_process_did_not_deregister() {
15332        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
15333        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15334        let deregistered = DetTid::from_raw(200);
15335        register_process(&mut scheduler, dead);
15336        register_process(&mut scheduler, deregistered);
15337        // `deregistered` finished its exit hook before exiting.
15338        assert!(scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(deregistered));
15339        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&deregistered, &deregistered, MmId::initial(deregistered));
15340
15341        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(deregistered));
15342        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
15343        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&dead));
15344        // A late DeregisterThread for the consumed thread is already accounted.
15345        assert!(!scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(dead));
15346        // Consuming twice is a no-op.
15347        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
15348    }

15351    fn a_dead_vfork_parent_cancels_its_barrier_and_settles_a_late_child() {

15359        assert!(!scheduler.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent));

15361        // without panicking.

15364        assert!(!scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.contains(&parent));

15604    #[test]
15605    fn physical_exit_barrier_precedes_empty_queue_timer_fast_forward() {
15606        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15607            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
15608            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
15609        });
15610        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
15611        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
15612        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
15613        let exit_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
15614        let first_process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
15615        let second_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
15616        let unrelated_process = DetPid::from_raw(300);
15617
15618        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
15619        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
15620        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(second_process));
15621        scheduler.register_alarm(
15622            first_process,
15623            first_process,
15624            initial_time,
15625            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
15626            LogicalTime::ZERO,
15627            Signal::SIGALRM,
15628        );
15629
15630        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
15631        assert_eq!(
15632            scheduler
15633                .blocked
15634                .timed_waiters
15635                .iter()
15636                .map(|(time, _)| time)
15637                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15638            vec![exit_deadline]
15639        );
15640        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
15641
15642        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(unrelated_process));
15643        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
15644        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
15645        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
15646        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
15647        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
15648
15649        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(second_process));
15650        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
15651        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
15652        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), exit_deadline);
15653    }

15655    fn physical_wait_handoff_queue(completion_before_wait: bool) -> Vec<DetTid> {
15656        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15657            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
15658            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
15659        });
15660        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
15661        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
15662        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
15663        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(200);
15664        let child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
15665        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
15666        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
15667        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waiter);
15668        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
15669
15670        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
15671        if completion_before_wait {
15672            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
15673        }
15674
15675        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(waiter), Some(waiter));
15676        assert!(
15677            scheduler
15678                .block_for_one_resource(
15679                    waiter,
15680                    &ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child),
15681                    &Permission::W,
15682                    None,
15683                    None,
15684                    &Ivar::new(),
15685                )
15686                .is_err()
15687        );
15688        assert_eq!(
15689            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15690            vec![sibling]
15691        );
15692
15693        if !completion_before_wait {
15694            assert!(
15695                scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err(),
15696                "a runnable sibling must not pass the pending physical-exit barrier"
15697            );
15698            assert_eq!(
15699                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15700                vec![sibling]
15701            );
15702            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
15703        }
15704
15705        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_ok());
15706        assert!(scheduler.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
15707        assert!(scheduler.blocked.physical_child_ready.contains(&waiter));
15708        scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect()
15709    }

15747    fn terminal_wait_selects_group_owner_and_clone_class() {

15751        let owner_b = DetTid::from_raw(102);
15752        let normal = DetPid::from_raw(200);
15753        let clone_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
15754        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
15755        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, owner_a, false);
15756        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, owner_b, false);
15757        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
15758            owner_a,
15759            normal,
15760            true,
15761            false,
15762            libc::SIGCHLD,
15763        );
15764        scheduler
15765            .thread_tree
15766            .add_child_with_wait_metadata(owner_b, clone_child, true, false, 0);
15767        let group = DetPid::from_raw(77);
15768        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(normal, group));
15769        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(clone_child, group));
15770        scheduler.logically_exited_processes.insert(normal);
15771        scheduler.logically_exited_processes.insert(clone_child);
15772
15773        assert_eq!(
15774            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
15775                parent,
15776                ChildWaitSpec {
15777                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(DetPid::from_raw(78)),
15778                    owner: Some(owner_a),
15779                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15780                },
15781            ),
15782            None,
15783            "a different process group must not match"
15784        );
15785        assert_eq!(
15786            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
15787                parent,
15788                ChildWaitSpec {
15789                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(normal),
15790                    owner: Some(owner_b),
15791                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15792                },
15793            ),
15794            None,
15795            "__WNOTHREAD must exclude a child created by another task"
15796        );
15797        assert_eq!(
15798            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
15799                parent,
15800                ChildWaitSpec {
15801                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(clone_child),
15802                    owner: Some(owner_b),
15803                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15804                },
15805            ),
15806            None,
15807            "a clone child must not enter the ordinary SIGCHLD population"
15808        );
15809        assert_eq!(
15810            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
15811                parent,
15812                ChildWaitSpec {
15813                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group),
15814                    owner: Some(owner_b),
15815                    exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Clone,
15816                },
15817            ),
15818            Some(clone_child)
15819        );
15820        assert_eq!(
15821            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
15822                parent,
15823                ChildWaitSpec {
15824                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
15825                    owner: Some(owner_a),
15826                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
15827                },
15828            ),
15829            Some(normal)
15830        );
15831    }
