15863    /// Populate a scheduler with a deadlock's worth of blocked state, inserting
15864    /// each collection in the caller's chosen order.
15865    ///
15866    /// `reverse` exists so the same logical state can be built two ways: the
15867    /// report must not depend on insertion order, because `futex_waiters` is a
15868    /// `HashMap`, `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, and
15869    /// `Resources::resources` a `HashMap`.
15870    fn deadlocked_scheduler(config: &Config, reverse: bool) -> Scheduler {
15871        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(config);
15872        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
15873        let mut futexes = vec![
15874            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100), 5),
15875            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200), 7),
15876            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404300), 9),
15877        ];
15878        let mut tids = vec![3, 5, 7, 9];
15879        if reverse {
15880            futexes.reverse();
15881            tids.reverse();
15882        }
15883
15884        for (futex_id, dettid) in futexes {
15885            scheduler
15886                .blocked
15887                .futex_waiters
15888                .entry(futex_id)
15889                .or_default()
15890                .push(futex_waiter(dettid, u32::MAX));
15891        }
15892        for dettid in tids {
15893            let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(dettid);
15894            // A request carrying several resources: `Resources::resources` is a
15895            // HashMap, so an unsorted render would vary here too.
15896            let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
15897            resources.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
15898            resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(dettid), Permission::RW);
15899            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15900                dettid,
15901                ThreadNextTurn {
15902                    dettid,
15903                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15904                    // A FULL ivar: `Debug` on this prints the parked waker's raw
15905                    // host pointers, which is exactly what must not reach stderr.
15906                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(resources)),
15907                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15908                    protocol: Default::default(),
15909                },
15910            );
15911            scheduler.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid);
15912        }
15913        scheduler
15914            .blocked
15915            .timed_waiters
15916            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(11));
15917        // A thread held at a happens-before gate, which adds a headline class
15918        // and renders its checkpoint request in the per-thread list.
15919        let held = DetTid::from_raw(13);
15920        let mut gate = Resources::new(held);
15921        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50), Permission::R);
15922        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15923            held,
15924            ThreadNextTurn {
15925                dettid: held,
15926                child_tid_addr: 0,
15927                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
15928                resp: Ivar::new(),
15929                protocol: Default::default(),
15930            },
15931        );
15932        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
15933            r#"{"version": 1,
15934                "events": {"never": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
15935                           "gate": {"thread": "13", "syscalls": 50}},
15936                "edges": [{"before": "never", "after": "gate", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
15937        );
15938        hb.parked.insert(held);
15939        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
15940        scheduler
15941    }
15942
15943    /// The deadlock report reaches stderr, so it must be byte-identical across
15944    /// runs of the same program. Codex measured the unguarded `{:?}` dump
15945    /// emitting `Waker { data: 0x557e90a74680, .. }` in one run and
15946    /// `Waker { data: 0x5654e2b08680, .. }` in the next: raw host pointers that
15947    /// move with ASLR. Assert the render carries no host pointer and no
15948    /// insertion-order dependence.
15949    #[test]
15950    fn deadlock_report_is_deterministic_and_carries_no_host_pointer() {
15951        let config = Config::default();
15952        let forward = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, false).format_terminal_deadlock();
15953        let reversed = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, true).format_terminal_deadlock();
15954
15955        // Same logical state built in two insertion orders must render
15956        // identically: no HashMap/HashSet iteration order may leak.
15957        assert_eq!(forward, reversed);
15958
15959        // No `Debug` of an Ivar/Waker, and so no host pointer.
15960        //
15961        // ⚠️ THIS LIST CANNOT SEE A SECTION THE FIXTURE NEVER RENDERS. It only
15962        // inspects the text `deadlocked_scheduler` happens to produce. When you
15963        // add a section to `format_terminal_deadlock`, add the state that triggers
15964        // it to the fixture in the same change, or this test will pass and say
15965        // nothing about your section.
15966        //
15967        // These tokens catch host POINTERS and raw thread ids. The subtler failure
15968        // is a host-influenced COUNTER, which looks like an ordinary small integer
15969        // and matches no banned word -- which is why the byte-identical assertion
15970        // above is the load-bearing check and this list is only a backstop.
15971        for banned in [
15972            "Waker", "Ivar", "vtable", "Mutex", "poisoned", "ThreadId", "0x7f",
15973        ] {
15974            assert!(
15975                !forward.contains(banned),
15976                "deadlock report leaked {banned:?}; it must print only guest-level \
15977                 identities.\n{forward}"
15978            );
15979        }
15980
15981        // The report is still substantive: it names every blocked thread, the
15982        // futex keys, and the indefinite deadline.
15983        for expected in [
15984            // This fixture holds BOTH pools and a held thread, so the
15985            // state-derived headline must name all three rather than whichever
15986            // branch happened to fire.
15987            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
15988             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), and \
15989             thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire, \
15990             but no runnable threads left.",
15991            "dtid 13: HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50): R",
15992            "dtid 3",
15993            "dtid 9",
15994            "0x404100",
15995            "0x404300",
15996            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)",
15997            "FutexWait: R, MemAddrSpace(DetPid(3)): RW",
15998        ] {
15999            assert!(
16000                forward.contains(expected),
16001                "deadlock report lost {expected:?}:\n{forward}"
16002            );
16003        }
16004    }
16005
16006    /// A `pause(2)` registers `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`, which is a sentinel for
16007    /// "no deadline", not a deadline. With nothing else left to run, the guest is
16008    /// permanently blocked and must be reported as such -- never woken.
16009    #[test]
16010    fn indefinite_waiter_alone_is_reported_as_a_deadlock() {
16011        let config = Config::default();
16012        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16013        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16014        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16015
16016        scheduler
16017            .blocked
16018            .timed_waiters
16019            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(100));
16020
16021        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16022
16023        // Asserting the verdict by value, not by catching a panic: the report is
16024        // recorded for `sched_loop_inner` to print and exit on, so the text is
16025        // checkable here rather than only through `#[should_panic]`.
16026        let report = scheduler
16027            .take_terminal_deadlock()
16028            .expect("an indefinite waiter with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
16029        assert!(
16030            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
16031            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
16032        );
16033        // Taking it is destructive, and the indefinite waiter is never woken.
16034        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
16035        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
16036        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
16037    }

16140    /// The `SignalEvt` arm is the sub-case whose behaviour this change actually
16141    /// alters, and it is reachable with no `pause` anywhere.
16142    ///
16143    /// `handle_timer_settime` adds a guest-supplied duration to now, and
16144    /// `LogicalTime`'s `Add` saturates, so an absurdly far-future POSIX timer
16145    /// (issue #219, the Java case) lands on `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` and
16146    /// `register_posix_timer` inserts it verbatim. Previously `step2d` popped it,
16147    /// fast-forwarded the clock ~584 years, and dispatched to `fire_alarm`, which
16148    /// -- unlike the `ThreadEvt` arm -- does NOT abort: it delivered a bogus
16149    /// year-2554 signal and the guest carried on. That is now a terminal
16150    /// deadlock, which is the faithful answer, because Linux will not fire that
16151    /// timer either and those threads genuinely hang.
16152    #[test]
16153    fn saturated_posix_timer_alone_is_a_deadlock_not_a_bogus_signal() {
16154        let config = Config::default();
16155        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16156        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16157        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16158        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
16159
16160        // The real production entry point, with the deadline a saturating add
16161        // produces. No `pause`, no `ThreadEvt`.
16162        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
16163            process,
16164            process,
16165            7,
16166            Some(LogicalTime::MAX - LogicalTime::from_nanos(0)),
16167            LogicalTime::ZERO,
16168            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
16169        );
16170        assert_eq!(
16171            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.next_deadline(),
16172            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
16173            "a saturated timer must land on the no-deadline sentinel"
16174        );
16175
16176        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16177
16178        let report = scheduler
16179            .take_terminal_deadlock()
16180            .expect("a saturated timer with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
16181        assert!(
16182            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
16183            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
16184        );
16185        // The signal was NOT delivered and the clock did NOT jump to the end of
16186        // logical time: both are what the old fast-forward did here.
16187        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
16188        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.is_empty());
16189        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
16190    }
16191
16192    /// The headline is derived from state, not from the branch that fired, so a
16193    /// genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer registered names
16194    /// both classes rather than being filed as an indefinite-wait bug.
16195    #[test]
16196    fn a_futex_deadlock_holding_a_saturated_timer_names_both_classes() {
16197        let config = Config::default();
16198        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16199        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16200        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
16201        scheduler
16202            .blocked
16203            .futex_waiters
16204            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
16205            .or_default()
16206            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
16207        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
16208            DetPid::from_raw(100),
16209            DetPid::from_raw(100),
16210            7,
16211            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
16212            LogicalTime::ZERO,
16213            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
16214        );
16215
16216        // Branch order sends this to the indefinite arm, because a timed waiter
16217        // exists; the headline must still say the futex pool is blocked.
16218        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16219        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().expect("terminal");
16220        let headline = report.lines().next().expect("a headline");
16221        assert_eq!(
16222            headline,
16223            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
16224             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), but no \
16225             runnable threads left.",
16226            "full report:\n{report}"
16227        );
16228    }

16230    /// The futex class shares `report_terminal_deadlock`, so it must record a
16231    /// verdict too -- otherwise fixing the teardown for one class silently
16232    /// leaves the other wedged.
16233    #[test]
16234    fn futex_deadlock_records_the_same_terminal_verdict() {
16235        let config = Config::default();
16236        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16237        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16238        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
16239        scheduler
16240            .blocked
16241            .futex_waiters
16242            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
16243            .or_default()
16244            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
16245
16246        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16247
16248        let report = scheduler
16249            .take_terminal_deadlock()
16250            .expect("futex waiters with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
16251        assert!(
16252            report.contains("thread(s) waiting on futex"),
16253            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
16254        );

16257    /// The positive half of the bracket: refusing to fast-forward onto an
16258    /// indefinite waiter must not make the fast-forward machinery inert. A real
16259    /// deadline still fires, the clock still advances to exactly that deadline
16260    /// (not to the end of logical time), and the indefinite waiter stays parked.
16261    #[test]
16262    fn finite_deadline_still_fast_forwards_alongside_an_indefinite_waiter() {
16263        let config = Config::default();
16264        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16265        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16266        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16267        let alarm_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
16268        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
16269        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(200);
16270
16271        scheduler
16272            .blocked
16273            .timed_waiters
16274            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
16275        scheduler.register_alarm(
16276            process,
16277            process,
16278            initial_time,
16279            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
16280            LogicalTime::ZERO,
16281            Signal::SIGALRM,
16282        );
16283
16284        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16285        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), alarm_deadline);
16286        assert_eq!(
16287            scheduler
16288                .blocked
16289                .timed_waiters
16290                .iter()
16291                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
16292            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
16293        );
16294    }

16296    /// Outstanding blocking external IO can still deliver the signal an
16297    /// indefinite waiter is waiting for, so the deadlock verdict must be
16298    /// deferred rather than reported. `step2c` does not cover this case: it only
16299    /// spins when `timed_waiters` is *empty*, and an indefinite waiter is an
16300    /// entry.
16301    #[test]
16302    fn outstanding_external_io_defers_the_indefinite_wait_verdict() {
16303        let config = Config::default();
16304        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16305        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16306        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16307        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(100);
16308        let io_thread = DetTid::from_raw(101);
16309
16310        scheduler
16311            .blocked
16312            .timed_waiters
16313            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
16314        scheduler
16315            .blocked
16316            .external_io_blockers
16317            .insert(io_thread, ExternalOpId::new(io_thread, 0));
16318
16319        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16320        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
16321        assert_eq!(
16322            scheduler
16323                .blocked
16324                .timed_waiters
16325                .iter()
16326                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
16327            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
16328        );
16329    }

16407    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order: explicit SIG_IGN wins over blocking,
16408    /// blocking over default-ignore, and only a default-ignored, unblocked
16409    /// SIGCHLD is discarded.
16410    #[test]
16411    fn sigchld_notification_classification_follows_do_notify_parent() {
16412        use ChildExitNotification::*;

16414            (true, false, false, None),
16415            (true, false, true, None),
16416            (false, false, false, Discard),
16417            (false, false, true, Deliver),
16418            (false, true, false, Deliver),
16419            (false, true, true, Deliver),
16420        ] {
16421            assert_eq!(
16422                classify_sigchld_notification(ignored, caught, blocked),
16423                expected,
16424                "ignored {ignored}, caught {caught}, blocked {blocked}"
16425            );

16427    }

16450    const SIGCHLD_BIT: u64 = 1 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
16451
16452    /// A parent process 100 and its child 200 (exit signal `exit_signal`),
16453    /// the parent parked on a request labelled `fyi`, with /proc reporting
16454    /// `ignored`, `caught` and `blocked` as SIGCHLD's state for the parent.
16455    fn child_exit_fixture(
16456        reports_publication: bool,
16457        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
16458        fyi: Option<&str>,
16459        masks: Option<(bool, bool, bool)>,
16460    ) -> (Scheduler, DetPid, DetPid) {
16461        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16462            backend.reports_child_exit_publication = reports_publication;
16463        });
16464        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16465        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
16466        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
16467        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16468        scheduler
16469            .thread_tree
16470            .add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, child, true, false, exit_signal);
16471        let req = match fyi {
16472            Some(label) => {
16473                let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
16474                request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
16475                request.fyi(label);
16476                Ivar::full(Ok(request))
16477            }
16478            Option::None => Ivar::new(),
16479        };
16480        for tid in [parent, child] {
16481            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16482                tid,
16483                ThreadNextTurn {
16484                    dettid: tid,
16485                    child_tid_addr: 0,
16486                    req: if tid == parent {
16487                        req.clone()
16488                    } else {
16489                        Ivar::new()
16490                    },
16491                    resp: Ivar::new(),
16492                    protocol: Default::default(),
16493                },
16494            );
16495            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16496        }
16497        if let Some((ignored, caught, blocked)) = masks {
16498            let bit = |set: bool| if set { SIGCHLD_BIT } else { 0 };
16499            scheduler
16500                .test_signal_masks
16501                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigIgn"), bit(ignored));
16502            scheduler
16503                .test_signal_masks
16504                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigCgt"), bit(caught));
16505            scheduler
16506                .test_signal_masks
16507                .insert((parent, Some(parent), "SigBlk"), bit(blocked));
16508        }
16509        (scheduler, parent, child)
16510    }
16511
16512    #[test]
16513    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_when_every_input_is_known() {
16514        use ChildExitNotification::*;
16515        let classify = |exit_signal, fyi, masks| {
16516            let (scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(true, exit_signal, fyi, masks);
16517            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
16518        };
16519        let read = Some("read");
16520        assert_eq!(
16521            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((true, false, true))),
16522            None
16523        );
16524        assert_eq!(
16525            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, false))),
16526            Discard
16527        );
16528        assert_eq!(
16529            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, true, false))),
16530            Deliver
16531        );
16532        assert_eq!(
16533            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, true))),
16534            Deliver
16535        );
16536        // Not an effective SIGCHLD, the receiving task not parked, a
16537        // temporary-mask syscall, or /proc unreadable: Undecided.
16538        assert_eq!(
16539            classify(libc::SIGUSR1, read, Some((false, false, false))),
16540            Undecided
16541        );
16542        assert_eq!(classify(0, read, Some((false, false, false))), Undecided);
16543        assert_eq!(
16544            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Option::None, Some((false, false, false))),
16545            Undecided
16546        );
16547        for label in ["ppoll", "pselect6", "epoll_pwait"] {
16548            assert_eq!(
16549                classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Some(label), Some((false, false, false))),
16550                Undecided,
16551                "{label}"
16552            );
16553        }
16554        assert_eq!(classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Option::None), Undecided);
16555    }

16557    /// A managed wait installs Detcore's private blocking mask, which /proc
16558    /// then reports; the saved guest mask decides instead.
16559    #[test]
16560    fn child_exit_notification_reads_the_saved_guest_mask() {
16561        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
16562            true,
16563            libc::SIGCHLD,
16564            Some("wait-child-lifecycle"),
16565            Some((false, false, true)),
16566        );

16568            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
16569            ChildExitNotification::Deliver
16570        );

16573            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
16574            ChildExitNotification::Discard
16575        );
16576        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Some(SIGCHLD_BIT)));

16582        assert!(!scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(DetPid::from_raw(999), Some(0)));

16585    fn child_exit_timer_armed(scheduler: &Scheduler, child: DetPid) -> bool {
16586        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().any(|(_, event)| {
16587            matches!(
16588                event,
16589                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child: exited, .. }, ..)
16590                    if exited == child
16591            )
16592        })
16593    }

16595    fn grant_group_exit(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, child: DetPid) {
16596        grant_group_exit_from(scheduler, child, child);
16597    }

16599    /// Grants `thread` an exit_group request that names `child` as its process.
16600    fn grant_group_exit_from(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, child: DetPid) {
16601        assert!(
16602            scheduler
16603                .block_for_one_resource(
16604                    thread,
16605                    &ResourceID::Exit {
16606                        group: true,
16607                        process: child,
16608                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
16609                    },
16610                    &Permission::RW,
16611                    Option::None,
16612                    Option::None,
16613                    &Ivar::new(),
16614                )
16615                .is_ok()
16616        );
16617    }

16619    /// A child's effective exit signal follows Linux: the clone's signal; its
16620    /// creator's process's signal under CLONE_PARENT; SIGCHLD after the child's
16621    /// own successful exec, which also moves it out of the clone wait class.
16622    /// The parent's exec changes only the notification of the children it
16623    /// created before (`parent_exec_id`), not their wait class, and not that of
16624    /// a child it creates afterwards. Before, the clone's requested signal was
16625    /// kept for good (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3895).
16626    #[test]
16627    fn a_childs_effective_exit_signal_follows_exec_and_clone_parent() {
16628        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
16629        let creator = DetPid::from_raw(200);
16630        let usr1_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
16631        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(400);
16632        let late_child = DetPid::from_raw(500);
16633        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
16634        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16635        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, creator, true, false, libc::SIGCHLD);
16636        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, usr1_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
16637        // CLONE_PARENT with SIGUSR1 requested: the creator's SIGCHLD, and the
16638        // creator's parent.
16639        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(creator, grandchild, true, true, libc::SIGUSR1);
16640        let exit_signal = |tree: &ThreadTree, pid| tree.process_wait[&pid].exit_signal;
16641        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, grandchild), libc::SIGCHLD);
16642        assert_eq!(tree.process_wait[&grandchild].wait_parent, Some(parent));
16643        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
16644
16645        // The parent's exec: the existing SIGUSR1 child still waits as a clone
16646        // child but notifies with SIGCHLD; one created afterwards does not.
16647        tree.record_successful_exec(parent);
16648        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, late_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
16649        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, usr1_child), libc::SIGUSR1);
16650        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
16651        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
16652
16653        // The child's own exec: SIGCHLD for both.
16654        tree.record_successful_exec(late_child);
16655        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, late_child), libc::SIGCHLD);
16656        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
16657        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(DetPid::from_raw(999)), None);
16658    }
16659
16660    /// The exit-notification classifier reads the effective notification
16661    /// signal: a clone(SIGUSR1) child that exec'd notifies with SIGCHLD, so an
16662    /// ignored SIGCHLD is classified (here Discard) rather than left Undecided.
16663    #[test]
16664    fn child_exit_notification_uses_the_effective_exit_signal() {
16665        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
16666            true,

16670        );

16672            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),

16674        );
16675        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);

16677            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),

16679        );
16680    }

16682    /// For an ignored notification the exit grant arms no synthetic SIGCHLD
16683    /// and holds every turn until the backend reports the kernel published
16684    /// the exit; caught, blocked and unclassifiable notifications keep the
16685    /// timer, as does a backend that makes no publication report.
16686    #[test]
16687    fn ignored_child_exit_holds_turns_instead_of_arming_the_timer() {
16688        for masks in [(true, false, false), (false, false, false)] {
16689            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
16690                child_exit_fixture(true, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), Some(masks));
16691            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
16692            assert!(!child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child), "{masks:?}");
16693            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
16694            assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(DetPid::from_raw(999)));
16695            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
16696            assert!(scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
16697            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{masks:?}");
16698        }
16699        for (reports, masks) in [
16700            (true, Some((false, true, false))),
16701            (true, Some((false, false, true))),
16702            (true, Option::None),
16703            (false, Some((false, false, false))),
16704        ] {
16705            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
16706                child_exit_fixture(reports, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), masks);
16707            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
16708            assert!(
16709                child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child),
16710                "{reports} {masks:?}"
16711            );
16712            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
16713        }
16714    }

16716    /// An exit_group from a thread that, in the thread tree, leads its own
16717    /// process but names another process (ptrace names a raw clone child with a
16718    /// non-SIGCHLD exit signal by its creator's pid) does not end the named
16719    /// process, which is never reported consumed. It must keep the synthetic
16720    /// timer and install no hold, which would stop every turn for good.
16721    #[test]
16722    fn an_exit_that_names_another_process_installs_no_hold() {
16723        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
16724            true,
16725            libc::SIGCHLD,
16726            Some("read"),
16727            Some((false, false, false)),

16729        let clone_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
16730        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
16731            child,
16732            clone_child,
16733            true,
16734            false,
16735            libc::SIGUSR1,
16736        );
16737        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16738            clone_child,
16739            ThreadNextTurn {
16740                dettid: clone_child,
16741                child_tid_addr: 0,
16742                req: Ivar::new(),
16743                resp: Ivar::new(),
16744                protocol: Default::default(),
16745            },
16746        );
16747        scheduler.priorities.insert(clone_child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16748        grant_group_exit_from(&mut scheduler, clone_child, child);
16749        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
16750        assert!(child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child));
16751        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());

16754    /// A process consumed before its Exit request is granted (killed while

16784    /// Only an internal polling probe or a child wait is classified; a parent
16785    /// in rt_sigsuspend, with a signal in flight, or in any other wait is
16786    /// Undecided and keeps the synthetic SIGCHLD.
16787    #[test]
16788    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_in_covered_parent_states() {
16789        let classify_with = |resource: ResourceID, fyi: &str, sigsuspend: bool| {
16790            let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
16791                true,
16792                libc::SIGCHLD,
16793                Some("read"),
16794                Some((false, false, false)),
16795            );
16796            let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
16797            request.insert(resource, Permission::W);
16798            request.fyi(fyi);
16799            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
16800            if sigsuspend {
16801                scheduler
16802                    .blocked
16803                    .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
16804                    .insert(parent, crate::resources::ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1));
16805            }
16806            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
16807        };
16808        let wait = ResourceID::WaitChild {
16809            parent: DetPid::from_raw(100),
16810            spec: crate::types::ChildWaitSpec {
16811                selector: crate::types::ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
16812                owner: Option::None,
16813                exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
16814            },
16815        };
16816        assert_eq!(
16817            classify_with(wait, "wait-child-lifecycle", false),
16818            ChildExitNotification::Discard
16819        );
16820        assert_eq!(
16821            classify_with(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, "read", true),
16822            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
16823        );
16824        assert_eq!(
16825            classify_with(
16826                ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)),
16827                "",
16828                false
16829            ),
16830            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
16831        );
16832        assert_eq!(
16833            classify_with(ResourceID::FutexWait, "futex_wait", false),
16834            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
16835        );
16836    }

16838    #[test]
16839    fn final_child_exit_does_not_block_parent_timer() {
16840        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16841            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
16842            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
16843        });
16844        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16845        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16846        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16847        let deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
16848        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
16849        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
16850        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16851        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
16852        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16853            parent,
16854            ThreadNextTurn {
16855                dettid: parent,
16856                child_tid_addr: 0,
16857                req: Ivar::new(),
16858                resp: Ivar::new(),
16859                protocol: Default::default(),
16860            },
16861        );
16862        scheduler.priorities.insert(parent, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16863        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, parent);
16864
16865        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
16866        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16867        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
16868        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
16869        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
16870        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
16871        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
16872    }
16873
16874    type LoopProbe = Box<dyn FnMut(SchedLoopPoint, &mut Scheduler)>;
16875
16876    thread_local! {
16877        static LOOP_PROBE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<LoopProbe>> =
16878            const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
16879    }
16880
16881    /// Called by [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] in test builds. The probe is
16882    /// thread-local, so only a daemon loop polled on the installing test's own
16883    /// thread (a current-thread runtime) reaches it.
16884    pub(super) fn fire_loop_probe(point: SchedLoopPoint, sched: &mut Scheduler) {
16885        // Taken out while it runs, so the probe may use the scheduler freely.
16886        let Some(mut probe) = LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take()) else {
16887            return;
16888        };
16889        probe(point, sched);
16890        LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| {
16891            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
16892            if slot.is_none() {
16893                *slot = Some(probe);
16894            }
16895        });
16896    }
16897
16898    /// Uninstalls the loop probe when the test ends, including by panic.
16899    struct LoopProbeGuard;
16900
16901    impl LoopProbeGuard {
16902        fn install(probe: LoopProbe) -> Self {
16903            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| *slot.borrow_mut() = Some(probe));
16904            LoopProbeGuard
16905        }
16906    }
16907
16908    impl Drop for LoopProbeGuard {
16909        fn drop(&mut self) {
16910            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take());
16911        }
16912    }
16913
16914    /// Records, in order, the text of every INFO event from
16915    /// `detcore::scheduler`: the stream the L2 verify comparator reads.
16916    ///
16917    /// It is a thread-scoped subscriber, so a test that reads it must start
16918    /// with `exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test`. `tracing` caches
16919    /// callsite interest for the whole process, and a parallel in-process test
16920    /// that reaches a scheduler callsite with no subscriber can cache `never`
16921    /// and drop a real record from this capture
16922    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3366).
16923    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
16924    struct SchedulerInfoLog(Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>);
16925
16926    struct MessageText(Option<String>);
16927
16928    impl tracing::field::Visit for MessageText {
16929        fn record_debug(&mut self, field: &tracing::field::Field, value: &dyn std::fmt::Debug) {
16930            if field.name() == "message" {
16931                self.0 = Some(format!("{value:?}"));
16932            }
16933        }
16934    }
16935
16936    impl tracing::Subscriber for SchedulerInfoLog {
16937        fn register_callsite(
16938            &self,
16939            _: &'static tracing::Metadata<'static>,
16940        ) -> tracing::subscriber::Interest {
16941            tracing::subscriber::Interest::sometimes()
16942        }
16943
16944        fn enabled(&self, metadata: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
16945            *metadata.level() == Level::INFO
16946        }
16947
16948        fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
16949            tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
16950        }
16951
16952        fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
16953
16954        fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
16955
16956        fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
16957            if !event.metadata().target().starts_with("detcore::scheduler") {
16958                return;
16959            }
16960            let mut text = MessageText(None);
16961            event.record(&mut text);
16962            if let Some(text) = text.0 {
16963                self.0.lock().unwrap().push(text);
16964            }
16965        }
16966
16967        fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
16968
16969        fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
16970    }
16971
16972    /// What one daemon run to shutdown shows: its scheduler INFO lines, in
16973    /// order, and the logical state it leaves.
16974    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
16975    struct ShutdownObservation {
16976        scheduler_info: Vec<String>,
16977        turn: u64,
16978        global_time: LogicalTime,
16979    }
16980
16981    const FIZZLE: &str = "zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.";
16982    const SCHED_LOOP_EXIT: &str = "[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.";
16983
16984    /// Run the real daemon loop, `sched_loop`, from the state `setup` builds
16985    /// until it exits. When the loop reaches `landing` -- (pass number, point)
16986    /// -- run `report` there, inside that lock hold, as a backend thread that
16987    /// took the scheduler lock at that moment would. Returns the observation
16988    /// and whether `report` ran.
16989    async fn run_daemon_to_shutdown(
16990        config: &Config,
16991        setup: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler),
16992        landing: Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>,
16993        report: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler) + 'static,
16994    ) -> (ShutdownObservation, bool) {
16995        let log = SchedulerInfoLog::default();
16996        let _subscriber = tracing::subscriber::set_default(log.clone());
16997        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(config)));
16998        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(config)));
16999        {
17000            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17001            setup(&mut s);
17002            s.started_up.try_put(());
17003        }
17004
17005        let landed = std::rc::Rc::new(std::cell::Cell::new(false));
17006        let probe: LoopProbe = {
17007            let landed = landed.clone();
17008            let mut report = Some(report);
17009            let mut pass = 0u64;
17010            Box::new(move |point, s| {
17011                if point == SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop {
17012                    pass += 1;
17013                    // A hang guard, not a timing assumption: every schedule
17014                    // here exits by its third pass.
17015                    assert!(pass <= 8, "the daemon loop did not exit in 8 passes");
17016                }
17017                if landing == Some((pass, point))
17018                    && let Some(report) = report.take()
17019                {
17020                    report(s);
17021                    landed.set(true);
17022                }
17023            })
17024        };
17025        let _probe = LoopProbeGuard::install(probe);
17026        sched_loop(sched.clone(), global_time.clone()).await;
17027
17028        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17029        assert!(s.run_queue.is_empty());
17030        assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17031        assert!(s.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
17032        let observation = ShutdownObservation {
17033            scheduler_info: log.0.lock().unwrap().clone(),
17034            turn: s.turn,
17035            global_time: global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
17036        };
17037        (observation, landed.get())
17038    }
17039
17040    /// Each point a host-timed report can land in the daemon's last two passes:
17041    /// the pass that drains the last thread's removal, and the pass after it.
17042    const SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS: [(u64, SchedLoopPoint); 6] = [
17043        (1, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
17044        (1, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
17045        (1, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
17046        (2, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
17047        (2, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
17048        (2, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
17049    ];
17050
17051    /// Every run must match the first exactly, and the first must report the
17052    /// empty state once, as its last line before the loop exits.
17053    fn assert_one_shutdown_log(runs: &[(Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>, ShutdownObservation)]) {
17054        let fizzles = |observation: &ShutdownObservation| {
17055            observation
17056                .scheduler_info
17057                .iter()
17058                .filter(|line| line.contains(FIZZLE))
17059                .count()
17060        };
17061        // Every landing's count, so a failure shows the whole pattern.
17062        let counts = runs
17063            .iter()
17064            .map(|(landing, observation)| (*landing, fizzles(observation)))
17065            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
17066        let (first, canonical) = &runs[0];
17067        assert_eq!(
17068            fizzles(canonical),
17069            1,
17070            "landing at {first:?} must log the empty state once; fizzle lines per landing: \
17071             {counts:?}; {canonical:#?}"
17072        );
17073        let tail = &canonical.scheduler_info[canonical.scheduler_info.len() - 2..];
17074        assert!(
17075            tail[0].contains(FIZZLE) && tail[1] == SCHED_LOOP_EXIT,
17076            "the empty state must be reported just before the loop exits: {canonical:#?}"
17077        );
17078        for (landing, observation) in &runs[1..] {
17079            assert_eq!(
17080                observation, canonical,
17081                "a report landing at {landing:?} instead of {first:?} changed the scheduler's \
17082                 INFO log or logical state; fizzle lines per landing: {counts:?}"
17083            );
17084        }
17085    }
17086
17087    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360: on SaBRe the last
17088    /// thread's logical exit opens a physical-exit barrier, and the ptrace
17089    /// supervisor closes it when the kernel's final wait status arrives -- a
17090    /// host-timed moment. Before the fix the empty-queue step logged its
17091    /// "fizzling" line only when that status had already landed by the time the
17092    /// step ran, so the line appeared zero or one times depending on the host.
17093    /// Land it at every point of the last two passes; the scheduler's INFO log
17094    /// and state must not change.
17095    #[tokio::test]
17096    async fn sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands() {
17097        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
17098        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
17099            module_path!(),
17100            "sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands",
17101        ) {
17102            return;
17103        }
17104        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
17105            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
17106            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
17107        });
17108        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17109        let mut runs = Vec::new();
17110        for landing in SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS {
17111            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
17112                &config,
17113                |s| {
17114                    s.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
17115                    register_known_thread(s, root);
17116                    // step6 re-enqueued the thread after its committed
17117                    // `exit_group` turn; then its exit hook ran.
17118                    s.runqueue_push_back(root);
17119                    s.logically_kill_thread(&root, &root, MmId::initial(root));
17120                    assert_eq!(s.pending_physical_process_exits, BTreeSet::from([root]));
17121                },
17122                Some(landing),
17123                move |s| assert!(s.complete_physical_process_exit(root)),
17124            )
17125            .await;
17126            assert!(landed, "the final wait status never landed at {landing:?}");
17127            runs.push((Some(landing), observation));
17128        }
17129        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
17130    }
17131
17132    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223, the same defect on
17133    /// ptrace: a worker's `exit_group` logically kills its parked sibling at
17134    /// once, and the kernel's physical kill later runs the sibling's exit hook,
17135    /// which calls `logically_kill_thread` again. The second call finds nothing
17136    /// to remove but still queues a removal, which the daemon must drain
17137    /// before it may exit. Before the fix, if that arrived after the empty-queue
17138    /// step had logged its line, the drain pass logged it a second time. Land
17139    /// it at every reachable point, and after the loop has exited (`None`); the
17140    /// scheduler's INFO log and state must not change.
17141    #[tokio::test]
17142    async fn redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands() {
17143        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
17144        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
17145            module_path!(),
17146            "redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands",
17147        ) {
17148            return;
17149        }
17150        let config = Config::default();
17151        assert!(!config.backend.reports_physical_process_exits);
17152        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17153        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(4);
17154        // With no physical-exit barrier the loop exits at the top of pass 2,
17155        // before pass 2's empty-queue step, so those two points are unreachable.
17156        let landings = SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS[..4]
17157            .iter()
17158            .copied()
17159            .map(Some)
17160            .chain([None]);
17161        let mut runs = Vec::new();
17162        for landing in landings {
17163            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
17164                &config,
17165                |s| {
17166                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
17167                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
17168                    register_known_thread(s, leader);
17169                    register_known_thread(s, worker);
17170                    // step6 re-enqueued the worker after its committed
17171                    // `exit_group` turn. The leader is parked, not queued.
17172                    s.runqueue_push_back(worker);
17173                    // After granting the exit, `finish_resource_response`
17174                    // logically kills the sibling; then the worker's own exit
17175                    // hook kills the worker.
17176                    s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
17177                    s.logically_kill_thread(&worker, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
17178                },
17179                landing,
17180                // The kernel's kill of the leader runs its exit hook.
17181                move |s| s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader)),
17182            )
17183            .await;
17184            assert_eq!(
17185                landed,
17186                landing.is_some(),
17187                "the redundant exit hook landed wrongly for {landing:?}"
17188            );
17189            runs.push((landing, observation));
17190        }
17191        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
17192    }

17194    /// Build an `HbRuntime` from a JSON happens-before spec for testing.
17195    fn hb_runtime(json: &str) -> HbRuntime {
17196        let program = detcore_model::happens_before::HappensBeforeSpec::from_json(json)
17197            .unwrap()
17198            .normalize()
17199            .unwrap();
17200        HbRuntime::new(program)
17201    }
17202
17203    /// A spec whose only edge gates dettid 5 on dettid 3, for the empty-queue
17204    /// tests below.
17205    const HB_GATE_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
17206        "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
17207                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
17208        "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;
17209
17210    /// A source fired and opened a parked thread's gate (`wake_pending`), and
17211    /// the source thread then left the run queue: the maintenance prefix must
17212    /// re-admit the parked thread before the empty-queue step classifies the
17213    /// state, not leave it to be reported as a deadlock
17214    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
17215    #[test]
17216    fn empty_queue_step_readmits_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_opened() {
17217        let config = Config::default();
17218        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
17219        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17220        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17221        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
17222        hb.fired.insert("src".to_owned());
17223        hb.parked.insert(target);
17224        hb.wake_pending = true;
17225        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
17226        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17227
17228        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17229        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_ok());
17230        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17231        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
17232        assert!(hb.parked.is_empty() && !hb.wake_pending);
17233        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17234    }
17235
17236    /// The nearby case that must NOT wake: the target is parked and no source
17237    /// has fired, nothing else can run, so no anchor can ever fire. The
17238    /// empty-queue step must report a terminal deadlock naming the gate rather
17239    /// than treat the scheduler as empty (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
17240    #[test]
17241    fn empty_queue_step_reports_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_cannot_open() {
17242        let config = Config::default();
17243        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
17244        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17245        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17246        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
17247        hb.parked.insert(target);
17248        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
17249
17250        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
17251        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17252        let report = scheduler
17253            .take_terminal_deadlock()
17254            .expect("a parked thread with no possible source must be a reported deadlock");
17255        assert!(
17256            report.contains("held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire"),
17257            "{report}"
17258        );
17259    }

17261    /// A signal the scheduler sends to a thread held at a happens-before gate
17262    /// (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) must leave the thread held, with its
17263    /// gate's checkpoint request intact. The held thread used to be reported as
17264    /// gone, which panicked `wake_signaled_guest` and hung the run; and had it
17265    /// been force-unblocked, the substituted request would have let it past
17266    /// its gate before the source fired.
17267    #[test]
17268    fn signal_to_a_thread_held_at_a_gate_leaves_it_held() {
17269        let config = Config::default();
17270        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
17271        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17272        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
17273        hb.parked.insert(target);
17274        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
17275        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17276        let mut gate = Resources::new(target);
17277        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43), Permission::R);
17278        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
17279            target,
17280            ThreadNextTurn {
17281                dettid: target,
17282                child_tid_addr: 0,
17283                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
17284                resp: Ivar::new(),
17285                protocol: Default::default(),
17286            },
17287        );
17288
17289        assert!(matches!(
17290            scheduler.thread_status(target),
17291            ThreadStatus::NotRunning
17292        ));
17293        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
17294
17295        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17296        assert!(
17297            scheduler
17298                .happens_before
17299                .as_ref()
17300                .unwrap()
17301                .parked
17302                .contains(&target)
17303        );
17304        let request = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
17305            .req
17306            .try_read()
17307            .expect("the held thread's request is still filled")
17308            .expect("the held thread's request is not an error");
17309        assert!(
17310            request
17311                .resources
17312                .contains_key(&ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43))
17313                && request.resources.len() == 1,
17314            "the gate's checkpoint request was replaced: {:?}",
17315            request.resources.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()
17316        );
17317    }
17318
17319    /// One syscall can reach a count anchor and a syscall-occurrence anchor at
17320    /// once (the commit claims both are evaluated): the checkpoint must fire
17321    /// both. Of the occurrence anchors the guest names, only those on this
17322    /// thread fire; a spawn-ordinal anchor that resolves to another thread, and
17323    /// a name that is not an anchor, are ignored.
17324    #[test]
17325    fn checkpoint_fires_count_and_occurrence_anchors_reached_at_one_syscall() {
17326        let config = Config::default();
17327        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
17328        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
17329            r#"{"version": 1,
17330                "threads": {"S2": {"spawn_ordinal": 2}},
17331                "events": {"count": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 13},
17332                           "occ": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2},
17333                           "other": {"thread": "S2", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}}}"#,
17334        ));
17335        let named = ["occ", "other", "missing"].map(str::to_owned);
17336        assert!(
17337            scheduler
17338                .hb_checkpoint(DetTid::from_raw(5), 13, &named)
17339                .is_ok()
17340        );
17341        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
17342        let fired: Vec<&str> = hb.fired.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
17343        assert_eq!(fired, ["count", "occ"]);
17344        assert!(hb.wake_pending);
17345    }
17346
17347    /// A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired is refused by name when the
17348    /// run finishes, with its position and the edges that use it. A count
17349    /// anchor that never fired is not part of the refusal (unchanged behavior),
17350    /// and once every occurrence anchor has fired there is nothing to refuse.
17351    #[test]
17352    fn unfired_occurrence_anchor_is_reported_by_name() {
17353        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
17354            r#"{"version": 1,
17355                "events": {"c": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
17356                           "w": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}},
17357                "edges": [{"before": "c", "after": "w", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
17358        );
17359        let report = hb
17360            .unfired_occurrence_report()
17361            .expect("an unfired occurrence anchor must be refused");
17362        assert!(
17363            report.starts_with("HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: 1 happens-before"),
17364            "{report}"
17365        );
17366        assert!(
17367            report.contains("anchor 'w' on thread 5: writev(fd=9)#2 never fired (edges: c -> w)"),
17368            "{report}"
17369        );
17370        assert!(!report.contains("anchor 'c'"), "{report}");
17371        hb.fired.insert("w".to_owned());
17372        assert!(hb.unfired_occurrence_report().is_none());
17373    }
17374
17375    /// A version-2 spec that holds dettid 5 at its 43rd syscall until both
17376    /// sources fire, with an unrelated anchor on dettid 7 and a 1000 ns budget.
17377    const HB_BUDGET_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,
17378        "events": {"src1": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
17379                   "src2": {"thread": "4", "syscalls": 42},
17380                   "other": {"thread": "7", "syscalls": 9},
17381                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
17382        "edges": [{"before": "src1", "after": "dst"},
17383                  {"before": "src2", "after": "dst"}]}"#;
17384
17385    /// Select `dettid` as step3 would and let it reach its checkpoint at
17386    /// syscall `count`, at committed time `now_ns`.
17387    fn hb_reach(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, dettid: DetTid, count: u64, now_ns: u64) -> bool {
17388        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(now_ns);
17389        scheduler
17390            .priorities
17391            .entry(dettid)
17392            .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17393        if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
17394            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
17395        }
17396        scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(dettid).unwrap();
17397        let granted = scheduler.hb_checkpoint(dettid, count, &[]).is_ok();
17398        if granted {
17399            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
17400        }
17401        granted
17402    }
17403
17404    /// A posthook anchor on the same thread as an entry that returned an
17405    /// internal restart code is refused by name and does not fire, the turn
17406    /// grants nothing (the thread leaves the run queue), and the thread it
17407    /// gates stays held; an earlier pending verdict is kept. A spawn-ordinal
17408    /// anchor the guest named at another thread's interrupted call is not on
17409    /// that thread, and its turn proceeds (the Claude review of
17410    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048). A completed entry's
17411    /// posthook checkpoint fires it like a prehook one
17412    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929).
17413    #[test]
17414    fn an_interrupted_posthook_anchor_is_refused_and_does_not_fire() {
17415        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
17416            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
17417            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
17418                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
17419                                       "phase": "posthook"},
17420                       "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
17421            "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;
17422        let source = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17423        let anchors = ["src".to_owned()];
17424        let interrupt = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, anchors: &[String]| {
17425            scheduler
17426                .priorities
17427                .entry(source)
17428                .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17429            if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source) {
17430                scheduler.runqueue_push_back(source);
17431            }
17432            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(source).unwrap();
17433            let granted = scheduler
17434                .hb_posthook_interrupted(source, 9, anchors, "ERESTARTSYS")
17435                .is_ok();
17436            if granted {
17437                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
17438            }
17439            granted
17440        };
17441        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17442        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
17443        // The helper's spawn-ordinal anchor, named at dtid 3's call: not on
17444        // dtid 3, so nothing is refused and the turn proceeds.
17445        assert!(interrupt(&mut scheduler, &["helper_wait".to_owned()]));
17446        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
17447        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
17448        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source));
17449        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
17450        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().fired.is_empty());
17451        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
17452        assert_eq!(
17453            scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(),
17454            "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid 3 reached posthook happens-before anchor(s) \
17455             [\"src\"] at syscall count 9, and the call was interrupted (ERESTARTSYS); whether \
17456             it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
17457             checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook or \
17458             on a call that is not interrupted."
17459        );
17460
17461        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17462        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
17463        scheduler.terminal_deadlock = Some("earlier".to_owned());
17464        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
17465        assert_eq!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(), "earlier");
17466
17467        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17468        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
17469        assert!(scheduler.hb_checkpoint(source, 9, &anchors).is_ok());
17470        assert!(
17471            scheduler
17472                .happens_before
17473                .as_ref()
17474                .unwrap()
17475                .fired
17476                .contains("src")
17477        );
17478        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
17479    }
17480
17481    /// Through a whole turn (`block_for_one_resource`): an interrupted entry
17482    /// whose posthook anchor is on its thread commits no turn and gets no
17483    /// response, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit; one whose
17484    /// only anchor is another thread's spawn-ordinal anchor is an ordinary
17485    /// turn (the Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048).
17486    #[tokio::test]
17487    async fn an_interrupted_posthook_refusal_grants_no_turn() {
17488        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
17489            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
17490            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
17491                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
17492                                       "phase": "posthook"}}}"#;
17493        for (anchor, refused) in [("helper_wait", false), ("src", true)] {
17494            let config = Config::default();
17495            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17496            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
17497            let thread = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17498            register_known_thread(&mut sched, thread);
17499            sched.runqueue_push_back(thread);
17500            let mut request = Resources::new(thread);
17501            request.insert(
17502                ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
17503                    count: 9,
17504                    anchors: vec![anchor.to_owned()],
17505                    code: "ERESTARTSYS".to_owned(),
17506                },
17507                Permission::R,
17508            );
17509            sched.next_turns[&thread].req.put(Ok(request));
17510            let response = sched.next_turns[&thread].resp.clone();
17511            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
17512            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17513            let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
17514                Duration::from_secs(5),
17515                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
17516            )
17517            .await
17518            .expect("the turn must not stall");
17519            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17520            assert_eq!(outcome.is_err(), refused, "{anchor}: {outcome:?}");
17521            assert_eq!(response.try_read().is_none(), refused, "{anchor}");
17522            assert_eq!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some(), refused, "{anchor}");
17523        }
17524    }

17526    /// The hold budget is charged in committed virtual time from the moment
17527    /// the thread is first parked. A wake caused by an unrelated anchor, and a
17528    /// gate only partly opened, re-park the thread without restarting its
17529    /// hold; past the budget the run is refused by name, naming the BEFORE
17530    /// anchor still missing. The check runs in `step2_drain_prefix`, which both
17531    /// turn loops call before selection.
17532    #[test]
17533    fn a_hold_is_charged_from_its_first_park_and_refused_past_its_budget() {
17534        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17535        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
17536        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17537        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
17538        let hold = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held].clone();
17539        assert_eq!(hold.since_ns, 5000);
17540
17541        // An unrelated anchor fires: the wake re-admits and clears the
17542        // physical park, and the thread re-parks; the hold is unchanged.
17543        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(7), 9, 5200));
17544        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17545        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().parked.is_empty());
17546        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5500));
17547        // One of two sources fires: still held, still the same hold.
17548        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5600));
17549        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17550        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5700));
17551        assert_eq!(
17552            scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held],
17553            hold
17554        );
17555
17556        // Exactly the budget is not over it.
17557        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6000);
17558        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17559        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17560        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6001);
17561        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
17562        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
17563        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
17564        assert_eq!(
17565            report,
17566            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid 5 has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
17567             [\"dst\"] for more than max_hold_ns = 1000 virtual ns, waiting on:\n  anchor 'src2' \
17568             on thread 4: after 42 syscalls never fired (edge src2 -> dst)"
17569        );
17570    }
17571
17572    /// A hold that ends inside its budget is gone: once the gate opens and the
17573    /// thread passes, no later committed time can refuse it. A version-1 spec
17574    /// has no budget at all.
17575    #[test]
17576    fn a_released_hold_and_a_version_1_hold_are_never_refused() {
17577        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17578        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
17579        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17580        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
17581        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
17582        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
17583        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17584        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5300));
17585        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
17586        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
17587        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17588        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17589
17590        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17591        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
17592            &HB_BUDGET_SPEC.replace(r#""version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,"#, r#""version": 1,"#),
17593        ));
17594        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
17595        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(u64::MAX / 2);
17596        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17597        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17598    }

17600    /// A non-leader exec hands the caller's task the leader's identity. When a
17601    /// relative anchor (with its base, on the same thread) is on either
17602    /// identity, the handoff is refused by name; any other exec is unaffected.
17603    #[test]
17604    fn a_non_leader_exec_on_a_relative_anchors_thread_is_refused() {
17605        let hb = hb_runtime(
17606            r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
17607                "m": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 2},
17608                "r": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"},
17609                "x": {"thread": "8", "syscall": "getppid"}}}"#,
17610        );
17611        let tid = DetTid::from_raw;
17612        let expected = |caller: i32, leader: i32| {
17613            format!(
17614                "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {caller} execs and takes \
17615                 over the identity of dtid {leader}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' \
17616                 (from 'm') are on these threads; relative anchors are not carried across a \
17617                 non-leader exec."
17618            )
17619        };
17620        // The relative anchor's thread is the leader that is replaced...
17621        assert_eq!(
17622            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(7), tid(5)),
17623            Some(expected(7, 5))
17624        );
17625        // ...or the worker whose task takes over.
17626        assert_eq!(
17627            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(5), tid(9)),
17628            Some(expected(5, 9))
17629        );
17630        // An absolute anchor alone on either thread is not affected.
17631        assert_eq!(hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(8), tid(9)), None);
17632    }

17634    /// A version-2 spec with a relative anchor (and its base) on dettid 17.
17635    const HB_RELATIVE_ON_17: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
17636        "m": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 1},
17637        "r": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"}}}"#;
17638
17639    /// The refusal goes through the real exec-reconnect handlers: a non-leader
17640    /// exec on the relative anchor's identity is recorded as a policy refusal
17641    /// on both the ordinary and the transferred path, while a same-identity
17642    /// exec (the leader itself execs) keeps the anchor and is not refused.
17643    #[test]
17644    fn exec_reconnect_refuses_a_relative_anchor_only_across_a_non_leader_exec() {
17645        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
17646        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
17647        for transferred in [false, true] {
17648            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17649            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
17650            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
17651            if transferred {
17652                reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
17653            } else {
17654                reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
17655            }
17656            assert!(sched.terminal_is_refusal, "transferred: {transferred}");
17657            let report = sched.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
17658            assert!(
17659                report.starts_with(
17660                    "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid 18 execs and takes over \
17661                     the identity of dtid 17, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' (from 'm')"
17662                ),
17663                "transferred: {transferred}: {report}"
17664            );
17665        }
17666
17667        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17668        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
17669        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
17670        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, leader, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
17671        assert!(sched.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17672        assert!(!sched.terminal_is_refusal);
17673    }
