17675    /// Once the exec reconnect has recorded the identity refusal, the next
17676    /// turn grants nothing: an unrelated thread waiting at an ordinary request
17677    /// gets no response, so no guest runs concurrently with the policy exit.
17678    /// (Adopted from the review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4004.)
17679    #[tokio::test]
17680    async fn the_identity_refusal_grants_no_further_turn() {
17681        let config = Config::default();
17682        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17683        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
17684        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
17685        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
17686        let other = DetTid::from_raw(31);
17687        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
17688        register_known_thread(&mut sched, other);
17689        sched.runqueue_push_back(other);
17690        let mut pending = Resources::new(other);
17691        pending.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(other), Permission::RW);
17692        sched.next_turns[&other].req.put(Ok(pending));
17693        let other_response = sched.next_turns[&other].resp.clone();
17694
17695        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
17696        assert!(sched.terminal_deadlock.is_some() && sched.terminal_is_refusal);
17697        sched.next_turns[&leader]
17698            .req
17699            .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
17700
17701        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
17702        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17703        let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
17704            Duration::from_secs(5),
17705            do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
17706        )
17707        .await
17708        .expect("the turn must not stall");
17709        assert!(outcome.is_err(), "a turn was committed: {outcome:?}");
17710        assert!(
17711            other_response.try_read().is_none(),
17712            "dtid 31 was granted a turn after the identity refusal was recorded"
17713        );
17714        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17715        assert_eq!(s.turn, 0);
17716        assert!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some());
17717    }

17719    /// A held thread that is removed (killed) leaves no hold behind, so a
17720    /// later committed time cannot refuse the run for it.
17721    #[test]
17722    fn a_removed_held_thread_leaves_no_hold_behind() {
17723        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17724        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
17725        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17726        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
17727        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&held);
17728        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
17729        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
17730        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17731        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17732    }

17734    /// A hold whose gate has opened is not refused while the re-admitted
17735    /// thread waits to be selected again, however late that is.
17736    #[test]
17737    fn an_opened_gate_is_not_refused_before_its_thread_runs_again() {
17738        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17739        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
17740        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17741        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
17742        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
17743        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
17744        // The hold record stays until the thread passes its checkpoint.
17745        assert!(
17746            scheduler
17747                .happens_before
17748                .as_ref()
17749                .unwrap()
17750                .holds
17751                .contains_key(&held)
17752        );
17753        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
17754        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
17755        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
17756    }

17758    /// A relative anchor that never fired is reported with its base, and the

17761    fn an_unfired_relative_anchor_names_its_base() {

17785    /// A child wait is part of a happens-before deadlock only when every child
17786    /// it could reap has all its live threads held at gates or parked in a
17787    /// futex wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904). A child
17788    /// thread doing anything else, an exited child, a child a committed
17789    /// SIGKILL has doomed, a wait with no matching child, an unnamed SIGKILL,
17790    /// and a run with no held thread keep the wait counted as input that may
17791    /// still arrive; a thread that has exited no longer counts.
17792    #[test]
17793    fn a_child_wait_settles_only_on_children_held_or_in_futex_waits() {
17794        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17795        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
17796        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17797        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17798        let child_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
17799        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
17800        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
17801        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
17802        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
17803            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
17804            owner: None,
17805            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
17806        };
17807        scheduler
17808            .blocked
17809            .child_waiters
17810            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
17811        let park_in_futex = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, addr: usize| {
17812            let mut futex_request = Resources::new(tid);
17813            futex_request.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::RW);
17814            s.next_turns.get_mut(&tid).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(futex_request));
17815            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(5)), addr);
17816            s.blocked
17817                .futex_waiters
17818                .entry(futex)
17819                .or_default()
17820                .push(futex_waiter(tid.as_raw(), u32::MAX));
17821        };
17822        // No held thread: the wait still counts as input, even with the
17823        // child's only thread parked in a futex wait (the held-thread guard,
17824        // not the child's state, decides this case).
17825        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child, 0x404000);
17826        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17827        scheduler.blocked.futex_waiters.clear();
17828        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&child).unwrap().req = Ivar::new();
17829        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17830        let hold = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid| {
17831            s.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().parked.insert(tid);
17832        };
17833        hold(&mut scheduler, child);
17834        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17835
17836        // A thread the child had that is no longer registered: if it left by
17837        // its own committed exit it is gone harmlessly; if it left without one
17838        // (a fatal signal, or a kill of its process), the process is going
17839        // down and the wait is real.
17840        let gone = DetTid::from_raw(8);
17841        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, gone, false);
17842        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17843        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
17844        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17845        // A new thread on that tid has not exited.
17846        scheduler.forget_committed_exit(gone);
17847        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17848        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
17849
17850        // A committed SIGKILL dooms the child: it will die, so the wait is
17851        // real, whenever its host-timed retirement arrives.
17852        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17853        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17854        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
17855        // A SIGKILL named by thread maps to its process.
17856        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, None);
17857        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17858        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
17859        // A process-group kill dooms every process in the group.
17860        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(Some(DetPid::from_raw(3)));
17861        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17862        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17863        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
17864        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17865
17866        // A second child thread that is neither held nor in a futex wait could
17867        // still run.
17868        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, child_worker, false);
17869        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child_worker);
17870        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17871        // Parked in a futex wait, it can only be woken by another thread.
17872        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child_worker, 0x404110);
17873        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17874
17875        // A child that has exited logically is reapable.
17876        scheduler
17877            .logically_exited_processes
17878            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5));
17879        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17880        scheduler
17881            .logically_exited_processes
17882            .remove(&DetPid::from_raw(5));
17883
17884        // A wait that matches no child is left alone.
17885        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
17886            parent,
17887            (
17888                DetPid::from_raw(3),
17889                ChildWaitSpec {
17890                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
17891                    ..spec
17892                },
17893            ),
17894        );
17895        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17896
17897        // A SIGKILL whose victim cannot be named disables settling for good.
17898        scheduler
17899            .blocked
17900            .child_waiters
17901            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
17902        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17903        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(None);
17904        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17905
17906        // Reaping a doomed process drops its record (last: reaping also drops
17907        // the child's wait entry).
17908        scheduler
17909            .thread_tree
17910            .process_parent
17911            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5), DetPid::from_raw(3));
17912        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17913        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17914        scheduler.consume_child_wait(DetPid::from_raw(3), DetPid::from_raw(5));
17915        assert!(!scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
17916    }
17917
17918    /// A chain of child waits down to a held child is stuck: the root waits
17919    /// for its child, which waits for a grandchild held at a gate, and the
17920    /// root's ordinary wait does not hide the cycle below it (the Codex design
17921    /// re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929). A middle
17922    /// process that could still run, or a wait in the chain that matches no
17923    /// child, keeps the chain counted as input that may still arrive.
17924    #[test]
17925    fn a_chain_of_child_waits_down_to_a_held_child_settles() {
17926        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17927        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
17928        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
17929        let middle = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17930        let leaf = DetTid::from_raw(7);
17931        let middle_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
17932        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
17933        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, middle, true);
17934        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, leaf, true);
17935        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle);
17936        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
17937        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
17938            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
17939            owner: None,
17940            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
17941        };
17942        scheduler
17943            .blocked
17944            .child_waiters
17945            .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
17946        scheduler
17947            .blocked
17948            .child_waiters
17949            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
17950        // The leaf runs: nothing is stuck.
17951        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17952        scheduler
17953            .happens_before
17954            .as_mut()
17955            .unwrap()
17956            .parked
17957            .insert(leaf);
17958        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17959
17960        // The middle process's wait matches no child: it may still end.
17961        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
17962            middle,
17963            (
17964                DetPid::from_raw(5),
17965                ChildWaitSpec {
17966                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
17967                    ..any
17968                },
17969            ),
17970        );
17971        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17972        scheduler
17973            .blocked
17974            .child_waiters
17975            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
17976        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17977
17978        // A second middle thread that could run keeps the root's wait open.
17979        scheduler
17980            .thread_tree
17981            .add_child(middle, middle_worker, false);
17982        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle_worker);
17983        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
17984    }
17985
17986    /// A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is never stuck: the
17987    /// kernel kills it at a host-timed moment when its parent thread exits.
17988    /// The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the caller's turn
17989    /// (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` in `syscalls/misc.rs`). Another parent-death signal
17990    /// is held off a gated wait like any host-timed signal, so it does not
17991    /// change the answer (the second Claude re-check of
17992    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013).
17993    #[test]
17994    fn a_process_armed_with_a_parent_death_sigkill_is_not_stuck() {
17995        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
17996            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
17997            owner: None,
17998            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
17999        };
18000        // The held child, and the middle of a chain down to a held child.
18001        for armed in [5, 7] {
18002            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
18003            scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
18004            let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
18005            let (child, leaf) = (DetTid::from_raw(5), DetTid::from_raw(7));
18006            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
18007            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, child, true);
18008            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
18009            scheduler
18010                .blocked
18011                .child_waiters
18012                .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
18013            let held = if armed == 7 {
18014                scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, leaf, true);
18015                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
18016                scheduler
18017                    .blocked
18018                    .child_waiters
18019                    .insert(child, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
18020                leaf
18021            } else {
18022                child
18023            };
18024            scheduler
18025                .happens_before
18026                .as_mut()
18027                .unwrap()
18028                .parked
18029                .insert(held);
18030            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
18031            let doomed = if armed == 7 { child } else { held };
18032            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
18033                doomed,
18034                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
18035                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM),
18036            );
18037            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
18038            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
18039                doomed,
18040                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
18041                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL),
18042            );
18043            assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
18044        }
18045    }
18046
18047    /// The enforcement predicates that drive `hb_checkpoint`: an anchor is
18048    /// reached at exactly its `SyscallCount` on the right thread, an AFTER anchor
18049    /// of a Hard edge is blocked until its BEFORE anchor fires, and firing the
18050    /// BEFORE anchor opens the gate. This mirrors the two-thread race validated
18051    /// end-to-end (main_write < worker_write forcing A before B).
18052    #[test]
18053    fn hb_runtime_gate_opens_only_after_before_anchor_fires() {
18054        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
18055            r#"{
18056              "version": 1,
18057              "threads": { "main": {"dettid": 3}, "worker": {"dettid": 5} },
18058              "events": {
18059                "main_write":   {"thread": "main",   "syscalls": 47},
18060                "worker_write": {"thread": "worker", "syscalls": 8}
18061              },
18062              "edges": [ {"before": "main_write", "after": "worker_write", "strength": "hard"} ]
18063            }"#,
18064        );
18065        let main = DetTid::from_raw(3);
18066        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
18067
18068        // Anchors resolve to the addressed (thread, count) and nothing else.
18069        assert_eq!(
18070            hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 47),
18071            vec!["main_write".to_string()]
18072        );
18073        assert_eq!(
18074            hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 8),
18075            vec!["worker_write".to_string()]
18076        );
18077        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 8).is_empty());
18078        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 47).is_empty());
18079        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 7).is_empty());
18080
18081        // Before its gating BEFORE anchor fires, the AFTER anchor is blocked and
18082        // the BEFORE anchor is free (it gates nothing).
18083        assert!(hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
18084        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("main_write"));
18085
18086        // Firing the BEFORE anchor opens the gate exactly once.
18087        assert!(hb.fired.insert("main_write".to_string()));
18088        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
18089    }
18090
18091    /// A soft edge never parks its AFTER thread, and `spawn_ordinal` addressing
18092    /// resolves against the observed spawn order (index 0 = root).
18093    #[test]
18094    fn hb_runtime_soft_edge_and_spawn_ordinal_resolution() {
18095        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
18096            r#"{
18097              "version": 1,
18098              "threads": {
18099                "root":  {"spawn_ordinal": 0},
18100                "child": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}
18101              },
18102              "events": {
18103                "a": {"thread": "root",  "syscalls": 3},
18104                "b": {"thread": "child", "syscalls": 4}
18105              },
18106              "edges": [ {"before": "a", "after": "b", "strength": "soft"} ]
18107            }"#,
18108        );
18109        // A soft edge biases but never hard-blocks, so its AFTER is never parked.
18110        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("b"));
18111
18112        // spawn_ordinal is unresolved until threads are observed at creation time.
18113        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
18114        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
18115        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3).is_empty());
18116        hb.note_spawn(root); // index 0 -> root
18117        hb.note_spawn(child); // index 1 -> first spawned child
18118        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3), vec!["a".to_string()]);
18119        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
18120        // note_spawn is idempotent, so a re-registration does not shift indices.
18121        hb.note_spawn(root);
18122        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
18123    }
18124
18125    /// A thread with an emulated sleep filed as its request, the way
18126    /// `handle_pause` and `nanosleep` file one, parked in the timed waiters at
18127    /// its deadline unless `queued`, which leaves it on the run queue with the
18128    /// request not yet admitted.
18129    fn filed_sleep(
18130        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
18131        deadline: LogicalTime,
18132        fyi: &str,
18133        queued: bool,
18134    ) -> DetTid {
18135        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
18136        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
18137        let mut request = Resources::new(target);
18138        request.insert(ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline), Permission::W);
18139        request.fyi(fyi);
18140        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
18141        if queued {
18142            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
18143        } else {
18144            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, target);
18145        }
18146        target
18147    }
18148
18149    /// A sleeper's kernel signal state: `caught` handled, `ignored` set to
18150    /// `SIG_IGN`, the rest at their default action; `blocked` its mask and
18151    /// `pending` its pending set.
18152    fn sleeper_state(caught: u64, ignored: u64, blocked: u64, pending: u64) -> KernelSignalState {
18153        KernelSignalState {
18154            caught,
18155            ignored,
18156            blocked,
18157            pending,
18158            thread_pending: pending,
18159            ..Default::default()
18160        }
18161    }
18162
18163    fn set_sleeper_state(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid, state: KernelSignalState) {
18164        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(target, state);
18165    }
18166
18167    /// Records `signals` as sent to `target` in one sender turn, each made
18168    /// pending as the kernel queues it, then installs `at_drain` (if any) as the
18169    /// state the drain reads and drains.
18170    fn send_cross_task(
18171        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
18172        target: DetTid,
18173        signals: &[i32],
18174        at_drain: Option<KernelSignalState>,
18175    ) {
18176        for signal in signals {
18177            if let Some(state) = scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.get_mut(&target) {
18178                state.pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
18179                state.thread_pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
18180            }
18181            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(*signal));
18182        }
18183        if let Some(state) = at_drain {
18184            set_sleeper_state(scheduler, target, state);
18185        }
18186        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18187        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
18188    }
18189
18190    fn assert_sleep_parked(
18191        scheduler: &Scheduler,
18192        target: DetTid,
18193        deadline: LogicalTime,
18194        case: &str,
18195    ) {
18196        assert_eq!(
18197            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18198            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
18199            "{case}"
18200        );
18201        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
18202        assert!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target).is_some(), "{case}");
18203    }
18204
18205    fn assert_sleep_woken(scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid, signals: &[i32], case: &str) {
18206        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty(), "{case}");
18207        assert_eq!(
18208            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18209            vec![target],
18210            "{case}"
18211        );
18212        assert_eq!(
18213            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
18214            signals
18215                .iter()
18216                .map(|signal| SigWrapper(*signal))
18217                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18218            "{case}"
18219        );
18220        assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{case}");
18221    }
18222
18223    /// A cross-task signal that is caught, or whose default action terminates
18224    /// the process, ends a `pause` parked in the timed waiters at
18225    /// `INDEFINITE`: the request becomes the signal set and the thread is
18226    /// queued, so its turn answers `Signaled`. Before the fix the signal was
18227    /// never recorded and the pause slept forever
18228    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
18229    #[test]
18230    fn a_caught_or_fatal_cross_task_signal_ends_a_parked_pause() {
18231        for (signal, caught) in [(libc::SIGUSR1, true), (libc::SIGTERM, false)] {
18232            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18233            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18234            let case = format!("signal {signal}, caught={caught}");
18235            assert_eq!(
18236                scheduler.signal_sleep(target),
18237                Some(SignalSleep::Pause),
18238                "{case}"
18239            );
18240            let caught_set = if caught { kernel_signal_bit(signal) } else { 0 };
18241            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught_set, 0, 0, 0));
18242            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
18243            assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[signal], &case);
18244        }
18245    }
18246
18247    /// A pause whose request is filed but still queued, not yet admitted to
18248    /// the timed waiters, is ended in place: it stays queued exactly once with
18249    /// the signal set as its request.
18250    #[test]
18251    fn a_cross_task_signal_ends_a_pause_still_on_the_run_queue() {
18252        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18253        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, true);
18254        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
18255        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
18256        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], "queued pause");
18257    }
18258
18259    /// Signals a pause does not return for leave it parked: one its mask
18260    /// blocks, one set to `SIG_IGN`, and `SIGWINCH` and `SIGCONT` with their
18261    /// default action, which ignores them. In a batch with one that does end
18262    /// it, only that one is delivered as the wake's signal set.
18263    #[test]
18264    fn a_blocked_or_ignored_cross_task_signal_leaves_a_pause_parked() {
18265        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18266        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18267        let state = sleeper_state(
18268            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
18269            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
18270            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGHUP),
18271            0,
18272        );
18273        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, state);
18274        let quiet = [libc::SIGHUP, libc::SIGUSR2, libc::SIGWINCH, libc::SIGCONT];
18275        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &quiet, None);
18276        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "quiet signals");
18277
18278        let mut batch = quiet.to_vec();
18279        batch.push(libc::SIGUSR1);
18280        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &batch, None);
18281        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "batch with SIGUSR1");
18282    }
18283
18284    /// A signal recorded in the sender's turn but no longer pending at the
18285    /// drain does not end the sleep: a caught `SIGTSTP` that the same turn's
18286    /// `SIGCONT` cancelled, or a `SIGUSR1` flushed when its disposition became
18287    /// `SIG_IGN` and then a handler again. Linux would leave the sleep asleep.
18288    #[test]
18289    fn a_cross_task_signal_withdrawn_before_the_drain_leaves_the_sleep_parked() {
18290        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
18291        for (fyi, deadline) in [
18292            (PAUSE_FYI, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
18293            (NANOSLEEP_FYI, deadline),
18294        ] {
18295            let caught = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18296            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18297            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
18298            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0));
18299            send_cross_task(
18300                &mut scheduler,
18301                target,
18302                &[libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGCONT],
18303                Some(sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0)),
18304            );
18305            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, deadline, fyi);
18306        }
18307    }
18308
18309    /// A signal that is unblocked and ignored when it is sent is discarded by
18310    /// Linux at generation, so a handler installed later in the sender's turn
18311    /// does not make it end the sleep, although ptrace left it pending.
18312    #[test]
18313    fn a_signal_ignored_when_sent_never_ends_the_sleep() {
18314        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18315        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18316        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18317        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, 0, 0));
18318        send_cross_task(
18319            &mut scheduler,
18320            target,
18321            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
18322            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
18323        );
18324        assert_sleep_parked(
18325            &scheduler,
18326            target,
18327            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
18328            "ignored when sent",
18329        );
18330
18331        // Blocked when sent, it is kept pending and does end the sleep once it
18332        // is caught and unblocked, as Linux delivers it.
18333        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18334        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18335        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, usr1, 0));
18336        send_cross_task(
18337            &mut scheduler,
18338            target,
18339            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
18340            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
18341        );
18342        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "blocked when sent");
18343    }
18344
18345    /// The signals a gated wait holds are never recorded for a sleep, although
18346    /// caught and pending: `SIGCHLD`, and a signal a host-timed source armed by
18347    /// the guest can post to its process, as for a parked futex waiter. The
18348    /// kernel can post either at a host-chosen moment, so neither the pending
18349    /// bit nor the recorded send could tell whether a later guest call, a
18350    /// `sigaction(SIG_IGN)` or a `SIGCONT`, took the guest's copy back.
18351    #[test]
18352    fn a_held_signal_never_ends_the_sleep() {
18353        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18354        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
18355        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18356        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18357        scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr2);
18358        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(chld | usr2, 0, 0, 0));
18359        for signal in [libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2] {
18360            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(signal));
18361            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{signal}");
18362        }
18363        send_cross_task(
18364            &mut scheduler,
18365            target,
18366            &[libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2],
18367            None,
18368        );
18369        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "held signals");
18370    }

18372    /// A state the drain cannot read never invents an interruption: a thread
18373    /// that is gone is left to its retirement, and a live one ends the run with
18374    /// a diagnostic.
18375    #[test]
18376    fn an_unreadable_sleeper_state_never_wakes_the_sleep() {
18377        for failure in [
18378            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
18379            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Unreadable(reverie::Errno::EMFILE),
18380        ] {
18381            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18382            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18383            scheduler.test_sleeper_read_failures.insert(target, failure);
18384            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
18385            let case = format!("{failure:?}");
18386            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, &case);
18387            assert_eq!(
18388                scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_some(),
18389                failure != sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
18390                "{case}"
18391            );
18392        }
18393    }

18395    /// A default stop ends a pause, which Linux then restarts once the process
18396    /// continues (`Detcore::handle_pause` returns `ERESTARTNOHAND`), but never a
18397    /// `nanosleep`, whose restart would have to keep its deadline: the stop
18398    /// takes effect when the sleep ends. A caught or fatal signal ends both.
18399    #[test]
18400    fn a_default_stop_ends_a_pause_but_not_a_nanosleep() {
18401        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
18402        for signal in [libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGSTOP] {
18403            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18404            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18405            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
18406            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
18407            assert_sleep_woken(
18408                &scheduler,
18409                target,
18410                &[signal],
18411                &format!("pause, signal {signal}"),
18412            );
18413
18414            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18415            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
18416            assert_eq!(
18417                scheduler.signal_sleep(target),
18418                Some(SignalSleep::Nanosleep { deadline })
18419            );
18420            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
18421            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
18422            assert_sleep_parked(
18423                &scheduler,
18424                target,
18425                deadline,
18426                &format!("nanosleep, signal {signal}"),
18427            );
18428        }
18429        for (signal, caught) in [(libc::SIGUSR1, true), (libc::SIGTERM, false)] {
18430            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18431            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
18432            let caught_set = if caught { kernel_signal_bit(signal) } else { 0 };
18433            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught_set, 0, 0, 0));
18434            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
18435            assert_sleep_woken(
18436                &scheduler,
18437                target,
18438                &[signal],
18439                &format!("nanosleep, signal {signal}"),
18440            );
18441        }
18442    }
18443
18444    /// A signal drained once a `nanosleep`'s deadline has passed leaves the
18445    /// sleep to complete normally at its timed pop, as Linux completes a sleep
18446    /// whose timer has fired; the signal is delivered as the call returns.
18447    #[test]
18448    fn a_cross_task_signal_after_a_nanosleep_deadline_leaves_it_to_complete() {
18449        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
18450        for committed in [deadline, deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1)] {
18451            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18452            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
18453            scheduler.committed_time = committed;
18454            let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18455            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, 0));
18456            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], None);
18457            assert_sleep_parked(
18458                &scheduler,
18459                target,
18460                deadline,
18461                &format!("committed {committed}"),
18462            );
18463        }
18464    }

18466    /// What is not recorded at all: a `SIGKILL`, which the kernel acts on for
18467    /// a traced thread without the thread running, as before; a sleep request
18468    /// that is neither a tagged `pause` nor a tagged `nanosleep`; and any sleep
18469    /// on a backend that does not report the guest's signal state, which keeps
18470    /// its previous behavior.
18471    #[test]
18472    fn sleeps_that_cross_task_signals_do_not_reach() {
18473        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18474        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
18475        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGKILL));
18476        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "SIGKILL");
18477
18478        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
18479        for (deadline, fyi) in [
18480            (deadline, ""),
18481            (deadline, PAUSE_FYI),
18482            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, ""),
18483        ] {
18484            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18485            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
18486            assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{deadline} {fyi:?}");
18487            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGTERM));
18488            assert!(
18489                scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(),
18490                "{deadline} {fyi:?}"
18491            );
18492        }
18493
18494        for (deadline, fyi) in [
18495            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
18496            (deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI),
18497        ] {
18498            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
18499                sequentialize_threads: true,
18500                ..Config::default()
18501            });
18502            assert!(!scheduler.models_signal_targets);
18503            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
18504            assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{fyi}");
18505            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGTERM));
18506            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{fyi}");
18507        }
18508    }

18510    #[test]
18511    fn backoff_sleep_doubles_each_round_then_caps() {
18512        let got: Vec<u64> = (1..=15).map(backoff_sleep_micros).collect();
18513        assert_eq!(
18514            got,
18515            vec![
18516                2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 10_000, 10_000
18517            ]
18518        );

18520    /// File the exact owner-turn snapshot without registering a real host PID.
18521    fn in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18522        deadline: LogicalTime,
18523        fyi: &str,
18524        snapshot: crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm,
18525        queued: bool,
18526    ) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, Resources) {
18527        let config = Config {
18528            sequentialize_threads: true,
18529            ..Config::default()
18530        }
18531        .with_backend(|backend| *backend = BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST);
18532        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
18533        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, queued);
18534        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(target, target, true);
18535        scheduler
18536            .exec_incarnations
18537            .insert(target, MmId::initial(target));
18538        let mut request = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
18539            .req
18540            .try_read()
18541            .unwrap()
18542            .unwrap();
18543        request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm = Some(snapshot);
18544        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request.clone()));
18545        (scheduler, target, request)
18546    }
18547
18548    fn default_sleep_alarm_snapshot() -> crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm {
18549        crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm {
18550            disposition: crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Default,
18551            blocked: false,
18552        }
18553    }
18554
18555    /// Drive the real pop, diversion and typed grant boundaries directly,
18556    /// so an unexpected rejection cannot send a physical signal to a fake PID.
18557    /// Guest probes exercise the complete dispatcher against real targets.
18558    #[test]
18559    fn in_guest_one_shot_alarm_grants_fatal_sleep_without_host_send() {
18560        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
18561        for (deadline, fyi) in [
18562            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
18563            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(20), NANOSLEEP_FYI),
18564        ] {
18565            for normal_due in [true, false] {
18566                let (mut scheduler, target, original) =
18567                    in_guest_alarm_sleep(deadline, fyi, default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(), false);
18568                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_alarm(
18569                    expiry,
18570                    target,
18571                    target,
18572                    Signal::SIGALRM,
18573                    LogicalTime::ZERO,
18574                );
18575                let (event_ns, TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, tid, signal)) =
18576                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.pop().unwrap()
18577                else {
18578                    panic!("the alarm must expire before its sleep");
18579                };
18580                assert_eq!(event_ns, expiry);
18581                assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_state(target), None);
18582                // Models empty-queue dispatch with committed_time still behind
18583                // the event, as well as the ordinary due-event path.
18584                scheduler.committed_time = if normal_due {
18585                    expiry
18586                } else {
18587                    LogicalTime::ZERO
18588                };
18589                let turn_before = scheduler.turn;
18590                let committed_before = scheduler.committed_time;
18591                let observed_now = if normal_due {
18592                    expiry
18593                } else {
18594                    expiry + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1)
18595                };
18596                assert!(scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18597                    event_ns,
18598                    id,
18599                    tid,
18600                    match signal {
18601                        timed_waiters::TimerSignal::Send(signal) => signal,
18602                        other => panic!("an alarm sends a deliverable signal, not {other}"),
18603                    },
18604                    observed_now
18605                ));
18606                assert_eq!(
18607                    scheduler.turn, turn_before,
18608                    "diversion is not an extra guest grant"
18609                );
18610                assert_eq!(scheduler.committed_time, committed_before);
18611                assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
18612                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
18613                assert_eq!(
18614                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
18615                    None
18616                );
18617                assert_eq!(
18618                    scheduler
18619                        .run_queue
18620                        .tids()
18621                        .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
18622                        .count(),
18623                    1
18624                );
18625
18626                // A later signal and even a direct generic substitution cannot
18627                // steal the typed response from the consumed alarm.
18628                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18629                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
18630                let mut generic = Resources::new(target);
18631                generic.insert(
18632                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)),
18633                    Permission::W,
18634                );
18635                scheduler.force_unblock_thread(target, generic);
18636                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
18637                assert_eq!(
18638                    scheduler
18639                        .run_queue
18640                        .tids()
18641                        .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
18642                        .count(),
18643                    1
18644                );
18645
18646                let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
18647                assert!(scheduler.unblock_guest(target, &response).is_ok());
18648                assert_eq!(
18649                    scheduler.turn,
18650                    turn_before + 1,
18651                    "the fatal continuation consumes exactly one ordinary grant"
18652                );
18653                assert!(matches!(
18654                    response.try_read(),
18655                    Some(SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm)
18656                ));
18657                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18658                    target,
18659                    target,
18660                    Some(MmId::initial(target)),
18661                    &original,
18662                ));
18663                assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
18664                assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
18665            }
18666        }
18667    }

18669    #[test]
18670    fn in_guest_ignored_and_blocked_alarm_preserve_filed_or_parked_sleep() {
18671        use crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm;
18672        use crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition;
18673        for snapshot in [
18674            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
18675                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Ignored,
18676                blocked: false,
18677            },
18678            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
18679                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Default,
18680                blocked: true,
18681            },
18682            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
18683                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Handled,
18684                blocked: true,
18685            },
18686        ] {
18687            for (deadline, fyi) in [
18688                (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
18689                (LogicalTime::from_nanos(20), NANOSLEEP_FYI),
18690            ] {
18691                for queued in [false, true] {
18692                    let (mut scheduler, target, _) =
18693                        in_guest_alarm_sleep(deadline, fyi, snapshot, queued);
18694                    assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18695                        LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
18696                        timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18697                        target,
18698                        Signal::SIGALRM,
18699                        LogicalTime::ZERO
18700                    ));
18701                    // This method is the wake half after a successful physical
18702                    // send. Kernel pending semantics belong to the guest probes.
18703                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGALRM);
18704                    assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), queued);
18705                    assert_eq!(
18706                        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
18707                        (!queued).then_some(deadline)
18708                    );
18709                    assert_eq!(
18710                        scheduler.next_turns[&target]
18711                            .req
18712                            .try_read()
18713                            .unwrap()
18714                            .unwrap()
18715                            .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep(),
18716                        Some((snapshot, deadline))
18717                    );
18718                    assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
18719                }
18720            }
18721        }
18722    }

18724    #[test]
18725    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_other_identities_and_rearmed_timers() {
18726        let (mut scheduler, target, _) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18727            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
18728            PAUSE_FYI,
18729            default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
18730            false,
18731        );
18732        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
18733        for (id, signal) in [
18734            (
18735                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(target, 1),
18736                Signal::SIGALRM,
18737            ),
18738            (
18739                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit {
18740                    child: DetPid::from_raw(200),
18741                    parent: target,
18742                },
18743                Signal::SIGALRM,
18744            ),
18745            (
18746                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
18747                Signal::SIGALRM,
18748            ),
18749            (timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target), Signal::SIGUSR1),
18750        ] {
18751            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18752                expiry,
18753                id,
18754                target,
18755                signal,
18756                LogicalTime::ZERO
18757            ));
18758        }
18759        for interval in [LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::from_nanos(5)] {
18760            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_alarm(
18761                expiry,
18762                target,
18763                target,
18764                Signal::SIGALRM,
18765                interval,
18766            );
18767            if interval != LogicalTime::ZERO {
18768                assert!(matches!(
18769                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.pop(),
18770                    Some((_, TimedEvent::SignalEvt(..)))
18771                ));
18772            }
18773            assert!(
18774                scheduler
18775                    .blocked
18776                    .timed_waiters
18777                    .alarm_state(target)
18778                    .is_some(),
18779                "unconsumed one-shot or rearmed recurring identity"
18780            );
18781            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18782                expiry,
18783                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18784                target,
18785                Signal::SIGALRM,
18786                LogicalTime::ZERO
18787            ));
18788        }
18789        assert_eq!(
18790            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
18791            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE)
18792        );
18793        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
18794    }

18796    #[test]
18797    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_unqualified_requests_and_states() {
18798        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
18799        for case in 0..10 {
18800            let (mut scheduler, target, mut request) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18801                LogicalTime::from_nanos(20),
18802                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
18803                default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
18804                false,
18805            );
18806            match case {
18807                0 => scheduler.backend = Config::default().backend,
18808                1 => request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm = None,
18809                2 => request.fyi = String::new(),
18810                3 => request.insert(ResourceID::TraceReplay, Permission::W),
18811                4 => {
18812                    scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
18813                }
18814                5 => scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(target),
18815                6 => {
18816                    scheduler
18817                        .thread_tree
18818                        .add_child(target, DetTid::from_raw(101), false);
18819                }
18820                7 => {
18821                    let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
18822                    hb.parked.insert(target);
18823                    scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
18824                }
18825                8 => {
18826                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(target);
18827                    scheduler
18828                        .blocked
18829                        .timed_waiters
18830                        .insert(LogicalTime::from_nanos(21), target);
18831                }
18832                9 => {
18833                    request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm.as_mut().unwrap().disposition =
18834                        crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Handled;
18835                }
18836                _ => unreachable!(),
18837            }
18838            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
18839            assert!(
18840                !scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18841                    expiry,
18842                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18843                    target,
18844                    Signal::SIGALRM,
18845                    LogicalTime::ZERO
18846                ),
18847                "case {case}"
18848            );
18849            assert!(
18850                !scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target),
18851                "case {case}"
18852            );
18853        }
18854    }

18856    #[test]
18857    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_sleep_deadline_equality_and_already_ahead_time() {
18858        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(20);
18859        for (committed, event_ns, observed_now) in [
18860            (LogicalTime::ZERO, deadline, LogicalTime::ZERO),
18861            (
18862                LogicalTime::ZERO,
18863                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
18864                LogicalTime::ZERO,
18865            ),
18866            (deadline, LogicalTime::from_nanos(10), LogicalTime::ZERO),
18867            (
18868                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
18869                LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
18870                LogicalTime::ZERO,
18871            ),
18872            // A control hook crossed the sleep deadline while committed_time
18873            // and the popped event still lag. The clock must not rewind into
18874            // permission to interrupt a completed sleep.
18875            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::from_nanos(10), deadline),
18876            (
18877                LogicalTime::ZERO,
18878                LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
18879                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
18880            ),
18881        ] {
18882            let (mut scheduler, target, _) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18883                deadline,
18884                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
18885                default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
18886                false,
18887            );
18888            scheduler.committed_time = committed;
18889            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18890                event_ns,
18891                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18892                target,
18893                Signal::SIGALRM,
18894                observed_now
18895            ));
18896            assert_eq!(
18897                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
18898                Some(deadline)
18899            );
18900            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
18901        }
18902    }

18904    #[test]
18905    fn in_guest_fatal_response_requires_original_sleep_current_mm_and_owned_grant() {
18906        let (mut scheduler, target, original) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18907            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
18908            PAUSE_FYI,
18909            default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
18910            false,
18911        );
18912        let mm = MmId::initial(target);
18913        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18914            target,
18915            target,
18916            Some(mm),
18917            &original
18918        ));
18919        assert!(scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18920            LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
18921            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18922            target,
18923            Signal::SIGALRM,
18924            LogicalTime::ZERO
18925        ));
18926        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
18927        assert!(scheduler.unblock_guest(target, &response).is_ok());
18928        assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18929            target,
18930            target,
18931            Some(mm),
18932            &original
18933        ));
18934        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(target, target, None, &original));
18935        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18936            target,
18937            DetPid::from_raw(200),
18938            Some(mm),
18939            &original
18940        ));
18941        let mut unqualified = original.clone();
18942        unqualified.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm = None;
18943        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18944            target,
18945            target,
18946            Some(mm),
18947            &unqualified
18948        ));
18949        let mut fabricated = Resources::new(target);
18950        fabricated.insert(ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm, Permission::W);
18951        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18952            target,
18953            target,
18954            Some(mm),
18955            &fabricated
18956        ));
18957        scheduler
18958            .exec_incarnations
18959            .insert(target, MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(200)));
18960        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18961            target,
18962            target,
18963            Some(mm),
18964            &original
18965        ));
18966        scheduler.exec_incarnations.insert(target, mm);
18967        scheduler.parked.running = None;
18968        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
18969            target,
18970            target,
18971            Some(mm),
18972            &original
18973        ));
18974    }

18976    #[test]
18977    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_retirement_leaves_no_pending_typed_request() {
18978        let (mut scheduler, target, _) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
18979            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
18980            PAUSE_FYI,
18981            default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
18982            false,
18983        );
18984        assert!(scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
18985            LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
18986            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
18987            target,
18988            Signal::SIGALRM,
18989            LogicalTime::ZERO
18990        ));
18991        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
18992        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&target, &target, MmId::initial(target));
18993        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
18994        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&target));
18995        assert_eq!(
18996            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
18997            None
18998        );
18999        assert!(matches!(
19000            response.try_read(),
19001            Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(None))
19002        ));
19003    }

19005    #[test]
19006    fn in_guest_handled_sleep_alarm_still_uses_existing_ledger() {
19007        let snapshot = crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm {
19008            disposition: crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Handled,
19009            blocked: false,
19010        };
19011        let (mut scheduler, target, _) =
19012            in_guest_alarm_sleep(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, snapshot, false);
19013        scheduler.set_sigalrm_handled(target, true);
19014        scheduler.set_sigalrm_blocked(target, false);
19015        assert!(scheduler.divert_sigalrm(target, Signal::SIGALRM));
19016        assert!(scheduler.sigalrm_pending(target));
19017        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
19018        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
19019    }
